assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. ONE GREAT RIFT — the single wide split that eventually calves a berg off the front of a glacier — seen from directly above and ALONE, its long axis running UP the frame. ONE CRACK AND ONLY ONE. No second crevasse, no parallel companion, no branch, no scatter of small splits alongside it, no group of any kind, and never two or three pieces stacked up the frame. The engine places many of these; this picture supplies one. ⚠️ IT IS LONG AND IT IS THIN, AND THIS IS THE ONE THING THE LAST ROUND GOT WRONG. Measured on the last delivery this came back at 3.8 : 1 against the 8 to 1 asked — a fat lozenge, not a crack. So here it is as a picture rather than as a ratio: THE CRACK RUNS THE WHOLE HEIGHT OF THIS TALL FRAME, from close to the top edge to close to the bottom edge, and AT ITS WIDEST POINT IT IS NO WIDER THAN ONE 8TH OF THAT LENGTH. Lay 8 copies of its width end to end and they make its length. THE FRAME IS TALL AND THAT IS THE MEASURE: the crack runs almost its whole height, and AT ITS WIDEST IT COVERS NO MORE THAN ONE THIRD OF THE FRAME'S WIDTH. ⚠️ IF IT LOOKS LIKE A LEAF, AN EYE, A CANOE, A POD OR A POINTED OVAL IT IS FAR TOO FAT. A crevasse is a LINE in the ice that happens to have width. AND IT IS AN ANTARCTIC CREVASSE, NOT A CRACK IN A PAVEMENT: about 130 metres from end to end and 16 metres across at its widest, cut into an ice sheet hundreds of metres thick, and deep enough that the bottom of it is not visible. It is MARKEDLY WIDER THAN AN ORDINARY CREVASSE and wide enough to see well down into, and its line is not ruled straight: it steps once or twice along its length by about a third of its own width, the way a fracture jogs where it crosses an older healed crack. ⚠️ IT IS NOT A SYMMETRICAL LENS, AND THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT SOUNDS. The last delivery came back as a fat pointed almond — mirror-symmetric about its long axis AND about its short axis, with even concentric rings inside it and a slit down the exact centre. A shape built that way stops reading as a crack in ice and starts reading as ANATOMY, and it is an unusable picture whatever else is right about it. THE FIX IS GEOMETRY AND IT IS THREE THINGS. (1) THE CENTRELINE WANDERS. It is not a straight line and not a smooth arc: it bends and jogs along its length, and the bands inside follow that wander, so they are NOT concentric ellipses. (2) THE SNOW LIP IS NOT AN EVEN BORDER. It is drifted snow, so it is fat here and thin there, and wider on one side than the other over long stretches. ⚠️ THAT APPLIES TO THE OUTER SNOW LIP ONLY — inside it the OPENING itself, shoulder and throat and core, stays centred and even, because that is the acceptance test above and it is the one thing a tilted camera cannot fake. Uneven snow outside, symmetrical opening inside. (3) THE TWO ENDS ARE NOT ALIKE AND THE WIDEST POINT IS NOT IN THE MIDDLE: it sits about a third of the way along, one end closes gradually over a long snow-choked stretch and the other stops more abruptly at a jog. NO POINTED OVAL, no almond, no leaf, no eye, no vesica, no mirror-image halves, and no smooth unbroken curve running the whole length of either edge — every edge of a fracture is built from short straight steps meeting at angles. ⚠️ THE ONLY THING DRAWN IS THE CRACK ITSELF. Everything outside its snow lip is FULLY TRANSPARENT. The engine already draws the ice this sits in; this art only adds the split. Do NOT draw a patch of snow, a plate, a tile, a rounded field or ANY pale shape around it — a background behind the crack lands on the ice as a visible rectangle of slightly wrong white. ⚠️ A CREVASSE SEEN FROM STRAIGHT ABOVE IS A SET OF NESTED BANDS SHARING ONE CENTRELINE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE PICTURE. Working from the outside in, each band lying INSIDE the last and running the full length of the crack: (1) the SNOW LIP, a crisp near-white band all the way round; (2) the SHOULDER, pale blue ice where the opening flares; (3) the THROAT, a stronger blue band inside that; (4) the CORE, the darkest tone, a long thin lens running down the MIDDLE and closed at both ends. Four bands, hard edges between them, no soft gradient anywhere. ⚠️ THE ACCEPTANCE TEST IS THAT THE CORE IS CENTRED, and it is the one thing a tilted camera cannot fake. Cut across the crack anywhere along its length: the pale ice on the two sides of the core must be THE SAME WIDTH on both sides. A crack drawn with the pale gathered along one long edge and the dark gathered along the other is a picture taken from BESIDE it rather than above it, and it is wrong however good it looks. ⚠️ AND THERE IS NO FAR WALL. If one side shows a broad blue face receding away from you while the other side shows only a thin edge, the camera was tilted. You are directly over this, so the two sides are the same. ⚠️ BECAUSE IT IS WIDE, ITS BANDS ARE BROAD AND THE THROAT SHOWS STRUCTURE — and this is the one place in this family where interior detail is wanted, so put it there and nowhere else. The throat band breaks into two or three long flat facets down EACH side, the divisions running square across the crack rather than along it, each facet a single flat tone. One or two near-white ICE LEDGES sit within the throat where a slab has dropped from the lip, hard-edged and small. THE BANDS STAY NESTED WHILE THIS HAPPENS: whatever the facets do, the dark core still runs down the middle with equal pale ice on both sides of it. ⚠️ THE WHITE KEEPS ITS SHARE OF THE WIDTH AS THE CRACK GETS BIGGER. Snow lip and pale shoulder together take about HALF the crack's total width, so the dark core never spreads beyond the middle half of it. A big crevasse is a big crack with a big white edge — it is NOT a wide blue channel with a thin white line drawn round it, and at this size that is the difference between a crack in the ice and a stretch of open sea. ⚠️ IT IS A HOLE, NOT A BLADE. A long shape with a bright face down one side and a dark face down the other is a SPLINTER OF ICE LYING ON THE SNOW, not a gap in it. This is an EMPTINESS: the darkest tone in the picture is in the middle of it, it has no top, nothing about it stands up, and NOTHING GLOWS. Do not put a soft white halo, a rim-light or an outline stroke around the outside — an even glow tracing the shape is precisely what makes a thing float above its background. The snow lip is the outer band and it is SNOW: opaque, hard-edged, RAGGED, overhanging the opening in places and worn back in others, and plainly wider in some stretches than in others. It never traces the crack at an even width. THE LIGHT COMES FROM THE UPPER LEFT AND IT DOES NOT GET IN. Direct light lands only on the snow lip up at the surface, where it may make the lower-right side of the lip a shade brighter and the upper-left side a shade cooler — a whisper, no more. Below the lip no sunlight reaches at all: the inside of a crevasse is lit by the open sky alone, which arrives from every direction equally, so THE INTERIOR HAS NO LIT FACE AND NO SHADED FACE. Each band is simply darker than the band outside it, and that stepping-down is the only reason any part of the interior is dark. EACH END CLOSES BLUNT AND SNOW-CHOKED. The crack narrows over its last stretch and drifted snow fills it before it stops, so the final tenth at each end is WHITE rather than a black point. ⚠️ A RAZOR-SHARP NEEDLE TIP AT EACH END IS ONE OF THE THINGS THAT MAKES THESE READ AS BLADES. It narrows at BOTH ends alike, which is not the same thing as converging: a converging shape is one that is plainly wider at one end than at the other, and that is the tilt this picture must not have. Colours: snow lip #F4FAFF, shoulder #C6DEF1, throat #7FAECF, core #3F7CA9, and a deepest note no darker than #235C86. ⚠️ IT MUST NOT READ AS OPEN WATER, AND AT THIS SIZE THAT IS A REAL RISK RATHER THAN A THEORETICAL ONE. A long dark-blue channel with soft edges is a lead of open sea, and this venue is full of real water at #1D4066 — a player who reads one of these as a passage has been lied to. So: nothing here goes navy, nothing goes near-black, the hard white lip runs the whole way round without a break, and the blues stay clean and CYAN rather than deep and grey. NOTHING ELSE: no water, no boat, no floe, no rock, no meltwater pond, no snowfield, no drift lobe, no second crack, no wildlife, no track, no footprint. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the crack stands alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies the ice it is cut into.
assets.note: THE VENUE'S STORY IN ONE PROP, AND THE ONE THAT IS PLACED ALONE. Glacier Sound's signature moment is a calving that reshapes the return leg (venues.md 9), and a rift is the calving that has not happened yet: ONE of these, parallel to and set back from the ice front on `shape-3` or `shape-4`, and the player sails past the next berg before it exists. Never two, and never inside a field — [[arctic-crevasse]] is the one that scatters, and a rift with cracks all round it is just the biggest crack in a field. ⚠️ WATCH THE WIDTH ON DELIVERY, BECAUSE IT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE ROW. 1200u at 8:1 is 150u across — sixteen metres, nearly three boat lengths — against [[arctic-crevasse]]'s 56u at 14:1. If the generator returns this family's habitual hairline the asset is just a long [[arctic-crevasse]] and should be rejected. Measure the two on the same contact sheet rather than by eye on the masters, where everything looks wide. bake 2 and a 3072 master: 1200 x 2 is 2400px of bake, against 2642px of subject available from a 3072 master at fillTo 0.86. At the profile's 4x it would want 4800px and invent most of them — the trap the world-prop profile names. Read [[arctic-crevasse]]'s note first: it carries the round-1 rejection, the nested-bands construction and the placement recipes for all three. ── ✅ ACCEPTED AS DELIVERED 2026-08-23, owner's call: 'they look good enough'. The rework block is cleared, so this row is finished art rather than a placeholder. TWO KNOWN DEPARTURES STAY ON THE RECORD, because accepting them is a decision and not an oversight. (1) It measures 3.8:1 where the subject asks 8:1 — a fatter rift than specced, which reads fine and makes the width ladder against [[arctic-crevasse]] shallower than designed. (2) It was drawn for world 440 and ships at 1200, so it UPSCALES 1.43x and is soft at full size. If it is ever placed large and the softness shows, the cheap fix is to drop `world` to ~720, which is the honest size for the pixels present; the expensive fix is a re-roll at 8:1 in a tall frame.

You are directly over this, so the two sides are the same. ⚠️ A BRIDGE IS SNOW, NOT A GAP, AND THIS IS THIS ROW'S DEFINING FAILURE. Where a bridge crosses, what you see is the BRIDGE: unbroken opaque white snow, the same tone as the lip, filling the whole width of the crack and hiding everything below it. THE SPRITE IS ONE CONTINUOUS SHAPE FROM END TO END. Cut across it anywhere along its length and you cut through either open crack or white bridge — never through empty background. The last round came back as THREE SEPARATE PIECES floating one above another with transparent gaps where the bridges should have been, and that is the single thing this picture must not do. ⚠️ AND A BRIDGE IS PART OF THE SURFACE, NOT A STRAP LAID ON TOP. It is continuous with the snow lip on both sides — the lip runs into it and out the other side with no step, no outline and no change of tone — so bridge and lip are plainly one unbroken sheet of snow with a hole in it. Its two edges facing into the open crack are TORN and scalloped, thicker where the drift is deep and thinning to a ragged overhang where it is about to collapse; they are never parallel and never straight. A white rectangle with clean straight edges lying across the crack is a piece of tape. ⚠️ THE WHITE KEEPS ITS SHARE OF THE WIDTH AS THE CRACK GETS BIGGER. Snow lip and pale shoulder together take about HALF the crack's total width, so the dark core never spreads beyond the middle half of it. A big crevasse is a big crack with a big white edge — it is NOT a wide blue channel with a thin white line drawn round it, and at this size that is the difference between a crack in the ice and a stretch of open sea. ⚠️ IT IS A HOLE, NOT A BLADE. A long shape with a bright face down one side and a dark face down the other is a SPLINTER OF ICE LYING ON THE SNOW, not a gap in it. This is an EMPTINESS: the darkest tone in the picture is in the middle of it, it has no top, nothing about it stands up, and NOTHING GLOWS. Do not put a soft white halo, a rim-light or an outline stroke around the outside — an even glow tracing the shape is precisely what makes a thing float above its background. The snow lip is the outer band and it is SNOW: opaque, hard-edged, RAGGED, overhanging the opening in places and worn back in others, and plainly wider in some stretches than in others. It never traces the crack at an even width. THE LIGHT COMES FROM THE UPPER LEFT AND IT DOES NOT GET IN. Direct light lands only on the snow lip up at the surface, where it may make the lower-right side of the lip a shade brighter and the upper-left side a shade cooler — a whisper, no more. Below the lip no sunlight reaches at all: the inside of a crevasse is lit by the open sky alone, which arrives from every direction equally, so THE INTERIOR HAS NO LIT FACE AND NO SHADED FACE. Each band is simply darker than the band outside it, and that stepping-down is the only reason any part of the interior is dark. EACH END CLOSES BLUNT AND SNOW-CHOKED. The crack narrows over its last stretch and drifted snow fills it before it stops, so the final tenth at each end is WHITE rather than a black point. ⚠️ A RAZOR-SHARP NEEDLE TIP AT EACH END IS ONE OF THE THINGS THAT MAKES THESE READ AS BLADES. It narrows at BOTH ends alike, which is not the same thing as converging: a converging shape is one that is plainly wider at one end than at the other, and that is the tilt this picture must not have. Colours: snow lip #F4FAFF, shoulder #C6DEF1, throat #7FAECF, core #3F7CA9, and a deepest note no darker than #235C86. ⚠️ IT MUST NOT READ AS OPEN WATER, AND AT THIS SIZE THAT IS A REAL RISK RATHER THAN A THEORETICAL ONE. assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. ONE SERAC — a single leaning tower of glacier ice, standing where the sheet has fractured — seen from directly above and ALONE. ONE BLOCK, ALONE: no second tower, no rubble field, no companion, nothing leaning against it. Its plan is a blunt angular polygon of four to six straight-ish sides meeting at hard corners, roughly as tall as it is wide, no two sides the same length and nothing rounded or lobed anywhere. ⚠️ IT IS A TOWER AND YOU ARE OVER THE TOP OF IT, WHICH IS THE HARD PART OF THIS PICTURE. From straight above you cannot see how tall a thing is, so the height has to be carried by STEPS AND VALUE instead: the summit plane is the smallest and brightest shape in the picture, the ice below it steps outward in two or three broad ledges, each a flat even tone a clear step darker than the one above it, and the lowest ledge is darkest. Hard straight edges between the steps, no soft gradient anywhere. The light comes from the UPPER LEFT of the frame, so every step shows a narrow band of shaded wall on its LOWER-RIGHT side and none on its upper-left. ⚠️ THAT BAND IS A RIM, NOT A FACE. If a whole wall is standing up in the picture — a facet as wide as the top, with its own shape and its own shading — the camera was tilted and the image is wrong however good it looks. You are not beside this thing, you are directly over it. IT IS GLACIER ICE, NOT SNOW: hard, dense and blue where it is thick. ⚠️ AND IT IS BUILT FROM LARGE FLAT PLANES — every surface ONE flat tone edge to edge, meeting its neighbour on a hard line, fewer than a dozen tones in the whole picture. No airbrush, no soft shading, no gloss, no sheen, and none of the crumpled-paper or draped-cloth look that comes of shading a slope smoothly: measured on this venue's peaks, that failure put only 14% of the picture on a flat plane where the style wants four fifths. ⚠️ DEEP IS NOT THE SAME AS BLUE, AND THIS IS WHAT THE FIRST THREE SERACS GOT WRONG. Glacier ice is blue where it is thick, but on this venue a saturated blue is WATER: the sound's water is #1D4066 and a serac stands within a few boat lengths of it. Every tone below must stay close to neutral — grey-blue, not rich blue — and no tone anywhere may come within 25 units of colour distance of that water. That offset is the only cue for the lean that a straight-down camera can give, so it must be unmistakable. At the foot on the low side, a SHORT SKIRT OF FALLEN ICE BLOCKS — five or six angular chips, none more than a fifth of the tower's width, lying at scattered angles and touching the tower rather than ringed around it. NOTHING ELSE: no snow field, no ground, no water, no crevasse, no rock, no wildlife. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the object is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies the ice it sits on.
assets.note: THE SMALL SHARP ONE. assets.note: THE ICEFALL, AND THE ONE ASSET IN THIS BATCH THAT ARGUES WITH art-pipeline 3b. assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. A GREAT DARK NUNATAK — a whole massif of bare granite standing up THROUGH an ice sheet, the summits of a buried mountain — seen from directly above and ALONE. THIS IS THE LARGEST THING IN THIS VENUE AND IT SHOULD LOOK IT. A broad, heavy, compact mass roughly as tall as it is wide, with TWO SUMMITS, one clearly higher than the other, joined by a sagging ridge crest. From those two summits, FOUR OR FIVE SPUR RIDGES run outward and downward to where the rock disappears under the ice. ⚠️ THE SPURS ARE NOT A STAR. They are of four different lengths, they leave at four unequal angles, two of them are close together on one flank and the others well apart, and one is long enough to be almost a second arm of the massif. Nothing here is evenly spaced, nothing is mirrored, and there is no centre point that everything radiates from. ⚠️ THE ACCEPTANCE TEST IS THAT THE SUMMIT IS SURROUNDED, and it is the one thing a tilted camera cannot fake. PUT A FINGER ON THE HIGHEST POINT AND TRAVEL STRAIGHT UP FROM IT. If you reach the top edge of the picture without crossing any rock, the camera was tilted and the image is wrong however good it looks — because that is a mountain drawn against a SKY, and from directly overhead there is no sky. THE SUMMIT SITS IN THE MIDDLE OF THE SHAPE, NOT AT THE TOP OF IT. Rock falls away from it in every direction of the compass, DOWNWARD in the frame exactly as much as upward, and the ridges running toward the bottom of the picture are as long, as detailed and as fully drawn as the ones running toward the top. ⚠️ SO THE OUTLINE IS AS WIDE ACROSS THE TOP AS ACROSS THE BOTTOM. Measure the shape across its topmost tenth and across its lowest tenth: those two widths must be about the SAME. Narrow at the top and broad at the bottom is a mountain seen from BESIDE it, and that is exactly what came back last time. NO TRIANGLE, no cone, no pyramid outline, no apex, no skyline, no mountain pictogram, no peak standing against empty background. They are also the safe ones to put near a shore, where the big two are not. 400u at bake 2 is an 800px bake from a 1024 master at fillTo 0.86 — 880px of subject available, so it just clears without upscaling. That asset asked for a top plane filling four fifths of the silhouette, measured 45-47% across two rounds, and was accepted anyway on the reduction test — because the metric conflates camera tilt with light direction and there is no cheap master-size number that separates them on a blocky subject. Expect the same here. JUDGE IT AT 400px ON ICE, and do not re-roll for a number this pipeline has already proved it cannot measure. ⚠️ CARRIES THE SUMMIT-SURROUNDED CLAUSE ADDED 2026-08-23 — see [[arctic-nunatak-massif]]'s note for the measured round-1 rejection, the top-decile/bottom-decile width ratio that replaces the blind aspect check, and why the peaks got the clause before they were ever generated. ⚠️ anchorPx CORRECTED BY HAND ON INGEST 2026-08-23, art-pipeline 3. ingest seeds it from the bbox centre of ALL ink and the talus tail spills to the lower left, so the seed [0.4995, 0.4995] sat in open background below and left of the rock. Reset to the ROCK MASS's own bbox centre [0.4906, 0.4656] — 3.4% of the sprite higher, 13.6px at world 400. This is the debris problem showing up in a second place: it moves the anchor as well as shrinking the object, and both are silent. ── ✅ DELIVERED, KEYED AND INGESTED 2026-08-23, THE FIRST OF THE TWELVE TO SHIP. Round 1 was accepted on the measurements in [[arctic-nunatak-massif]]'s note: top/bottom-decile width ratio 1.2x and left/right 1.0x against the 1.6x that says a skyline is showing, so this is a genuine plan view — the only one of the six mountains in the batch that came back square to the camera first time. ⚠️ AND THE SNOW DID NOT NEED REMOVING, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE THE OWNER OFFERED TO AND THE OFFER WAS REASONABLE. The delivery arrived as an opaque JPEG on white, and this asset's snow band runs OFF the silhouette at the upper right — textbook for the README's standing warning that dekey.py's flood fill 'can walk into a near-white marking that touches the silhouette edge'. It is avoidable rather than fatal: a BORDER-SEEDED fill, which only ever spreads from the frame edge through background-coloured pixels, cannot reach an enclosed marking however bright it is. Cut at a min-channel threshold of 246 — on the plateau, where 245-250 all remove 56.7-56.8% of the frame — 100% of the 111,580 snow pixels survived. THE GENERAL LESSON: dekey's limit is its SEEDING, not the colour white, so a white subject on white is cuttable when the marking is enclosed and is not when it runs to the edge. The peaks are the genuinely uncuttable case and stay a --bg magenta family. ⚠️ AND THE SNOW SHOULD STAY ON DESIGN GROUNDS, WHICH THE NUMBERS NOW SETTLE. Measured on the shipped sprite, the rock body sits dE 19 from this venue's water #1D4066 and its darkest tone dE 21 — BELOW the 25 floor. Colour alone does NOT keep this rock from reading as a lead of open water, which is exactly why the subject names four defences and not one. Snow is the strongest of the four and the only one water can never imitate: it puts WHITE INSIDE THE DARK SHAPE, here 5.9% of the sprite. Strip it and the not-water read falls back on the jagged outline and the facet tones alone, at dE 19 from the water it stands beside. SHIPPED NUMBERS: 800px bake at 2x for a 400px display, 688px of subject from an 881px working master = 0.78x, so it is a touch soft at full size and clean at race scale. Flat-plane pixels 44% against the 70% the style asks — well short, but three times the peaks' 14% and it reads correctly on the sheet, so it is accepted as delivered rather than re-rolled. Contrast against the ice ground is ample at dE 61-79. ⚠️ THE TALUS COST IS REAL AND MEASURED: the loose chips are 3.0% of the ink and push the content bbox from the rock's 1501x1579 to 1621x1715, so the ROCK draws at 92% of its declared world size — a 400u crag is a 368u rock. Accepted here, and it is the reason the subject was amended to require the apron to touch. If this family is ever re-rolled, that alone buys back 8%. THE CUTOUT CAME FROM THE OWNER and it is the better of the two: 0.13% partial alpha against a flood fill's 0.00%, the README's point about a real remover keeping a softer edge. It carried 3,123px of backdrop residue at alpha 50 reaching the frame corner, which would have inflated the bbox to 1798x1858 and shrunk the rock another 8% — stripped with batch_generate.normalise's own floating-alpha pass, which exists for exactly that and preserves the outline antialiasing.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. AN ICY PEAK — a snow-and-ice pyramid rising out of an ice cap, white on white — seen from directly above and ALONE. ONE SUMMIT, a small sharp point set a little off the middle of the mass, with THREE OR FOUR SNOW RIDGES running down and outward from it to where the slopes flatten into the sheet. ⚠️ THE RIDGES ARE NOT A STAR. Different lengths, unequal angles, two of them closer together than the rest, and one of them carrying a lower SHOULDER — a second, much smaller high point partway down — which is what stops the whole thing looking like a drawn cone. Between the ridges lie broad snow faces, one of them scooped into a shallow bowl at its head. ⚠️ THE ACCEPTANCE TEST IS THAT THE SUMMIT IS SURROUNDED, and it is the one thing a tilted camera cannot fake. PUT A FINGER ON THE HIGHEST POINT AND TRAVEL STRAIGHT UP FROM IT. If you reach the top edge of the picture without crossing any rock, the camera was tilted and the image is wrong however good it looks — because that is a mountain drawn against a SKY, and from directly overhead there is no sky. THE SUMMIT SITS IN THE MIDDLE OF THE SHAPE, NOT AT THE TOP OF IT. Rock falls away from it in every direction of the compass, DOWNWARD in the frame exactly as much as upward, and the ridges running toward the bottom of the picture are as long, as detailed and as fully drawn as the ones running toward the top. ⚠️ SO THE OUTLINE IS AS WIDE ACROSS THE TOP AS ACROSS THE BOTTOM. Measure the shape across its topmost tenth and across its lowest tenth: those two widths must be about the SAME. Narrow at the top and broad at the bottom is a mountain seen from BESIDE it, and that is exactly what came back last time. NO TRIANGLE, no cone, no pyramid outline, no apex, no skyline, no mountain pictogram, no peak standing against empty background. Seen from straight above, a mountain is a roughly round, ragged, LOBED PATCH of rock with ridge lines radiating out of one interior point, and it is those radiating lines and the light either side of them — never the outline — that say how tall it is. ⚠️ AND THE LIGHT SPLITS IT RADIALLY, WHICH IS THE OTHER PLAN-VIEW SIGNATURE. With the sun in the upper left and the summit in the middle of the shape, every flank on the upper-left side of the summit is lit and every flank on the lower-right side is in shade, and THE DIVISION BETWEEN THEM RUNS THROUGH THE SUMMIT ITSELF, out to the edge on both sides. A picture whose light divides along a horizontal band — bright upper half, dark lower half, or the reverse — is lit like a hillside seen from the valley, and it is a side view. ⚠️ THIS IS A WHITE THING THAT WILL BE DRAWN ON A WHITE GROUND, AND ITS OUTLINE WILL NOT CARRY IT. The engine's ice is near-white at #E6F2FB, so the silhouette of a snow peak against it is nearly invisible and every bit of the read has to be INTERNAL: crest lines and shaded flanks. The shading therefore goes MUCH DEEPER THAN SNOW USUALLY DOES — lit slopes near #FBFDFF and #EAF3FC, shaded slopes stepping down through #B3C6D6 and #8CA3B8 to #6A8298 in the deepest hollows, and never darker than #5F7488. That is four full steps below anything the ground can do, and a pale, delicately shaded, tastefully restrained version of this picture is a FAILED version of it. ⚠️ BUT DEEP IS NOT THE SAME AS BLUE, AND THAT IS THE TRAP THIS SUBJECT FELL INTO LAST TIME. Snow in shadow loses LIGHT, not COLOUR: it goes a dim GREY-blue, close to neutral, never a rich saturated blue. Every tone named above is deliberately desaturated and none of them may be pushed toward a strong blue — because a strong blue is WATER, and this venue's water at #1D4066 sits directly alongside every one of these peaks. The last delivery came back with its deepest shadows at #20639E and #13447A, which measure 11 to 19 units of colour distance from that water when 25 is the floor. IF A FLANK STARTS TO LOOK LIKE THE SEA, TAKE THE COLOUR OUT OF IT AND LEAVE THE DARKNESS IN. The light comes from the UPPER LEFT of the frame: every slope facing up and left is near-white, every slope facing down and right is deep grey-blue, and the change happens on a HARD LINE at the crest, never as a gradient. ⚠️ THE WHOLE PICTURE IS BUILT FROM LARGE FLAT PLANES, AND THE LAST DELIVERY WAS NOT. Every surface is ONE flat tone from edge to edge, meeting its neighbour along a hard straight line. Count the tones: there are fewer than a dozen in the entire image. NO airbrush, no soft shading, no blur, no glow, no gloss, no sheen — and above all NONE OF THE CRUMPLED-PAPER OR DRAPED-CLOTH LOOK that comes of shading a slope smoothly, which is what came back last time and is the single thing that most stops this reading as a mountain. Measured on that delivery, only 14% of the picture sat on a flat plane where this style wants four fifths of it. If you can see a tone changing gradually anywhere across a slope, it is wrong. IT IS SNOW OVER ICE, SO IT IS SMOOTH-SURFACED AND SHARP-EDGED AT ONCE: broad clean facets with crisp straight crests between them; a few BOLD wind-carved flutings running straight down the steeper flanks — no more than five or six on any flank, each a single flat stripe of one tone with hard edges, never a soft ripple, never a gradient and never fine hatching; and a CORNICE on the shaded side of the main crest, a bright overhanging lip with a hard shadow line beneath it, which is the single most convincing thing a snow ridge can have. WHERE IT MEETS THE FLAT ICE, GIVE IT A FOOT: a narrow moat of deeper grey-blue shade running round the down-light side of the base, breaking into a few hard-edged shadowed dips, so there is a visible edge on at least one side of the object. ⚠️ THE MOAT IS PART OF THE OBJECT AND TOUCHES IT ALL ALONG ITS LENGTH. It is not a separate arc, crescent, line or cast shadow floating clear of the base — nothing in this picture stands free of the main mass with clear background between the two. On the up-light side the snow simply runs out and the edge softens away to nothing, which is honest and is why the moat has to be there. Near the summit, TWO OR THREE SMALL PATCHES OF BARE DARK ROCK break through the snow on the steepest shaded face — angular, hard-edged, near #4B5563 — because a peak with a little rock showing reads as a mountain and a peak of pure white reads as a meringue. Keep them small: together they are less than a tenth of what you can see. NOTHING ELSE: no water, no boat, no floe, no crevasse, no vegetation, no wildlife, no building, no track, no cloud, no sky. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the object is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies the ice it sits on.
assets.note: THE VENUE'S SKYLINE, FINALLY IN THE VENUE. Glacier Sound's card art has had mountains since the day it shipped and the racing surface has never had one — the sound is ringed by flat white polygons. This is the asset that closes that gap, and it is the reason the batch exists. Place them on the far ice, along the back of `coast` and on `shape-5`, where they are seen and never sailed near. ⚠️ WHITE-ON-WHITE IS THE ENTIRE TECHNICAL PROBLEM OF THIS SUB-FAMILY AND IT IS WORTH STATING IN NUMBERS. [[arctic-snow]] ships at LAND_TEXTURES alpha 0.3 over ISLAND_STYLES ice #E6F2FB, and its own subject holds it "inside a tight range from near-white to pale blue-grey" with "no dark shadow" — measured on screen its contrast is 0.30x the master's, std 3.1, range 228-243. THAT IS A FIFTEEN-VALUE GROUND. A peak drawn in the same register vanishes into it completely. The subject therefore specifies shaded slopes down to #5386B2, which is roughly 90 luma below the ground, and calls a restrained version a failed version. This is the one row in the batch where the acceptance test can be a single number: SHADED-FLANK LUMA MUST SIT AT LEAST 60 BELOW THE GROUND IT IS DRAWN ON. Measure it on the plate, not on the master. ⚠️ AND IT MUST NOT BECOME A SERAC. A white-blue faceted ice object is also what [[arctic-serac-cluster]] is, and the separation is SIZE and STRUCTURE: 620u against 170u is 3.6x, and a peak has crest lines converging on one point where a serac is concentric steps. Never place the two within sight of each other at similar scale. allowSymmetry TRUE for the ridges, planRound TRUE for the outline test, bake 2 / master 2048 / hand-run square gen — all three on [[arctic-nunatak-massif]]'s arguments. 620u sits deliberately BELOW the two big nunataks: the dark rock should be the biggest thing in the venue, because it is the thing that is hardest to mistake for anything else. ⚠️ CARRIES THE SUMMIT-SURROUNDED CLAUSE ADDED 2026-08-23 — see [[arctic-nunatak-massif]]'s note for the measured round-1 rejection, the top-decile/bottom-decile width ratio that replaces the blind aspect check, and why the peaks got the clause before they were ever generated. ⚠️⚠️ GENERATE THIS ONE ON A CHROMA KEY, NEVER ON WHITE — `prompt.py <key> --bg magenta`, then `dekey.py`. This is the family where the README's standing warning actually bites: 'never key on white with dekey.py, its flood fill can walk into a near-white marking that touches the silhouette edge'. A snow peak IS a near-white marking, edge to edge. Measured on the round-1 deliveries, 4-14% of each subject sits within 12 luma of the white backdrop it was drawn on, so there is no threshold that separates them — key it on white and the snow goes with the background. A dedicated background remover has the same problem here for the same reason, which is why this is a chroma-key row rather than a `--bg white` one. IT ALSO FIXES THE MEASUREMENT: on an opaque JPEG the tilt test has to build its own mask from luminance, and the answer moves with the threshold — the massif read 1.9x at one cut and 1.3x at another. With a real alpha channel the mask is not a judgement call. ── ⚠️⚠️ ROUND 1 MEASURED 2026-08-23 AND ALL THREE PEAKS WERE REJECTED, on three failures the whole sub-family shared — which makes them prompt faults, not luck. (1) NOT CUTTABLE: every one came back opaque on a near-white field. See the chroma-key note above; this is now a `--bg magenta` family. (2) THEY READ AS WATER: deepest tones measured dE 19, 16 and 11 from the venue's water #1D4066 against a floor of 25. ⚠️ THE SPEC COLOURS WERE NOT THE PROBLEM — #5386B2 measures dE 28.4 and would have passed. The subject overshot them because it set a LUMA FLOOR with no CHROMA CEILING: it said the shading must go 'much deeper than snow usually does' and called a restrained version a failed version, and the generator obeyed by going darker AND more saturated, straight past the hexes into navy. Contrast passed handsomely at the same time — 120 to 158 luma below the ice ground against the 60 asked — so the number this note set was met while the picture failed. A one-sided constraint is how that happens. Round 2 states both ends: a greyer ladder (#B3C6D6 / #8CA3B8 / #6A8298, chroma 10-15 against the old 18-29, all at dE 29+ from water) and the rule 'deep is not the same as blue' with the water distance named. (3) SOFT GRADIENTS: 14-15% of each picture sat on a flat plane where the house style wants four fifths. All three read as crumpled paper or draped cloth rather than faceted snow. The subject's own 'wind-carved flutings ... as narrow paired light-and-shade stripes' invited it — fine linear shading is the one instruction that most reliably produces an airbrush — so round 2 caps the flutings at five or six bold flat stripes per flank and states the flat-plane rule with the number attached. AND THE TILT, MEASURED ON BOTH AXES THIS TIME: dome 2.6x, pyramid 7.3x, ridge 2.1x, all side elevations. ⚠️ THE ROUND-1 NUNATAK NUMBERS WERE TAKEN ON ONE AXIS ONLY AND THAT WAS A BUG IN THE TEST, NOT IN THE ART: the axis was chosen by the bounding box's aspect, which gets a dome exactly backwards, since a dome's tilt shows top-to-bottom while its box is wider than tall. Re-measured on both axes the nunataks read crag 1.2x, massif 1.3x and horn 3.8x — so the massif is INSIDE the plan band, not tilted as first reported, and the horn remains the only nunatak that fails. ⚠️ AND THE NUMBER IS THRESHOLD-SENSITIVE ON AN OPAQUE JPEG: the massif read 1.9x at one luminance cut and 1.3x at another, because the mask has to be guessed from brightness when there is no alpha. Take the ratio on both axes, and take it on a keyed file. ── ✅ ROUND 2 DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-23, AND THE COLOUR FIX IS THE HEADLINE. This is the FIRST asset in the whole commission to clear the water floor: dE 35 from #1D4066 against the 25 asked, where the four before it landed 16, 17, 18 and 19. The change that did it was the greyer ladder plus the 'deep is not the same as blue' paragraph — a CHROMA CEILING beside the luma floor. The round-1 note diagnosed a one-sided constraint and the two-sided one worked on the first try, which is worth trusting the next time a subject specifies only a floor. Its darkest tone is #455766, nowhere near black. It also came back with real alpha and transparent corners, so the --bg instruction landed too. ACCEPTED ON THE REDUCTION TEST, NOT ON A NUMBER, and that is art-pipeline 8 doing exactly what it is for: 'the only question that matters is whether the thing reads at the size it actually occupies'. Composited at 620px it is unmistakably a peak seen from above — interior summit, ridges radiating to every edge including the bottom, terminator running through the summit. ⚠️⚠️ THREE METRICS HAVE NOW FAILED TO SEPARATE A PLAN-VIEW PEAK FROM A TILTED ONE, AND THE THIRD WAS BUILT FOR THIS ASSET. Recording all three so nobody builds them a fourth time. (1) ORTHO_ROUND's ASPECT: 1.03 here, and blind — [[river-boulder-large]] proved it blind on a blocky stone and this batch proved it again on a cone. (2) THE TOP/BOTTOM DECILE RATIO: 2.44 here, which is in the failing band, and it is a FALSE POSITIVE for the third time on a radial subject — a peak with one ridge pointing UP has a narrow top decile for an honest reason ([[arctic-nunatak-horn]] read 1.68 and is fine). (3) A 'SUMMIT SURROUNDED' TEST, written to mechanise this row's own clause: find the summit as the terminator's most-interior point, then measure the mass lying above it. It read 41.9% here against 44.9 / 41.9 / 55.5 on the three accepted plan views — apparently perfect. IT IS USELESS. Fed a SYNTHETIC side elevation (the accepted horn with its upper 42% cut off, so the summit sits on the skyline by construction) it returned 54.6% and passed it. The flaw: the terminator's most-interior point is always near the shape's centroid, so 'mass above the summit' is really 'mass above the middle', which is ~50% for anything. ⚠️ THE LESSON IS THE PROCEDURE, NOT THE METRIC: a test calibrated only on things that PASS has not been tested. Build the synthetic failure first. ⚠️ ONE REAL SHORTFALL, AND IT IS RESOLUTION. The delivery carried 684px of subject in a 1408x768 frame, so at world 620 and bake 2 it UPSCALES 1.60x — against the massif's 2480px, the ridge's 2614px and the crevasse's 2808px. It reads fine at race scale and it will not survive being placed large, which is the one thing the owner's standing instruction on this batch asks for. RE-RENDER THIS ONE AT SCALE when convenient; nothing else about it needs to change.

assets.note: THE HORIZON-MAKER. One of these laid along the back of an ice mass does more for the venue's sense of enclosure than three separate peaks, because a sound is a place with WALLS and a scatter of cones is a place with lumps. Place it parallel to the coastline it stands behind, on `coast` or `shape-4`, and let [[arctic-peak-pyramid]] and [[arctic-peak-dome]] sit in front of and beside it. THE ONLY planRound FALSE AMONG THE NINE MOUNTAINS AND SERACS, and ORTHO_LONG is honest for it: a real arête does hold roughly constant width along its length, and its two flanks genuinely are parallel. The subject spends a sentence designing the taper out of the ends. [[arctic-crevasse]] reaches the same place from the other side and is worth reading next to this: it CANNOT design its taper out, because a crevasse closes at both ends by definition, so it reconciles instead — narrowing at both ends alike is not CONVERGING, and convergence, one end plainly smaller than the other, is the tilt ORTHO_LONG is actually about. 3:1 at 700u long means 233u across, so a SQUARE gen frame is still the right one at this aspect; the tall-frame argument the cargo family makes starts to pay past about 4:1. ⚠️ THE CORNICE IS THE ASSET. Everything else here is a bigger, longer version of [[arctic-peak-pyramid]]; the continuous overhanging lip with a hard shadow under it is the thing this one has that nothing else in the library does, and it is what will make a 700u white object read as a knife-edged ridge rather than as a long white smear. If the delivery comes back without it, that is a reject regardless of how good the rest is. Its shadow line is also the most reliable place to measure the white-on-white number [[arctic-peak-pyramid]]'s note sets: shaded flank at least 60 luma below the ground. fillTo 0.92 and bake 2 / master 2048 as the rest of the big rows. ⚠️ CARRIES THE SUMMIT-SURROUNDED CLAUSE ADDED 2026-08-23 — see [[arctic-nunatak-massif]]'s note for the measured round-1 rejection, the top-decile/bottom-decile width ratio that replaces the blind aspect check, and why the peaks got the clause before they were ever generated. ⚠️⚠️ GENERATE THIS ONE ON A CHROMA KEY, NEVER ON WHITE — `prompt.py <key> --bg magenta`, then `dekey.py`. This is the family where the README's standing warning actually bites: 'never key on white with dekey.py, its flood fill can walk into a near-white marking that touches the silhouette edge'. A snow peak IS a near-white marking, edge to edge. Measured on the round-1 deliveries, 4-14% of each subject sits within 12 luma of the white backdrop it was drawn on, so there is no threshold that separates them — key it on white and the snow goes with the background. A dedicated background remover has the same problem here for the same reason, which is why this is a chroma-key row rather than a `--bg white` one. IT ALSO FIXES THE MEASUREMENT: on an opaque JPEG the tilt test has to build its own mask from luminance, and the answer moves with the threshold — the massif read 1.9x at one cut and 1.3x at another. With a real alpha channel the mask is not a judgement call. ⚠️ ROUND 1 REJECTED 2026-08-23 — see [[arctic-peak-pyramid]]'s note for the three measured failures the whole peak family shared and what changed. ── ✅ ROUND 2 DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-23 — `ridge-1` of two candidates, and the FIRST ICY PEAK TO SHIP. In its own frame it measures 0.53 on the skyline test (wider at the top, which is fine) against `ridge-2`'s 2.01, a plain side elevation. TRUE aspect 3.77:1 against the ~3:1 asked, ends within 1.09x so ORTHO_LONG's parallel-sides clause holds, zero debris, 36% snow inside the mass — the highest in the batch. ⚠️ IT ARRIVED ON A 20.5-DEGREE DIAGONAL and was ROTATED to vertical on the way in, because the subject asks for 'its long axis running UP the frame' and the engine treats sprite-up as zero heading. One bicubic pass on a 2816px master that bakes down to 2100px, so the resample is invisible. It cost nothing in size — a diagonal object is LONGER than its own bounding box's long side, so it was drawing at 104% of `world` before the rotation, not less. ⚠️⚠️ TWO METRIC LESSONS FROM JUDGING THIS PAIR, AND BOTH NEARLY PRODUCED A WRONG VERDICT. (1) THE PCA LONG AXIS IS SIGN-AMBIGUOUS. Laying each ridge flat by its principal axis and then measuring the skyline flipped `ridge-2` through 180 degrees, turning a 2.01 into a 0.50 and swapping the verdicts. Normalise the angle into ±90 before rotating; never let a long-axis fit decide which way is up. (2) A 'CREST-CENTRED' TEST WAS TRIED AND IS UNSOUND — record it so nobody builds it again. The idea was the crevasse's core-centred test transposed: in plan view the crest should sit mid-flank, and a tilt shoves it to one edge. It measured 0.32 and 0.25 against a 0.12 threshold and would have rejected BOTH. The flaw is that it locates the crest as the brightest pixels, and on a snow ridge lit from the upper left an ENTIRE FLANK is bright — so it measures the lighting the subject asks for, not the camera. Same class of error as [[river-boulder-large]]'s top-plane metric, which conflated tilt with light direction for the same reason. The skyline ratio, measured in the object's own frame, is the test that works. TWO KNOWN SHORTFALLS, ACCEPTED. dE 18 from the water against the 25 floor — the fourth asset in a row to land 16-19, which now reads as a fact about dark rock and navy water in CIELAB rather than a per-asset failure; the not-water read rests on the snow, and at 36% this one carries more of it than anything else here. And flat-plane 22% against the 70% the style wants — short, but the best of the six white-mountain deliveries (the rest ran 13-16%) and half again the crag's 44% is still the only asset that got it right. `ridge-2` REJECTED: skyline 2.01, i.e. the mass bulges below the crest, which is what you see looking at a ridge from above and to one side. Its aspect was closer to spec at 2.71:1 and its flat-plane worse at 15%.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. ONE ICE DOME — a smooth swelling cupola of ice, the high point of a small ice cap, with no peak, no crest and no rock in it at all — seen from directly above and ALONE. ONE DOME AND ONLY ONE. Roughly as tall as it is wide. Its outline is an irregular rounded blob, dented on one flank and drawn out into a low shoulder on another, never a true circle and never mirrored — it is round because it is domed, not because it is squashed. ⚠️ EVERYTHING ON IT IS ARRANGED AROUND ONE CENTRE POINT, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE PICTURE. A dome seen from directly above is CONCENTRIC: a small pale crown in the MIDDLE, then a ring of slightly deeper tone around it, then another around that, out to the foot. Rings inside rings, all sharing one centre, like the contour lines on a map of a hill. Flutings run OUTWARD from that centre in EVERY direction of the compass — down-left and down-right and toward the bottom of the frame exactly as much as toward the top. ⚠️ THE ACCEPTANCE TEST IS THAT THE PALE CROWN IS CENTRED, and it is the one thing a tilted camera cannot fake. Cut across the dome through its middle, in ANY direction, and the two halves must match: the same pale in the centre, the same rings either side of it, the same depth at both edges. ⚠️ IT IS NOT A BALL, AND A BALL IS WHAT THIS SUBJECT KEEPS COMING BACK AS — six times over. A bright cap sitting off to ONE side with a large dark mass filling the other, the two divided by a single curve, is a SPHERE LIT FROM THE SIDE: a pebble, a bowl, a marble. It is the way a round object is drawn when you are standing beside it. There is no lit half and no shaded half here, no bright cap in a corner, no dark mass opposite it, and no single curve dividing the picture in two. If you can point at one side of the dome and call it the light side, the camera was tilted and the image is wrong however good it looks. THERE IS NO SUN IN THIS PICTURE. Glacier Sound's sky is low grey overcast, and under overcast light a snow surface has no lit face and no shaded face — relief reads ONLY because a hollow collects less light than the open surface beside it. So every dark tone here is an OCCLUSION, sitting in a hollow or under a lip, and it is the same on all sides of the dome. There is no light angle to get right, which is deliberate. WHAT YOU ACTUALLY SEE, working from the middle outward. (1) THE CROWN: a small irregular near-white area at the centre, flattish, maybe a fifth of the dome across — an ice dome has a blunt top, not a point. (2) THE FLANKS: two or three broad concentric rings, each one flat and meeting its neighbour on a crisp line — but they are a WHISPER, not a staircase. Each ring differs from the one inside it by only a few levels, and EVERY ONE OF THEM stays at or above the brightness of the ice ground. The flanks are not where the darkness lives. (3) THE FLUTINGS: long shallow wind-flutings running straight out from the crown to the foot as narrow paired stripes of one flat tone, at uneven spacings, curving very slightly, and spread ALL THE WAY AROUND the dome rather than gathered on one side — they are what tells the eye this surface swells. (4) THE FOOT, which is the strongest plan-view cue on the whole object: two or three hard-edged ARCS OF CREVASSING where the dome pulls away from the flat ice, short blue slots following the CURVE of the foot, and they appear on SEVERAL sides of it, not just one — a ring of them, broken and uneven, never a single crescent on one edge. ⚠️ THREE FLAT TONES AND HARD EDGES. Every ring and every fluting is one flat tone from edge to edge, meeting its neighbour on a crisp line. NO airbrush, no soft gradient, no blur, no glow, no gloss, no sheen — a dome is the one subject in this venue that most invites an airbrush, and an airbrushed version is a failed version however round it looks. Measured across this venue's white deliveries, that failure put only 13-27% of each picture on a flat plane where the style wants four fifths. ⚠️ THE DARKNESS LIVES ONLY IN THE NARROW FEATURES, AND GETTING THIS BACKWARDS IS WHAT RUINED THE LAST ATTEMPT. A dome is not an object sitting on the ice — it IS the ice, gently swelling. Its surface is the SAME SNOW as the ground around it and must therefore be the SAME BRIGHTNESS: the whole broad body of it sits within a few levels of #E6F2FB and NEVER BELOW, with the crown a touch brighter near #FBFDFF because fresh snow gathers on a rise. Every deep tone in this picture belongs to something NARROW — the thin paired lines of the flutings, and the slots of the foot crevassing — and those may go right down to #9FB3C6 and #7E93A6, because a slot is a hollow and a hollow is dark. Broad and pale, with thin dark marks on it. ⚠️ THE TEST IS WHERE THE DARK LIVES, NOT HOW MUCH OF IT THERE IS. The broad body may sit a LITTLE below the snow around it — ten or fifteen levels, which is what makes the dome visible at all — but no more, and the crown sits a little ABOVE. Everything deeper than about twenty levels below the ground must be confined to the narrow marks, and should be well under a quarter of the picture. The version that failed had its whole body 51 levels down and its rings 84 down, and on the real ice it read as a DARK DISC WITH A BRIGHT HOLE IN THE MIDDLE. ⚠️ WHICH IS TO SAY: IT MUST NOT READ AS A MELT POND, A CRATER OR A HOLE IN THE ICE. That is this subject's failure, and it is worse than the tilt was, because a pond is a thing this venue actually has. A swelling is BRIGHT with dark lines on it; a pond is DARK with a bright rim. If the middle of the picture is darker than the snow outside the picture, it is a hole. AND WHAT DARKNESS THERE IS STAYS A GREY-BLUE. Snow in a hollow loses light, not colour, so nothing may be pushed toward a rich saturated blue — a rich blue is WATER, and this venue's water at #1D4066 is never far away. Keep every tone at least 25 units of colour distance from it; the last attempt's deepest note measured 25.4, which is on the line. NOTHING ELSE: no water, no boat, no floe, no rock, no peak, no crest, no cornice, no ridge line, no vegetation, no wildlife, no building, no track, no cloud, no sky. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the dome stands alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies the ice it sits on.
assets.note: THE QUIET ONE, AND IT EARNS ITS SLOT BY BEING THE ONLY ROUNDED FORM IN TWELVE. Eleven angular assets on one ice sheet is a texture, not a landscape; one soft swelling among them is what makes the sharp ones read as sharp. It is also the only member of the batch that can sit in the OPEN middle of an ice mass without looking like it fell there — a dome IS the middle of an ice cap. Place two or three per venue, on `shape-3` and `shape-5` and out in the body of `coast`. ⚠️ IT IS THE MOST LIKELY OF THE TWELVE TO COME BACK SOFT, and softness is the one thing the house style does not allow: visual-style's rule is hard two-tone shading and no gradients, and a dome is exactly the subject that invites an airbrush. The subject answers that by specifying the picture as FOUR FLAT TONES AND ONE CURVE and naming the airbrushed version as the failure. THE ACCEPTANCE TEST IS AN EDGE, NOT A SHAPE: run the delivered master through a hard threshold at the terminator's value — if the boundary comes out as a clean curve the asset is right, and if it comes out as a wide fuzzy band it is a reject no matter how good the form looks. ⚠️ AND IT MUST NOT READ AS A FLOE, which is a live risk that the other two peaks do not have: a rounded pale ice object is a floe's whole description, and the venue's median floe is 238u against this one's 420u. Only 1.8x, and the shapes rhyme. WHAT SEPARATES THEM IS THE FLUTING AND THE TERMINATOR — a floe is one flat plate with an edge, this is a swelling with a bold light/dark split across it and stripes running down its shaded side. Check it on a plate with floes IN FRAME, the same test [[arctic-serac-cluster]] takes, and if it fails, push the terminator harder rather than making the dome taller. allowSymmetry TRUE because a dome is honestly radial; the subject buys the irregularity back with the dent and the shoulder. 420u at bake 2 from a 1024 master at fillTo 0.86 is 840px of bake against 880px available — it clears, but as with [[arctic-nunatak-crag]], raising `world` on this row without raising `master` starts inventing pixels. ⚠️ ONE WORD IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT FROM THE SUBJECT: 'oval'. ROUND_NEGATIVE, which prompt.py appends to every planRound asset, refuses "oval silhouette" and "flattened disc" by name, because those are the signature of a tilted camera. A dome described as an oval would have put the instruction and its refusal in the same prompt — the failure prompt.py's own comments record four times over. It says 'rounded blob, as tall as it is wide' instead, which is the same shape and agrees with the negative list. ⚠️ CARRIES THE SUMMIT-SURROUNDED CLAUSE ADDED 2026-08-23 — see [[arctic-nunatak-massif]]'s note for the measured round-1 rejection, the top-decile/bottom-decile width ratio that replaces the blind aspect check, and why the peaks got the clause before they were ever generated. ⚠️⚠️ GENERATE THIS ONE ON A CHROMA KEY, NEVER ON WHITE — `prompt.py <key> --bg magenta`, then `dekey.py`. This is the family where the README's standing warning actually bites: 'never key on white with dekey.py, its flood fill can walk into a near-white marking that touches the silhouette edge'. A snow peak IS a near-white marking, edge to edge. Measured on the round-1 deliveries, 4-14% of each subject sits within 12 luma of the white backdrop it was drawn on, so there is no threshold that separates them — key it on white and the snow goes with the background. A dedicated background remover has the same problem here for the same reason, which is why this is a chroma-key row rather than a `--bg white` one. IT ALSO FIXES THE MEASUREMENT: on an opaque JPEG the tilt test has to build its own mask from luminance, and the answer moves with the threshold — the massif read 1.9x at one cut and 1.3x at another. With a real alpha channel the mask is not a judgement call. ⚠️ ROUND 1 REJECTED 2026-08-23 — see [[arctic-peak-pyramid]]'s note for the three measured failures the whole peak family shared and what changed. ── ⚠️⚠️ REWRITTEN 2026-08-23 AFTER SIX FAILED GENERATIONS, AND THE SUBJECT WAS ASKING FOR THE FAILURE IN THREE PLACES AT ONCE. Every delivery came back as a sphere lit from one side — a bright elliptical cap in one corner, a large dark mass filling the opposite one, split by a single curve. That is precisely what the old text specified. (1) Its own paragraph: 'the read comes entirely from a broad hard-edged TERMINATOR: the up-light half is near-white and the down-light half is deep blue, and the line between them is a single bold curve running across the mound'. (2) The next sentence: 'a brighter cap at the TOP of the lit side, a deeper hollow at the FOOT of the shaded side' — and TOP and FOOT are ELEVATION words. From directly overhead a dome has no top and no foot; those two words only mean anything if the camera is tilted, so the sentence cannot be obeyed and drawn from above at the same time. (3) It inherited PEAK_SHARED, which says 'the light comes from the UPPER LEFT ... every slope facing up and left is near-white, every slope facing down and right is deep grey-blue' — written for a peak with ridges, and on a dome it IS the instruction to shade a ball. Six generations was the generator obeying, politely, three times over. ⚠️ AND THE SHARED CLAUSE WAS THE REAL BUG, WHICH IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART. PEAK_SHARED also gave this row crest lines, a cornice 'on the shaded side of the main crest' and 'flutings down the steeper flanks' — a dome has no crest, no cornice and no steeper flank. A block of text shared across three subjects fitted two of them and quietly mis-specified the third. When one row of a family keeps failing where its siblings pass, read what the SHARED text is telling that row before rewriting its own. FIXED, and the construction is [[arctic-crevasse]]'s nested bands transposed from a LINE to a POINT: the dome is CONCENTRIC RINGS ABOUT ONE CENTRE, and the acceptance test is that the pale crown is CENTRED — cut through the middle in any direction and the halves match, which a tilt cannot fake. The sun is removed outright (overcast, occlusion only, the same move the drifts make), so there is no lit half to draw. The ball, the pebble and the bowl are named as the failure. And the foot crevassing is promoted to the strongest cue on the object precisely because arcs on SEVERAL sides can only be seen from above — one crescent on one edge is the tilted version of the same feature. Note ROUND_NEGATIVE already refuses 'elliptical crown' by name, which is exactly what six deliveries produced; it was outvoted by the subject. ⚠️ IF ROUND 7 FAILS, CUT THIS ROW RATHER THAN ROLLING AGAIN. Its stated purpose in this note is to be 'the only rounded form in twelve ... one soft swelling among them is what makes the sharp ones read as sharp'. [[arctic-drift-bank]] and [[arctic-drift-barchan]] were declared after it and now do that job — both are smooth rounded snow forms — and they do it with shapes that have a real plan-view read, where a dome from directly overhead is close to featureless by physics rather than by prompt. Seven generations is already more than any other row in the commission has cost. ── ⚠️⚠️ ROUND 7 FIXED THE CAMERA AND EXPOSED A SECOND FAULT THAT WAS ALSO MINE. The concentric rewrite WORKED, first try: crown offset 0.5% of the dome's width against the 5% the test allows, aspect 0.95, radial flutings on every side, foot arcs on several. The tilt this row cost six generations is gone and those clauses stay. ⚠️ BUT IT CAME BACK READING AS A MELT POND, and the owner's note — 'it looks more icy than snowy' — is that failure in plain words. Measured: only 6.4% of the dome sits at or above the brightness of the ice ground it is drawn on. Its median body is 51 luma BELOW the ground and its rings 84 below, so composited on the real surface (snow.png at alpha 0.3 over #E6F2FB) it is a DARK DISC WITH A BRIGHT HOLE IN THE MIDDLE — a pond, a crater, a lens. At 240u and 140u it reads more like a hole, not less. ⚠️ THE CAUSE IS THAT THIS ROW WAS BUILT FROM PEAK CLAUSES AND IS NOT A PEAK. PEAK_SHARED's value logic — 'the shading goes MUCH DEEPER THAN SNOW USUALLY DOES ... a tastefully restrained version is a FAILED version' — is correct for a peak, which is a tall object with real shaded flanks standing against the ground beside it. A dome is the OPPOSITE KIND OF THING: a broad low swelling made of the same snow as the ground, which should therefore be the same brightness almost everywhere, with darkness confined to the narrow hollows. My rewrite pulled the peak LIGHT clause out of this row and left the peak VALUE ladder in — half the fix. The ladder even specified it: #C6D6E4 and #9FB3C6 are 28 and 63 levels below the ground, so the broad-dark-body was mine before the generator exaggerated it. ⚠️ IT IS REALLY A DRIFT, NOT A PEAK, AND THAT IS THE STRUCTURAL LESSON. [[arctic-drift-bank]] and [[arctic-drift-barchan]] are broad low snow swellings too, and their clauses already carry the right value logic: relief only, dark confined to hollows, no sun. The dome sat in the peak family for a naming reason (it is a summit feature) and inherited the wrong physics for three rounds. The key is left as `arctic-peak-dome` — manifest keys are the one thing this pipeline promises never change — but read it beside the drifts, not beside the peaks. FIXED FOR ROUND 8: the body must sit at or above the ground's brightness and never below, the rings become a whisper rather than a staircase, all deep tone moves into the flutings and the foot arcs, the melt pond is named as the failure, and there is a number to check — AT LEAST 80% OF THE DOME AT OR ABOVE THE GROUND, against the 6.4% delivered. Flat-plane also measured 16%: the rings came back smoothly graded, which is what makes it read as glass rather than snow, and the flat-planes clause needs to bite here. ── ✅ ROUND 8 DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-23. It reads as a SWELLING on the real ice ground at 420u, 240u and 140u — the melt-pond read is gone. Crown centred to 2.3% of the dome's width against the 5% allowed, aspect 1.05, darkest tone dE 40 from the water against the 25 floor, one component, real alpha. The concentric construction and the retone both did what they were written to do. ⚠️⚠️ AND THE ACCEPTANCE NUMBER I SET LAST ROUND WAS WRONG — the art passed and my test failed it. 'AT LEAST FOUR FIFTHS AT OR ABOVE THE BRIGHTNESS OF THE GROUND' scored this delivery at 14.9%, which reads as a catastrophe and is nothing of the kind. The ground is #E6F2FB at luma 240, which is very bright, so a body three levels under it fails a strict at-or-above test while being visually identical — and a body that is never below the ground is INVISIBLE on it, which is the opposite of what this row needs. What the delivery actually does is right: body p50 at 11 below the ground, crown p98 at 11 above, and only 6.1% of the sprite more than 40 below — the deep tone confined to the flutings and the foot arcs exactly as asked. THE CRITERION IS NOW WHERE THE DARK LIVES RATHER THAN HOW MUCH THERE IS, which is what the paragraph above it always said in words. ⚠️ THAT IS THE FOURTH METRIC THIS COMMISSION HAS HAD TO WITHDRAW, and the pattern across all four is the same: top-plane fraction conflated tilt with light direction, crest-centring conflated tilt with lighting, summit-surrounded measured the shape's middle, and this one turned a soft physical statement into a hard threshold on the wrong side of it. A number is only worth setting when you can say what a PASS and a FAIL both look like — and when in doubt, composite it on the ground it will actually be drawn on, which is what settled this row in one picture after three rounds of argument. FLAT-PLANE 14% against the 70% the style wants, which is short and in family with everything else white in this batch (13-27%). Accepted as delivered on the same basis as [[arctic-nunatak-crag]] and [[arctic-peak-pyramid]]: it reads correctly at the size it occupies. SHIPPED at bake 3 / master 1578, 1084px of subject from a 1356px master = 0.80x, so it holds up scaled a little either way. NOT CUT — the note above offered that after round 7 and the fix landed on round 8 instead.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. ONE LEE DRIFT — the long tongue of snow that piles up downwind of an obstacle and streams away from it — seen from directly above and ALONE, its long axis running UP the frame. ONE DRIFT AND ONLY ONE: no second tongue, no companion, no scatter. ⚠️ FIVE TIMES AS LONG AS IT IS WIDE, AND THE LAST ONE CAME BACK AT 3.4. Lay five copies of its widest point end to end and they make its length; it runs almost the full height of this tall frame and is no wider than a fifth of that. A short fat teardrop is the wrong landform. IT IS A COMET, NOT A BAR: it is at its widest and deepest at the UPWIND end, where the obstacle stood, and it narrows and thins steadily along its length to a feathered point at the far end. That taper is the whole shape and it must be unmistakable — the two ends of this object are nothing like each other, and the narrow end simply runs out rather than stopping. The obstacle itself is NOT drawn: the drift begins where the rock was and the rock is not in this picture. Along its length the tongue is not ruled straight — it swings a little, the way a wind-shadow does, and its edges are scalloped rather than smooth. ⚠️ THE DRIFT IS MADE OF THE SAME SNOW AS THE GROUND, SO IT IS VERY NEARLY THE SAME BRIGHTNESS. This is the thing every drift so far has got wrong, and it is what makes them read as OBJECTS LYING ON the snow instead of swellings IN it. The drift's broad back is NEAR-WHITE. It may sit a little below the snow around it — ten or fifteen levels, which is what makes it visible at all — and NO MORE THAN THAT. Best of all, leave the back FULLY TRANSPARENT so the engine's own ice at #E6F2FB shows through and there is no edge to seam; but if it is painted, it must be that near-white and not a shade darker. ⚠️ A GREY SHAPE ON A WHITE FIELD IS NOT A DRIFT. If the broad body of this picture is plainly darker than the snow around it, you have drawn a stone, a leaf or a moon lying on the ice, and it is wrong however good the outline is. The last barchan came back with NINETY-NINE PERCENT of itself more than twenty levels below the ground, and its very brightest area still twenty-six below. WHAT YOU ACTUALLY SEE: down ONE LONG EDGE of the tongue runs the SLIPFACE — a hard-edged BAND of shade lying beside the crest and running the WHOLE LENGTH, widest at the upwind end and tapering away with the drift — with the BRIGHT CREST LINE running along its inner edge. The far side of the crest falls away more gently and carries a wider, fainter shade of its own — fainter than the lee band, but never nothing. ⚠️ IT IS A BAND ALONG AN EDGE, NOT A BOWL IN THE MIDDLE, AND THAT IS WHAT THE LAST DELIVERY GOT WRONG. A rounded hollow cupped in the middle of the wide end is a SCOOP, a claw or a shell — not a wind shadow. The shade never crosses to the far edge and never closes into a ring. Keep it to a band no wider than a third of the tongue at its widest, which is also why only a small part of this picture should be deeply shaded: the last one put a quarter of itself more than forty levels below the ground, against the under-a-tenth asked. Across the tongue, two or three shallow CROSS-RIPPLES: short arcs of the same shade, lying square across the drift at uneven spacings, which is what a long drift always has and what stops it reading as a painted stripe. THERE IS NO SUN IN THIS PICTURE AND NOTHING CASTS A SHADOW. Glacier Sound's sky is low grey overcast, and under overcast light a snow surface has no lit side and no shaded side — relief reads ONLY because a hollow collects less light than the open surface around it. So the dark here is an occlusion, not a shadow: it lies IN the trough at the foot of the slipface, deepest where the hollow is deepest, and it does not fall away from the drift in any direction. There is no light angle to get right, which is deliberate — the engine spins these to point them downwind, and a baked sun would spin with them. ⚠️⚠️ IT IS PILED UP, NOT SCOOPED OUT, AND THIS IS THE HARDEST THING IN THE PICTURE. Seen from straight above with no sun, a mound and a hollow look the same — the only thing that tells them apart is WHICH WAY THE TONE RUNS ACROSS THE FORM. So: THE CREST IS A CLEAR BRIGHT LINE RUNNING THE WHOLE LENGTH, DOWN THE MIDDLE OF THE FORM, AND THE TONE FALLS AWAY FROM IT TO BOTH EDGES. Not one edge — BOTH. The lee side falls fast, so its shade is a narrow hard-edged band close under the crest; the windward side falls slowly, so its shade is a wider, fainter, softer fade. They are not equal and they are both there.  ⚠️⚠️ BUT THE FALL-OFF HAPPENS AT THE EDGES, NOT ACROSS A WHOLE FLANK, AND THESE TWO INSTRUCTIONS FIGHT EACH OTHER UNLESS YOU READ THIS ONE. The broad top of the drift — about four fifths of its width — stays NEAR-WHITE and almost flat. Only the OUTER FIFTH on each side darkens, and it darkens fast: a narrow hard band at the lee foot, a slightly wider and fainter one to windward. ⚠️ DO NOT SHADE A WHOLE FLANK GREY. The last two deliveries did exactly that — one put 39% and the other 61% of the picture more than forty levels below the ground — because 'the tone falls away to both edges' was read as 'paint one side grey'. A DRIFT IS A WHITE THING WITH DARK EDGES, not a half-white half-grey thing. ⚠️ CUT ACROSS THE DRIFT ANYWHERE ALONG ITS LENGTH: the brightest point is in the MIDDLE of that cut and both ends of the cut are clearly darker. If the middle is dark, or if the bright is at one edge and the dark at the other, you have drawn a GROOVE — a furrow, a ski track, a gouge pressed INTO the snow — and that is exactly what the last delivery looked like. Its middle was only eight levels brighter than its edges while a hard dark stripe ran down one flank, and the stripe won. THE MIDDLE MUST BEAT BOTH EDGES BY A REAL STEP, not by a whisker. Everything BROAD stays near-white. assets.note: ⚠️ THREE DRIFTS, AND THEY ARE THE VENUE'S ONLY PROP THAT SAYS WHICH WAY THE WIND BLOWS. Glacier Sound's identity is katabatic wind pouring off the ice cap, and until now nothing on the land showed it: the ice masses are a flat white sheet with a coastline, and [[arctic-snow]]'s own sastrugi are tile-scale and read as material rather than as direction. A drift is the one landform whose SHAPE is a record of the wind that built it, so a venue laid out with these tells a player something true before they have sailed a metre. ⚠️ THE PLACEMENT RULE IS THE WHOLE VALUE AND IT IS ONE SENTENCE: EVERY DRIFT IN A VENUE POINTS THE SAME WAY. Pick one wind direction for the layout and make all three families obey it — tails streaming off the lee side of every obstacle, barchan horns opening downwind, banks with their steep face on the lee. Scatter them at random headings and they stop being wind and become texture, which is what [[arctic-snow]] is already for. Prop-spin ON, as with the crevasses, and for the same reason made explicit in the subjects: overcast light means no baked sun to rotate out of alignment. AND THEY PAIR WITH THE ROCK. A tail drift behind [[arctic-nunatak-crag]], a bank piled against the lee flank of [[arctic-nunatak-massif]], drifts tucked behind [[arctic-station]] and its huts — the drift is evidence that the obstacle has been standing in this wind for a long time, and it costs nothing to place them that way. ⚠️ A SASTRUGI FIELD WAS CONSIDERED AS THE THIRD AND DELIBERATELY NOT DECLARED. It would have been many small parallel ridges, which art-pipeline 3b says must be composed from an element rather than generated as a group — and worse, it duplicates the ground: arctic-snow's subject already asks for 'short broken sastrugi ... lying in loosely the same direction'. A prop that repeats the texture underneath it adds nothing and costs a draw. The three declared here are three different SILHOUETTES — a tongue, a crescent and a ridge — which is the lesson [[river-boulder-large]] paid for: a family that differs only in size cannot be told apart at race scale. ⚠️ CONSTRUCTION IS THE CREVASSE'S, NOT THE MOUNTAINS'. These draw ONLY their relief — the shaded hollow and the bright lip — on a transparent field, so the engine's own snow shows through and there is no patch edge to seam against the ground. That is the one thing in this commission that came back right first time ([[arctic-crevasse]]), and it is right here for a stronger reason: a drift is nearer to the ground's own colour than a crack ever was, so a painted body would seam worse. ROLE `landmark` LIKE THE REST OF THE BATCH, AND NOT `ambient`, even though ambient's 'soft, rounded or organic' silhouette clause finally fits a subject here — because it would fight the HARD-EDGED SLIPFACE these subjects are built on, and a prompt carrying an instruction and its opposite is the failure this file has recorded five times. ── THE ONE THAT PAIRS WITH EVERY OTHER PROP IN THE VENUE. Place a tail off the LEE side of anything that stands up — [[arctic-nunatak-crag]], [[arctic-serac-tower]] once it exists, [[arctic-station]] and its huts — with the wide end touching the obstacle and the tongue streaming away downwind. It is the cheapest way to make the rock look like it has been standing there a long time. 320u is 35 m, about six boat lengths. In ones, always: two tails off one rock is a fork, which is a different landform. 5:1 AND planRound FALSE, so ORTHO_LONG applies — and this is the rare subject where its 'far end exactly as wide as the near end' clause is genuinely WRONG, because a comet tail is defined by its taper. The subject spends a sentence making the taper the point, so expect the assembled prompt to argue with itself here by one clause. That is the [[river-log]] situation exactly: the log admits its taper and takes the mismatch. If a delivery comes back as a parallel-sided bar, the fault is the clause, not the generator — reject it anyway, because a bar is a different object. ── ⚠️⚠️ ROUND 1 REJECTED FOR BOTH DRIFTS 2026-08-23, AND `RELIEF_ONLY` HAS NOW BEEN IGNORED THREE TIMES OUT OF THREE. Every drift delivered so far — bank, tail, barchan — came back with its body PAINTED, despite a paragraph refusing it in capitals. That is not three unlucky rolls; it is evidence that asking this generator for a transparent body does not work. It thinks in SHAPES, and a shape has a fill. ⚠️ SO THE INSTRUCTION CHANGED FROM 'DO NOT FILL IT' TO 'IF YOU FILL IT, FILL IT WITH THIS VALUE'. The bank survived only because its fill happened to land within ~6 levels of the ground, which made it keyable at ingest; the tail and the barchan filled theirs with the SHADE tone instead, and a drift whose body is the shade tone is a grey object lying on snow. If the broad body of this picture is plainly darker than the snow around it, you have drawn a stone, a leaf or a moon lying on the ice, and it is wrong however good the outline is. assets.note: THE FREE-STANDING ONE, and the only prop in the batch that belongs OUT IN THE OPEN. Barchans form where there is plenty of wind and not much snow, which is exactly the windward middle of an ice sheet, so scatter these across the body of `coast` and `shape-3` well away from anything else — a barchan tucked behind a rock would be a tail drift and is the wrong asset. Threes and fours per mass, all opening the same way. 180u is 20 m across, honest for a real barchan and about three boat lengths. ⚠️ allowSymmetry TRUE, and it is the fourth row in this batch to need it. A crescent is bilaterally symmetric by definition, and ARRANGEMENT_NEGATIVE refuses 'symmetrical arrangement' — so the guard would have fought the subject. The cost is paid in the subject, which spends a paragraph making the two horns unequal; see [[arctic-nunatak-massif]]'s note for the full argument, which now covers five rows. If round 1 comes back as a drawn crescent moon, strengthen that paragraph rather than turning the flag off. planRound TRUE gives ingest a real aspect check, and it is honest here: a barchan measured across its horns is about as wide as it is deep. It is the only drift that gets a mechanical check on delivery — the other two are long subjects and ORTHO_LONG's parallel sides do not apply to a scalloped bank or a tapering tongue. Judge those two on the contact sheet. ── ROUND 2 2026-08-23: THE VALUE FIX LANDED, THE SHAPE DID NOT. Body p50 moved from 68 levels below the ice ground to 16.9 below, and the crown from 26 below to 11 ABOVE — which is the accepted [[arctic-peak-dome]]'s profile almost exactly, and the owner's 'too blue, not like snow' is answered. Round 1's fix added 'the horns are SHORT and BLUNT-ENDED' while the original sentence still read 'TWO HORNS that reach forward and TAPER TO POINTS'. Both were in the same paragraph. That is the sixth time in this commission a subject has carried an instruction and its opposite, and the generator resolved it the way it always does — by picking one.
