assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. ONE DRIFT BANK — the deep wall of packed snow that builds along the lee of a ridge or a bank and stands there all winter — seen from directly above and ALONE, its long axis running UP the frame. ONE BANK AND ONLY ONE. About four times as long as it is wide, and it is the BIGGEST and DEEPEST of this venue's drifts: where a lee tongue tapers away to nothing, this holds its bulk from end to end. Its line is not straight. It bows gently along its length and its edge is deeply scalloped — a run of shallow bays and blunt noses, at uneven sizes, each a few tenths of the bank's width. At one end it swells thickest; at the other it steps down once and runs out. ⚠️ THE DRIFT IS MADE OF THE SAME SNOW AS THE GROUND, SO IT IS VERY NEARLY THE SAME BRIGHTNESS. This is the thing every drift so far has got wrong, and it is what makes them read as OBJECTS LYING ON the snow instead of swellings IN it. The drift's broad back is NEAR-WHITE. It may sit a little below the snow around it — ten or fifteen levels, which is what makes it visible at all — and NO MORE THAN THAT. Best of all, leave the back FULLY TRANSPARENT so the engine's own ice at #E6F2FB shows through and there is no edge to seam; but if it is painted, it must be that near-white and not a shade darker. ⚠️ A GREY SHAPE ON A WHITE FIELD IS NOT A DRIFT. If the broad body of this picture is plainly darker than the snow around it, you have drawn a stone, a leaf or a moon lying on the ice, and it is wrong however good the outline is. The last barchan came back with NINETY-NINE PERCENT of itself more than twenty levels below the ground, and its very brightest area still twenty-six below. WHAT YOU ACTUALLY SEE: a BROAD BAND OF SHADE running the whole length down ONE side — the slipface and the trough at its foot, several times wider than anything in the other two drifts, and the deepest tone in the picture sitting in the bays where the hollow is deepest. Along its top edge a hard BRIGHT LIP, unbroken, following every scallop of the edge, and in two or three places OVERHANGING it slightly so a thin sliver of the deepest tone shows directly beneath the lip — that overhang is what says this drift is deep rather than merely wide, and it is the most convincing thing on the asset. On the far side the bank runs down into the ground and carries nothing. THERE IS NO SUN IN THIS PICTURE AND NOTHING CASTS A SHADOW. Glacier Sound's sky is low grey overcast, and under overcast light a snow surface has no lit side and no shaded side — relief reads ONLY because a hollow collects less light than the open surface around it. So the dark here is an occlusion, not a shadow: it lies IN the trough at the foot of the slipface, deepest where the hollow is deepest, and it does not fall away from the drift in any direction. There is no light angle to get right, which is deliberate — the engine spins these to point them downwind, and a baked sun would spin with them. ⚠️⚠️ IT IS PILED UP, NOT SCOOPED OUT, AND THIS IS THE HARDEST THING IN THE PICTURE. Seen from straight above with no sun, a mound and a hollow look the same — the only thing that tells them apart is WHICH WAY THE TONE RUNS ACROSS THE FORM. So: THE CREST IS A CLEAR BRIGHT LINE RUNNING THE WHOLE LENGTH, DOWN THE MIDDLE OF THE FORM, AND THE TONE FALLS AWAY FROM IT TO BOTH EDGES. Not one edge — BOTH. The lee side falls fast, so its shade is a narrow hard-edged band close under the crest; the windward side falls slowly, so its shade is a wider, fainter, softer fade. They are not equal and they are both there.  ⚠️⚠️ BUT THE FALL-OFF HAPPENS AT THE EDGES, NOT ACROSS A WHOLE FLANK, AND THESE TWO INSTRUCTIONS FIGHT EACH OTHER UNLESS YOU READ THIS ONE. The broad top of the drift — about four fifths of its width — stays NEAR-WHITE and almost flat. Only the OUTER FIFTH on each side darkens, and it darkens fast: a narrow hard band at the lee foot, a slightly wider and fainter one to windward. ⚠️ DO NOT SHADE A WHOLE FLANK GREY. The last two deliveries did exactly that — one put 39% and the other 61% of the picture more than forty levels below the ground — because 'the tone falls away to both edges' was read as 'paint one side grey'. A DRIFT IS A WHITE THING WITH DARK EDGES, not a half-white half-grey thing. ⚠️ CUT ACROSS THE DRIFT ANYWHERE ALONG ITS LENGTH: the brightest point is in the MIDDLE of that cut and both ends of the cut are clearly darker. If the middle is dark, or if the bright is at one edge and the dark at the other, you have drawn a GROOVE — a furrow, a ski track, a gouge pressed INTO the snow — and that is exactly what the last delivery looked like. Its middle was only eight levels brighter than its edges while a hard dark stripe ran down one flank, and the stripe won. THE MIDDLE MUST BEAT BOTH EDGES BY A REAL STEP, not by a whisker. AND THE DARK BELONGS AT THE FOOT, ON THE OUTSIDE. It is the shadow in the corner where the drift meets flat ground, so it hugs the OUTER edge of the form. A hard dark stripe sitting INSIDE the body, with bright on both sides of it, is the inside wall of a trench. ⚠️ ALL THE DARK LIVES IN THE NARROW MARKS AND NOWHERE ELSE. The deep tones belong to the SLIPFACE BAND and the TROUGH at its foot, and to nothing else: those may drop through #9FB3C6 to #7E93A6, about 95 below the ground, because a hollow is dark. Everything BROAD stays near-white. The crest lip is the brightest thing here, near #FBFDFF, a shade ABOVE the ground rather than under it. ⚠️ AND THE DARK STAYS A GREY-BLUE. Snow in a hollow loses light, not colour, so nothing may be pushed toward a rich saturated blue — a rich blue is WATER, and this venue's water at #1D4066 is never far away; keep every tone at least 25 units of colour distance from it. ⚠️ THREE FLAT TONES AND ONE HARD EDGE, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT A SMOOTH SNOW SURFACE INVITES. Every tone is flat from edge to edge and meets its neighbour on a crisp line. NO airbrush, no soft gradient, no blur, no glow, no sheen, and above all none of the crumpled-paper or draped-cloth look that comes of shading snow smoothly — measured across this venue's white deliveries, that failure put only 13-22% of each picture on a flat plane where the style wants four fifths. A crevasse is a NARROW SLOT: a hard white lip on BOTH sides with a dark core running down the middle between them. ONE SECTION OF A CALVING GLACIER FRONT — the broken ice cliff where a glacier ends at the sea — seen from directly above and ALONE. It is a STRAIGHT STRIP running UP the frame, about five or six times as long as it is wide across. Everything in between is the cliff. ⚠️⚠️ IT MUST TILE END TO END, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS ASSET. The engine lays these in a row to build a whole waterfront, so the TOP EDGE of this picture has to continue seamlessly into the BOTTOM EDGE of the next copy of itself. That means the two short edges carry the IDENTICAL cross-section: the cliff lip sits at exactly the same distance across the frame at the top as at the bottom, the face is the same width across at both, and the tone at every point along the top edge matches the tone at the same point along the bottom edge. Anything crossing one short edge reappears at the matching point on the other, unbroken and at the same size. The strip must also run DEAD STRAIGHT — it may not curve, taper or drift sideways down its length, because a curve cannot be laid end to end. ⚠️ AND IT MUST CARRY NO LANDMARK. Nothing in it may be big enough or odd enough to be recognised twice on screen: no single great bay, no one huge block, no obvious notch. The player will see four or five copies of this at once, and one distinctive feature becomes a stamp they can count. Spread the incident evenly along the whole length. WORKING ACROSS THE STRIP FROM THE ICE SIDE TO THE WATER SIDE — four bands and then nothing. (1) THE BACK: a narrow band of plain near-white ice at the left edge, the same brightness as the sheet behind it, fading out to nothing at the very edge so there is no line where the prop stops. (2) THE LIP: a hard, ragged, near-white crest running the whole length — the top of the cliff — notched and stepped every so often where blocks have already gone, never a ruled straight line. (3) THE FACE: the wall itself, a band of deeper grey-blue below the lip, broken by vertical fracture lines into a run of tall narrow panels of slightly different tone. This is the darkest part of the picture and it runs the whole length. (4) THE FOOT: where the face meets the sea, a broken fringe of fallen ice — a scatter of small angular blocks and brash, densest right at the wall and thinning out into the water, and NOT a continuous line. (5) THE WATER SIDE: transparent. Draw no sea, no foam line and no wave — the engine draws its own water and its own shoreline foam, and anything painted here will disagree with them. Ice and snow in shadow lose LIGHT, not COLOUR, so every tone here stays close to neutral — a grey-blue, never a rich saturated blue. A rich blue is WATER, and this venue's water is #1D4066: keep every tone at least 25 units of colour distance from it. assets.note: THE VENUE'S SIGNATURE PIECE OF GEOGRAPHY, AND THE FIRST TILEABLE PROP IN THE GAME. Glacier Sound is named for a glacier the player has never actually been able to see: the ice masses end in the engine's ordinary coastline stroke, the same line a beach gets. This strip is what turns that edge into a calving front, laid end to end along the water side of `coast`, `shape-3` or `shape-4`. Two or three sections make a bay; eight make the front the card art promises. ⚠️ ONE-AXIS TILING IS NEW HERE AND IT IS NOT THE TEXTURE RULE. A `texture` wraps on all four edges and has no silhouette; this is a SPRITE that wraps on TWO — its two short ends — and keeps a real front-to-back structure across the other axis. The wrap discipline is borrowed wholesale from the texture class (identical cross-sections, no centred feature, no landmark) and the rest is an ordinary world-prop. Judge the wrap the way textures are judged: lay two copies end to end at race scale and look at the join, not at the master. ⚠️ PROP-SPIN OFF, AND `heading °` PER PLACEMENT — non-negotiable on this one. The strip has a water side and an ice side, so it must be turned to face the sea, and a run of sections only tiles if every section in the run carries the SAME heading. This is the one prop in the venue where two neighbouring placements have to agree exactly. Anchor `center` so the spacing between sections is the length, with nothing to work out. 800u is 87 m per section, so a 1200u stretch of shore is a section and a half — place them nose to tail, not overlapping, and let the engine's own coastline run behind them. ⚠️ THE WATER SIDE MUST BE TRANSPARENT AND THE SUBJECT SAYS SO TWICE, because this is the asset most likely to try to paint its own sea. The engine already draws water, shoreline foam and drifting floes there; a painted sea would disagree with all three and would move with the prop instead of with the waves. Same reasoning as the crevasse family's relief-only construction, and the same failure if it is ignored. CONTACT none: the ice behind it is already land and already stops a boat. ⚠️ BUT NOTE THE PROP DRAWS PAST THE LAND EDGE — the fallen brash at its foot deliberately overhangs into the water — so the sprite will extend over sailable water where nothing stops the hull. That is a cosmetic overhang and it is intended; keep it SHORT, because a long one is a visual promise of shallows the physics does not keep. ⚠️ ONE WORD KEPT OUT OF THE SUBJECT: 'depth'. NEGATIVE ends 'depth, receding ground, vanishing point, foreshortening' — a cluster about PICTORIAL depth, the perspective cue a nadir camera must not have. A cliff face's physical depth is a different thing wearing the same word, and [[arctic-crevasse]] hit this first; the subject says 'width across' instead. ── ✅ ROUND 1 DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-23, owner: "pretty good". ⚠️⚠️ AND THE WRAP TEST I BUILT OVER-CALLED IT, WHICH IS THE FIFTH METRIC IN THIS COMMISSION TO DO THAT. Measured on the master the seam is 4.5x an interior row boundary and the strip edges shift 10px and 42px between top and bottom, which reads as an outright failure. LAID THREE SECTIONS END TO END AT RACE SCALE ON THE REAL WATER, THE JOINS ARE INVISIBLE — the three read as one continuous cliff. That is exactly the finding [[river-outcrop]] records for textures: all four of those carry a master-scale seam of 1.5x to 3.3x and none of them shows it once composited and drawn at size, and two earlier deliveries were rejected on the master number alone before anyone noticed. JUDGE A TILE TILED, COMPOSITED AND AT SIZE. ⚠️ fillTo IS 1.0 ON THIS ROW AND MUST STAY THERE. Every other prop in the batch takes 0.86 or 0.92, which leaves a transparent margin for rotation — and a margin on a tiling strip means sections laid at spacing ==  do not touch. [[cove-wall-stone]] is the precedent and took 1.0 for the same reason. The consequence is that ingest warns 'content reaches within 6% of the edge' on every delivery of this row; that warning is CORRECT and expected, and the asset would be broken without it. TWO DEPARTURES ACCEPTED. The cliff reads GREY rather than as ice: only 7% of it sits at or above the ice ground and its darkest tone is dE 20 from the water, under the 25 floor. And the ice-side edge does not fade out as the subject asks, so there is a tonal step where the strip meets the sheet. Both are the one-sided-constraint fault again — the subject named the face as the darkest part and gave a ladder, without bounding the light end or saying what share should be near-white. Against navy water it reads well, which is where it spends its life. If it is ever re-rolled, bound both ends and ask for a real near-white band at the ice edge.

assets.note: THE FIRST OF TWO, AND THE FIRST ART THIS VENUE'S GRANITE HAS EVER HAD. Arctic authors three `granite` shapes — `granite-isle` at 629u, `shape-2` at 248u and `shape-1` at 150u — and until now they were bare tiled rock with nothing on them, which is why the Rock reads as a grey blob rather than as a place. ⚠️ AND `granite-isle` IS THE COURSE'S ROUNDING MARK, so this is the one prop family in the commission that the fleet passes CLOSE ABOARD every lap. It gets more looks than anything else here. 140u is 15 m, about two and a half boat lengths, and roughly a fifth of the Rock's width — big enough to read at speed, small enough that three or four fit on it without becoming the island's colour. Scatter them in the hollows and on the shaded side; leave the crests bare, because wind-scoured rock is why a nunatak is black in a white landscape and the same logic applies at this scale. ⚠️ THE FLOE CONFUSION IS THE REAL RISK AND IT IS WORSE HERE THAN FOR THE SERACS. A serac is white ice on white ice and only its stepping separates it; this is white on DARK, which is precisely a floe's value relationship, and the venue has 112 floes drifting a few boat lengths away. The whole defence is THICKNESS — a floe is a plate with a clean rim, a patch is a skin with a torn edge and rock showing through it — and the subject spends its longest paragraph there. CHECK IT ON A PLATE WITH FLOES IN FRAME, which is the only honest test, the same call [[arctic-serac-cluster]] and [[arctic-peak-dome]] both take. PROP-SPIN ON: no baked sun, so rotating one costs nothing and it is what lets four of these look like four different patches. planRound TRUE gives ingest a real aspect check, which this family can actually pass — unlike every long subject in the batch. ── ✅ ROUND 1 DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-23 — the only asset in this commission to pass on its FIRST generation, and it is worth asking why. It is the one row whose subject was written after every other lesson had landed, and the one whose ground is DARK: white on granite needs none of the deep-shading, seam, value-inversion or mound-versus-hollow machinery that the snow-on-snow props each cost three to eight rounds. THE HARD PROBLEMS IN THIS BATCH WERE ALL WHITE-ON-WHITE. MEASURED: 8.3% of the patch is INTERIOR TRANSPARENT HOLES, so the granite genuinely shows through it rather than being painted in — which is the skin-not-plate distinction the subject spends its longest paragraph on, delivered exactly. 50 components: the main mass plus 49 separate flecks carrying 2.1% of the ink, which is the torn margin. luma p50 244 against granite's ~86, so 95% of it is well clear of its own ground. ⚠️ IT TRIPS ingest's NOT ORTHOGRAPHIC WARNING AT 1.21 AND THAT IS A FALSE POSITIVE. A snow patch has no intrinsic aspect — an irregular blob 1.2x taller than wide is exactly what one looks like — so the check has nothing true to measure here. planRound stays TRUE anyway, because the clause it puts in the prompt ('as tall as it is wide') is a useful nudge toward a compact patch, and the alternative state would hand this row ORTHO_LONG's parallel-sides rule, which is worse. EXPECT THE WARNING ON EVERY DELIVERY OF THIS ROW; it is the fourth documented false positive of that check. SHIPPED at 560px bake / 4x for a 140px display, 0.37x resolution — plenty of headroom for the scatter this family is placed by.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. ONE PATCH OF OLD SNOW LYING ON BARE GRANITE — a SECOND patch, and it must not be the first one again — seen from directly above and ALONE. ONE PATCH AND ONLY ONE, roughly as tall as it is wide. ⚠️ IT IS LOBED WHERE THE OTHER IS RAGGED. Build it from THREE OR FOUR ROUNDED LOBES that swell out of one another like the leaves of a clover, meeting at soft waists rather than at points, with one lobe clearly larger than the rest and one barely more than a bulge. Its outline is therefore SMOOTH AND ROUNDED at the large scale and torn only in the small — the opposite balance to its sibling, which is angular at the large scale and reaches out in thin arms. Two patches on one island have to be told apart by SHAPE with the colour taken out, which is why this one is specified as lobes and not as a size. ITS OUTLINE IS THE WHOLE ASSET AND IT IS DEEPLY IRREGULAR: a rounded but ragged blob, pinched in at two or three places where the rock rises through it, drawn out into a couple of narrow lobes where the snow has run into cracks, and nowhere near a circle or an oval. The edge is SCALLOPED at two scales at once — big soft bays a fifth of the patch across, and a fine torn fretting along them — and at the thinnest margins it breaks up completely into a scatter of small separate flecks of snow that trail away from the main mass. INSIDE IT, TWO OR THREE SMALL DARK ISLANDS where the granite pushes through, irregular and off-centre, plus one or two thin dark hairlines where a crack in the rock shows as a line in the snow. Those holes are what make it a skin rather than a plate. ⚠️ THIS ONE LIES ON DARK ROCK, NOT ON SNOW, WHICH MAKES IT THE EASY CASE IN THIS VENUE AND CHANGES WHAT THE PICTURE IS FOR. The ground under it is Glacier Sound's granite — a cold blue-grey rock around #4B5563, dark — so a white patch on it has all the contrast it could want and needs none of the deep shading the venue's snow-on-snow props fight for. The read here is the SHAPE OF THE EDGE, not the tone. ⚠️ AND IT MUST NOT READ AS A FLOE, WHICH IS THE ONE REAL RISK. This venue has 112 drifting ice floes, and a floe is a white shape on a dark ground — exactly the value relationship this prop has. THE DIFFERENCE IS THICKNESS. A floe is a PLATE: hard clean outline, an even rim, a body that reads as solid, because it is a slab you could stand on the edge of. A snow patch is a SKIN: it has no thickness at all, its edge is torn and scalloped and feathers away to nothing, and the rock shows through it in places near the margin as small dark islands and dark hairlines where the stone breaks the surface. Never give it a clean continuous outline, never give it a rim, and never give it a drop shadow — a patch that casts a shadow is a plate. That distinction has to survive with the colour taken out. THERE IS NO SUN IN THIS PICTURE. The venue's sky is low grey overcast, so there is no lit side and no shaded side and nothing casts a shadow. What little modelling there is comes from occlusion: the snow is a touch dimmer where it thins into a hollow in the rock and where the stone shoulders through it. This is deliberate — the engine spins these to scatter them, and a baked sun would spin with them. TONES: the snow is NEAR-WHITE and stays there — #FBFDFF where it is deep, #E9F3FC over most of it, and no lower than #C6D6E4 in its thinnest, dirtiest margins. It is the brightest thing in the frame by a long way and that is correct. The rock that shows through is the granite's own cold grey — #5C6674 for a shouldered edge, #4B5563 for a bare patch, #333C48 in a crack — never black, never warm, never brown. ⚠️ DEEP IS NOT THE SAME AS BLUE. Ice and snow in shadow lose LIGHT, not COLOUR, so every tone here stays close to neutral — a grey-blue, never a rich saturated blue. A rich blue is WATER, and this venue's water is #1D4066: keep every tone at least 25 units of colour distance from it. This has failed five times in this commission and it is always the same cause — a luma floor stated with no chroma ceiling beside it. ⚠️ FLAT PLANES AND HARD EDGES. Every tone is flat from edge to edge and meets its neighbour on a crisp line — no airbrush, no soft gradient, no blur, no glow, no gloss, and none of the crumpled-paper look that comes of shading snow smoothly. Measured across this venue's white deliveries that failure has put only 13-27% of each picture on a flat plane where the style wants four fifths. NOTHING ELSE: no water, no ice floe, no crevasse, no boat, no wildlife, no track, no footprint, no vegetation, no lichen. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the patch stands alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies the rock it lies on.
assets.note: THE SECOND GRANITE PATCH, AND IT REPLACES A GULLY. The row was declared as `arctic-snowpatch-gully`, a snow-filled crack — a STREAK against the blob, on the [[river-boulder-large]] principle that a family must differ in silhouette rather than in size. The owner's call 2026-08-23 was a second BLOB instead, so the key changed while the row was still an undrawn slot. Manifest keys are the one thing this pipeline promises never change, and that promise binds art which EXISTS: renaming a slot with no files, no ingest and no PROP_KINDS entry costs nothing, where leaving it called `-gully` while it drew a blob would cost the next reader an hour. ⚠️ SO THE SILHOUETTE RULE MOVES INSIDE THE PAIR. Two blobs on one 629u island is exactly the failure that principle warns about, so the distinction is now LOBED versus RAGGED: this one is smooth and rounded at the large scale and torn only in the small, where [[arctic-snowpatch]] is angular at the large scale and reaches out in thin arms. That survives greyscale, which is the test. If a delivery comes back a near-twin of the first it is a reject however good it looks alone — the whole value of a second patch is that it does not read as the first one placed twice. 170u against the first's 140u, a deliberate 20% step so a scatter has two sizes as well as two shapes. Everything else is inherited from [[arctic-snowpatch]]: the skin-not-plate defence against the venue's 112 floes, transparent holes so the granite shows through, no sun so prop-spin is free, and the near-white value that white-on-dark makes easy.

assets.subject: Dry beach sand seen from directly overhead from about ten metres up, in flat even light — the pale warm tan of an open ocean-facing beach. AT THIS HEIGHT SAND IS ALMOST FEATURELESS, and that is the subject: a quiet, near-uniform field whose only structure is broad, soft, irregular patches of very slightly different tone, each blending into its neighbours with no hard edge, the way dampness and grain size drift across an open beach. NO RIPPLES OF ANY KIND. There are no crests, no troughs, no ridges, no parallel lines, no repeating waves in the sand and no direction the eye can follow — nothing in the frame lines up with anything else, and no spacing repeats. Scattered thinly through it, the only hard marks in the frame: a few small pale shell fragments and tiny stone chips, each drawn as a small shaped mark, never as fine speckle or photographic grain. The whole image holds a very narrow warm range from #cdb79f to #ecd6b7 around a mean of #e1c6a7 — a greyed, slightly brown tan, never a bright buttery yellow and never white. No water, no foam, no wave, no wet sand, no waterline, no shoreline, no vegetation, no beach grass, no seaweed, no driftwood, no dune, no dune shadow, no rocks larger than a chip, no cast shadows, no footprints, no tracks, no trails, no raked or combed pattern, no wind ripple, no sand ripple, no ridged or corrugated surface
assets.note: Third texture-class asset — Lighthouse Cove's shoreline, wired to the `tropical` LOOK rather than to the bay, so bay (10 isles), lake (4) and lagoon (2) all share it. Ships at tileWorld 128, alpha 0.7, over an ISLAND_STYLES.tropical body of #ddc39a. V2, AND THE V1 IT REPLACES IS THE WHOLE LESSON. v1 asked for wind ripples 'lying in loosely the same direction' — what a beach looks like from head height, not from the height this game is drawn at. Measured against aerial reference photography resampled to the game's own scale, the gap was never amplitude (v1 contrast 6.31 against a reference band of 2.95-11.92) but STRUCTURE: v1 carried one dominant crest direction (anisotropy 0.656) and a strong preferred wavelength (periodicity 5.77); real aerial sand has neither (0.15-0.48, 1.65-2.16). ⚠️ RETILING CANNOT FIX A PERIODICITY PROBLEM — the finding worth carrying to the next texture. Shrinking v1's tile 512 -> 90 moved periodicity 5.44 -> 6.70, i.e. not at all: a smaller tile makes a ripple smaller, never rarer. Only redrawing fixed it. Ask what structure the material has AT THE CAMERA'S ALTITUDE before writing the subject; when the honest answer is 'almost none', the texture's job is broad tonal drift, not a pattern. V2 MEASURED IN GAME: anisotropy 0.656 -> 0.177 (matches the most isotropic reference, 0.149) — the directional ripples are gone. Periodicity 5.77 -> 4.23, and the residual is NOT a defect: the peak sits at 21px on screen = 2.3m, which is the mottle's own blob size, not a tile harmonic (128/64/43px) and not a ripple. Real sand photographs score low here because their texture is scale-free down to the grain; v2 having a characteristic patch size is a fair description of sand, where v1's parallel crests every 4.35m were not. Closing it further would need mottle across several scales — a refinement, not a blocker. SIZING, unchanged by the reroll: tileWorld 128 is where the resolvable features land at true size. At 9.2 world units per metre (the 56.4-unit hull read as a 6.1m sportboat) it puts shell chips at 4.9cm median / 14cm p95. The 512 tile made them 20cm cobbles and 56cm boulders. v2 was authored FOR 128, so its minfeature was 32px in the master rather than the 8px a 512 intent implies. COLOUR, AND THE PROPERTY WORTH KEEPING: v2 came back at mean #ddc39a against the #e1c6a7 the subject asked for — 12 RGB units, almost all of it blue channel (154 vs 167), so slightly warmer and less grey than the Varkala plate. Inside the natural spread of the three references (#e1c6a7 / #eac8b1 / near-neutral #cdcac6) and accepted rather than rerolled. ISLAND_STYLES.tropical.body is set to the TILE'S OWN MEAN, not to the reference: with base equal to tile mean the blend cannot move the colour, only the spread around it, so alpha became a pure contrast knob and the rendered shore held #dac198 across alpha 0.5/0.7/0.85/1.0. That is the fix granite's note asked for (normalize the tile's mean to the base), reached from the other end, and it is why alpha could be tuned on looks alone. If the shore must sit exactly on a reference colour, normalize the TILE to it at pattern-bake time and set the body to match — do not split them, or alpha silently becomes a colour control again. ALPHA 0.7, up from v1's 0.5: v2's mottle is much softer than v1's ripples, and at 0.5 on-screen contrast fell to 1.94, BELOW the reference band. 0.7 gives 4.12, between the smooth-beach plate (2.95) and Varkala (8.33). The curve flattens past there (0.85 -> 4.39, 1.0 -> 4.78), so 0.7 buys nearly all the contrast available and keeps headroom. WRAP: delivered at 1254px, ingest resampled to the 1024 master through wrap_resize. Roll-by-half shows a faint tonal step at the horizontal midline and no hard seam; edge-to-edge difference is 2.4x (left-right) and 3.0x (top-bottom) the interior neighbour difference against the snow tile's 1.95x — slightly looser, invisible at the 8x downsample to 128. STILL MISSING, and it is the strongest sand cue in every reference: the WET BAND at the waterline. Reference runs #c89760 at the swash and #dcb78b damp against #e1c6a7 dry — a wide saturated dark band, not the 6px stroke drawIslands paints today. Engine work, not art. ONE AUTHORING CONFLICT, resolved in the subject: v2 first asked for the faint scuffed walking trails the reference shows, which argues with the texture class NEGATIVE's 'footprints, tracks'. The negative won — a trail is a distinctive feature and at 128 the tile repeats ~11 times per viewport, so it would stamp out countably. Trails belong in a decal or a much bigger tile.

assets.subject: A closed sward of coastal upland grass and low scrub seen from directly overhead from about ten metres up, in flat even light — the sun-faded green of a Cape Cod bluff top, salt-pruned and wind-dried rather than lush inland pasture. AT THIS HEIGHT INDIVIDUAL BLADES DO NOT RESOLVE, and that is the subject: the sward reads as a soft clumpy mottle, rounded tussock crowns a shade lighter where the grass mounds up and narrow sinks a shade darker between them, every clump blending into its neighbours with no hard edge and at roughly the same density everywhere. THROUGH THE SWARD, LOW SCRUB — broader, rounder, slightly darker and greyer patches where bearberry, beach plum and bayberry lie flat against the wind. Each is a soft-edged mound a little denser than the grass around it, scattered unevenly, covering perhaps a fifth of the frame. THEY ARE PATCHES OF A DIFFERENT PLANT, NOT BUSHES: no branch, no stem, no drawn outline, no cast shadow, and nothing tall enough to read as an object sitting on top of the ground. NOTHING LEANS ANY PARTICULAR WAY. No combed direction, no mowing stripes, no swirls, no rows, no terracing, nothing lining up with the frame or with itself, and no spacing that repeats anywhere in the image. A few broad drifts of paler, drier, straw-tinted grass move through at the largest scale, soft and wide, where salt and wind have burned the sward back — drifts of tone only, never a shape with an edge. THE WHOLE IMAGE HOLDS A NARROW SUN-FADED RANGE from #8CA03A to #BAC96C around a mean of #A3B845. IT IS SUN-BLEACHED, NOT SUN-GREYED, and that distinction is the whole colour brief. Bleached grass goes LIGHTER and YELLOWER; it does not go gritty or grey. So this is a bright, clean, confident yellow-green — paler and drier than a lush inland meadow, but every bit as alive. NOTHING HERE IS OLIVE, KHAKI, SAGE, GREYED-DOWN, DUSTY, MUTED OR ARMY-DRAB, and nothing is the cured tan-olive of a dead sward. If a green looks washed out or dirty it is wrong; take the fading upward into light, never sideways into grey. Hold the whole image inside a narrow value range. No visible soil, no sand, no rock, no flowers, no individual drawn blades, no fine hairline strokes, no paths, no tracks, no footprints, no fences, no stone walls, no water and no shoreline
assets.note: Lighthouse Cove's UPLAND GROUND — the material most of the venue's land is made of, and the one that has to bridge between the houses, the shore trees and the rock. Wired as LAND_TEXTURES.coastalscrub at tile 128 / alpha 0.5 over an ISLAND_STYLES.coastalscrub body of #A3B845. THE BODY IS THE SPEC MEAN AND MUST BE RESET TO THE DELIVERED TILE'S OWN MEAN ON INGEST, the coralsand precedent: with base equal to tile mean the blend cannot move the colour, only the spread around it, so alpha stays a pure contrast knob and the mean-luma-shift warning the arctic textures carry cannot happen. THE COLOUR IS DERIVED, NOT PICKED, and it is deliberately NOT the venue card's turf. Measured off assets/images/venues/bay.png, the card's sunlit headland turf runs hue 73-75 deg at saturation 0.92-0.99 across three separate headlands — a bright, almost fully saturated yellow-green. That is right for a 1254px illustration and wrong for a ground tile, on the texture class's own rule that this is the surface every boat, mark and prop is drawn ON TOP of and so must lose the contrast fight with them. #A3B845 holds the card's hue family (71 deg) and buys 'sun-faded' by lifting VALUE (L* 63 -> 71) while HOLDING saturation at 0.62. ⚠️ CORRECTED FROM #8CA24A, WHICH CUT SATURATION TO 0.54 INSTEAD, and the correction is the reusable part. Every shipped land body meant to read as alive holds its chroma — grass 0.83, redrock 0.75 — while 0.48 belongs to `swampgrass`, a CURED DEAD sward. Rendered beside the venue card, the desaturated version read army-olive: it had left the family. Sun-bleached grass is lighter and yellower, never greyer. This is the same error the cedar's note already warns about in this venue's own tree set ("when a subject wants muted, say which direction it is muted TOWARD, or you simply desaturate") — made again, one asset later, on a ground instead of a crown. It sits between the two existing swards by construction: dE 15.5 from `grass` (#7aaa1d, bright meadow) and 28.1 from `swampgrass`. Against what it actually touches in the cove it is far clear — dE 41.2 from the bay's sand and 52.0 from the coastal rock. ALTITUDE DISCIPLINE PER bay-sand v2, which is the transferable lesson of this class: ask what structure the material really has at ten metres before writing the subject. Blades do not resolve, so the honest structure is tussock mottle plus scrub patches, and any combed direction is banned outright — one dominant direction repeats as visible banding at tile scale, which is how bay-sand v1 died. ⚠️ THE SCRUB PATCHES ARE THIS TILE'S PERIODICITY RISK, the way ripples were sand's: they are the only discrete feature here, so if they arrive evenly sized and evenly spaced they will read as a countable stamp at 128 (the tile repeats ~11 times per viewport). Measure anisotropy and periodicity on delivery against bay-sand v2's accepted 0.177 / 4.23, and remember that retiling cannot fix a periodicity problem — only redrawing can. ALPHA 0.5 is the pre-registered sward value, not a measurement; the two existing swards use it because their mottle is busier than sand's. Retune on delivered contrast, and note the direction of travel is set by what the tile arrives at: if the sward reads dead at race scale the move is UP, as bayou-mud's note argues. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-10. STRUCTURE PASSED OUTRIGHT: anisotropy 0.179, essentially bay-sand's 0.183 and grass's 0.174 and nowhere near the 0.656 that killed bay-sand v1, so no combing and no banding direction; wrap measured 1.62x left-right and 1.47x top-bottom against an ordinary neighbour difference, the TIGHTEST of the ten tiles in the library. The scrub patches that this note flagged as the periodicity risk did not become a countable stamp — dominant grain is 314px in the master, i.e. a 3.5m patch at tile 128, which is a patch of bearberry and not a tile harmonic. TWO THINGS MOVED ON DELIVERY. (1) ALPHA 0.5 -> 0.40, and it is the marsh's argument repeating: the pre-registered value assumed this tile would arrive at the two swards' contrast and it did not. Delivered luma sd is 14.30 at tile 128 against swampgrass's 10.20, half again as busy, so 0.5 would have landed on-screen sd 7.15 — the loudest ground in the game and past `grass` (6.75). Backwards for the material MOST of the venue's land is made of. 0.40 lands 5.72, between swampgrass and grass, structure intact. THE GENERAL RULE: a pre-registered alpha is a guess about a tile that does not exist yet, so it is a starting point and never a spec. (2) COLOUR DRIFTED 11.1 dE TOWARD YELLOW — hue 71 -> 62 deg, L* 71 -> 66 — almost all of it in the green channel. ACCEPTED RATHER THAN REROLLED, and the reasoning is worth keeping because the session's whole colour argument runs the other way. The drift is toward the cured-sward family this asset was rewritten to escape, and it did NOT arrive: dE to `swampgrass` is 17.5, down from the spec's 28.1 but still clear, and saturation held at 0.60 against the spec's 0.62 — the tile is yellower, not greyer, and greyer was the failure mode. Judged on the rendered fill with the three shore trees on it rather than on the swatch, which is the honest test: the sward reads as sun-faded coastal grass and the trees separate strongly on top of it. If it is ever regenerated, push the subject's mean hex greener to leave room for the same drift.

assets.subject: Bare weathered coastal rock seen from directly overhead from about ten metres up, in flat even light — the grey-tan stone of a New England headland, glacial rock rounded and smoothed by salt, ice and centuries of sea. AT THIS HEIGHT THE SHAPE OF THE ROCK IS THE SUBJECT AND ITS MINERAL GRAIN IS NOT: the surface reads as a mosaic of broad ROUNDED humps and whalebacks, each one a soft-edged swell of stone a shade lighter across its crown and a shade darker where it rolls away, packed against its neighbours with shallow seams and hollows between them. ROUNDED, NOT SHATTERED, and this is the whole difference between this rock and a mountain granite: there are no straight-edged fractures, no sharp angular plates, no jagged blocks, no knife-edged cracks meeting at blunt angles and no fresh broken faces. Every edge in this image has been worn soft. A few narrow JOINTS wander across the stone as thin darker lines, curving and irregular, dividing it loosely into large rounded panels — three or four in the whole frame, never a network, never a grid and never parallel. Scattered thinly, the only hard marks in the image: small pockets of coarse gravel and a few loose rounded pebbles caught in the hollows, each drawn as a small shaped mark and never as fine speckle or photographic grit. A LICHEN CAST RATHER THAN LICHEN PATCHES: a faint, soft, irregular paling across some of the crowns, a little cooler and a little lighter but still the stone's own colour, with no hard edge and no separate hue of its own — this is weathering, not a plant, so nothing orange, nothing yellow-green and nothing that reads as a drawn blotch. NOTHING LINES UP. No bedding direction, no parallel seams, no repeating spacing, no direction the eye can follow, and nothing in the frame agreeing with anything else. THE WHOLE IMAGE HOLDS A NARROW GREY-TAN RANGE from #83786B to #B9AFA0 around a mean of #9D9080 — a soft warm grey stone, never a cold blue-grey mountain granite, never an orange or rust sandstone, and never a brown earth or mud. Hold the whole image inside a narrow value range. No water, no foam, no spray, no wet rock, no waterline, no tide line, no seaweed, no barnacles, no shells, no sand, no soil, no moss, no grass and no vegetation of any kind
assets.note: Lighthouse Cove's HARD SHORELINE — points, islets, harbour edges, rocky coves, bridge abutments. Wired as LAND_TEXTURES.coastalrock at tile 256 / alpha 0.35 over an ISLAND_STYLES.coastalrock body of #9D9080; body is the SPEC mean and must be reset to the delivered tile's own mean on ingest, per coralsand and bay-sand. THE COLOUR IS THE INTERESTING DECISION AND IT WAS MEASURED TWICE. Sampled off the venue card's three rock areas (headland cliff, islet boulders, left shore) with water, foam and foliage masked out, the card's rock means #786C55-#8C7858 at hue 37-40 deg and saturation 0.24-0.38. Taking that mean directly gives #7D6F56 — and it FAILS, at dE 5.3 from the bayou's `mudflat` (#6e6449) and 11.0 from `marsh`, i.e. two materials a designer picks from the same twenty-three-row list. The card mean is dragged dark and warm by the shadow crevices BETWEEN boulders, which are not what the material looks like; the stone itself reads at the lit end. #9D9080 keeps the card's hue (33 deg) and moves to saturation 0.18 at L* 60, which is also what 'grey-tan' means in a number. If it reads too grey once the tile lands, move WARMER (toward #9a8c77) rather than more saturated: warmth is what the card's stone actually has. SEPARATION WAS SCORED IN TWO TIERS, and that distinction is the reusable part: IN-VENUE separation is what matters in play, because sand and rock share a shoreline and a player has to read them apart at race scale — this holds dE 23.9 from the bay's sand (#ddc39a) and 52.0 from the new coastal scrub. CROSS-VENUE separation is only a picker-swatch concern, since mudflat and coastal rock can never appear in the same race, so 19.2 there is acceptable where 5.3 was not. TILE 256, NOT 128, and it follows the material rather than the venue: rounded whalebacks are metre-scale features where a grass tussock and a shell chip are centimetre-scale, and 256 is the size both existing rock tiles use (arctic-granite, redrock-sandstone). At 9.2 units per metre a 256 tile spans 27.8m, which puts a hump at roughly 3-6m across — a boulder, which is what it should be. ALPHA 0.35 is the rock precedent (granite and sandstone both), pre-registered rather than measured; retune on delivered contrast. ⚠️ THE FAILURE TO WATCH FOR IS ANGULARITY. Every generator's prior for 'rock texture from above' is fractured plates, because that is what arctic-granite's own subject asks for and what most reference photography of bare rock shows. This material is the opposite and the subject spends its second-longest clause saying so. If the delivery comes back with straight-edged plates it has failed on MATERIAL, not on rendering — check that before checking colour. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-10, PASSING EVERY GATE, and the numbers are all measured with ONE script across all nine shipped textures rather than quoted from their notes — which matters, because the figures recorded in this file were computed by different scripts at different times and are NOT comparable to each other. A first pass scored this tile's periodicity at 6633 against bay-sand's recorded 4.23 and looked like a catastrophic failure; re-running the same metric over every shipped tile put the set's range at 2098-38867 with bay-sand itself at 13642, i.e. this tile is mid-pack and better than half the library. ⚠️ WHENEVER A TEXTURE METRIC IS COMPARED TO A NUMBER IN A NOTE, RECOMPUTE THE BASELINE. THE MEASUREMENTS: anisotropy 0.155, inside the shipped range of 0.025-0.591 and below bay-sand's 0.183, so no directional bias — the failure that killed bay-sand v1 at 0.656. Dominant grain 179px in the master, which at tile 256 is a boulder 4.0m across, squarely inside the 3-6m the sizing argument asked for. Wrap measured 1.81x left-right and 1.65x top-bottom against an ordinary neighbour difference — tighter than the snow tile's 1.95x and bay-sand's 2.4x/3.0x — and confirmed by eye on a roll-by-half, which shows no seam cross. Colour landed at #a19481 against a spec of #9d9080, 5.8 RGB units warmer and lighter, accepted rather than rerolled and now carried into ISLAND_STYLES as the body. THE MATERIAL RISK THIS SLOT WAS WRITTEN AGAINST DID NOT MATERIALISE: the crown structure came back genuinely ROUNDED — packed whalebacks with soft seams and pebbles caught in the hollows — with no straight-edged plates and no fractured-granite prior anywhere in it. The second-longest clause in the subject is what bought that, and it should stay if this is ever regenerated.

assets.subject: A CRUSHED-SHELL AND SAND LANE seen from directly overhead from about ten metres up, in flat even light — the pale unpaved track that runs between the cottages of a Cape or Nantucket village. AT THIS HEIGHT A LANE IS ALMOST FEATURELESS, and that is the subject: a quiet, near-uniform pale surface whose only structure is broad, soft, irregular patches of very slightly different tone, each blending into its neighbours with no hard edge, the way a track packs harder in some places than others. SCATTERED THINLY THROUGH IT, the only hard marks in the frame: small pale SHELL FRAGMENTS — broken quahog and scallop, a shade whiter and cooler than the ground — together with a few tiny grey pebbles, each drawn as a small shaped mark and never as fine speckle or photographic grain. They are what makes this a shell lane rather than bare dirt, so they must read as chips with edges. ⚠️ NO WHEEL RUTS, NO TRACKS, NO PATH EDGES AND NO DIRECTION OF ANY KIND. There are no parallel lines, no twin ruts, no centre crown, no verge, no kerb and no boundary anywhere in the image — nothing in the frame lines up with anything else and no spacing repeats. This tile is the SURFACE only; the lane's shape and its edges are drawn by the engine, and any edge painted into the tile would repeat as a stripe every time it is laid. THE WHOLE IMAGE HOLDS A VERY NARROW PALE RANGE from #B0A68E to #D4CBB6 around a mean of #C2B8A0 — a soft warm grey-tan, cooler and greyer than beach sand and much paler than any soil, never yellow, never orange, never brown. Hold it inside a narrow value range. No water, no puddle, no wet patch, no grass, no weed, no moss growing through, no tyre mark, no footprint, no vegetation of any kind, no kerbstone and no drain.
assets.note: Lighthouse Cove's FOURTH GROUND, and the answer to the 'lanes' question that had been open since the town set was listed. A LANE IS A GROUND, NOT A PROP, and that is the whole design decision: a prop is a fixed-size sprite, so a village lane would be a dozen placements with a seam at every join — the exact problem cove-quay took two rounds to solve. A ground has no such limit. drawIslands walks the islands in DOCUMENT ORDER (compileVenueDoc's shapeOrder is the designer's stacking), so a thin lane polygon listed AFTER a scrub island simply paints over it, at any length, width or curve, with no seam anywhere by construction. Verified in the renderer before this slot was written. COLOUR CHOSEN AGAINST THE THREE SHIPPED GROUNDS IT WILL TOUCH: #C2B8A0 sits dE 39 from coastal scrub — which is the one that matters, since a lane is nearly always drawn across the scrub — and 12 from sand and 13 from coastal rock, which are close but rarely adjacent to it and are genuinely similar materials (a shell lane IS pale like a beach). tileWorld 128 with the sand family, because shell chips and pebbles are the same centimetre scale as the sand's. ALPHA 0.7 PRE-REGISTERED from bay-sand, whose quiet broad-mottle structure this shares; retune on delivery and reset ISLAND_STYLES.lane.body to the delivered tile's own mean, per coralsand. ⚠️ THE PERIODICITY RISK IS RUTS. bay-sand v1 died of directional ripples and the note there records the finding that RETILING CANNOT FIX A PERIODICITY PROBLEM — only redrawing can. A lane is the most rut-prone subject in the set, so the subject bans parallel lines, twin ruts, a centre crown and any verge outright, and measures against bay-sand v2's accepted anisotropy of 0.177 on delivery. ROUND 1 ACCEPTED AND WIRED. ⚠️ ANISOTROPY 0.039 — THE LOWEST OF ANY TEXTURE IN THE LIBRARY (sand 0.183, scrub 0.181, rock 0.155), so the rut risk this note called the asset's top danger did not materialise at all: there is no directional bias to become banding at tile scale. Colour landed #cac2ad against a #C2B8A0 spec, 8 units light. Wrap 1.69x left-right and 2.89x top-bottom — the vertical is the loosest of the bay's four grounds but sits inside bay-sand's accepted 2.4/3.0, and at the 8x downsample to tile 128 it is invisible. ALPHA 0.5, MEASURED RATHER THAN THE 0.7 PRE-REGISTERED FROM SAND: the delivered tile has sd 7.28 at tile 128 against sand's 4.00, so 0.7 would land on-screen 5.10 — near the top of the library's 1.38-6.75 band and wrong for a narrow strip whose job is to read as a path without pulling the eye off the water. 0.5 lands 3.64, between sand (2.80) and the scrub it is drawn across (5.72), with the shell chips intact. Same finding as the scrub's: A PRE-REGISTERED ALPHA IS A GUESS ABOUT A TILE THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET. body reset to the delivered mean so alpha stays a pure contrast knob.

assets.subject: coconut palm seen from directly above — a single crown of long feathered fronds radiating from a central hub, each frond one chunky tapering blade of clustered leaflet-mass in two flat greens with soft rounded tips — a sunlit top tone near #6FA61B and a deep shade tone near #2E5408 over a body near #4F8410. ⚠️ THIS IS A VIVID, SATURATED, SUNLIT TROPICAL GREEN and it must not drift dull or cool: it stands in a grove with four other palms and thirty-odd copies of itself, and every one of them has to read as the same island on the same afternoon. Nothing here is dusty, muted, sage, olive, grey-green or washed out. ⚠️ THE FRONDS MUST NOT BE EVENLY SPACED, and this is the failure to watch. They sit at PLAINLY UNEVEN lengths and at uneven angles: the gaps between neighbouring fronds differ by a factor of two or more round the crown, at least two fronds droop noticeably shorter than the rest, and at least two CROSS OVER a neighbour rather than sitting beside it. There is one clear sector where the fronds are sparse and one where they crowd. If a viewer could measure an equal angle between fronds all the way round, it has been drawn as a geometric star or a sunburst and it is wrong however handsome it looks — the crown must read as a living tree that has lost a frond here and grown two there. At the hub, a tight cluster of three or four brown coconuts and the top of the trunk. ⚠️ THE TRUNK IS A CROSS-SECTION, NOT A SHAFT, AND THIS IS THE SHARPEST TEST IN THE PICTURE. This palm stands UPRIGHT, so its trunk points straight at the lens and you are looking down the end of it: what shows is a small pale grey-brown DISC near #9C8B72, wedged in among the frond bases and the coconuts, no wider than a coconut and going NOWHERE. You never see the trunk's length, its side, or its rings running away from you. ⚠️ IF A PALE SHAFT RUNS OUT FROM THE HUB IN ANY DIRECTION, THE CAMERA WAS TILTED AND THE PICTURE IS WRONG however good the crown is. An upright palm photographed from directly overhead cannot show a run of trunk — that is geometrically impossible — so a visible run is proof of the fault, and its absence is proof the camera was right. (Its neighbour [[lagoon-palm-leaning]] uses the SAME evidence to mean the opposite: there a long visible trunk is exactly what proves the lean. Same tell, opposite verdict, because one tree is upright and one is not.)
assets.note: First lagoon asset — Pearl Lagoon's island palm, the lagoon counterpart to bayou-cypress. allowSymmetry because a top-down palm crown is genuinely radial, same reasoning as the mark; the subject asks for uneven frond lengths and angles so the rosette still reads organic rather than mandala. anchor trunk-base assumes a vertical palm — a leaning palm from overhead offsets crown from base, so the subject keeps it straight (the leaning variant is lagoon-palm-leaning). world 70 ≈ 7.6m crown at 9.2 units/m, a full-grown coconut palm. ⚠️ GIVEN planRound 2026-08-16, subject otherwise unchanged and art not rejected. See [[lagoon-palm-dense]] for why the flag matters in the PROMPT and not only at ingest. This is the FRUITING crown of the pair — it keeps the coconuts and the glimpse of trunk-top at the hub, and its neighbour at world 74 is the denser, fruitless one. ⚠️ COLOUR AND SPACING CLAUSES PATCHED 2026-08-16 AFTER A REROLL WAS REJECTED, and the rejection was caused by a defect I had already found on this asset's siblings and chose not to fix here. When [[lagoon-palm-dense]] and [[lagoon-palm-young]] were patched for unbounded colour, this subject was audited in the same pass, recorded as 'fine, minor', and given only the planRound flag — even though it carried the identical defect: 'two flat greens (a sunlit top tone and a deep shade tone)' names no hex and sets no floor. THE VERY NEXT ROLL DEMONSTRATED IT. Delivered saturation 0.70 against a family of 0.85-0.99, hue 102.2 against 81.1-95.7, and dE 8.4-13.4 from its four siblings where the sprite it would have replaced sits at 1.6-6.5. Milder than [[lagoon-palm-fan]]'s sage disaster (dE 41.7-46.7 at saturation 0.22) but the same defect and the same direction. AN UNBOUNDED COLOUR CLAUSE IS NOT A MINOR FINDING; it is a coin toss that has now come up wrong twice on this venue. ⚠️ THE ORTHOGRAPHICS, MEANWHILE, WERE THE BEST IN THE FAMILY, which is the planRound change paying off on its first roll: bbox ratio 1.07 against 1.04-1.10 across the palms, radial gradient 1.52 (family 1.59-1.97), ink-centroid offset 0.007. The camera was never the problem on this one. ALSO PATCHED: FROND SPACING. The reroll came back at alpha angular harmonic 31.2% at n=14 against the shipped 17.3% at n=9 — roughly double the family's worst, i.e. fourteen fronds at near-equal angles, drifting toward the geometric star the old clause named but did not make checkable. The clause now asks for measurable unevenness: neighbouring gaps differing by 2x or more, two fronds noticeably short, two crossing, one sparse sector and one crowded one. Its ellipse fill also fell to 60.5% from 72.5%; it is meant to be the OPENER of the pair against palm-dense's 82.4%, but 60.5% reads thin, so the next roll should land near 0.72. ⚠️ METHOD CORRECTION 2026-08-16, AND IT INVALIDATES A TEST USED THROUGHOUT THIS VENUE. The reroll above was judged against 'dE from its siblings' — 1.6-6.5 good, 8-14 bad — with the siblings being [[lagoon-palm-dense]], [[lagoon-palm-young]] and [[lagoon-palm-leaning]]. ALL THREE ARE FROM A SINGLE OpenAI BATCH DATED 2026-08-08 AND ALL THREE ARE BEING REPLACED: in-game sprites are now generated on Gemini, which the owner judges better for this class (OpenAI is still used for venue art and character portraits). Measured, that old batch sits at saturation 0.94-0.99 while the one Gemini palm on this venue, [[lagoon-palm-fan]], sits at 0.85. So 'match the family' was an instruction to match the style being migrated AWAY from, and passing that test would have been the wrong outcome. ⚠️ A CROSS-SPRITE CONFORMITY TEST IS ONLY VALID WITHIN ONE GENERATOR ERA. During a migration the correct anchor is the newest asset of the same class, not the majority of the folder. For this venue that anchor is palm-fan alone. RE-JUDGED AGAINST palm-fan (Gemini, lagoon, palm — the only valid comparison): saturation 0.76 against 0.85 is a mild undershoot, not the failure it was called; the hexes in this subject specify 0.84-0.90 and palm-fan hits 0.86 from the same palette, so the clause is correctly anchored and the roll simply fell short. THE REAL DEFECTS ARE GEOMETRIC AND UNCHANGED: ellipse fill 61.8% against palm-fan's 89.2% and a 0.72 target, and alpha angular harmonic 32.7% at n=14 against palm-fan's 12.9% — fourteen fronds at near-equal angles, the geometric star the subject explicitly refuses. ⚠️ THE OLD SPRITE SHOULD NOT BE KEPT ON THESE GROUNDS EITHER. It was recommended as the better option on style-conformity numbers that were themselves anchored on the old style — circular reasoning. It is 2026-08-08 OpenAI art in a venue migrating to Gemini. PLAN: reroll this one for FILL and FROND SPACING, not colour, and regenerate palm-dense, palm-young and palm-leaning on Gemini as one batch so the grove is internally consistent in the new style rather than one new sprite trying to match three retiring ones. ⚠️ TRUNK CLAUSE REWRITTEN 2026-08-16 AFTER A ROLL CAME BACK WITH A FULL TRUNK SHAFT, and the old clause asked for it: 'the pale grey-brown top of the trunk just visible between the frond bases' invites a trunk, and the generator drew the whole thing. Measured on the pale, low-saturation, non-green pixels: the rejected roll's trunk reaches 1.00 OF THE CROWN RADIUS from the hub (2.30% of all ink), the accepted one 0.15 (0.25% of ink). That distance is the acceptance test — a cross-section reaches ~0.2 or less, a shaft reaches ~1.0 — and it is cheap to measure. ⚠️ NOTE THE SYMMETRY WITH [[lagoon-palm-leaning]], because it is the tidiest example in this manifest of evidence cutting both ways. An upright palm seen from straight overhead CANNOT show a run of trunk; a leaning one MUST. So the same measurement — how far pale trunk colour reaches from the hub — is a reject on this asset and a requirement on that one. Where a prohibition can be dodged by a picture that avoids the issue, a geometric impossibility cannot: this is the same class of test as the camera-pointing stubs on [[lagoon-coral-staghorn]] and the frond crossings on [[lake-fern-bracken]]. ⚠️ ACCEPTED 2026-08-16 AS THE OWNER'S PICK OVER A LATER ROLL, AND THE ANCHOR WAS CORRECTED BY HAND. The later roll was rejected on the trunk: its pale trunk colour reached 1.00 of the crown radius from the hub — a full shaft, which an upright palm photographed from directly overhead cannot show — against 0.15 on this one, a cross-section as it should be. See the trunk clause note above. ⚠️ THE ANCHOR WAS STALE AND INGEST SAID SO: it printed 'anchor kept at [0.4536, 0.5479]' because an anchorPx already existed, and that value was measured off the 2026-08-08 OpenAI sprite whose trunk sat off-centre. This sprite's trunk hub measures [0.5068, 0.4975]. Left alone, all 32 placed palms would have sat about 3.7 world units from where the designer put them — small against a 56u hull, but wrong and free to fix. Corrected to the measured hub. ⚠️ AN ANCHOR IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY VALID ACROSS A REDRAW. ingest.py only seeds anchorPx when the field is absent and otherwise keeps it, which is right for a re-ingest of the same picture and wrong for a genuine replacement — exactly the case during the OpenAI-to-Gemini migration, where the new art is a different composition. Re-measure the anchor on any redraw; ingest prints the bbox centre next to the kept value precisely so the discrepancy is visible. TWO KNOWN SHORTFALLS ACCEPTED, both geometric and both already written into the subject for the next roll: ellipse fill 61.8% against [[lagoon-palm-fan]]'s 89.2% and a 0.72 target, and alpha angular harmonic 32.7% at n=14 against palm-fan's 12.9%. It is taken anyway because it replaces 2026-08-08 OpenAI art in a venue migrating to Gemini, and style fit outranks both.

assets.subject: coconut palm leaning far out sideways, seen from directly above — only the TOP of the tree is visible, never its side. The slim ringed grey-brown trunk runs as one gently curved line from its base in the lower third of the frame up to the crown in the upper third, so trunk and crown together read as a lollipop on a bent stick. ⚠️ THE ACCEPTANCE TEST IS THAT YOU CAN SEE A RUN OF TRUNK, and it is the one thing this picture cannot fake: a palm standing UPRIGHT, seen from straight above, shows no length of trunk at all — just a crown with a hub. So the visible trunk IS the lean, and it must be unmistakable. The crown's centre sits at least a full crown-radius away from the point where the trunk enters the frame, and the trunk runs a clear distance across open ground before it reaches the fronds. If the crown sits centred over its own base with no trunk showing, this is an ordinary upright palm and it is wrong however good the crown is. The crown is a loose spray of long feathered fronds fanning out around the hub, fuller on the far side of the lean and sparser back toward the trunk, each frond one chunky tapering blade of clustered leaflet-mass in two flat greens with soft rounded tips — a sunlit top tone near #6FA61B and a deep shade tone near #2E5408 over a body near #4F8410, the same vivid saturated tropical green as every other palm on this island. ⚠️ IT MUST NOT DRIFT DULL OR COOL: nothing here is dusty, muted, sage, olive, grey-green or washed out. The trunk is a pale grey-brown near #9C8B72, ringed with darker scars. A couple of coconuts at the hub. The trunk's own top surface shows as a narrow lit band along the curve with a darker edge — a line with thickness, not a wire
assets.note: The postcard beach palm — the one shape that says 'tropical island' at race scale, and deliberately NOT radial, so it does NOT take allowSymmetry: the arrangement negatives (rosette, radial symmetry) are doing useful work here, pushing the generator away from collapsing it back into a centred star. Lean direction is toward the TOP of the frame per the class rule (sprite-up = zero heading), so code can aim the lean — over the water, downwind, wherever. ⚠️ anchor trunk-base is OFF-CENTRE by construction (base in the lower third, crown above): check what ingest measures for anchorPx and hand-correct it to the trunk-ground contact point if it defaults to bbox centre — a leaning palm anchored mid-trunk would stand in the water. world 84 is the base-to-crown-edge span, ≈9m at 9.2 units/m. ⚠️ AUDITED 2026-08-16 AND DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE, WHICH IS THE FINDING. The subject is already right: it describes the lean IN PLAN — a ringed trunk running as one curved line from a base in the lower third of the frame to a crown in the upper third, a lollipop on a bent stick, the crown fuller on the far side of the lean and sparser back toward the trunk. That is the positive-evidence pattern that worked on [[lagoon-coral-staghorn]]: a VERTICAL palm seen from overhead shows no trunk length at all, so a visible run of trunk is proof of a lean and is the one thing that cannot be faked from any other camera. ⚠️ THE DELIVERY SIMPLY DID NOT DO IT. Measured, the shipped sprite's ink centroid sits 0.011 of its bbox from centre — indistinguishable from the four palms that are NOT leaning (0.011 to 0.026) — and no trunk runs to any base. It reads as [[lagoon-palm]] with coconuts. So this one wants a REROLL, not a rewrite, and the acceptance test is already written: is there a trunk, and is the crown off-centre from where it starts. ⚠️ planRound STAYS OFF, deliberately. prompt.py's own comment names a leaning palm as the example of an honestly elongated subject; with trunk plus crown this is long, and ORTHO_LONG's parallel-sides test is the correct one for it. Do not add the flag. ⚠️ COLOUR BOUNDED AND THE LEAN MADE MEASURABLE, 2026-08-16. This was the ONLY palm left carrying no hex at all — 'two flat greens', a direction with no floor — and it is also the one queued for a reroll, so it was the worst place in the manifest to leave that defect standing. The same clause shape has now failed twice on this venue: [[lagoon-palm-fan]] came back at saturation 0.22 against a family of 0.94-0.99, and [[lagoon-palm]] came back at 0.70 with dE 8.4-13.4 from its siblings. Bounded to the family palette. THE LEAN NOW HAS AN ACCEPTANCE TEST rather than only a description. The old subject described the lean correctly and in plan, and the delivery still ignored it — shipped ink-centroid offset 0.011, indistinguishable from the four palms that do not lean. So the brief now states the thing that CANNOT be faked, in the pattern that worked on [[lagoon-coral-staghorn]]'s camera-pointing stubs: an upright palm seen from straight above shows NO length of trunk, therefore visible trunk IS the lean, and the crown centre must sit at least one crown-radius from where the trunk enters the frame. That is checkable on delivery by measuring the centroid offset against the four upright palms.

assets.subject: coconut palm seen from directly above — a full crown of feathered fronds radiating from the hub, fronds at plainly uneven lengths and angles, two flat greens with soft rounded tips — a lit tone near #6FA61B, a body near #4F8410 and a deep shade near #2E5408, the vivid saturated green of a healthy coconut palm in full sun. ⚠️ THIS IS THE STERILE PALM OF THE PAIR, AND THAT — NOT DENSITY — IS ITS JOB. It stands beside a fruiting coconut palm of almost the same size, and the thing a player actually reads between them is the MIDDLE: its neighbour shows a pale knot of coconuts and a trunk cross-section at the hub, and this one shows NOTHING THERE — the frond bases meet over the middle, so the centre is ordinary green leaf like the rest of the crown, with no pale knot, no nuts and no trunk disc anywhere in it. ⚠️ THAT IS A STATEMENT ABOUT THE HUB AND NOTHING ELSE. It does not mean the crown is closed or solid; the gaps described below apply across the whole crown, middle included. It is also a little fuller, but that is the lesser difference and it must not be bought by sealing the crown shut. HOW MUCH SHOULD SHOW THROUGH: roughly ONE PART IN FIVE of the crown is dark gap — real openings between and under the fronds where you look straight past the tree to the shadow beneath. ⚠️ THAT IS A LOT MORE OPEN THAN IT SOUNDS: this is a full crown with daylight genuinely coming through it in a dozen places, not a closed one with a few nicks in the rim. Its thinner neighbour shows about one part in four, so this crown is only a LITTLE fuller than that one — a shade denser, not a different order of thing. ⚠️ IF NO GROUND SHOWS THROUGH ANYWHERE IT IS WRONG, and this has already come back sealed shut twice. A crown with no gaps reads as a flat green medallion, a rosette stamped out of card, and the fronds stop being separate leaves. Fronds overlap their neighbours over MUCH of the crown and the hub is buried, but between the outer HALVES of neighbouring fronds there are wide genuine slots of dark — widest where two long fronds diverge, and several smaller ones nearer the middle. Count them: a dozen or more separate openings, not three or four nicks. NO COCONUTS — the fruiting crown is its neighbour's
assets.note: Fourth crown variant, owner-supplied art (2026-08-08): a dense closed crown that matched none of the three authored slots — not coconut-clustered (lagoon-palm), not leaning, not a trunkless tuft — so it got its own slot rather than being forced into the fan-palm slot, which stays open for a genuinely pleated-fan generation. The subject above is written to match the delivered art, not the other way round. ⚠️ SUBJECT PATCHED 2026-08-16, ART NOT REJECTED. At 217 characters this was the shortest world-prop subject in the manifest and it named NO COLOUR AT ALL, relying entirely on the venue clause. It delivered at saturation 0.99, which is the right answer arrived at by luck. Now bounded with hexes. ALSO MADE ITS JOB EXPLICIT: it sits at world 74 beside [[lagoon-palm]] at 70, and the two measure dE 1.6 apart in colour — they are deliberately the same species, so the ONLY thing separating them is density (fill 82.4% against 72.5%) and fruit. The brief now says so, and says the coconuts belong to the other one. ⚠️ AND IT NOW DECLARES planRound, WHICH IS NOT JUST AN INGEST CHECK. prompt.py:593 selects ORTHO_ROUND vs ORTHO_LONG on that flag, so until now every palm crown was being given the LONG subject's acceptance test — 'your two long edges must run parallel for the whole length' — instead of the one that actually catches a tilted camera on a crown, 'the silhouette must be as tall as it is wide'. All four round palms measure 0.91-0.93 aspect, comfortably inside the 1.12 gate, so nothing already shipped is retroactively flagged; the flag pays off on the next roll. ⚠️ DENSITY CLAUSE REWRITTEN 2026-08-17 AFTER A ROLL CAME BACK SEALED SHUT, and the brief asked for exactly that in two places at once: the opening said 'with no gaps, closed and lush' and the density clause said 'there is no gap anywhere you could see ground through'. Two absolutes, and the delivery honoured both. MEASURED, THE USEFUL NUMBER IS NOT FILL BUT SKY-INSIDE-THE-CROWN — the share of the inner 85% of the bounding ellipse that is NOT ink, i.e. what you can actually see through. The roll came back at 2.8%, level with [[lagoon-palm-fan]] at 3.3% and the retiring OpenAI sprite at 3.2%, against [[lagoon-palm]]'s 24.8%. The owner's call is that it should sit between the two and nearer the thin one, so the brief now names ~one part in seven (about 14%) and states the neighbour's one-in-four as the reference. Ellipse fill for the record: 82.9% delivered, 61.8% on lagoon-palm; the target lands near 70%. ⚠️ AN ABSOLUTE IS A BOUND WITH ONLY ONE END, which is the same defect as the unbounded colour comparatives that made [[lagoon-palm-fan]] sage and [[lake-pine-white]] teal — just pointing the other way. 'No gap anywhere' has no floor under it any more than 'cooler than' has. Give density a number and a neighbour to sit between. EVERYTHING ELSE ON THAT ROLL WAS THE BEST IN THE FAMILY and should not be disturbed: alpha angular harmonic 4.9% (family 9.9-33.2%), bbox ratio 1.02 (family 1.02-1.10), saturation 0.82 beside palm-fan's 0.85. This is a density-only reroll. ⚠️ TARGET LOOSENED AGAIN 2026-08-17, SECOND PASS: one part in seven -> ONE PART IN FIVE (about 20% sky inside the crown) on the owner's call after the first loosening still read too dense. Ellipse fill target moves with it, from ~70% to roughly 66-68%. ⚠️ THE HONEST CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED SO IT IS A CHOICE AND NOT A DRIFT: [[lagoon-palm]] sits at 24.8% sky, so at 20% these two coconut palms are about FIVE POINTS apart on the one axis that was supposed to separate them. Density was this asset's stated whole job — 'the difference the player reads is DENSITY' — and five points of sky is not something a player reads at 74 world units. What still separates them is FRUIT: lagoon-palm carries the coconut cluster and the trunk cross-section at its hub, this one carries neither. If the pair ever looks redundant in play, that is why, and the answer is to widen the density gap again or to give this one a different silhouette job — not to add coconuts, which would collapse them completely. ⚠️ ACCEPTED 2026-08-17 ON THE THIRD ROLL, AND THE PAIR'S DIFFERENTIATOR IS FORMALLY MOVED FROM DENSITY TO FRUIT. Delivered: sky inside crown 15.5% against a 20% ask — still a shade denser than requested but close, and every other number is the best or near-best in the family (bbox ratio 1.00, the roundest of all five; alpha angular harmonic 19.4%, mid-family; saturation 0.89, closest to [[lagoon-palm-fan]]'s 0.85). Ellipse fill 67.8%, inside the 66-68% target. ⚠️ THE REASON FOR THE REFRAME IS MEASURED, NOT AESTHETIC. Density was written as this asset's whole job and it never worked: three rolls landed at 2.8%, 2.8% and 15.5% sky against [[lagoon-palm]]'s 24.8%, and even the good one is only 9.2 points away on a continuum nobody reads at 74 world units. What DOES separate them, composited side by side at their real sizes on coral sand, is the hub: non-green core pixels are 3.28% of ink on lagoon-palm (coconuts plus trunk disc) against 0.07% here — effectively a categorical difference, present or absent, which a player can see at a glance where a nine-point density gap cannot be. THE ART FOUND THE BETTER DIFFERENTIATOR BEFORE THE BRIEF DID; the brief now says so. ⚠️ ONE HONEST REALISM CAVEAT, RECORDED BECAUSE IT WAS ASKED. A real coconut palm carries 25-35 fronds in a tight spiral and always shows SOMETHING at the centre — crownshaft, nut cluster, old frond bases. This crown has about twelve fronds and a perfectly clean green middle where they all converge to a point, which is the least realistic thing about it. That is a deliberate consequence of the no-coconuts rule and it is the right trade for this game (the base style asks for storybook clarity over realism), but it is the thing to revisit first if the palm ever looks synthetic in play. KEEPING THE ASSET WAS ALSO A DECISION. Dropping it and remapping its 37 placements to [[lagoon-palm]] was on the table; rejected because the two now read clearly apart at play size, and 69 identical palms would be a worse grove than 69 palms of two kinds. ⚠️ SELF-INFLICTED REGRESSION FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-17. The reframe from density to fruit, written one turn earlier, said the crown was 'unbroken green from RIM TO RIM'. That was meant to say 'no coconuts and no trunk disc at the hub' and it reads as 'NO GAPS ANYWHERE' — the exact absolute deleted two turns before it, reintroduced while fixing something unrelated, and left sitting three sentences from the clause asking for one part in five of open sky. The subject contradicted itself. THE NEXT ROLL DID WHAT THE CONTRADICTION IMPLIED: sky inside crown fell to 8.1% from the accepted 15.4%, and ellipse fill rose to 75.6% from 68.0% — back toward the sealed crowns the whole thread was trying to escape, against a 20% ask. Rejected; roll 3 stays shipped. ⚠️ THE LESSON IS ABOUT EDITING, NOT ABOUT PALMS. A subject is now long enough that a clause added to fix one fault can silently restate a fault removed elsewhere, and the generator will obey whichever is more absolute. THE REASON IS GEOMETRIC, not a wording failure: sky is measured over the inner 85% of the crown, and a rosette of BROAD fronds springing from one point is necessarily solid near that point — the only place gaps can live is the outer band, which cannot supply a fifth of the whole disc on its own. assets.subject: fan palm seen from directly above — a compact crown of large ROUND PLEATED FANS, completely different from a feather palm: each fan is one stiff chunky disc of folded pleats, drawn as alternating lighter and darker wedge facets radiating within the fan like a folded paper fan opened flat, with a bluntly toothed outer edge. Five to seven fans overlap at uneven heights and angles, the upper ones casting one hard flat shade tone onto the ones beneath, so the crown reads as layered plates rather than a single rosette. ⚠️ COLOUR, AND THIS IS THE CLAUSE THE LAST DELIVERY FAILED ON. THIS IS A TROPICAL PALM AND IT IS VIVID. Build the fans from a lit tone near #6FA61B, a body near #4F8410 and a shade near #2E5408 — a strong, saturated, sunlit green. It may be a TOUCH cooler and a TOUCH greyer than the coconut palm beside it, but only a touch, and it must never be less vivid: it stands in the same grove and has to look like the same island. ⚠️ THE FAILURE HAS A NAME: SAGE. The previous brief said only 'a cooler slightly grey-green than a coconut palm' — a direction with no floor — and the delivery went the whole way to a dusty grey-green at saturation 0.22, against 0.92 to 0.99 for every other palm in the game, landing 42 to 47 CIELAB units away from its own siblings. NOTHING HERE IS SAGE, DUSTY, MUTED, CHALKY, PASTEL, OLIVE-GREY OR EUCALYPTUS. If the fan looks like a garden succulent or a dried herb, it is wrong however well the pleats are drawn. At the centre, the stout trunk top just visible in the gaps, wrapped in a rough criss-cross of old leaf bases in warm brown
assets.note: Second lagoon canopy shape — pleated fans against lagoon-palm's feathered blades, so mixed plantings read as two species at a glance even with colour removed. The pleat wedges are exactly the house style's faceted brush planes, which is why a fan palm suits this set better than most foliage. allowSymmetry as with lagoon-palm: each fan is genuinely radial and the crown is a rough rosette of them; the uneven overlap in the subject keeps it organic. world 60 ≈ 6.5m crown — fan palms carry a tighter head than coconuts. ⚠️ SUBJECT'S COLOUR CLAUSE REWRITTEN 2026-08-16. THE GEOMETRY DELIVERED AND THE COLOUR DID NOT, so only the palette changed and the pleated-fan description is untouched. Measured on the delivery: alpha angular harmonic 19.7% at n=4 and radial gradient 1.57 — both INSIDE the family ([[lagoon-palm]] 17.3% / 1.69, palm-dense 9.9% / 1.97, [[ocean-palm-coconut]] 27.4% / 2.03) — with fill 66.5% and interior 81.3% likewise in range. The fans read as discs from overhead and the brown trunk-top shows correctly in the gaps. ⚠️ THE COLOUR CLAUSE WAS AN UNBOUNDED COMPARATIVE AND IT FAILED THE SAME WAY THE WHITE PINE DID. It read, in full, 'Fan colour a cooler slightly grey-green than a coconut palm' — a DIRECTION with no floor. [[lake-pine-white]] carried 'if a green is in doubt push it toward BLUE, never toward yellow' and came back 99.4% teal. This came back at saturation 0.22 where every other palm in the game sits at 0.92-0.99, and dE 41.7-46.7 from its four lagoon siblings — separation that would be excellent between ROLES and is simply wrong inside one grove. A one-way comparative with no bound is now a known defect in this manifest; write both ends or name hexes. ONE THING TO WATCH ON THE NEXT ROLL: content aspect came in at 0.67 against 0.91-0.99 for the sibling palms. The 1.83:1 canvas encourages horizontal sprawl and has done the same to [[lagoon-coral-elkhorn]], [[lagoon-coral-table]] and [[lagoon-coral-bommie]]. ⚠️ ACCEPTED 2026-08-16, COLOUR FIXED ON ONE ROLL. assets.subject: young trunkless palm seen from directly above — a low dense tuft of short arching fronds erupting straight out of the sand from a single point, no trunk visible at all. The fronds are shorter, broader and more upswept than a grown palm's, so from overhead they foreshorten into a compact tuft of stubby chunky blades. ⚠️ NOT A STAR AND NOT A BADGE: the blades are at plainly uneven lengths and angles and several cross over one another, so no viewer could count them or find a regular spacing. COLOUR: a fresh young green, a lit tone near #7ABF1E, a body near #58941A and a shade near #2F5A10. It is a SHADE fresher and a touch more yellow than the mature crowns beside it, and no more than that — it is the same species on the same island and must read as one. ⚠️ NOTHING HERE IS PALE, PASTEL, ACID OR LIME, and it must never be less vivid than a grown palm; the failure to avoid is a washed-out seedling. Two flat tones with soft rounded tips. Frond count and spacing slightly uneven, one blade folded over another, so the tuft reads as a scruffy living plant rather than a geometric badge. A hint of the pale fibrous heart at the very centre
assets.note: The understory scale — scattered between the big palms it breaks up size monotony, and near beaches it reads as dune vegetation. It has not bitten here: measured, this palm sits at hue 92.4 against [[lagoon-palm]]'s 91.4, i.e. the clause moved nothing at all. A clause that does nothing until it goes wrong is worth replacing.
