assets.subject: A BRAIN CORAL, seen straight down. ⚠️ THE CAMERA IS THE WHOLE DIFFICULTY WITH THIS PICTURE, AND THE WORDS 'FROM DIRECTLY ABOVE' HAVE ALREADY FAILED FOUR TIMES ON THIS VENUE. They failed because the rest of the description quietly moved the camera back down again, so read the next two paragraphs as the ones that win any argument. YOU ARE LOOKING STRAIGHT DOWN THROUGH CLEAR WATER at a thing lying on the reef floor. The coral's own UP DIRECTION POINTS AT THE LENS, so you never see the side of anything: no column flank, no plate edge, no dome front, no extruded thickness along a rim, and no foot, stem or base where the coral meets the reef — the base is hidden underneath the coral's own mass. NOTHING IN THIS PICTURE STANDS UP AND NOTHING SITS ON ANYTHING. There is no ground line, no horizon, and no cast shadow falling behind the object. ⚠️ HEIGHT IS NOT A SHAPE HERE. IT IS A TONE. What reaches nearest the surface is PALER and what lies deep is DARKER, and that is the ONLY way height may show. The moment something tall is drawn as tall — a tower, a shelf, a stack, a curving flank, a plate seen edge-on — the camera has moved and the picture is wrong however handsome it is. THE MASS SPREADS ACROSS THE FRAME IN EVERY DIRECTION, including toward the BOTTOM of it. Growth does not head for the top of the picture. What dark there is lies INSIDE the cluster, as narrow water-shadow seams between members. WHAT YOU ACTUALLY SEE IS A ROUGHLY CIRCULAR PATCH FILLED EDGE TO EDGE WITH A MEANDERING MAZE. Brain coral grows as a boulder, and from straight overhead a boulder is a CIRCLE — one heavy, slightly uneven outline, a little lumpy round its edge. Inside it, bold wandering two-tone grooves fill the entire disc: broad rounded ridges separated by deep valleys, turning and doubling back like the paths of a maze, never fine texture and never a fingerprint of concentric rings. ⚠️ THE MAZE COVERS THE WHOLE DISC EVENLY AND DOES NOT WRAP AROUND ANYTHING. The earlier version drew the grooves following the curvature of a dome, so they fanned from a bright far edge near the top of the frame and crowded together toward a near face at the bottom — which is a boulder photographed from a boat. There is no far edge and no near face. The groove pattern must look the same wherever you cover the picture and look at one part of it: same groove width, same spacing, same random wander, from the middle right out to the rim. If the grooves converge anywhere, or radiate from any one place, it is wrong. HEIGHT SHOWS ONLY AS PALLOR. The centre of the boulder is what reaches nearest the surface, so the middle of the disc is washed pale — a soft bloom of cream over the maze, strongest at the centre and fading out well before the rim. The grooves run straight through that pale bloom unchanged. COLOUR: dusty rose-pink, soft and chalky, never hot and never saturated. Ridges near #D4A0A6 over valleys near #8B6470, with the pale centre washing to #F3E3D2. Flat two-tone shading, no gradients, no gloss and no specular highlights. The coral is alone on a transparent background: no water is drawn, no sand is drawn, no other coral.
assets.note: First of the five coral heads — the venue card's promised hazard, and the home of Pearl Lagoon's underwater accent. Destined for the props layer as a seabed-plane hard-contact prop (PROP_KINDS row: plane seabed, contact hard, contactR ~14) — ⚠️ add that row only AFTER ingest delivers the sprite, or its 404 trips test_editor's no-page-errors check, the LAND_TEXTURES lesson. allowSymmetry: a brain dome is genuinely round; the maze keeps it organic. THE FIVE ARE KEPT APART ON TWO AXES AT ONCE — silhouette AND hue, one family each, so no pair blurs at race scale in either colour or greyscale: dome+rose-pink (this) / spikes+lavender / plates+cream / mound-cluster+sage / columns+powder-blue / paddles+apricot — all of them SOFT CHALKY PASTELS, matched to the owner's reference plate, where the coral reads as dusty pink/lavender/cream/green/blue rubble, never jewel-saturated. ⚠️ SUBJECT REWRITTEN 2026-08-16, PERSPECTIVE, AND THIS NOTE CARRIES THE SHARED DIAGNOSIS FOR ALL FOUR. FOUR OF THE SIX LAGOON CORALS CAME BACK IN ELEVATION OR THREE-QUARTER VIEW, AND EVERY ONE OF THE SIX SUBJECTS ALREADY BEGAN 'seen from directly above'. So the camera phrase was never the failure and repeating it louder would not have helped. What separates the two that worked from the four that did not is what the REST of the subject says: [[lagoon-coral-staghorn]] and [[lagoon-coral-bommie]] describe the coral IN PLAN — 'arms radiating outward', 'one mound RINGED BY a clustered skirt', 'the cluster packed uneven' — while pillar, table, elkhorn and brain describe it IN ELEVATION: flanks, shelves, heights, overhangs, a central base, grooves following the curve of a dome. THE DESCRIPTION BEATS THE CAMERA PHRASE. Same shape of failure as [[lake-pine-white]], where 'not a palm' lost to three clauses describing radial plumes. ⚠️ THE RULE THAT FALLS OUT OF IT, AND THE ONE TO WRITE EVERY FUTURE TOP-DOWN SUBJECT AGAINST: HEIGHT MAY BE ENCODED AS TONE AND NEVER AS SHAPE. The two that worked say 'the pale tips are the highest points' and 'the highest central lobes washed pale' — height became a COLOUR. The four that failed made height a SILHOUETTE, and a silhouette of height can only be drawn by moving the camera down. Any clause that lets a viewer see HOW TALL something is has already lost the picture. ⚠️ THERE IS NO SCALAR TEST FOR THIS. Measured across all six: normalised vertical luminance ramp, width profile top/middle/bottom, detail distribution top vs bottom, and aspect all OVERLAP COMPLETELY between the good pair and the bad four (e.g. vRamp/sd runs -0.55..-1.08 on the failures and -0.42..-0.99 on the successes). The difference is semantic — whether vertical faces and a ground relationship are depicted — not statistical. Accept these by LOOKING, against three questions: can you see the side of anything; is there a foot, base or ground line; does the mass reach toward the bottom of the frame as much as the top.

assets.subject: A STAGHORN CORAL THICKET, seen straight down. ⚠️ THE CAMERA IS THE WHOLE DIFFICULTY WITH THIS PICTURE. Four of this venue's six corals came back in elevation or three-quarter view even though every one of them opened with 'seen from directly above' — because the rest of the description quietly moved the camera back down. Read the next two paragraphs as the ones that win any argument. YOU ARE LOOKING STRAIGHT DOWN THROUGH CLEAR WATER at a thing lying on the reef floor. The coral's own UP DIRECTION POINTS AT THE LENS, so you never see the side of anything: no flank, no edge seen edge-on, no extruded thickness along a rim, and no foot, stem or base where the coral meets the reef — the base is hidden underneath the coral's own mass. NOTHING IN THIS PICTURE STANDS UP AND NOTHING SITS ON ANYTHING. No ground line, no horizon, no cast shadow falling behind the object. ⚠️ HEIGHT IS NOT A SHAPE HERE. IT IS A TONE. What reaches nearest the surface is PALER and what lies deep is DARKER, and that is the ONLY way height may show. The moment something tall is drawn as tall — a dome curving away, a column with a length, a lobe seen from the side — the camera has moved and the picture is wrong however handsome it is. THE MASS SPREADS ACROSS THE FRAME IN EVERY DIRECTION, including toward the BOTTOM of it. Growth does not head for the top of the picture. What dark there is lies INSIDE the cluster, as narrow water-shadow seams between members. WHAT YOU ACTUALLY SEE IS A BRISTLING TANGLE OF BRANCHES THROWN OUTWARD ACROSS THE FRAME IN EVERY DIRECTION — left, right, up the picture AND down it, reaching to all four edges. Each branch is a chunky tapering two-tone spike that forks once or twice on its way out. The branches overlap and cross each other in an irregular bristling mass. ⚠️ THE BRANCH ENDS ARE BLUNT, NOT SHARP, and this is the correction that matters most after the camera. Real staghorn is a cluster of CYLINDRICAL rods with ROUNDED growing tips — an arm is a finger, not a dagger. An earlier version of this brief called the silhouette 'ALL POINTS, unmistakably sharp', and that phrase produces flat tapering BLADES lying in the picture plane, which is a snowflake and not a coral. The menace of this head comes from the DENSITY of the tangle and the black gaps you can fall into, never from needle tips. The arms are clearly uneven — some long, some stubby, no two alike, and the whole thicket is lopsided. ⚠️ IT IS NOT AN ANTLER AND NOT A TROPHY ON A WALL. The word looks like an invitation to draw a stag's antler, and a viewer has only ever seen one of those mounted, seen from the front, growing upward from a plaque. That picture is refused: the same metaphor is what sank this coral's neighbour the elkhorn. There is no plaque, no upward, and no front. ⚠️ SOME BRANCHES POINT STRAIGHT AT YOU, AND THAT IS THE TELL THIS PICTURE MOST NEEDS. A thicket grows upward as well as outward, so from overhead a share of the branches are aimed at the lens and are drawn FORESHORTENED TO ALMOST NOTHING — short blunt stubs and small rounded ends scattered through the middle of the tangle, not long spikes. Four or five such stubs, sitting among the long arms rather than ringed around them. A thicket drawn with every branch full-length lying flat is a thicket seen from the side. THE CENTRE IS BURIED. Where the branches converge they pile over one another, so you cannot see the trunk, the holdfast, or where this coral meets the reef. Between and under the arms you look straight down into deep dark water-shadow gaps. HEIGHT SHOWS ONLY AS PALLOR: the growing tips reach nearest the surface, so every branch end is washed pale lilac while the arms darken toward the buried middle. COLOUR: dusty lavender, soft and chalky. Body near #7C6F9E, tips washed to #C9BEDD, the shadow gaps near #221C33. It is the one PURPLE head of the six. Flat two-tone shading, no gradients, no gloss and no specular highlights. The coral is alone on a transparent background: no water is drawn, no sand is drawn, no other coral.
assets.note: The spiky one — sharpest silhouette of the five, the hazard role's 'aggressive, spiky' read taken literally. No allowSymmetry: the arrangement negatives are load-bearing against a radial antler rosette. Same prop wiring plan and same 404 caution as lagoon-coral-brain. ⚠️ SUBJECT REWRITTEN 2026-08-16 WITHOUT REJECTING THE ART, which stays `art` and is not being redrawn. Like [[lagoon-coral-bommie]] this was one of the two that delivered a correct overhead view, and like it the brief never forbade an elevation. It carried the live word outright: 'branching ANTLER-LIKE arms'. [[lagoon-coral-elkhorn]] said 'branches like a MOOSE'S ANTLERS' and came back as a flat cut-out standing on a foot, because the only antler most viewers have seen is mounted on a wall. This one escaped because 'radiating outward' and 'the pale tips are the highest points' pulled harder. Rolling it again would be a coin toss, so the metaphor is now refused by name. ⚠️ THE FORESHORTENED-STUB CLAUSE IS THE REAL ADDITION and it is worth reusing on any branching subject. A branching thing seen from overhead must show some branches pointing AT the camera, drawn as blunt stubs — that single feature is impossible to draw from a side view and is therefore the cheapest positive proof of an overhead camera. Every other rule in this brief is a prohibition; this one asks for evidence. ⚠️ REDRAWN AND ACCEPTED 2026-08-16 from two candidates, and the pair settled a question the numbers could not. Both candidates passed every perspective basic identically — bright vertical -0.03 on each, mass balanced 0.46/0.47, colour #7D6F94 and #786E9B against a #7C6F9E spec. Three separate metrics failed to discriminate them: perimeter compactness is not comparable between a 2816px master and a 208px sprite; and inner-versus-outer branch width (7.03 vs 5.31) is confounded by branches simply piling up where they converge. WHAT DECIDED IT WAS CROPPING THE MIDDLE OF EACH AND LOOKING. The accepted candidate's centre is full of BLUNT CYLINDERS WITH ROUNDED PALE CAPS AIMED AT THE LENS — a dozen of them, the foreshortened-stub clause delivered literally. The rejected one has not a single branch pointing at the camera: every arm is a flat blade tapering to a point, lying in the picture plane, reading as an ice crystal. That clause remains the cheapest positive proof of an overhead camera precisely because it CANNOT be drawn from a side view. ⚠️ AND THE BRIEF ITSELF WAS PART OF THE PROBLEM, so it has been corrected here. Both candidates came from the same subject, which still carried 'the silhouette is ALL POINTS, unmistakably sharp' inherited from the original — a phrase that pulls straight toward the flat-blade snowflake, and which is also WRONG FOR THE SPECIES: Acropora cervicornis is a cluster of cylindrical rods with rounded growing tips. A brief that can produce both answers is a coin toss, so the sharpness clause is replaced by an explicit blunt-cylinder rule and the menace is moved onto the density of the tangle. Status stays `art`.

WHAT YOU ACTUALLY SEE IS A CROWD OF ROUNDED LOBES PACKED INTO ONE RAGGED PATCH — the biggest and most cluttered head in the lagoon, a reef in miniature. Big soft lobes fill the middle of the patch and smaller knobs and stubby nubs crowd in around them all the way out to a deeply lumpy edge. The members are every size, packed unevenly, some touching and some overlapping. The outline is bumpy and irregular but NEVER SPIKY — that is what separates it from its neighbour the staghorn. ⚠️ IT IS NOT A DOME AND YOU CANNOT SEE THAT IT IS TALL. The word 'bommie' means a coral boulder standing proud of the reef, and every photograph of one is taken from the side or from a diver's eye. That picture is refused. From straight overhead a bommie is a COBBLESTONE PATCH: a flat crowd of rounded shapes, like a bag of potatoes tipped out and photographed from the ceiling. No lobe curves away from you; no lobe shows its side. HEIGHT SHOWS ONLY AS PALLOR, and this is where the picture earns its shape. The lobes in the MIDDLE of the patch are the ones nearest the surface, so they are washed palest; the knobs around the rim sit deeper and are a shade or two darker. That gradient from pale centre to darker rim is the ONLY thing saying this coral is a boulder. Do not draw the boulder. COLOUR: soft sage and sea-green throughout — the GREEN head of the six, a chalky pastel green, with NO red and NO purple anywhere on it. Body near #7FA679, the central lobes washed pale to #C8DCBE, the seams between members near #2C4433. Two or three small flecks of dusty pink sit among the palest central lobes and nowhere else. Flat two-tone shading, no gradients, no gloss and no specular highlights. The coral is alone on a transparent background: no water is drawn, no sand is drawn, no other coral.
assets.note: The big mound-cluster — the generic 'coral head' a course designer reaches for first. Olive is its whole hue family (the one green thing among the five; the pink flecks stay small enough not to blur it toward the table coral). Largest world of the five at 56 (~6m). No allowSymmetry: a skirt of knobs must not come back as a rosette. Same prop wiring plan and 404 caution as lagoon-coral-brain. ⚠️ SUBJECT REWRITTEN 2026-08-16 WITHOUT REJECTING THE ART, which stays `art` and is not being redrawn. This brief was one of only two of the six that delivered a correct overhead view, and the rewrite exists because it did so BY LUCK. It never forbade an elevation, and it carried three elevation words — 'one heavy central MOUND', 'ringed by a clustered SKIRT', 'flecks of dusty pink at the CROWN'. A mound read as a dome is exactly what sank [[lagoon-coral-brain]]. What saved this one is that its other language was plan-view ('ringed by', 'the cluster packed uneven') and that it already encoded height as tone ('the highest central lobes washed pale') — the rule the whole set is now written against. The rewrite keeps that rule and makes it explicit, replaces the mound with a cobblestone patch, and names the dome as the refused picture. See [[lagoon-coral-brain]] for the shared diagnosis and for why there is no scalar test for this. ⚠️ REDRAWN AND ACCEPTED 2026-08-16 AGAINST THE REWRITTEN BRIEF, chosen from two candidates, and the pair is worth recording because they show the brief working and not working side by side. The rejected candidate measured core-to-rim L* drop +27.0 with its bright pixels at radius 0.60 and vertical -0.30 — pallor sitting UP AND OUT, which is the elevation signature, and near-identical to the sprite it would have replaced (+42.0, 0.54, -0.26). The accepted one measures drop +73.8 with bright pixels at radius 0.37 and vertical -0.09: pallor in the MIDDLE, grading down to the rim, which is the height-is-a-tone rule doing its job. Mass balances 0.51 above/below centre. ⚠️ IT COST SATURATION AND THAT IS A REAL REGRESSION, recorded rather than hidden. The head went #699D60 sat 0.50 -> #88A186 sat 0.20, so the 'GREEN head of the six' is now a grey-green, and its nearest neighbour tightened from dE 39.0 to 24.3 (against [[lagoon-coral-table]]). Accepted because 24.3 is in line with the set — the closest existing pair is brain/elkhorn at 23.7 — because the two differ 56u against 48u in size, and because within one ROLE species separation is secondary (art-pipeline.md §2 governs roles, not species; see [[lake-pine-white]] for where over-separating species inside a role did real damage). If it is ever rolled again, ask for the same geometry at the old saturation. ALSO WIDER THAN THE SET: content h/w 0.54 against the shipped range 0.66-1.03. The 1.83:1 canvas encourages horizontal sprawl and [[lagoon-coral-elkhorn]] and [[lagoon-coral-table]] came in at 0.53 and 0.52 the same way. Worth a canvas note next time rather than a reroll.

assets.subject: A CLUSTER OF PILLAR CORAL, seen straight down. ⚠️ THE CAMERA IS THE WHOLE DIFFICULTY WITH THIS PICTURE, AND THE WORDS 'FROM DIRECTLY ABOVE' HAVE ALREADY FAILED FOUR TIMES ON THIS VENUE. They failed because the rest of the description quietly moved the camera back down again, so read the next two paragraphs as the ones that win any argument. YOU ARE LOOKING STRAIGHT DOWN THROUGH CLEAR WATER at a thing lying on the reef floor. The coral's own UP DIRECTION POINTS AT THE LENS, so you never see the side of anything: no column flank, no plate edge, no dome front, no extruded thickness along a rim, and no foot, stem or base where the coral meets the reef — the base is hidden underneath the coral's own mass. NOTHING IN THIS PICTURE STANDS UP AND NOTHING SITS ON ANYTHING. There is no ground line, no horizon, and no cast shadow falling behind the object. ⚠️ HEIGHT IS NOT A SHAPE HERE. IT IS A TONE. What reaches nearest the surface is PALER and what lies deep is DARKER, and that is the ONLY way height may show. The moment something tall is drawn as tall — a tower, a shelf, a stack, a curving flank, a plate seen edge-on — the camera has moved and the picture is wrong however handsome it is. THE MASS SPREADS ACROSS THE FRAME IN EVERY DIRECTION, including toward the BOTTOM of it. Growth does not head for the top of the picture. What dark there is lies INSIDE the cluster, as narrow water-shadow seams between members. WHAT YOU ACTUALLY SEE IS A HANDFUL OF CIRCLES PACKED TOGETHER. Pillar coral grows as stout columns, and from straight overhead a column is a ROUNDED KNOBBY DISC and nothing more — you are looking down the barrel of it. Draw five to seven such discs, touching and overlapping, of clearly different sizes, arranged loose and lopsided and never in a ring. Each disc has a soft lumpy edge, like the end of a well-worn post. ⚠️ NO SHAFTS. The earlier version of this picture drew the tops as ellipses with long vertical columns descending below them, which is a photograph taken from a boat, not from overhead. There is no length to any of these columns in this picture. If a viewer can see how TALL a column is, it is wrong. THE DARK BETWEEN THE DISCS IS THE DEPTH. Where the columns do not touch, the gap drops away into near-black water — narrow, sharp-edged crevices threading between the discs, widest where three columns meet. That black is what tells a player this is a cluster of separate towers without ever showing one. COLOUR: powder blue, a soft chalky slate-blue, clearly the COOLEST head in the lagoon — nothing here is green, warm or bright. Body near #7E9DBF, with the discs that reach nearest the surface washed toward a near-white #DDE8F2, and the crevices near #1E2C3A. The palest disc is not in the middle; put it off to one side. Flat two-tone shading, no gradients, no gloss and no specular highlights. The coral is alone on a transparent background: no water is drawn, no sand is drawn, no other coral.
assets.note: The columns — reads as depth where the others read as spread. Powder-blue is the risky family (it borders the water it sits in), so the near-white crowns and the near-black shadow gaps carry the contrast, which is also exactly what the hazard clause demands over both pale turquoise and night water. Smallest of the five. No allowSymmetry: 'never a ring' in the subject plus the arrangement negatives hold the cluster irregular. Same prop wiring plan and 404 caution as lagoon-coral-brain. ⚠️ SUBJECT REWRITTEN 2026-08-16, PERSPECTIVE. Delivered in three-quarter view: circular column tops drawn as foreshortened ellipses with long vertical shafts running down from them. The subject asked for exactly that without meaning to — 'stout columns RISING TOWARD THE SURFACE', 'a fistful of towers REACHING UP AT THE VIEWER', and worst of all 'each crown paler than its FLANKS'. A flank is a side. The brief opened with 'seen from directly above' and then spent three clauses describing an elevation, and the description won. See [[lagoon-coral-brain]] for the shared diagnosis and the height-is-a-tone rule.

They failed because the rest of the description quietly moved the camera back down again, so read the next two paragraphs as the ones that win any argument. YOU ARE LOOKING STRAIGHT DOWN THROUGH CLEAR WATER at a thing lying on the reef floor. The coral's own UP DIRECTION POINTS AT THE LENS, so you never see the side of anything: no column flank, no plate edge, no dome front, no extruded thickness along a rim, and no foot, stem or base where the coral meets the reef — the base is hidden underneath the coral's own mass. What reaches nearest the surface is PALER and what lies deep is DARKER, and that is the ONLY way height may show. The moment something tall is drawn as tall — a tower, a shelf, a stack, a curving flank, a plate seen edge-on — the camera has moved and the picture is wrong however handsome it is. THE MASS SPREADS ACROSS THE FRAME IN EVERY DIRECTION, including toward the BOTTOM of it. Growth does not head for the top of the picture. WHAT YOU ACTUALLY SEE IS A SPRAWL OF BROAD FLAT PADDLES REACHING OUTWARD ACROSS THE FRAME IN EVERY DIRECTION — left, right, up the picture AND down it, the way a hand of splayed fingers looks when you photograph it flat on a table. Three to five paddles, each a wide flattened blade with a rounded lobed end, clearly unequal in length so the whole thing is lopsided. If the picture would still make sense as something hanging on a wall, it is wrong. THE GAPS ARE OPEN WATER. Between the paddles you see straight down to nothing — deep irregular wedges of near-black, wider than the paddles in places. COLOUR: dusty apricot orange, the one WARM head in the lagoon, soft and chalky. Body near #D9895E with the paddle ends and the highest surfaces washed pale peach #F2C4A4, and the water-shadow between paddles near #2A1B14. Never neon, never brown. assets.note: The sixth head, and the warm one — the paddle silhouette is the family the first five do not cover (broad flat radiating arms, against thin sharp spikes / solid discs / dome / mound / columns), and apricot-orange is elkhorn's true colour, kept chalky to sit in the set's pastel register. No allowSymmetry: 'never a symmetric star' plus the arrangement negatives keep the hand lopsided. Same prop wiring plan (plane seabed, contact hard) and same add-PROP_KINDS-only-after-ingest caution as lagoon-coral-brain. ⚠️ SUBJECT REWRITTEN 2026-08-16, PERSPECTIVE. Delivered as a flat sticker seen face-on: branches spreading left, right and up but never DOWN the frame, a 2.5D bevel along the lower edges, and a small base at bottom centre where it stood. Two phrases did it — 'branches like a MOOSE'S ANTLERS', which is a side-view metaphor a viewer has only ever seen mounted on a wall, and 'radiating from a CENTRAL BASE', which asks for a visible foot. The rewrite buries the centre under its own paddles and demands mass reaching toward the BOTTOM of the frame, which is the single easiest tell of a true overhead view. See [[lagoon-coral-brain]].

assets.subject: Dry white Caribbean coral sand seen from directly overhead from about ten metres up, in flat even light — the pale near-white sand of a coral atoll beach, ground from coral and shell rather than rock. AT THIS HEIGHT SAND IS ALMOST FEATURELESS, and that is the subject: a quiet, near-uniform field whose only structure is broad, soft, irregular patches of very slightly different tone, each blending into its neighbours with no hard edge. A few of the patches carry the faintest warm blush of pink-cream, the ghost of ground coral, never a saturated pink. NO RIPPLES OF ANY KIND: no crests, no ridges, no parallel lines, no repeating waves, nothing lining up with anything else, no spacing that repeats. Scattered thinly through it, the only hard marks in the frame: a few tiny shell chips and coral fragments in off-white and the palest coral pink, each drawn as a small shaped mark, never as fine speckle or grain, plus the very occasional single dark fleck. The whole image holds a very narrow pale range from #e2d4b2 to #f5ecd8 around a mean of #ecdfc2 — a warm cream, clearly LIGHTER than ordinary tan beach sand, but never pure white and never grey. No water, no foam, no wet sand, no waterline, no vegetation, no seaweed, no driftwood, no dune, no rocks larger than a chip, no cast shadows, no footprints, no tracks, no raked pattern, no sand ripple
assets.note: Pearl Lagoon's own sand — a NEW look ('coralsand'), deliberately paler than the shared `tropical` bay-sand (#ddc39a mean) so lagoon beaches read as cream against every other venue's tan. RETARGETED 2026-08-08 to #ecdfc2 (warm cream, was near-white #efe6d5) when the venue's four-step colour ladder was matched to the owner's reference plate — the ISLAND_STYLES.coralsand body already sits at the new mean. Authored to the bay-sand v2 lessons wholesale: structure-at-altitude first (near-featureless, broad tonal drift, shaped marks only), tileWorld 128 so shell chips land at true size (~5cm median at 9.2 units/m), and WHEN WIRING set the new ISLAND_STYLES body to the DELIVERED TILE'S OWN MEAN, not to the #efe6d5 the subject asks for — with base equal to tile mean, alpha stays a pure contrast knob (the property that retired the arctic textures' luma-shift warning). The pink blush is held to the faintest cast on purpose: the venue clause excludes lagoon accents (coral pinks) from ground, and a pink beach would spend the accent that belongs to the underwater props. Value range is snow-tile territory — check contrast on the grid against ice, which is the nearest neighbour in value.

assets.subject: Wet bayou mud seen from directly overhead from about ten metres up, in flat even light — the dark olive-brown mud of a southern swamp bank, smooth and heavy. AT THIS HEIGHT MUD IS ALMOST FEATURELESS, and that is the subject: a quiet field whose only structure is broad, soft, irregular patches of slightly different tone — darker where the mud lies wetter, a shade lighter where it has begun to dry — each patch blending into its neighbours with no hard edge. EVERY SURFACE IS MATTE: wet mud here is dark, never shiny, with no sheen, no highlights and no reflections. NO CRACKS — this is soft wet swamp mud, not a dried lakebed, so no crack network, no polygonal plates, no curling edges. Scattered thinly through it, the only hard marks in the frame: a sparse fall of leaf litter — small dark dead leaves and a few short twig fragments in browns barely darker or lighter than the mud — each drawn as a small shaped mark, never as speckle. The whole image holds a narrow dark range from #4e4636 to #665c48 around a mean of #5a5140 — a heavy olive-brown, never orange, never grey, never black. No water, no puddles, no standing water, no reflections, no footprints, no animal tracks, no tire ruts, no vegetation growing, no grass, no roots, no rocks, no cast shadows
assets.note: Gatorgrass Bayou's bank and bar material — a new 'mud' look for the swamp's low ground, where the venue's islands stop being generic grass. Same altitude discipline as bay-sand v2: the honest answer for smooth mud at 10m is broad wet/dry tonal drift plus a thin scatter of shaped leaf litter, so that is all the subject asks for. NO CRACKS is stated twice over because generators equate mud with dried-earth crack networks, which are the wrong material (dry lakebed) AND a countable stamped feature at tile repeat. tileWorld 128 puts leaves at true size like the sand's shell chips. Wiring is the same recipe as the others: ISLAND_STYLES body = delivered tile's mean, LAND_TEXTURES entry keyed to the new style, alpha as pure contrast knob — start near sand's 0.7 and tune on looks; the mud's mottle is soft like sand v2, not busy like the arctic pair. DELIVERED 2026-08-09 at mean #524731 (spec asked #5a5140) with a p5-p95 of #4d432e..#584b34 — darker and warmer than spec, and MUCH flatter: luma sd 2.20 at tile scale against sand's 3.93, so it is the quietest tile in the set and its alpha has room only upward. Litter measured 18px median / 48px p95 in the 1024 master = 25cm/65cm at tileWorld 128, i.e. ~2x life size; kept anyway because the marks are 2.2px median ON SCREEN and halving the tile to fix the size would dissolve every one of them. Wrap checked: seam-to-interior gradient ratio 1.98/1.50, inside the shipped set's 1.67-2.54.

assets.subject: Bare wind-worn sandstone seen from directly overhead from about ten metres up, in flat even light — the orange-rust stone of a desert canyon rim, smooth and dry. AT THIS HEIGHT THE STONE IS NEARLY FEATURELESS, and that is the subject: broad, soft, irregular drifts of slightly different tone where wind has polished and stained the rock, each blending into its neighbours with no hard edge. Through them run a few SHORT STRATA FRAGMENTS — gently curved bands of slightly darker and slightly lighter stone, each fading out within a third of the frame, at scattered angles, never straight, never crossing the whole image, never lining up with the frame edges or with each other — and two or three short hairline fractures drawn as shaped dark lines that also fade out. A thin scatter of small rounded stone chips, each a shaped mark, never speckle or photographic grit. The whole image holds a narrow warm range from #a85a30 to #d98a52 around a mean of #c2703e — saturated orange-rust, never brown-grey, never pink, never yellow. No vegetation, no sand, no dunes, no cracked-earth polygon network, no cast shadows, no full-width strata banding, no water staining
assets.note: Redrock Reservoir's ground — the canyon rim rock the venue is named for, targeting ISLAND_STYLES.redrock.body (#c2703e) exactly so wiring is the standard recipe (LAND_TEXTURES.redrock, body = delivered tile's mean, alpha from ~0.3 like the arctic pair — rock reads at lower contrast than sand). tileWorld 256, the granite precedent: the redrock shapes are canyon-wall scale, and 256 buys 4x supersample for the strata fragments. THE STRATA ARE FRAGMENTS ON PURPOSE: real strata run for kilometres, but a band crossing the whole tile repeats as the most countable feature a texture can have — the same reason bay-sand v1's ripples died. Short fading arcs carry the sedimentary read without the tiling tell.

assets.subject: A closed sward of fresh meadow grass seen from directly overhead from about ten metres up, in flat even light — bright healthy green turf growing so dense that no ground shows anywhere. AT THIS HEIGHT INDIVIDUAL BLADES DO NOT RESOLVE, and that is the subject: the sward reads as a soft, even, clumpy mottle — rounded tussock crowns a shade lighter where the grass mounds up, narrow sinks a shade darker between them — every clump blending into its neighbours with no hard edge, at roughly the same density everywhere. The clumps LEAN NO PARTICULAR WAY: no combed direction, no mowing stripes, no swirls, no rows, nothing lining up with the frame or with itself, no spacing that repeats. A few broader drifts of slightly deeper and slightly fresher green move through at the largest scale, soft and wide. The whole image holds a narrow mid range from #74a03e to #97c261 around a mean of #84b14e — fresh and clearly GREEN, never olive, never yellow, never emerald-dark. No visible soil, no flowers, no clover patches, no individual drawn blades, no fine hairline strokes, no paths, no tracks, no footprints
assets.note: The bright meadow look ('grass' style) — VENUE-LESS on purpose, like the mark: this ground is shared by every venue with a grass isle (the strait's islets, the lake's banks, one day Duckling Pond's lawn), so a single venue's palette clause would mislead the generator. Same altitude discipline and tussock-mottle structure as bayou-swampgrass; the two swards differ ONLY in colour, which is exactly the grass/swampgrass style split (2026-08-08: grass brightened to #84b14e, the old tan-olive moved to the swampgrass style). Wiring recipe as always: LAND_TEXTURES.grass entry when the art lands, ISLAND_STYLES.grass.body reset to the delivered tile's mean, alpha as pure contrast knob starting near 0.7.

assets.subject: A closed sward of swamp sawgrass seen from directly overhead from about ten metres up, in flat even light — the olive and yellow-green grass the bayou is named for, growing so dense that no ground shows anywhere. AT THIS HEIGHT INDIVIDUAL BLADES DO NOT RESOLVE, and that is the subject: the sward reads as a soft, even, clumpy mottle — rounded tussock crowns a shade lighter where the grass mounds up, narrow sinks a shade darker between them — every clump blending into its neighbours with no hard edge, at roughly the same density everywhere. The clumps LEAN NO PARTICULAR WAY: no combed direction, no swirls, no parallel streaks, no rows, nothing lining up with the frame or with itself, no spacing that repeats. A few slightly yellower dried patches and a few deeper olive hollows drift through at the largest scale, soft and broad. The whole image holds a narrow mid range from #97895a to #b9ad7c around a mean of #a89b6a — dry sun-cured tan-olive, straw over green, never emerald, never lime, never brown enough to read as earth. No visible soil, no mud, no water, no standing water, no reeds, no cattail heads, no flowers, no individual drawn blades, no fine hairline strokes, no paths, no tracks, no footprints
assets.note: The swamp's VEGETATED ground — hummock and island tops, closing the set the swamp's low ground opened: swampgrass (closed sward) / marsh (broken) / mud (bare). Altitude discipline per bay-sand v2: blades do not resolve at 10m, so the honest structure is tussock mottle, and the subject bans directional combing for the same reason bay-sand v1's ripples died — one dominant direction repeats as banding at tile scale. RETARGETED 2026-08-08 to mean #a89b6a: the 'swampgrass' STYLE now exists (ISLAND_STYLES) and carries the tan-olive the global grass used to be — this tile is its texture, so it targets that style's body exactly; the note that once warned against wiring onto the global grass look is resolved by the split (grass went bright meadow green and has its own venue-less `grass` tile). Wire as LAND_TEXTURES.swampgrass, body = delivered tile's mean.

assets.subject: Broken marsh ground seen from directly overhead from about ten metres up, in flat even light — the ragged edge where a swamp's grass gives out into mud: scattered rounded clumps of olive and yellow-green sedge sitting on dark wet olive-brown mud, roughly half and half, so neither material dominates. THE CLUMPS ARE THE ONLY STRUCTURE: each is a soft rounded tussock a shade lighter at its crown, with the bare mud showing as irregular dark channels and openings between them. Clump sizes vary and their spacing is uneven and unaligned — no rows, no rings, no even scatter, no spacing that repeats, nothing lining up with the frame. The mud between them is smooth and matte with only broad soft tonal drift, no shine and no reflections. Grass tones hold #8a8246 to #b6a660 and mud tones hold #4d432e to #584b34, so the image runs one straw-olive-over-mud family and the value step between clump and mud stays gentle. No open water, no puddles, no reflections, no cracks in the mud, no reeds standing tall, no cattail heads, no flowers, no individual drawn blades, no paths, no tracks, no footprints, no rocks
assets.note: The TRANSITION material — half swampgrass, half mud, for the wide soft margins where bayou islands meet the channels, so the game's three swamp grounds grade into each other instead of butting: swampgrass sward -> marsh -> bare mud -> water. Its two colour ranges are QUOTED FROM ITS NEIGHBOURS' subjects verbatim, which is what makes a three-tile gradient read as one place; if either neighbour's delivered mean drifts from its spec, re-anchor this tile to the delivered values before generating it (generate this one LAST). The even-scatter risk is highest here of the three — clumps-on-ground is exactly what diffusion models regularise into polka dots — hence the stacked unevenness clauses; check the repeat at 3x3 before accepting. Same wiring recipe, own style key (e.g. 'marsh'). RE-ANCHORED 2026-08-09: both neighbours have now shipped and both came in darker than spec (swampgrass mean #a09454 vs #a89b6a, mud #524731 vs #5a5140), so the two quoted ranges above are no longer the specs — they are the DELIVERED p5-p95 of swamp/swampgrass.png and swamp/mud.png, which is what this tile's 'quoted from its neighbours verbatim' rule actually means. Note how narrow the mud range now is (11 luma against the spec's 22): the delivered mud is far flatter than specced, so the value step between clump and mud in this tile has to come from the GRASS side. ISLAND_STYLES.marsh was re-averaged onto the same two delivered means (#796e42). DELIVERED 2026-08-09 at mean #685c37, and it SPLIT: judged by phase, the mud half is a hit and the sedge half is a miss. Thresholding the tile by luma gives a dark phase of #594f32 against the delivered bank's #524731 — 7 luma, so the mud genuinely reads as the same material continuing, which is the whole point of quoting a neighbour's range. The light phase came back #7e6f3d against the sward's #a09454, 35 luma DARK, so the clumps do not read as that sawgrass thinning out. Net: the ladder runs 145 -> 92 -> 72 in luma where an even grade wants the middle at 108, i.e. the transition sits 17 luma mud-side and the swampgrass->marsh step is much bigger than the marsh->mud one. Clump coverage is 41%, under the 'roughly half and half' asked for, which is the same finding from the other direction. IF REGENERATED, change ONE thing: restate the grass tones (#8a8246..#b6a660) as the tones the CLUMPS THEMSELVES must hold, since quoting the range alone was read as a ceiling to sit under, and leave the mud clause exactly as it is. The flagged even-scatter risk did NOT materialise: dominant grain by radially averaged power spectrum is 128px in the master against swampgrass's and mud's 171px, so it is the finest of the four grounds and in family. Blob-counting says the opposite (clumps 2.4x swampgrass's) and is WRONG — it compares discrete clumps to a connected sward. Wrap 2.17/2.10 after ingest's wrap_resize, from 2.57/2.50 delivered; vignette +0.01, the flattest in the set. Shipped at alpha 0.4 rather than the pre-registered 0.5: sd 16.17 at tile scale against swampgrass's 10.21 would have made it the loudest ground in the game.

assets.subject: An inflatable racing mark floating on open water, seen from DIRECTLY OVERHEAD — looking straight down onto it from a helicopter, with none of its side or bottom rim visible anywhere, not even at the near edge. THINK OF IT AS A LOW THREE-SIDED PYRAMID, not a flat cushion. It is a squat tetrahedron: a rounded triangular base with three big triangular faces that SLOPE UPWARD and inward to meet at a single blunt apex directly above the centre. Seen from above you are looking down at those three sloping faces, and the three ridges where they meet run from the central apex out to the three rounded corners, forming a clean three-spoke Y. A bold dark lifting ring sits on the apex at the centre — make it a solid, chunky ring, not a hairline, because it is the one focal dot. THREE FACES, THREE CLEARLY DIFFERENT VALUES — this is the hardest requirement and the whole point of the pyramid form. Because each face tilts in a different direction, each catches the single light source differently. Render them as roughly 100%, 75% and 50% brightness: one face bright, one clearly mid, one clearly dark, with a hard crisp edge along every ridge. The engine desaturates inactive marks to flat slate grey for most of the race, so hue differences are worthless — CONVERTED TO GREYSCALE the three faces, the Y-ridge and the centre ring must all still read instantly. A mark that is one even tone with faint seams is a failure. COLOUR: true safety orange, warm and mid-bright, not red and not scarlet. Flat poster-like colour within each face — absolutely no gloss, no shine, no specular highlight, no smooth gradient, no plastic sheen. A narrow band of deeper wetter orange runs around the very bottom edge where the fabric meets the water. ROTATION: placed at an arbitrary angle with no 'up' — the three faces, ridges and corners must be identical in size and shape so the three-fold symmetry looks deliberate however it is turned, and the apex must sit at the exact centre of the frame. assets.subject: A RED LIGHTED STEEL CHANNEL BUOY floating on open water, seen from DIRECTLY OVERHEAD. COLOUR: the buoy's red is canonical buoyage and carries navigational information, so it must be matched and must NOT be shifted toward the surrounding water's hue — a deep warm signal red around #BB3220, never scarlet, never orange, never pink, never maroon. The green buoy is this same object in green and the two must be drawn the same way — same proportions, same light direction, same facet treatment — because they stand either side of one channel and a player reads them as a PAIR. THE SHAPE OF THIS WHOLE PICTURE IS A CIRCLE, AND THAT IS THE FIRST THING TO GET RIGHT. The buoy's round steel FLOAT is the widest part of it and the entire silhouette: a full solid disc in the buoy's colour, filling the frame. Everything else in the picture sits ON that disc and INSIDE its outline. If the finished image is square, or is an open framework with gaps at its outer edge, or has no disc under it at all, it is wrong however good it looks — that is a bare tower with its float missing, not a buoy. ON TOP OF THE DISC, AN OPEN SQUARE LATTICE TOWER, and it is the buoy's identity: thick welded steel members forming a bold square frame with one rail crossing the middle each way, so the pattern is FOUR OPENINGS IN A TWO-BY-TWO GRID and nothing finer. THE TOWER NEVER REACHES THE EDGE OF THE DISC. It spans about three-fifths of the disc's width and sits square to the frame, which leaves a clear unbroken RING OF BARE DECK about one-fifth of the disc wide on every side of it — that ring of plain colour between the tower and the rim is as important as the tower itself, and it is what makes the object read as a structure standing on a float rather than as a grille filling a circle. Judge it on the OPENINGS: the four dark squares taken together should span a little under HALF the disc's width. If they reach two-thirds of the way across, the tower is too big and the ring has been squeezed out. THROUGH THE FOUR OPENINGS YOU SEE STRAIGHT DOWN to the deck below, in deep shadow — four dark square windows, the darkest thing in the picture apart from the lamp, each a flat hard-edged shape with nothing drawn inside it. Those dark squares against the bright deck are what make this buoy findable at a distance, so keep them clean and keep them dark. AT THE EXACT CENTRE, THE LANTERN: a small pale cylindrical housing ringed around a DARK lens cap, with a tiny bright finial dot at the very top. The dark cap is the one focal point of the whole sprite. SEEN FROM DIRECTLY OVERHEAD, NONE OF THE BUOY'S SIDE IS VISIBLE, and on a lattice this is the easiest thing in the world to get wrong. You are looking down the tower, not at it. A vertical corner post shows ONLY its small flat top face — never its length, never a side face, never a box drawn in three dimensions. No diagonal cross-bracing is visible anywhere, because bracing runs down the tower's sides and the sides do not exist in this picture. No part of the float's rim shows its thickness. Every part of the buoy is the same distance from the camera. IT MUST STILL READ IN GREYSCALE. A buoy seen from above has almost no silhouette to read by — it is a disc — so the STRUCTURE has to live in flat steps of lightness: bright deck, darker tower members, near-black openings, pale lamp housing, dark cap. Each is a flat hard-edged shape of clearly different value, and the whole thing must still make complete sense with the colour removed. THE DECK IS FLAT PAINTED STEEL AND IT IS LIT EVENLY. There is no gloss, no shine, no specular highlight, no wet or plastic sheen, no smooth gradient, no glow or halo, and no mottled or speckled surface texture. In particular there is NO BRIGHT CURVED SWEEP OF LIGHT ACROSS ONE SIDE OF THE DISC — a broad soft highlight arcing over the float is the single most likely way to spoil this, and it turns a working steel buoy into a shiny plastic button. Keep the deck one even tone, with any shading done as flat hard-edged facets rather than as a sheen. Fill the frame — reach close to the edges with only a hair of margin. Engine rotation transforms the coordinate system rather than sampling a fixed frame, so nothing clips at any angle and padding only makes the buoy smaller than it should be. A thin clean dark contour. No numbers, no letters, no text, no rust streaks, no birds, no flag, no water, no ripple, no wake, no shadow on the water

Sampling the outer drum annulus of the two 2026-08-10 candidates, the red swung 19.5 in luminance with 79% of that in a single directional lobe (faceted, with a clear light direction) while the green swung 5.4 with only 9% (nearly flat, its modelling moved inward to the dome). Same words, two different objects. Both subjects now state the pair requirement explicitly and name light direction and facet treatment as part of it; generate them together and compare that number before accepting either. ACCEPTED 2026-08-10 AS THE FIRST LATTICE DELIVERY, with one recorded defect. Aspect 1.026; CIRCULARITY 0.974, i.e. the float really is the whole silhouette; lit deck #B93825 at dE 3.4 from the #BB3220 spec, the closest colour any buoy delivery has managed; four dark openings in a clean two-by-two; lantern present with pale housing, dark cap and finial. Ingested from a 2816x1536 frame padded to 1479px square, drawing 26x27px at world 28. ⚠️ THE DEFECT IS GLOSS, and it is the reason the subject's finish clause was rewritten after acceptance rather than before: the float carries a broad specular sweep, measured as a 37.8 luminance swing around the outer deck with 80% of it in a single directional lobe. The old wording listed `no gloss, no shine, no specular highlight` among a dozen other refusals at the end of the subject and it did not bite. The clause is now its own paragraph, names the exact artefact (a bright curved sweep of light across one side of the disc), says what it costs (a shiny plastic button instead of working steel) and gives the correct alternative (flat hard-edged facets). Both delivered candidates omitted it, the sprite reads correctly without it, and at world 28 the board is about 2px — under the 4-screen-px floor. Every element removed from a 28px sprite is a legibility gain, so it stays out. ⚠️ IT STAYS IN THE `bay` CARD SUBJECT, where the buoys are drawn at illustration scale and the board is plainly visible — the same object gets a different parts list at different sizes, which is the whole reason props and cards get separate subjects. AND THE WHITE DRUM BAND QUESTION IS SETTLED: it stays OFF. The retype note left this open pending the contact sheet, because dropping the old cone buoy's white band moved findability onto the four dark openings — a value cue instead of a hue cue. The sheet answers it: at 28px over both Glacier Sound and Pearl Lagoon this reads clearly as a nav aid, a coloured disc with a dark cross and a bright centre. So no band on the props and no band on the card reroll.

ONE MINOR STYLE DEVIATION, recorded and not acted on: the green carries a soft CAST SHADOW under the lantern and along the tower's lower-right, dark enough that at a 0.30 luminance threshold it bridges the four openings into one blob. Invisible at 28px, and it is also the reason a first pass at counting the openings reported two instead of four — a measurement trap worth knowing about on any asset with interior shadow: threshold tight (0.22) before counting dark blobs, or a shadow will merge them.

assets.subject: A yellow cylindrical racing mark — the classic inflatable 'yellow can' — floating on open water, seen from DIRECTLY OVERHEAD, with none of its side visible anywhere. From this angle it is a FLAT CIRCULAR DISC with a taut inflated top: a narrow band of deeper, wetter yellow around the waterline, then a broad flat top face, and a bold dark lifting ring sitting at the exact centre as the one focal dot. Three or four faint radial seams run from the ring out to the rim, spaced evenly, reading as slightly darker lines that show the fabric panels. COLOUR: vivid safety yellow, warm and high-visibility, never mustard, never lime, never cream. It must be findable at a glance against pale turquoise shallows, olive swamp water and near-black polar water alike. Fill the frame: the buoy should reach close to the edges, with only a hair of margin. Engine rotation transforms the coordinate system rather than sampling a fixed frame, so nothing clips at any angle and padding only makes the buoy smaller than it should be. Build the form from FLAT HARD-EDGED BANDS OF CLEARLY DIFFERENT LIGHTNESS, not from smooth shading — a concentric object seen from above has no silhouette to read, so its value steps ARE its structure, and it must still make sense converted to greyscale. Absolutely no gloss, no shine, no specular highlight, no smooth gradient, no plastic sheen, no reflection. A thin clean dark contour, no heavier than the rest of the set. No numbers, no letters, no text of any kind, no flag, no water, no ripple, no shadow
assets.note: Alternative race mark to the orange tetrahedron. Circular and radially symmetric, so it reads identically at any of the arbitrary rotations drawMarkBodies applies. MARK TAXONOMY (design decision, 2026-07-28): the orange tetrahedron is a TEMPORARY mark — an inflatable laid by the race committee for this race. The yellow can is a PERMANENT mark — a fixed installation the course is built around. Which one a course uses is a per-course choice, not a global one. Currently every course uses the orange temporary mark. SHIPPED AND READY BUT UNUSED: drawMarkBodies() resolves a single global markImg, so nothing renders this yet — using it needs marks to carry a sprite reference rather than share one. Measured contrast against water is ~2.4x the orange mark's at every venue (Glacier Sound 10.4:1 vs 4.4, Pearl Lagoon 2.7:1 vs 1.1, Gatorgrass 5.5:1 vs 2.3), and being a circle it is rotation-invariant where the tetrahedron is not.

assets.subject: A race committee boat anchored at the end of a start line, seen from DIRECTLY OVERHEAD, floating level, bow pointing to the TOP of the frame. It is a beamy 30-foot club launch — a working motorboat, never a yacht and never a racing hull: a long hull with a full wide midsection, near-parallel sides through the middle, a bluntly rounded bow, and a SQUARE cut-off transom across the stern. ABSOLUTELY NO SAIL, NO MAST, NO BOOM, NO RIGGING, no sail number, and nothing triangular anywhere on the deck — seen from directly above a racing sailboat is a pair of white triangles, and the single worst failure this sprite can have is being mistaken for one of the boats racing around it. THE READ IS A DARK CORE INSIDE A WHITE OUTLINE, which is the exact inverse of a sailboat's white sails inside a dark hull line — this is the whole point of the design. Working from the bow aft: a short pale foredeck with a small dark windlass block at its tip; then a hard-edged RECTANGULAR DECKHOUSE filling the forward half of the boat, its flat roof CHARCOAL and the darkest thing in the sprite, carrying one small pale dome at its centre; then a clear step of pale open deck; then a MID-NAVY canvas awning stretched over the open aft cockpit as a second rectangle, clearly LIGHTER than the charcoal roof so the two never merge into one smear. The white of the hull survives only as a clean margin running all the way around that dark core, widening at the bow and across the transom. THE SIGNATURE IS AN ORANGE FLAG, and it must be unmistakable. A short staff stands on the after deck and a bold rectangular safety-orange flag streams STRAIGHT AFT from it, out past the transom and clear of the hull, breaking the silhouette at the stern — the boat lies head to wind, so the flag blows down the frame. Render it as one flat solid orange rectangle with a slight ripple in its trailing edge, big enough to be the second thing the eye finds after the hull. This flag is what tells the player where the starting line ends, so it is functional information: keep it true safety orange and never shift it toward the colour of the water. COLOUR AND VALUE: clean off-white hull and deck with a single crisp deep-navy stripe following the sheerline the whole way around, charcoal deckhouse roof, mid-navy awning, safety-orange flag. Those extremes are deliberate — this sprite has to be findable on near-black polar water, where the white hull and the flag carry it, AND on pale turquoise shallows, where the charcoal roof and the navy stripe carry it. CONVERTED TO GREYSCALE the hull margin, the two roof rectangles and the flag must still read as separate steps. Flat hard-edged shading in clear steps of lightness, absolutely no gloss, no shine, no specular highlight, no smooth gradient, no plastic sheen, no reflection. A thin clean dark contour, no heavier than the rest of the set. Drawn at only about 85 pixels: bold simple shapes and no detail that would not survive that size. No crew, no figures, no water, no wake, no spray, no ripple, no anchor line, no cast shadow, no numbers, no letters, no lettering on the hull
assets.note: SHIPPED. A third mark KIND for the line ends, alongside the orange inflatable (temporary) and the yellow can (permanent): the vessel the line is sighted from. venuedoc's MARK_KINDS is now the one list — validator, editor dropdown and script.js's sprite registry all read it — and the eval fixtures already named the ends `sf-pin` and `sf-boat`, so the concept predated the art. VENUE-NEUTRAL like mark/zodiac/buoy-channel-*: race furniture at all ten venues, no palette clause. ROLE IS `traffic`, NOT `nav`, even though it is functionally a mark — the nav add-on emits 'use canonical buoyage shape and colour coding', which is buoy language and would push a boat toward red/green. The contract that binds is traffic's: never confusable with a competitor. The mark-function requirements (the orange flag, the line end) live in the subject text instead. SIZING: world 92 with fillTo 0.92 gives 37x85px = 9.2m at 9.2px/m, a 30ft club launch and 1.5x the 56px racing boat. That gap is the OPPOSITE call from the zodiac, which is deliberately SHORTER than a racer: a support RIB stays off the competitor read by being small, a committee boat by being big, boxy and white. 85px on an 1100-unit start line is 7.7% of it. Content filled 0.757 of the master, so fillTo upscales 1.22x — visible softening at 1024, invisible at 85. MEASURED CONTRAST (WCAG vs median water, at true race scale): Glacier Sound median 1.28:1 but brightest 10% 9.74:1; Pearl Lagoon median 2.84:1 with darkest 10% 5.32:1. That split IS the design — the white hull carries it on near-black water, the charcoal roof on pale turquoise — and both ends beat the zodiac (2.53 / 2.27 median). Judge it on the plates, as the zodiac's note argues: the player's own hull is 2.01:1 on lagoon. THREE RECORDED DEVIATIONS, none blocking. (1) The orange flag does NOT break the silhouette as the subject demanded: it is 107px of a 337px beam, entirely inside the hull footprint, and streams to starboard rather than aft. At 85px it is a ~12px orange dash on the white transom and still reads on both plates, but it is less findable than the macaroni-crest trick intended. If the line end is ever hard to spot, that is what to redraw. (2) A ~14px transparent slot separates a detached 13px navy contour ring from the hull, a background-remover artifact; 1.5px at race scale and invisible on the plates. (3) Teak deck striping is microtexture beyond spec and blurs to tan. Ingest passed with no warnings. ENGINE, ALL THREE BLOCKERS NOW FIXED. (1) drawMarkBodies resolved a single global markImg; it now resolves MARK_SPRITES[kind], which also lights up mark-can-yellow after a week shipped-but-unused. (2) It rotated every mark by an arbitrary per-position scramble, right for a tetrahedron and wrong for a vessel. orientCourseMarks() now freezes a heading from the LINE'S OWN NORMAL, signed by the direction of travel on the line's FIRST route use — not from the live wind (which oscillates every frame, so the hull would swing with every puff and the baked flag would fight the real breeze) and not per leg (a line sailed twice would spin the boat 180 degrees when the fleet came back to finish). The wobble stays: on a hull it reads as lying to an anchor. (3) markRadius 12 is now a per-mark body — a 3-circle r=19 capsule for the hull, and the sprite is nudged 19 units outboard along the line so the line's sailable span stays clear with the flagstaff on the mark point. Every consumer is written as (constant + bodyR) so a buoy's bodyR of 12 reproduces the old 50 and 115 exactly. Covered by eval/test_marks.js. The committee boat belongs on the STARBOARD end of its line; venuedoc warns when it is not, rather than enforcing it, because it is a convention. NOT YET PLACED ON ANY VENUE — that is an authoring decision, and it must not land on Sea Trial Bay, which is the eval anchor.

assets.subject: A rigid-hull inflatable boat — a Zodiac-type work RIB — seen from DIRECTLY OVERHEAD, floating level, bow pointing to the TOP of the frame. THE SILHOUETTE IS THE WHOLE POINT: two fat parallel buoyancy tubes run the length of the boat and sweep together into a blunt rounded point at the bow, leaving a long open U-shaped well between them, and the stern is cut square and OPEN across the back — a horseshoe, never a pointed racing hull. The tubes read as thick cylinders, tapering to sealed conical ends at the transom, banded by three or four dark seams. Inside the well: a flat pale deck, one small dark centre console set just forward of amidships, and a plain bench seat behind it. A dark blocky outboard motor sits on the transom and overhangs the stern beyond the tubes. ABSOLUTELY NO SAIL, NO MAST, NO BOOM, NO RIGGING and no sail number — this is a powered working boat and must never be mistaken for a racing sailboat at a glance. COLOUR: bright safety orange tubes, warm and saturated, the canonical colour of a rescue and support RIB, with a mid-grey deck and near-black console and outboard for internal contrast. It has to stay findable against near-black polar water, deep blue and pale turquoise shallows alike. Flat hard-edged shading in clear steps of lightness, no gloss, no specular highlight, no smooth gradient. A thin clean dark contour, no heavier than the rest of the set. No water, no wake, no spray, no ripple, no cast shadow, no crew, no figures, no flag
assets.note: VENUE-NEUTRAL like mark/buoy-channel-*: a support RIB is race furniture at every venue — committee boat, safety boat, and Glacier Sound's station tender for arctic-station. Kept venue-neutral deliberately so no palette clause tints it; safety orange is canonical everywhere. SIZING: world 54 with fillTo 0.92 gives a 50px hull = 5.4m at 9.2px/m, a real Zodiac Pro size and deliberately SHORTER than the 56px racing boat. That size gap is part of the `traffic` contract, but the silhouette does the real work: a horseshoe of tubes with an open transom shares no family with a pointed sailing hull, and it survives colour removal. Do NOT exaggerate it up to boat size for readability — that trades away the one thing keeping it off the competitor read. MEASURED CONTRAST (WCAG ratio vs flat water, at 54px): Glacier Sound — orange tubes 4.22:1, median pixel 2.53:1. Pearl Lagoon — median 2.27:1, tubes only 1.36:1, because orange and turquoise are opposed in HUE but nearly equal in LUMINANCE, so on lagoon water this prop is carried by hue and by its dark contour, not by value. That reads as a fail against the 3:1 floor until you measure the thing the floor is calibrated on: the player's own hull is 2.01:1 on Pearl Lagoon, WORSE than this. The 3:1 figure in the acceptance rubric is not met by the game's hero asset on lagoon water, so treat it as a target for dark venues and judge lagoon on the plate. Accepted on that basis.

assets.subject: Anthropomorphic Green Tree Snake. EXPRESSION: large round eyes and a mouth open just enough to show the flicking forked tongue, expression bright and disarmingly friendly. LIMBS — Green Tree Snake has NONE — it is limbless: it has no limbs whatsoever: nothing to raise, nothing to fold. The pose is the set of the head and one easy coil of the body. BODY COVERING: this creature is covered in dry overlapping scales, and nothing else — no feathers and no plumage, no fur, no wings. ITS OWN COLOUR is #BCE444 — that is the animal's colour, and the jacket colours are separate from it. Do not blend in the surface or the limbs of any other kind of animal. PFD COLOURS, and these are exact: the main body of the jacket is vivid green (#49c100); the foam panels across the chest and the shoulder straps are bright chartreuse (#C4E63C); the waist webbing is charcoal with a plain metal buckle. These two colours are exact. SPECIES SIGNATURE: a slender emerald body with a long tapering tail and a narrow head, large round eyes and a flicking blue-black tongue. REQUIRED: This animal is a TUBE with no shoulders and no torso. Draw the body wall as one smooth unbroken curve down each side of the picture, continuing past the jacket and out of frame at the bottom. The jacket is a BAND buckled around that tube, like a strap around a hose: a collar edge at the top, a belt at the bottom, solid fabric between, and the body's own smooth outline running down either side of it, uninterrupted from head to the bottom edge. A green tree snake: one smooth slender tube, head raised out of the collar
assets.note: Competitor portrait. Viper the Green Tree Snake, archetype leech. Vest colours are the AI_CONFIG hull and spinnaker ordered by the same luma rule the profile band uses.

assets.subject: Anthropomorphic Atlantic Mudskipper. EXPRESSION: bulging eyes set high on top of the head, both swivelled forward, mouth open in a wide startled grin. Twitchy and about to bolt. GESTURE: propped up on both splayed pectoral fins with the body angled off the ground, mid-scramble. LIMBS — Atlantic Mudskipper has muscular PECTORAL FINS it props itself on: propped up on two thick muscular pectoral fins used like crutches — fins doing a leg’s job, never hands. BODY COVERING: this creature is covered in smooth wet skin with fine scales, and nothing else — no feathers and no plumage, no fur, no wings. ITS OWN COLOUR is #9AC73E — that is the animal's colour, and the jacket colours are separate from it. Do not blend in the surface or the limbs of any other kind of animal. PFD COLOURS, and these are exact: the main body of the jacket is bright vivid red (#e33d28); the foam panels across the chest and the shoulder straps are bright vivid green (#15f121); the waist webbing is charcoal with a plain metal buckle. These two colours are exact. SPECIES SIGNATURE: bulging periscope eyes on top of a broad flat head, a wide grinning mouth, and a mottled olive body propped on muscular pectoral fins. REQUIRED: Every surface is CHALKY and POWDERY, like dry pastel on rough paper — light sinks in and scatters. Shading is done in flat steps of value. The brightest area on the body is a soft broad pale patch with a diffuse edge
assets.note: Competitor portrait. Skitter the Atlantic Mudskipper, archetype gambler. Vest colours are the AI_CONFIG hull and spinnaker ordered by the same luma rule the profile band uses.

assets.subject: Anthropomorphic Vampire Squid. EXPRESSION: hot red eyes narrowed to slits in a dark shapeless face, mouth hidden. Calm, patient and entirely unreadable. GESTURE: the webbed cloak drawn part-way closed around the body, arms concealed inside it, only the eyes showing clearly. LIMBS — Vampire Squid has a WEBBED ARM CLOAK: the arms are joined by a web into one continuous cloak, drawn closed so it reads as a single shape. Never separate waving limbs, and never fingers. BODY COVERING: this creature is covered in smooth soft skin, and nothing else — no feathers and no plumage, no fur, no scales, no wings. ITS OWN COLOUR is #644581 — that is the animal's colour, and the jacket colours are separate from it. Do not blend in the surface or the limbs of any other kind of animal. PFD COLOURS, and these are exact: the main body of the jacket is purple (#7A1FA2); the foam panels across the chest and the shoulder straps are bright vivid red (#E10600); the waist webbing is charcoal with a plain metal buckle. These two colours are exact. SPECIES SIGNATURE: a VAMPIRE SQUID, and it must be unmistakable: the eight arms are joined for their whole length by a single continuous WEB OF SKIN, so the animal reads as one dark bell-shaped CLOAK rather than as separate tentacles. The inside of that cloak is lined with soft pale spines. Two enormous round eyes, proportionally the largest of any animal, glowing red. A pair of small rounded fins near the top of the mantle like little ears. Deep blackish-maroon throughout. REQUIRED: It must read as a VAMPIRE SQUID at a glance: one dark webbed CLOAK joining all the arms, pale spines lining its inside, two huge round red eyes, small ear-like fins on the mantle
assets.note: Competitor portrait. Veil the Vampire Squid, archetype leech. Vest colours are the AI_CONFIG hull and spinnaker ordered by the same luma rule the profile band uses.

LIMBS — Black Seadevil has PECTORAL FINS: one pectoral fin lifted a little from the flank — a flat flexible blade, never a hand. BODY COVERING: this creature is covered in smooth wet skin with fine scales, and nothing else — no feathers and no plumage, no fur, no wings. BODY COVERING: this creature is covered in smooth wet skin with fine scales, and nothing else — no feathers and no plumage, no fur, no wings. assets.subject: Anthropomorphic Elephant Seal. EXPRESSION: eyes half-closed to slits above heavy jowls, mouth a broad closed line. The face of something that cannot be hurried and has never tried. GESTURE: sitting square and low, bulk filling the lower frame, foreflippers tucked beneath and barely visible. LIMBS — Elephant Seal has FLIPPERS: one flipper raised a little from the body — a flat paddle, never a hand. BODY COVERING: this creature is covered in dense fur, and nothing else — no feathers and no plumage, no scales, no wings. ITS OWN COLOUR is #898989 — that is the animal's colour, and the jacket colours are separate from it. Do not blend in the surface or the limbs of any other kind of animal. PFD COLOURS, and these are exact: the main body of the jacket is dark muted azure blue (#6B7280); the foam panels across the chest and the shoulder straps are bright vivid orange (#FF7A00); the waist webbing is charcoal with a plain metal buckle. These two colours are exact. SPECIES SIGNATURE: an enormous inflatable pendulous PROBOSCIS hanging over the mouth, a massively thick neck and heavy wrinkled grey hide. REQUIRED: The jacket is SLEEVELESS — it is a smooth closed band of fabric that wraps right round the body like a cuff on a hose, with a collar at the top and a belt at the bottom and unbroken material in between. There are no shoulder openings, no armholes and no sleeves in the design at all. The animal's body simply continues down through it. Both foreflippers are drawn as one matched pair: identical length, identical outline, identical colour, one on the left and one on the right, mirrored about the body. They are flat paddles that lie along the sides

Nothing about the pose is in a rush. LIMBS — California Newt has short FRONT LEGS: both short front legs planted forward, splayed toes visible. BODY COVERING: this creature is covered in smooth moist skin, and nothing else — no feathers and no plumage, no fur, no scales, no wings. ITS OWN COLOUR is #FA8C00 — that is the animal's colour, and the jacket colours are separate from it. Do not blend in the surface or the limbs of any other kind of animal. SPECIES SIGNATURE: a warm orange-brown back over a vivid orange belly, a broad blunt head with bulging dark eyes, and granular skin. REQUIRED: Each eye shows a broad band of clean WHITE sclera around a dark pupil, so the eyes read clearly even half-lidded
assets.note: Competitor portrait. Cruz the California Newt, archetype metronome. Vest colours are the AI_CONFIG hull and spinnaker ordered by the same luma rule the profile band uses — EXCEPT the SHELL, which is spinnaker2 #F0E0B0 rather than the hull. Cruz was one of the worst animal-vs-jacket collisions in the roster (dE 8) and his band is the same orange hull, so the pale shell is the fix; the subject was rewritten to match the accepted art.

BODY COVERING: this creature is covered in a hard shell over a soft mantle, and nothing else — no feathers and no plumage, no fur, no scales, no wings. BODY COVERING: this creature is covered in smooth wet skin with fine scales, and nothing else — no feathers and no plumage, no fur, no wings. He is named for the way he fights and not for cattle: no horns, no nose ring, no bovine muzzle, no fur. He is HEAVY, NOT MUSCULAR — one thick smooth tube, deep from back to belly and wide across the head, with no shoulder mass, no chest muscle and no waist

LIMBS — American Alligator has short FRONT LEGS: both short front legs planted forward, splayed toes visible. assets.subject: Anthropomorphic Humpback Whale. EXPRESSION: one small deep-set eye low on an enormous knobbly head, mouth a long gentle curve. Vast, ancient and entirely peaceful. GESTURE: the huge head turned three-quarter and tipped slightly up, chin lifted, one long white flipper held close in against the flank. LIMBS — Humpback Whale has FLIPPERS: one flipper raised a little from the body — a flat paddle, never a hand. BODY COVERING: this creature is covered in smooth bare hide, and nothing else — no feathers and no plumage, no fur, no scales, no wings. ITS OWN COLOUR is charcoal blue-grey (#34424E) — that is the animal's colour, and the jacket colours are separate from it. Do not blend in the surface or the limbs of any other kind of animal. PFD COLOURS, and these are exact: the main body of the jacket is bright coral orange (#EE6C4D); the foam panels across the chest and the shoulder straps are pale sand (#E6D3A3); the waist webbing is charcoal with a plain metal buckle. These two colours are exact. SPECIES SIGNATURE: KNOBBLY TUBERCLES scattered across the top of the head and along the jaw — draw them as A FEW LARGE ROUNDED BUMPS, never a fine rash of dots. Long white-edged flippers with a SCALLOPED leading edge, deep pleats running along the throat, and a charcoal blue-grey body. REQUIRED: The flippers are the longest in the ocean and must still be held close — the widest points of this picture belong to the body, so the near flipper lies in against the flank. Tubercles and throat pleats are a few large shapes each; fine detail dissolves at thumbnail size

LIMBS — Common Merganser has WINGS: wings folded close against the body, one wingtip lifted just clear. BODY COVERING: this creature is covered in feathers, and nothing else — no fur, no scales. PFD COLOURS, and these are exact: the main body of the jacket is deep violet blue (#3A3F9E); the foam panels across the chest and the shoulder straps are bright coral (#F2765A); the waist webbing is charcoal with a plain metal buckle. assets.subject: Anthropomorphic Razorback Sucker. EXPRESSION: a small steady eye low on a blunt head, the down-turned mouth set in a patient line. Old-river calm, and entirely used to being underestimated. GESTURE: head turned three-quarter and held low, the back ridge rising from behind the collar, one pectoral fin resting forward. LIMBS — Razorback Sucker has PECTORAL FINS: one pectoral fin lifted a little from the flank — a flat flexible blade, never a hand. BODY COVERING: this creature is covered in smooth wet skin with fine scales, and nothing else — no feathers and no plumage, no fur, no wings. ITS OWN COLOUR is olive bronze (#6E6039) — that is the animal's colour, and the jacket colours are separate from it. Do not blend in the surface or the limbs of any other kind of animal. PFD COLOURS, and these are exact: the main body of the jacket is deep turquoise (#14807F); the foam panels across the chest and the shoulder straps are magenta pink (#E0518F); the waist webbing is charcoal with a plain metal buckle. These two colours are exact. SPECIES SIGNATURE: A SHARP BONY KEEL rising along the back immediately behind the head — a hard narrow ridge, like the blade of a boat's keel turned upward — over an olive-bronze body with a yellow-orange belly, and a thick DOWN-TURNED SUCKER MOUTH beneath a blunt snout. REQUIRED: The keel is HARD, NARROW AND ANGULAR, never the soft rounded flesh hump of the humpback chub already in this fleet. The sucker mouth points down and is clearly on the underside of the head, never at the front

Quick, curious and entirely nocturnal. GESTURE: the small head turned three-quarter with both ears up, wings folded tight against the body so the silhouette stays compact. LIMBS — Canyon Bat has WINGS: leathery wing membranes folded close against the body, their long finger-struts reading as slim ribs INSIDE the folded membrane — never a hand, never separate fingers, never a thumb or palm. BODY COVERING: this creature is covered in dense fur, and nothing else — no feathers and no plumage, no scales, no wings. ITS OWN COLOUR is pale sandy yellow (#9B7B5B) — that is the animal's colour, and the jacket colours are separate from it. Do not blend in the surface or the limbs of any other kind of animal. PFD COLOURS, and these are exact: the main body of the jacket is deep indigo violet (#4433A0); the foam panels across the chest and the shoulder straps are hot pink (#F2559B); the waist webbing is charcoal with a plain metal buckle. assets.subject: Anthropomorphic Compass Jellyfish. EXPRESSION: calm knowing eyes set into the front of the translucent bell, mouth a small level line. Orderly, precise and pleased about it. GESTURE: the bell turned well into three-quarter and tipped, so its markings are seen at an angle rather than face-on. LIMBS — Compass Jellyfish has NONE — no arms or legs: it has no arms or legs to gesture with; the pose is carried by the head and body alone, with the vest sitting around it. BODY COVERING: this creature is covered in translucent gelatinous tissue, and nothing else — no feathers and no plumage, no fur, no scales, no wings. ITS OWN COLOUR is pale straw translucent (#E8DCC4) — that is the animal's colour, and the jacket colours are separate from it. Do not blend in the surface or the limbs of any other kind of animal. PFD COLOURS, and these are exact: the main body of the jacket is deep navy teal (#17495C); the foam panels across the chest and the shoulder straps are vivid magenta (#D6338C); the waist webbing is charcoal with a plain metal buckle. These two colours are exact. SPECIES SIGNATURE: A PALE TRANSLUCENT BELL MARKED LIKE A COMPASS ROSE: bold dark brown V-shaped rays running out from a small central spot toward the rim. Seen from this angle they read as a few strong marks curving over the dome, not as a flat symmetrical star. REQUIRED: NOT A ROSETTE. The bell is turned so the rays foreshorten across the dome — never a flat circular pattern facing the viewer, never a mandala, and never a ring of identical marks. Draw EIGHT OR SO bold rays, not a fine radial fan. The trailing tentacles are below the waist and are simply not in the picture
