Those two can never be in the same race, so the labels carry it: 'Coral Limestone' against 'Coastal Rock'. Body reset to the delivered mean; stroke/veg/rock are the spec's own offsets carried onto it. Registered `coralrock`, tile 128, alpha 0.20.

assets.subject: A closed sward of coarse tropical island grass and low scrub seen from directly overhead from about ten metres up, in flat even light — the dry-season interior of a small South Pacific island, sun-dried and salt-pruned rather than lush rainforest. AT THIS HEIGHT INDIVIDUAL BLADES DO NOT RESOLVE, and that is the subject: the sward reads as a soft clumpy mottle, rounded tussock crowns a shade lighter where the grass mounds up and narrow sinks a shade darker between them, every clump blending into its neighbours with no hard edge and at roughly the same density everywhere. This grass is COARSER AND MORE TUSSOCKY than a temperate pasture — the clumps are bigger and stand more separately, with more of the darker sink showing between them. THROUGH THE SWARD, LOW SCRUB — broader, rounder, distinctly DARKER and slightly BLUER patches where beach naupaka and low salt-tolerant shrubs lie flat against the trade wind. Each is a soft-edged mound a little denser than the grass around it, scattered unevenly, covering perhaps a quarter of the frame. THEY ARE PATCHES OF A DIFFERENT PLANT, NOT BUSHES: no branch, no stem, no drawn outline, no cast shadow, and nothing tall enough to read as an object sitting on top of the ground. This is where the olive in this ground lives — in the scrub and in the sinks, never in the mean. A few broad drifts of paler, drier, straw-tinted grass move through at the largest scale, soft and wide, where the dry season and the salt have burned the sward back — drifts of tone only, never a shape with an edge. NOTHING LEANS ANY PARTICULAR WAY. No combed direction, no mowing stripes, no swirls, no rows, no terracing, nothing lining up with the frame or with itself, and no spacing that repeats anywhere in the image. THE WHOLE IMAGE HOLDS A NARROW SUN-BLEACHED RANGE from #93A527 to #C2D160 around a mean of #AABD31. IT IS SUN-BLEACHED, NOT SUN-GREYED, and that distinction is the whole colour brief. Bleached grass goes LIGHTER and YELLOWER; it does not go gritty or grey. So this is a bright, clean, confident yellow-green — dried by hard tropical sun, but every bit as alive. NOTHING HERE IS KHAKI, SAGE, GREYED-DOWN, DUSTY, MUTED OR ARMY-DRAB, and nothing is the cured tan-olive of a dead sward. If a green looks washed out or dirty it is wrong; take the fading upward into light, never sideways into grey. Hold the whole image inside a narrow value range. No visible soil, no sand, no coral rubble, no rock, no flowers, no palm fronds, no fallen leaves, no individual drawn blades, no fine hairline strokes, no paths, no tracks, no footprints, no fences, no water and no shoreline
assets.note: BLUEWATER BONANZA'S PLAIN LANDMASS FILL — the ground a cay's interior is made of, between the beach and the trees. It exists to close a gap the venue actually has: with only `tropicsand` and three tree props, an island is either bare beach or solid forest, and there is nothing in between to draw. Registered as the `tropicscrub` kind / `tropicscrub` look, label 'Tropic Scrub'. ⚠️ THE BODY WAS PICKED AGAINST THE TREES, NOT AGAINST THE OTHER SWARDS, and that is the constraint to preserve. This ground carries trees: true and is what ocean-palm-coconut, ocean-pandanus and ocean-almond-tropical stand on. Measured: the body sits at L* 73.0 against those three crowns' lit tones at 74.3 / 66.0 / 59.3 and their mid tones at 61.9 / 48.1 / 42.7, so every crown reads DARK against its own ground. Lighthouse Cove is the precedent and works the same way — ground L* 66.4 under crowns at 59.7 and 46.1. The obvious 'lusher tropical green' lands at L* 56, inside the crown range, and would dissolve three trees into their own lawn. Anyone re-tuning this colour re-checks those seven numbers first. TILE 128, with `grass`, `swampgrass` and `bay-scrub`: tussock crowns are centimetre-scale and land at true size there. No argument on this one — it is the whole sward family's number. ALPHA 0.40 IS PRE-REGISTERED from coastalscrub's MEASURED value rather than from the swards' original 0.5, because this is the same kind of material and coastalscrub is the one that had to move: its delivered mottle came back at luma sd 14.30, which at 0.5 would have made it the loudest ground in the game. Starting from the corrected number is the cheap version of that lesson. ⚠️ STILL MEASURE IT. This subject asks for coarser, more separated tussocks and a full quarter of the frame in a second darker plant, so it may well arrive busier than bay-scrub did. Land inside the set's on-screen sd band of 1.38-6.75, ideally between swampgrass (5.10) and grass (6.75) where bay-scrub sits at 5.72. BODY IS THIS SPEC MEAN AND MUST BE RESET TO THE DELIVERED MEAN on ingest, per [[ocean-coralrock]] and the coralsand / bay-rock move. A FOURTH SWARD, AND THE LIGHTEST AND YELLOWEST OF THEM: dE 18.8 from `coastalscrub`, 14.8 from `grass`, 36.2 from `swampgrass`. All three are cross-venue and so picker-only under coastalrock's two-tier rule; in-venue, which is what matters in play, it is 60.5 from the sand it sits behind and 60.8 from the limestone it sits against. SATURATION IS HELD AT 0.74 ON PURPOSE — above coastalscrub (0.62), below `grass` (0.83) — and the 'sun-bleached' is bought with VALUE. This is coastalscrub's hardest-won lesson applied ahead of time rather than re-learned: its first answer cut chroma to 0.54 to buy sun-fading, landed with the cured DEAD sward `swampgrass` (0.48) and read army-olive. Cutting saturation is how a ground leaves the family, not how it gets weathered. The subject therefore refuses the drab words by name and states the tiebreaker direction. WHAT TO CHECK ON DELIVERY, in order: seamless wrap on all four edges; saturation of the lit tussocks (under 0.60 is a reject — that is the failure this family keeps having); mean within ~3 of #AABD31, then reset the body to it; the scrub patches present and genuinely darker AND bluer than the grass, not just darker; no combed direction and no repeating spacing; no soil, rubble or fallen frond anywhere. NO LAND_TEXTURES ROW YET — written out ready in the ISLAND_STYLES comment in script.js. DELIVERED AND ACCEPTED 2026-08-14, at 1254px (downsampled to 1024 by ingest; mean and sd unchanged). ALPHA MEASURED TO 0.30, one step under the sward family's 0.40-0.50, because this is the busiest sward ever delivered — luma sd 19.17 at tile 128 against bay-scrub's 14.21, which was itself described as 'much busier than the two swards'. 0.40 would have landed on-screen sd 7.67, past `grass` (6.66) and the loudest ground in the game. 0.30 lands 5.75, effectively on top of bay-scrub's 5.68 and between swampgrass (5.07) and grass (6.66). Third sward running to come off its pre-registered value for exactly this reason (marsh 0.5->0.40, coastalscrub 0.5->0.40, this 0.40->0.30) — the pattern is now strong enough to state as a rule: pre-register a sward at 0.30 and measure up, not 0.50 and measure down. ⚠️ PERIODICITY WAS MEASURED TWO WAYS AND THE FIRST ONE NEARLY GOT THIS REJECTED. On the radially averaged power spectrum it scores peak/mean 20.34 at 4 cycles per tile — by far the worst in the set, whose shipped range is 8.65 (grass) to 12.18 (bay-scrub) — which reads as a clear fail. It is not one. peak/mean is normalised by the BROADBAND FLOOR, and this art has an unusually smooth one, so the ratio inflates without the repeat being any stronger. Measured in absolute on-screen terms instead — the luma sd carried by the dominant band, times alpha — it is 3.48 at 0.30, BELOW bay-scrub's 3.72 and marsh's 3.68, both shipped and accepted. JUDGE A REPEAT ON ABSOLUTE AMPLITUDE; the ratio misleads in both directions, and this is the second metric on this venue to do so (see the elongation-vs-direction note on bayou-oak). WRAP IS CLEAN: 1.11 horizontal and 0.87 vertical against interior, i.e. at or below the interior neighbour difference, and no seam visible in a 3x3 tiling. ⚠️ THE CROWN CONSTRAINT SURVIVED, BUT ONLY WHEN CHECKED PROPERLY, and this is the finding worth carrying to any future ground that grows trees. Delivered mean is #A9AF2A at L* 68.9, four L* darker than the #AABD31 spec. Checked against the SPEC HEX LADDER the note above lists, that looks like an outright failure: the ground is 5.3 L* DARKER than the palm's lit frond tone (#94C701, L* 74.3), and the note demands it be lighter than every crown tone. It is not a failure, because a lit tone is a HIGHLIGHT on a minority of a crown's pixels and is never what the crown reads as. Measured on the real sprites: the shipped lagoon palms average L* 47.8 and 46.8, so this ground sits +21.2 above them — in family with the cove, where bay-scrub at L* 66.3 sits +26.0 / +37.2 / +32.2 above its own three trees. COMPARE CROWN MEANS TO GROUND MEANS. A spec hex ladder is for writing a prompt, not for judging one. SATURATION CLEARED COMFORTABLY at 0.76 against the 0.60 reject line, so the drab failure this family keeps having did not recur. Separations on the delivered mean: in-venue 58.3 from `coralsand` and 57.2 from `coralrock`; cross-venue 14.0 from `coastalscrub`, 18.4 from `grass`, 30.7 from `swampgrass`, all picker-only. Body reset to the delivered mean; stroke/veg are the spec's offsets carried onto it, `rock` is the venue's own limestone. Registered `tropicscrub`, tile 128, alpha 0.30.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH OF THE TOP OF ONE SHRUB, shot straight down from well above it the way a survey frames a single plant. YOU SEE FOLIAGE AND NOTHING ELSE: no trunk, no stem, no limb, no branch, no twig and no bark anywhere in this picture, and least of all in the middle. Where the mass parts you see hard-edged SHADOW INSIDE THE PLANT, never a branch. BEACH NAUPAKA — Scaevola taccada, the shrub that lines every sand beach in the South Pacific, growing in the salt spray right down to the high-water mark. It is THE DENSE ONE of this venue's three ground plants, and its whole job is to be a solid mass: a compact, closed, ROUNDED MOUND of leaf, tight and heavy, with no gaps you can see the ground through. THE LEAF IS THICK, FLESHY AND GLOSSY, and that is what separates this from any ordinary bush. Build the mound from broad SPOON-SHAPED leaves — widest near the blunt rounded tip and tapering back to the stalk — each one a chunky two-tone shape with a hard edge and a bright specular sheen along one side, because these leaves are succulent and wet-looking. The leaves crowd into tight spiral clusters at the end of every branch, so the surface of the mound reads as a quilt of overlapping ROSETTES of six to ten leaves each, packed together at plainly uneven sizes. COUNT NOTHING AND REPEAT NOTHING. The rosettes clump and crowd; they do not sit in a ring around a centre and there is no rosette in the middle with the others arranged about it. Walk around the rim, and if the same cluster spacing comes back four, five or six times on the way round, it has been drawn as a FLOWER and it is wrong however good it looks. AND YET IT IS ONE COMPACT CONNECTED MOUND, which is the other half of that rule and the easier half to lose. Every cluster touches or overlaps a neighbour and NOT ONE floats off on its own with clear space round it. Draw the smallest circle that contains the plant and the foliage fills about eight tenths of it — this is the densest thing in the venue's planting and it should read as solid. The rim is lumpy and bitten, with two or three shallow notches, and it is never a clean circle. THE WHITE HALF-FLOWERS ARE THE IDENTIFIER AND THEY ARE THE POINT OF THE NAME. Naupaka means half-flower: the bloom looks as though it has been torn down the middle, with every petal on ONE side of the centre and nothing on the other — a small white fan of five petals in a half-circle, faintly streaked purple at the throat. Scatter six to ten of them unevenly across the mound, each small, each sitting in the middle of a leaf rosette, and a few small round white berries among them. They are the ONLY light accent in the picture and the only thing that is not green. THE GREEN IS A BRIGHT GLOSSY TROPICAL YELLOW-GREEN, HIGH IN CHROMA. Build the whole plant from this set: a bright lit green near #7FB82A on the leaves that catch the sun, a mid green near #4D8C15, a full-bodied green near #2F6A0E, and a deep COOL shade near #16400A in the pockets between clusters. THERE IS NO OLIVE, NO KHAKI, NO MUSTARD, NO OCHRE, NO TAN, NO ARMY DRAB AND NO DUSTY, GREYED-DOWN OR MUTED GREEN ANYWHERE IN THIS PLANT. Where it turns into shadow it goes deeper and cooler, never browner and never duller. THE SILHOUETTE IS AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE. A mound seen from straight above is round; one wider than it is tall means the camera was tilted. NO WATER ANYWHERE: no waterline, no wet stain, no reflection. And no ground is DRAWN either — a sand beach is where it grows, not something painted into the sprite; the plant is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies the shore it stands on
assets.note: FIRST OF BLUEWATER BONANZA'S THREE UNDERBRUSH PLANTS, and the venue's default coastal bush — the one that will be placed most, behind beaches and along every shoreline. The set is separated on SILHOUETTE FIRST per art-pipeline 2's colour-removed test: this is a DENSE CLOSED MOUND, [[ocean-morning-glory]] is an OPEN SPRAWL OF RUNNERS, and [[ocean-grass-coastal]] is a SOFT FEATHERED TUFT. Size ladder 40 / 30 / 20 — 1.33x and 1.50x apart, matching the cove shrub family's own minimum. SIZE IS HONEST, NOT EXAGGERATED: an open-grown Scaevola taccada spreads about 4.35 m, and 4.35 x 9.2 units/m = 40u. It sits just above the cove's largest shrub (cove-oak-scrub, 36u), which is right — a naupaka thicket is bigger than a bear oak. ⚠️ IT IS COLOUR-TWINNED WITH THE COCONUT PALM AND THAT IS DELIBERATE, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Measured, its body sits dE 3.6 from the shipped palm crown — effectively the same green. art-pipeline 2 asks that role and identity survive with COLOUR REMOVED, which is exactly the axis these two are separated on: 40u against 70u, and a closed lumpy mound against a rosette of long feathered blades. Both are also genuinely the same bright glossy yellow-green in life. Do not 'fix' this by tinting one of them; that would trade a real distinction for a fake one. Same argument covers [[ocean-morning-glory]] at dE 7.9 from the pandanus. READS DARK ON BOTH ITS GROUNDS, the constraint the whole venue's planting is built on: L* 52.3 against tropicscrub's 68.9 (+16.6) and coralsand's 90.9 (+38.6). That is within 0.3 L* of the shipped coconut palm's own relationship to the same grounds, so a beach planted with both reads as one family. THE HALF-FLOWER IS WORTH THE PIXELS AT 40u and is the reason this slot names a flower at all, where the cove's shrubs mostly do not. It is the species' name and its one unmistakable feature, it is WHITE against a saturated green so it survives reduction better than any hue would, and it is the only light accent in the venue's entire planting — nothing else here reads as a bright speck. planRound true, fillTo 0.86, anchor trunk-base with no trunk drawn (the cove-oak-black convention: the stem's position is implied at the mound's centre). NO allowSymmetry — a shrub built from leaf ROSETTES sits right on the mandala attractor, which is why the subject spends a clause refusing evenness and states the clump construction instead, the cove-pine-pitch lesson. Plane `surface` and contact none when the art lands: nothing sails under a bush, and it stands on tropicsand and tropicscrub, both already `hard`. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6: slot, then art, then the kind. DELIVERED AND ACCEPTED 2026-08-14, pre-cut with real alpha, 2048px master, ingested with no warnings (160px bake for 40px display). EVERY GATE PASSED. Aspect 1.004 against the 1.12 planRound gate. One connected mound, no floating cluster. Circle fill 74.6% against the eight tenths asked — marginally under and correctly the densest thing in the venue's planting. Green-only hue 93 at saturation 0.81, so the bright glossy yellow-green arrived and the drab failure did not recur; 97.8% of opaque pixels are green and only 0.8% warm. THE HALF-FLOWERS AND BERRIES CAME THROUGH and they do the identifying work the note above predicted: white against a saturated green survives reduction where a hue would not, and at 40px they are the only bright specks in the whole venue's planting. READS AT ITS OWN SIZE ON BOTH GROUNDS, measured by compositing the 40px sprite over each: dE 27.3 from tropicscrub and 61.2 from coralsand, covering 59% of its own footprint. Body L* 50.2, so the scrub sits +18.7 above it and the sand +40.7 — in family with the shipped coconut palm's +16.4 / +38.4, which is what makes a beach planted with both read as one set. ROSETTE CHECK: strongest angular harmonic n=4 carrying 34.9%, a shade over the accepted cove oak's 33% and far under the rejected cove pine's 71%. Accepted — a shrub built from leaf rosettes has some angular structure by construction, and the bilateral test below confirms it is not a stamped mandala. No halo: the ordering test reads -0.28 luma mean at display size, so the pixels ship exactly as delivered. Registered `ocean-naupaka`, world 40, plane surface, contact none.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH OF ONE LOW VINE SPRAWLING ACROSS BARE SAND, shot straight down from well above it. You are looking at a plant that lies FLAT ON THE GROUND — it has no height at all, so nothing here is seen from the side and nothing casts a shape but itself. BEACH MORNING GLORY — Ipomoea pes-caprae, the goat's-foot vine, the first plant to colonise an open beach and the one that holds the sand together. It is THE OPEN ONE of this venue's three ground plants, and its whole job is to soften bare sand WITHOUT adding bushy volume. THE RUNNERS ARE THE SUBJECT, AND THEY MUST READ AS LINES. From a single off-centre root, five to eight long stems run outward across the ground in different directions, each one a clean narrow line of reddish-green that stays about the same width for its whole length and never tapers away. They do not radiate evenly: two or three run much further than the rest, one or two bend and curve as they go, and one crosses over a neighbour. Along every runner, single rounded leaves are spaced out at intervals on short stalks, alternating from side to side, closer together near the root and further apart toward the tip. ⚠️ THE SPACE BETWEEN THE RUNNERS IS EMPTY AND IT IS MOST OF THE PICTURE. This is a net over the ground, not a mass: the transparent background shows through everywhere between the stems, in big open wedges, and the plant covers only about a third of the circle it reaches across. IF IT COMES BACK AS A SOLID ROUND CUSHION OF LEAVES IT IS WRONG — that is a bush, and this venue already has one. The only thing holding it together is the runners themselves meeting at the root. THE LEAF IS A GOAT'S FOOT, which is the species' name and its identifier at any size: a thick, glossy, almost circular leaf with a deep NOTCH cut into its outer tip, splitting it into two rounded lobes exactly like a cloven hoof print. Every leaf shows that notch. Twenty to thirty-five leaves in the whole plant, each one flat to the ground and drawn as one chunky two-tone shape with a hard edge. THE FLOWERS ARE THE ONE THING THAT IS NOT GREEN AND THEY CARRY THE PLANT AT SMALL SIZE. Three or four open trumpets, seen from DIRECTLY ABOVE so each is a flat round disc — a shallow five-lobed pinwheel with faint radiating seams and a small paler star at the centre where the throat goes down. A deep orchid magenta near #BD3995, with the throat a paler warm pink. NOT a hot fluorescent pink, not red, not purple-blue: a rich saturated pink-magenta. Set them on the runners, never at the root, and never all on one side. A couple of unopened buds, tight furled cones of the same colour, among them. THE GREEN IS A DEEP GLOSSY SEA-BEACH GREEN. Build the leaves from this set: a lit green near #3FA83F on the leaves that catch the sun, a mid green near #17751B, a full-bodied green near #0C5416, and a deep cool shade near #04310F where a leaf overlaps a runner. The runners themselves are a shade warmer and redder than the leaves. NO OLIVE, NO KHAKI, NO MUSTARD, NO TAN, NO ARMY DRAB AND NO DUSTY OR GREYED-DOWN GREEN. TAKEN AS A WHOLE THE PLANT REACHES AS FAR UP AS IT DOES ACROSS — the runners go out in all directions, so the overall spread is roughly as tall as it is wide, even though the plant itself is mostly empty space. It must not become a one-sided fan or a streak running off in a single direction. NO WATER ANYWHERE, and NO SAND IS DRAWN either even though sand is where it grows — the vine is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies the beach under it. No shadow, no footprints, no shells, no driftwood
assets.note: THE VENUE'S GROUNDCOVER, and the answer to a real gap: palm, pandanus, almond and naupaka are all MASSES, so a cay planted only with those is a set of blobs on blank sand. This is the one that softens open sand without adding another blob. See [[ocean-naupaka]] for the family's size ladder and shared reasoning. SIZE IS HONEST AND CONSERVATIVE: 30u = 3.26 m across. A real Ipomoea pes-caprae runner goes 10 m and more, so if anything this under-sells it; 30 was chosen to sit a clean 1.33x under the naupaka rather than to match the plant. ⚠️ THIS IS THE ONE ASSET IN THE VENUE THAT MUST FAIL THE COMPACTNESS TEST, and that has to be written down before delivery or it will be rejected by a check that does not apply. [[ocean-naupaka]] asks for eight tenths of its enclosing circle and the trees ask for seven; this asks for about ONE THIRD, because the open sand between the runners IS the asset. [[ocean-pandanus]] already came in at 52% against a 70% ask and was accepted on the same reasoning — a subject whose gaps are the point cannot be judged by fill. The invariant that DOES apply here is connectedness: every runner must meet at the root, so one connected piece, no leaf drifting free. Check that, and check the overall reach is roughly as tall as it is wide; ignore fill entirely. MAGENTA IS INFORMATION, NOT DECORATION, which is what earns it under art-pipeline 3c — colour that carries information wins even where it appears nowhere else in the venue, and this flower appears nowhere else by a wide margin: measured, #BD3995 sits dE 87-128 from every green in the venue's planting. At 30u the leaves are 3-4 px each and the flowers are most of what a player actually resolves, so they are doing the identification work. The subject deliberately says orchid-magenta and refuses HOT pink, because the prop venue clause names neon and hot pink as alien hues and a prompt that asks for one while the clause refuses it is the self-contradiction this pipeline has paid for twice. READS DARK ON BOTH GROUNDS: L* 42.7, so tropicscrub sits +26.2 above it and coralsand +48.2 — the strongest separation of the three underbrush, which it needs, being the most open. Colour-twinned with the pandanus at dE 7.9; separated on size (30 vs 52) and on silhouette (an open net against spiky rosettes), per [[ocean-naupaka]]'s note on the same situation with the palm. planRound true — the RUNNERS reach equally in all directions even though the plant is mostly empty, so the bbox test still catches a tilted camera. fillTo 0.86, anchor trunk-base at the root. NO allowSymmetry: evenly radiating runners would read as a starfish. Plane `surface`, contact none, when the art lands. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. DELIVERED AND ACCEPTED 2026-08-14, pre-cut with real alpha, 2048px master, ingested with no warnings (120px bake for 30px display). THE OPEN-NET CONSTRUCTION ARRIVED EXACTLY AS SPECIFIED — runners radiating from an off-centre root, unevenly, some crossing, with round notched goat's-foot leaves spaced along them, three open magenta trumpets and three furled buds. Aspect 1.003. ⚠️ CIRCLE FILL 21.4%, AND THAT IS THE ASSET WORKING, NOT FAILING. The note above warned that a check written for compact crowns would reject this; the delivery came back more open still. The invariant that DOES apply was checked and holds: ONE connected piece, every runner meeting at the root, no leaf drifting free. It is also the least self-similar sprite in the venue by a wide margin — bilateral correlation 0.127 against the shipped cove oak's 0.696 — which is exactly right for an irregular sprawl and the strongest evidence the openness is real rather than a symmetric starfish. MAGENTA IS 10.8% OF THE OPAQUE PIXELS and is what carries the plant at size. At 30px the leaves are a few pixels each; measured over the scrub the whole plant reads dE 29.7 from its ground while covering only 29% of its footprint, so most of what a player resolves is the flowers. That is the art-pipeline 3c argument paying off — information-carrying colour doing the identification. Body L* 39.3: scrub +29.6, sand +51.6, the strongest separation of the three underbrush, which the most open one needs. Angular harmonic n=5 at 15.3%, the lowest of the set. No halo (-0.21 luma at display size). Registered `ocean-morning-glory`, world 30, plane surface, contact none.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH OF ONE SMALL CLUMP OF COASTAL GRASS, shot straight down from well above it. Nothing of any side is visible: you see the top of the clump and nothing else. SALT-TOLERANT BEACH GRASS — the fine wiry bunchgrass of a windswept back-beach and a low sandy islet, sun-cured and dry. It is THE SOFT ONE of this venue's three ground plants, and it exists to break up open ground and make the place feel breezy, dry and exposed. IT IS A TUSSOCK, AND ITS OUTLINE IS SOFT AND FEATHERED — this is the single most important thing about the drawing, because there is another plant in this venue it must never be confused with. Its blades are FINE, NUMEROUS AND HAIR-LIKE: many thin threads springing from a tight base, arching outward and DROOPING so their tips bend over and down, giving a rim that is soft, wispy and broken. It is NOT a star, NOT a spiky rosette, and NOT built from a few chunky straps with hard edges and sharp points — that is a screw pine and it is the wrong plant. Where a strap plant has ten stiff blades, this has fifty fine ones. TWO OR THREE TUSSOCKS, NOT ONE, at plainly different sizes and merged where they touch, so the clump reads as a patch of grass rather than a single specimen. One obviously the largest, the others crowding it off to one side. They form ONE connected patch: no tussock floats off on its own. IT IS SUN-CURED, AND THAT IS ITS COLOUR. Most of every blade is a dry STRAW GOLD, warm and clean: a lit tone near #E0BC7C on the tips that catch the sun and a body near #D1A964 through the mass. Down at the base, where the clump is still alive and shaded, it goes GREEN — a mid green near #6E8A2E deepening to near #3A4A16 in the dark heart of the clump, so the patch reads gold at the rim and green at the middle. THAT TWO-TONE IS DELIBERATE AND MUST NOT BE FLATTENED: the gold is what makes this plant legible against green ground, and the green base is what keeps it from reading as dead straw. IT IS DRY, NOT DEAD, AND NOT DIRTY. Nothing here is grey, khaki, army drab, dusty, brown, rust or muddy. Cured grass in hard tropical sun is a warm clean gold, closer to wheat or straw than to earth; if a tone is in doubt push it toward YELLOW and toward LIGHT, never toward grey and never toward brown. TWO OR THREE FINE SEED SPIKES stand up out of the clump, each a slender straight stem with a narrow head of tiny grains, a shade darker than the blades. No more than three, and none of them longer than about a third of the clump's width — this is drawn very small and they are the first thing that will turn to mush. THE SILHOUETTE IS AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE and the clump is compact taken as a whole: draw the smallest circle that contains it and the grass fills about six tenths of it. Uneven at the rim, yes; drifting apart into a streak or a crescent, no. NO WATER ANYWHERE, and NO GROUND IS DRAWN — dry sand is where it grows, not something painted into the sprite. The clump is alone on a transparent background. No shadow, no soil, no shells, no flowers, no driftwood
assets.note: THE VENUE'S FILLER, for windy scrubby back-beach and low island interiors. Smallest asset Bluewater Bonanza has. See [[ocean-naupaka]] for the family's ladder and shared reasoning. ⚠️ SIZE IS EXAGGERATED AND THE MANIFEST'S SCALE BLOCK REQUIRES THAT TO BE DECLARED: a real coastal bunchgrass tussock is 0.6-1 m across, which is 6-9u and cannot carry a silhouette — the same argument the scale note makes for the penguin at 4.6px. 20u is about 2.2 m, so roughly a 2.5x exaggeration, and the subject compensates by asking for TWO OR THREE tussocks merged rather than one giant one, so what is drawn is an honest patch at an honest size rather than one implausible plant. ⚠️ THE ONLY PLANT IN THE VENUE THAT DOES NOT READ DARK, and the reason is measured. Every other planting here is a dark mass on a lighter ground — the trees run +16 to +37 L* below tropicscrub. A sun-cured grass is genuinely LIGHTER than the sward it stands in, so this one sits at L* 71.5 against the ground's 68.9: 2.5 L* ABOVE it, effectively equal. It therefore separates on HUE AND CHROMA INSTEAD, and that is what picked the colour. Swept against both its grounds, a straw gold at hue 38 lands dE 32.4 from tropicscrub and 35.7 from coralsand — comparable to the coconut palm's own 31.8 against the scrub — where the obvious yellow-green answer (hue 60-68, matching the ground's family) measured dE 6.4-13.3 and would have been invisible on the exact ground this asset exists to break up. IF A DELIVERY COMES BACK YELLOW-GREEN RATHER THAN GOLD, REJECT IT: it will disappear into the scrub, which is the one thing this slot cannot do. IT IS ALSO THE ONLY NON-GREEN VEGETATION IN THE VENUE, which is a bonus rather than the reason — it gives a planted interior a second colour without a second species. ⚠️ CONFUSABILITY WITH [[ocean-pandanus]] IS THE REAL RISK AND THE SUBJECT ATTACKS IT DIRECTLY. Both are radiating blade plants drawn from above, and the pandanus is itself 'two to six spiky rosettes clustered', which is structurally what a grass patch is. The separations: 20u against 52u (2.6x), gold against green (dE 54.7), and — the one that survives colour removal, which is what art-pipeline 2 actually requires — FINE SOFT FEATHERED blades that droop, against FEW STIFF CHUNKY straps with hard edges and points. The subject names the screw pine as the wrong answer explicitly, the bayou-moss method: state the geometry, give the correct read, then name the failure so a generator can refuse it. AT 20u THE DETAIL BUDGET IS ABOUT 20 SCREEN PIXELS, so the subject asks for the blade mass, the arch, the two-tone and at most three seed spikes, and nothing else. The cove's hydrangeas ship at 18u, so this size is proven, but they carry one flower head and no interior structure at all. Anything more here delivers mush. planRound true, fillTo 0.86, anchor trunk-base, no allowSymmetry. Plane `surface`, contact none, when the art lands. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. DELIVERED AND ACCEPTED 2026-08-14, pre-cut with real alpha, 2048px master, ingested with no warnings (80px bake for 20px display). Two merged tussocks with fine drooping blades, gold at the rim and green at the heart, three seed spikes — the whole construction as asked, and NOT a small pandanus: the blades are fine and feathered where a screw pine's are few and stiff. Aspect 1.024, one connected patch (99.95% in the largest component; the rest are blade tips detached by antialiasing). ⚠️ THE TWO-TONE IS WHAT MAKES THIS WORK AND IT ARRIVED: 68.9% of opaque pixels are warm straw and 27.2% are the green base. The gold is the majority tone, which is what the colour argument depended on. ⚠️ IT CAME BACK 12 L* DARKER THAN SPEC AND STILL PASSES — read this before 'correcting' it. The slot specified a mean of #D1A964 at L* 71.5, deliberately 2.5 L* ABOVE the scrub ground, on the reasoning that a cured grass is lighter than the sward it stands in. The delivery means #9D8A4E at L* 58.1, i.e. 10.8 BELOW the ground — apparently a miss on the one axis the slot cared about. It is not, because a raw mean is the wrong statistic for a finely feathered subject: most of this sprite's area is the dark air between hair-thin blades, which drags the mean down while contributing nothing to what a player sees. MEASURED THE WAY IT SHIPS — the 20px sprite composited over the ground it stands on — it reads dE 27.1 from tropicscrub and 32.3 from coralsand, against the naupaka's 27.3 and the swept target of ~32. The hue-not-value strategy holds intact. COMPOSITE AT DISPLAY SIZE BEFORE JUDGING ANY SPARSE SUBJECT'S COLOUR; the master's mean will lie to you in proportion to how much air it contains. ⚠️ ANGULAR HARMONIC n=2 AT 66.8%, WHICH LOOKS LIKE A REJECT AND IS NOT. It is close to the cove pine's rejected 71% and would fail the check as written. But n=2 is BILATERAL, not rotational — it is what any compact, roughly balanced blob scores, and it says nothing about the flower/rosette defect the metric exists to catch. Tested directly by mirroring the sprite onto itself: left-right correlation 0.592, against the SHIPPED AND ACCEPTED cove-oak-black at 0.696. The accepted art is more self-similar than this is. THIS IS THE THIRD TIME IN ONE SESSION AN ANGULAR METRIC HAS MISFIRED ON A SUBJECT IT WAS NOT WRITTEN FOR — the pandanus's n=3 was its head count, the almond's bullseye was invisible to it entirely (that needed a cap-offset test), and this n=2 is compactness. The rule that falls out: the polar spectrum only answers 'is this a ring of identical things around a hub'. For anything else, pick the test that matches the defect. No halo (+0.05 luma at display size, the cleanest of the three). Registered `ocean-grass-coastal`, world 20, plane surface, contact none.

assets.subject: A NORTHERN WOODLAND FLOOR seen from directly overhead from about ten metres up, in flat even light — the dry forest ground of a Minnesota lake country pine wood in late summer, under a canopy that keeps most of the rain off. IT IS DRY AND FIRM, NOT WET, and that is the first thing to get right. This is packed earth with litter worked into it, not mud: nothing shines, nothing is dark and slick, there is no standing water, no wet gleam and no boggy black. AT THIS HEIGHT NOTHING RESOLVES AS AN OBJECT, and that is the subject. The ground reads as a QUIET MOTTLED SURFACE — soft irregular patches of slightly different tone drifting into one another with no hard edges, at roughly the same density everywhere. Four things are mixed through it and all four are drawn as TONE, not as things you could pick up: dry medium-brown soil showing through as the base; a scatter of rusty and tan LEAF FRAGMENTS, broken and half-buried, each a small soft shape and never a whole outlined leaf; drifts of muted grey-tan PINE NEEDLES lying in loose aligned rafts a few centimetres long, which are the finest marks in the picture; and occasional small patches of dull MOSS in a soft grey-green, flat and soft-edged, covering perhaps a tenth of the frame. A few tiny dark twigs, thin and short, scattered very sparsely. NOTHING IS A LANDMARK. No pinecone drawn as a recognisable pinecone, no large root, no log, no rock, no mushroom, no flower, no single leaf big enough to name — the engine repeats this square dozens of times across a landmass and any feature you could point at becomes a stamp the player can count. Keep every mark small: nothing may run more than about a third of the way across the frame. NOTHING LINES UP. No raked direction, no drifts running one way across the picture, no repeating spacing, and nothing in the frame agreeing with anything else. The needle rafts each have their own local direction and those directions disagree. THE WHOLE IMAGE HOLDS A NARROW WARM BROWN RANGE from #635843 to #A8946C around a mean of #8A7752 — a muted earthy brown, warm but not orange, with the rust of the leaf fragments and the grey-green of the moss as the only departures from it. NOTHING HERE IS BLACK BOG, WET CHOCOLATE, ORANGE CLAY, RED EARTH OR GREY DUST, and nothing is the olive of a swamp. Hold the whole image inside a narrow value range. No grass, no lush green, no thick carpet of whole leaves, no water, no shoreline, no footprints, no trail, no tyre tracks, no cast shadows and no light direction
assets.note: STILLWATER LAKE'S DEFAULT GROUND, and the material most of the venue is made of — under the forest, between the cabins, around the trails. Registered as the `forestfloor` kind / `forestfloor` look, label 'Forest Floor'. The venue had authored all eight of its islands as `isle`, the shared ocean-beach tan, which is the right default and says nothing about where it is; this is the first of three grounds that say Minnesota. ⚠️ THE MEAN IS LIGHTER THAN A WOODLAND FLOOR PHOTOGRAPH AND THAT IS THE POINT. L* 50.9 was picked against the TREES rather than against reference: it sits +22 above a white pine crown and +29 above a balsam fir, inside the cove's accepted +26/+37 band, so dark conifers read against it — and it sits 13-19 L* BELOW a paper birch or aspen crown, which is the same relationship inverted. This is the first ground in the game that has to carry BOTH light trees and dark trees, and a medium value is the only thing that lets both read. Darkening it toward the bayou's browns for richness would erase the birch. SEPARATIONS: in-venue, which is what matters in play, 22.9 from [[lake-sand]] and 28.9 from [[lake-gneiss]], against the cove's accepted sand-vs-rock 23.9. Cross-venue its nearest are `marsh` at 12 and `mudflat` at 11 — picker-only, since a lake and a bayou can never share a race, and both are comfortably past the 5.3 the coastalrock note calls a real collision. tile 128: leaf fragments and needle rafts are centimetre-scale and land at true size there, with the swards and sands. ALPHA 0.45 IS A GUESS. Measure it on delivery and expect to come DOWN — four grounds running have now come off their pre-registered value (marsh 0.5->0.40, coastalscrub 0.5->0.40, ocean-scrub 0.40->0.30, ocean-coralrock 0.35->0.20) and every one of them downward. Land inside the set's on-screen sd band of 1.38-6.66; a litter floor should sit at the quiet end, nearer bay-sand's 2.78 than grass's 6.66, because it is the surface a whole forest of props is drawn on top of. WHAT TO CHECK ON DELIVERY: seamless wrap on all four edges; mean within ~3 of #8A7752, then reset the ISLAND_STYLES body to it; no countable feature (a drawn pinecone or a whole leaf is the likeliest failure); nothing wet or black; and the needle rafts disagreeing about direction rather than combing one way. DELIVERED AND ACCEPTED 2026-08-14. Mean #7C633D against a spec of #8A7752 (dE 8.4), sd 6.97 at tile 128, wrap clean at 1.17/1.07. ALPHA MEASURED TO 0.45 — the pre-registered value, and the first on this venue that needed no correction, because the master arrived quiet: 6.97 against the ocean pair's 21.79 and 19.17. It lands on-screen sd 3.13, between bay-sand (2.78) and bay-lane (3.63), which is where the surface a whole forest is drawn on top of belongs. Verified in the running game at a rendered 3.30. ⚠️ THE DELIVERY IS 7.5 L* DARKER THAN SPEC AND THE TREE MARGINS MOVED WITH IT. This body was chosen against the TREES, not against reference — see the slot above — so a shift in it is a shift in the whole venue's canopy contrast. Measured: the white pine's margin fell from +22.1 to +14.7 and the balsam fir's from +28.1 to +20.8, while the paper birch improved from -9.2 to -16.5 and the bracken fern from -2.4 to -9.8. Accepted, because the darker floor moved the compromise toward the side that was always weaker: a ground carrying BOTH light and dark canopy cannot favour both, and the light half had almost no margin. All four still clear on dE (33.8 to 49.4). If the conifers ever read muddy against it, the fix is a lighter REDRAW, not a body nudge — base must equal tile mean. PERIODICITY 2.75 peak/mean, the lowest of any tile in the game, and absolute repeat amplitude 0.54 against grass's 3.34. Nothing to watch. In-venue triangle came out BETTER than spec: 26.0 to [[lake-sand]] and 28.5 to [[lake-gneiss]], against 22.9 and 28.9 planned.

assets.subject: A NORTHERN LAKE BEACH seen from directly overhead from about ten metres up, in flat even light — the coarse glacial shore of a Minnesota lake, where the sand was ground out of granite by ice rather than out of coral by the sea. IT IS SAND WITH STONES IN IT, and that mixture is the whole subject. The base is a warm buff-tan sand, quiet and near-featureless the way sand is from this height, with only broad soft patches of slightly different tone drifting through it. Scattered evenly but unevenly through that base lie SMALL ROUNDED PEBBLES — cool grey and grey-tan, each one a simple smooth blob a few centimetres across with a soft lighter crown and a slightly darker underside, all of them water-worn and none of them angular or broken. Perhaps a fifth of the frame is pebble; the rest is sand. Sizes vary plainly, from grit up to a stone that would fill a palm, and the bigger ones are much rarer than the small. A FEW DARKER DAMP PATCHES drift through at the largest scale — soft, wide, edgeless areas where the sand is a shade deeper and cooler, as it is near a waterline. Tone only, never a shape with an edge, and never a hard wet line. NOTHING LINES UP. No ripple, no crest, no parallel banding, no repeating spacing, no sorted stripes of pebble, and no direction the eye can follow. The pebbles must not fall into rows or rings, and no two areas of the frame may look like each other. THE WHOLE IMAGE HOLDS A NARROW RANGE from #9E917C to #D4C7B0 around a mean of #BCAE97 — a warm buff, clearly GREYER AND COOLER than a tropical beach and clearly WARMER than bare stone. THIS IS NOT A CORAL BEACH: nothing here is near-white, nothing is pink, and there is no shell, no coral fragment, no dune and no seaweed. Nor is it mud or soil. Hold the whole image inside a narrow value range. No water, no foam, no waterline, no vegetation, no driftwood, no footprints, no tracks, no raked pattern, no cast shadows and no light direction
assets.note: SWIMMING BEACHES, CANOE LAUNCHES AND CAMP WATERFRONTS — the places a player's eye lands when it reaches the shore. Registered as the `lakesand` kind / `lakesand` look, label 'Lake Sand'. ⚠️ IT IS A SEPARATE KIND FROM `isle` ON PURPOSE, and the case has to be made because `isle` is already 'Coastal Sand' and already the lake's default. `isle` is a warm tan OCEAN beach shared by bay, lake and lagoon; this is a glacial lake shore, greyer and coarser, with rounded granite pebbles worked through it. Measured, the two sit dE 13.5 apart — against the 16.8 that separates `coralsand` from that same `isle`, so this is the same size of statement Pearl Lagoon's white sand already makes and is precedented. Its nearest neighbour anywhere is bay's `lane` at 7.4, which is honest rather than awkward: crushed shell and glacial gravel are both pale mixed aggregate, and a village road and a lake beach can never share a race. In-venue: 22.9 from [[lake-forestfloor]] and 22.7 from [[lake-gneiss]]. THE PEBBLES ARE THE ASSET. Without them this is just a slightly grey beach and the kind does not earn its row; the brief's 'slightly coarse, glacial feel' is carried entirely by the stone fraction, so a delivery that comes back as clean sand with a tint should be rejected however pleasant it looks. Aim for about a fifth of the frame in pebble. tile 128 with the other sands. ALPHA 0.55 IS A GUESS and is deliberately above the sands' usual 0.70 floor being lowered rather than raised — this tile carries real objects where lagoon-coralsand carries almost nothing, so it will arrive far busier than coralsand's luma sd 2.64. Measure it; see [[lake-forestfloor]] for the four-in-a-row record of pre-registered alphas coming down. WHAT TO CHECK ON DELIVERY: wrap; mean within ~3 of #BCAE97, then reset the body; pebbles present at roughly a fifth of the frame and ROUNDED, not angular; no shell, coral or dune; and no sorted stripes or rings in the stone scatter. DELIVERED AND ACCEPTED 2026-08-14. Mean #B7A487 against a spec of #BCAE97 (dE 5.3), sd 9.32 at tile 128, wrap clean at 1.02/0.91. THE PEBBLES ARRIVED and they are what the slot was written for — rounded, plainly varied in size, roughly a fifth of the frame, with the broad damp patches drifting through as asked. ALPHA MEASURED TO 0.45, down from the pre-registered 0.55: it lands on-screen sd 4.19, between bay-lane (3.63) and arctic granite (4.89). That is deliberately louder than every shipped sand (bay-sand 2.78, coralsand 1.85) because those tiles carry almost nothing and this one carries real stones; at 0.30 the pebbles fade to a mottle and the kind stops earning its row. ⚠️ ITS PERIODICITY SCORE OF 21.4 IS A FALSE ALARM, and this is the third time this metric has misfired in one session. peak/mean 21.4 at 2 cycles is far past the shipped 8.65-12.18 band and reads as a reject; in absolute terms the dominant band carries amplitude 1.75, BELOW every shipped ground (grass 3.34, bay-scrub 3.72, marsh 3.68). The ratio is normalised by the broadband floor, so a smooth tile inflates it. Judge on absolute amplitude. Separations delivered: 26.0 from [[lake-forestfloor]], 25.5 from [[lake-gneiss]].

assets.subject: BARE GLACIER-WORN BEDROCK seen from directly overhead from about ten metres up, in flat even light — the ancient granite and gneiss of the Canadian Shield where it comes out at a Minnesota lake shore, scraped bare and rounded by the ice sheet that passed over it. SMOOTHED, NOT SHATTERED, and this is the whole difference between this rock and a mountain one. The surface reads as BROAD FLAT SHELVES AND ROUNDED SLABS: a few large irregular polygonal areas, each one a wide gently domed plane a shade lighter across its crown and a shade darker where it rolls away, meeting their neighbours along soft shallow seams. Every edge in this image has been worn round. There are no knife-edged fractures, no sharp angular plates, no fresh broken faces, no scree, no rubble and no cliff. THE MINERAL BANDING IS WHAT MAKES IT GNEISS. Through the grey stone run BROAD SOFT BANDS of different mineral — a warm dusty PINK feldspar, a rusty iron-stained brown, and a cool CHARCOAL band — each one a wide irregular sweep with soft edges, following its own wandering line across a slab and passing under the seams between slabs as though the rock were one body. Three or four such bands in the whole frame, restrained: this is a grey rock with colour IN it, not a colourful rock. A FEW CRACKS, and only a few — three or four thin darker lines wandering across the stone, curving and irregular, never a network, never a grid and never parallel. Here and there a shallow hollow holds a little grit or a patch of pale crusty LICHEN, drawn as a faint soft paling of the stone's own colour with no hard edge and no hue of its own. NOTHING LINES UP. No bedding direction the whole frame agrees on, no parallel seams, no repeating spacing, and nothing in one part of the picture matching another. THE WHOLE IMAGE HOLDS A NARROW COOL GREY RANGE from #74737B to #AFAEB6 around a mean of #93929A, with the pink and rust bands reaching a little warmer and the charcoal band a little darker. IT IS A COOL MEDIUM GREY: never the warm grey-tan of a New England headland, never black volcanic basalt, never an orange or rust sandstone, and never the near-white of limestone. Hold the whole image inside a narrow value range. No water, no wet rock, no waterline, no moss beds, no grass, no soil, no trees, no snow and no cast shadows
assets.note: THE HARD-ROCK ACCENT THAT MAKES THE LAKE READ AS NORTHERN — rocky points, tiny islands, shoreline shelves, the occasional boulder in the forest. Registered as the `gneiss` kind / `gneiss` look, label 'Glacial Granite'. ⚠️ IT IS NOT `granite`, AND THAT IS THE ONE CONFUSION THIS SLOT EXISTS TO PREVENT. `granite` is Glacier Sound's rock: dark cold blue-grey (#4b5563), FRACTURED, drawn with the ANGULAR tracer and a low-poly lit-facet fan, standing 55 m up a mountainside. This is the opposite geology — the ice did not break this rock, it SMOOTHED it — so it is rounded shelves a couple of metres proud of the water in a cooler, much lighter medium grey, and its kind stays on the ROUNDED tracer with the sandbanks. The two are dE 27 apart and sort adjacent in the editor's list, so the labels do the rest of the work. Anyone who ever adds `gneiss` to the angular tracer has turned it into scree. SEPARATIONS: in-venue 28.9 from [[lake-forestfloor]] and 22.7 from [[lake-sand]]. Nearest anywhere is ocean's `coralrock` at 13.5 and bay's `coastalrock` at 15.9, both cross-venue and both comfortable — and all three are separated on HUE as much as value, this being the only cool one of the three (hue 248 against 42 and 44). tile 256, with the other two hard rocks and against the other two lake grounds' 128: a glacial slab is METRE-scale, so 256 spans 27.8 world metres and puts a shelf at several metres across, which is what it should be. Halving it to 128 would make this a cobble field, which is the exact failure bay-rock's note warns about. ALPHA 0.30 IS A GUESS — granite's own number, taken because this is a rock. Measure it; the mineral banding may well arrive louder than a plain stone and the whole set's on-screen sd band is 1.38-6.66, with the two shipped hard rocks at 2.85 and 4.89. WHAT TO CHECK ON DELIVERY, in order: wrap; mean within ~3 of #93929A, then reset the body; saturation LOW and hue COOL — a warm grey means it has drifted to coastalrock and should be rejected; every edge rounded, no angular fracture (this is the likeliest failure, because every generator has more mountain granite than shield rock in it); the pink/rust/charcoal banding present but restrained, crossing the seams rather than stopping at them; and no more than four cracks. DELIVERED AND ACCEPTED 2026-08-14. Mean #807A7F against a spec of #93929A (dE 9.3, 9 L* darker), sd 6.74 at tile 256. THE ROCK IS SMOOTHED, NOT SHATTERED — rounded slabs meeting along soft seams, no angular fracture anywhere, which was named as the likeliest failure because every generator has more mountain granite in it than shield rock. THE BANDING IS RESTRAINED AND THAT WAS MEASURED, NOT EYEBALLED. It reads bold at master scale and looks like marble at first glance; measured, warm pink/rust pixels above sat 0.10 are 9.9% of the tile and overall saturation is mean 0.055 / p95 0.125. That is a grey rock with colour in it, which is exactly what the subject asked for. ALPHA MEASURED TO 0.40, UP from the pre-registered 0.30 — the first alpha on this venue pair to be measured upward rather than down. The slab is smooth, and its mineral banding is the entire reason the kind exists, so 0.30 left it at on-screen sd 2.02 with the pink and rust barely reading; 0.40 lands 2.70, level with bay-rock's 2.85. ⚠️ ITS WRAP RATIO OF 1.50x IS ALSO A FALSE ALARM AND THE REASONING GENERALISES. ocean-coralrock measured 1.47x and needed its alpha held down to hide the seam; this measures 1.50x and needs nothing, because the ratio is against a very smooth interior — in ABSOLUTE terms the seam is 0.81 luma units at alpha 0.40, invisible at any setting. Between this and the periodicity scores on [[lake-sand]] and [[ocean-scrub]], the rule is now established: a normalised ratio inflates on a quiet tile, so measure seams and repeats in absolute luma before acting on either. Separations delivered: 28.5 from [[lake-forestfloor]], 25.5 from [[lake-sand]] — the whole in-venue triangle came out at or above plan.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH OF THE TOP OF ONE TREE, shot straight down from well above it the way a forestry survey frames a single specimen. YOU SEE FOLIAGE AND NOTHING ELSE: no trunk, no length of bark, no limb running away from you, no side of anything. AN EASTERN WHITE PINE — the biggest tree on the lake and the one the whole shore is built around. ⚠️ THIS TREE IS NEVER SEEN ALONE. Several hundred of it stand shoulder to shoulder along a Minnesota lake shore, and its real job is to be one tuft in an unbroken forest canopy seen from the air. Judge it by that: the crowns must MERGE into a continuous rough green texture the way a boreal forest does in an aerial photograph. ⚠️ SO THE SILHOUETTE MUST NOT BE EXOTIC. From straight above, a north-woods tree is a ROUGHLY ROUND, RAGGED, CLOSED LUMP OF FOLIAGE. It is NOT a wheel, NOT a rosette, NOT a star, NOT a sunburst, NOT a snowflake, and above all NOT A PALM: no long separate fronds, blades, plumes or arms radiating out of a middle, and NO VISIBLE HUB OR CENTRE for anything to radiate from. If a viewer could count the arms, it is wrong. If the lighting makes bright lines run outward from the centre like the ribs of an umbrella, it is wrong. Break up any such radial pattern: the light in this crown falls in IRREGULAR PATCHES that have nothing to do with the middle. WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE: A BIG SOFT DARK-GREEN CLOUD. Think of a head of broccoli, or a thundercloud seen from above, or moss on a stone — one continuous billowing mass with a bumpy edge. That is the whole shape. The crown is BROAD, CLOSED AND DEEP, and its interior is completely filled: there are no windows through it and no gaps reaching in toward the middle. Draw the smallest circle that contains the tree; the foliage fills about EIGHT TENTHS of it. ⚠️ THE OLD VERSION OF THIS PICTURE CAME BACK AS A COCONUT PALM AND THAT IS THE ONE FAILURE THAT MATTERS. It had six to nine long feathered plumes reaching out of a middle, and a whole shoreline of them looked like the South Pacific. THERE ARE NO PLUMES IN THIS TREE. There is no middle for them to come out of. Whatever internal structure the crown has runs SIDEWAYS AND CROOKED, never outward from a centre. THE SURFACE IS THE SUBJECT, and it is made of many small BILLOWS. Across the crown lie twenty or thirty rounded soft clumps of needle-mass, each a couple of finger-widths across, packed tight against one another and overlapping — some catching the light, some sunk in shade, arranged with no pattern whatsoever. Between and under them run narrow CROOKED DARK CREASES, a few pixels wide, wandering across the crown like the seams between clouds. The creases must NOT converge anywhere. THE EDGE IS SOFT AND SHAGGY. White pine needles are long, slender and carried in soft bundles of five, so the whole rim breaks into a fine fur of needle-points — never a clean cut outline, never a scalloped flower edge. The outline is IRREGULAR: broad gentle bumps and one or two shallow notches, heavier on one side than the other, the lopsided shape of a tree that has grown where it could. ⚠️ THE COLOUR IS A GREEN WITH A LITTLE BLUE IN IT, AND THE FAILURE HAS A NAME: TEAL. Build the crown from a lit tone near #3C7A55, a body near #2C5B3E, and a deep shade near #17351F in the creases and under the rim. NOT teal, NOT cyan, NOT turquoise, NOT mint, NOT sea-green, NOT the blue-grey of a Colorado spruce. If any green here is in doubt, push it toward the YELLOW-GREEN side, never toward blue: slightly too grassy is fine, slightly too blue is a reject. IT MUST STAY THE PALER, BIGGER CONIFER. Its neighbour the balsam fir is a small, tight, almost black-green button; this is a broad, soft, mid-green cloud roughly twice the fir's width and clearly lighter. That size-and-value step is how a player tells them apart, so do not let this crown go dark. A few small brown CONES, long and slender, two or three in the whole crown, half-sunk in the needles. They are the only warm thing in the picture. THE SILHOUETTE IS AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE — round taken as a whole, with the raggedness in the rim and never in the overall proportion. NO WATER ANYWHERE, and no ground is DRAWN — the tree is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies the forest floor it stands on
assets.note: FIRST OF STILLWATER LAKE'S THREE TREES. The set is separated on SILHOUETTE FIRST per art-pipeline 2's colour-removed test: this is an OPEN TIERED RAFT-CROWN, [[lake-birch-paper]] is an AIRY ROUND CROWN WITH WHITE BRANCHES SHOWING THROUGH, and [[lake-fir-balsam]] is a SMALL TIGHT DARK ROSETTE. Size ladder 110 / 80 / 55 — 1.38x and 1.45x apart, both past the cove family's 1.33x minimum. SIZE IS HONEST: an open-grown eastern white pine spreads about 12 m, and 12 x 9.2 units/m = 110u. It lands on the same number as swamp-oak and ocean-almond, the game's other two big land trees, which is a coincidence worth keeping — they really are comparable crowns. ⚠️ IT IS COLOUR-TWINNED WITH [[lake-fir-balsam]] AT dE 8.8 AND THAT IS CORRECT. Two dark blue-green conifers in the same wood ARE nearly the same colour; art-pipeline 2 asks that identity survive with colour REMOVED, and these two are separated on exactly that axis — 110u against 55u, and an open ragged raft-crown against a tight closed rosette. Do not tint one of them apart. Same situation as the ocean's naupaka and coconut palm at 3.6. READS DARK ON EVERY GROUND IT STANDS ON: crown L* 28.8 against forest floor 50.9 (+22.1), lake sand 71.7 (+42.9) and gneiss 60.9 (+32.0). The +22 is the tight one and it is deliberate — see [[lake-forestfloor]], whose value was picked to carry dark conifers AND a light birch at the same time. planRound true, fillTo 0.86, anchor trunk-base with no trunk drawn. NO allowSymmetry: a conifer from directly overhead is the strongest mandala attractor in this library — cove-pine-pitch took four rounds to beat it — which is why the subject states the plate construction rather than merely refusing a star. PLANE `surface`, CONTACT none WHEN THE ART LANDS, and for this venue that is decided rather than argued: nothing on Stillwater Lake sails under a tree, so there is no canopy case to make and no see-through requirement to buy. The ocean's palm and pandanus were briefly `canopy` and had to be moved back for exactly this reason. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6: slot, then art, then the kind. DELIVERED AND ACCEPTED 2026-08-15, pre-cut with real alpha, 2048px master, ingested with one benign warning (downsample from 2048 to the 1024 profile). Aspect 1.051, one connected crown, halo -0.06 luma at display size so the pixels ship as delivered. THE TIERED-RAFT CONSTRUCTION ARRIVED and the crown is genuinely open: circle fill 41.8% against the ~60% the subject asked for, i.e. MORE open than specified. Accepted — an airy white pine is the point, and openness is this species' whole character — but it is worth recording because [[lake-pine-red]] is specified at ~50% and will now be the LESS open of the two pines, inverting the intended relationship. If the red pine delivers near its spec, their separation rests entirely on construction (tufts flung around spreading branches against stacked flat rafts) and on the 1.25x size step, not on density. Mandala check passed comfortably: strongest angular harmonic n=3 at 21.4%, under the accepted cove oak's 33%, and mirror correlation 0.146 — the least self-similar sprite in this batch. Reads dark on its ground at L* 32.1 against the delivered forest floor's 43.4 (+11.5, dE 36.2). ⚠️ THE CONIFER PAIR DRIFTED TEAL AND DID IT TOGETHER. Both this and its sibling came back at green-hue 169.7 against a spec of ~150 — a cyan-leaning green rather than the blue-green asked for. Accepted, on two grounds. It is CONSISTENT: the two are dE 8.7 apart, essentially the number the slots predicted (8.8), so the pair still reads as one genus and the separation work still falls on size and construction where it was designed to. And it suits the venue card, which commits to 'deep lake blue and pine green' — a teal conifer sits with that water rather than against it. If either is ever redrawn, redraw BOTH: the one thing that must not happen is one blue-green pine beside one teal one. ⚠️ SUBJECT REWRITTEN 2026-08-15 AFTER THE FIRST DELIVERY, WHICH FAILED ON BOTH OF ITS OWN HEADLINE REQUIREMENTS. Both failures are measured, and both were caused by wording in the previous subject rather than by the generator, which is why the rewrite is specific rather than a reroll. (1) COLOUR: 99.4% of the delivered green pixels landed in the TEAL/CYAN band, hue 163-200, median 169.8 — against named hexes at hue 148-153. Essentially NONE of it (0.3%) was in the blue-green band the subject asked for. Naming hexes was not enough because the prose overrode them: the old text paired 'a cool blue-green' with 'if a green is in doubt push it toward BLUE, never toward yellow', and a one-way tiebreaker with no floor reads as an instruction to go as blue as the palette allows. The rewrite keeps hexes (nudged warmer to #3C7A55 / #2C5B3E / #17351F), REFUSES the failure by name — teal, cyan, turquoise, aquamarine, mint, sea-green, spruce blue-grey — and REVERSES the tiebreaker so doubt resolves toward yellow-green. Same pattern that fixed the bayou's moss and the cove's drab palette: state the geometry, name the failure, give the correct answer. (2) DENSITY: circle fill came back 43.5% against the ~60% asked, and within 80% of the outer radius only 65% of the crown was inked — a crown with real holes in it, reading as a starfish rather than a tree. Three clauses were all pushing the same way: 'FIVE TO EIGHT SEPARATE PLATES', 'THE CROWN IS AIRY AND YOU SEE THROUGH IT', and 'this is the airiest conifer here, and the gaps are the point'. The last is a comparative with no bound. The rewrite asks for SEVEN TENTHS fill, makes the plumes OVERLAP into one continuous canopy with a lobed rim, closes the middle outright, and confines openness to narrow slots between plume tips in the outer third. ⚠️ THIS ALSO REPAIRS AN INVERSION AGAINST [[lake-pine-red]], which is still a slot. Red pine is specified as the OPEN one — discrete tufts flung around spreading branches at ~50% fill, a genuine starburst — and the first white pine delivery came back MORE open than that at 43.5%, which would have made the two pines tell the wrong story about themselves. With this rewrite the pair reads correctly: white pine a broad closed mass at ~70%, red pine an airy starburst at ~50%, and the size step 110u against 88u on top. ⚠️ REDRAW THE BALSAM FIR IN THE SAME BATCH. [[lake-fir-balsam]] came back at the IDENTICAL median hue of 169.7 — the two conifers drifted together, which is why the original acceptance note recorded them as a consistent pair and let it stand. Fixing one alone would leave one blue-green pine beside one teal fir, which is worse than both being teal. If only one can be redrawn, redraw neither. WHAT TO CHECK ON THE NEW DELIVERY, in order: median green hue between 135 and 160 with under 5% of green pixels above 163 (the old one was 99.4% above it); circle fill 0.66 to 0.75; interior ink within 80% of the radius above 85%; one connected crown; strongest angular harmonic under 33%; and aspect under 1.12. REDELIVERED AND ACCEPTED 2026-08-15 against the rewritten subject, and BOTH of the original failures are gone by a wide margin. Colour: median green hue 138.9 against 169.8, with 0.0% of green pixels above hue 163 where the first delivery had 99.4% — the teal is not reduced, it is absent. Mean #385B41, dE 4.6 from the specced body. Density: interior ink within 80% of the radius is 99.3% against 65.0%, so the holes are gone; one connected crown; angular harmonic n=7 at 29.2%, under the accepted 33%; aspect 1.002. ⚠️ CIRCLE FILL CAME IN AT 85.7% AGAINST THE 66-75% WINDOW THE REWRITE ASKED FOR — it overshot in the same direction it previously undershot, and it is ACCEPTED. The window was a proxy for the real requirement, which was 'a broad closed mass with a lobed rim, not a starfish', and that is delivered: the rim is scalloped with real slots between plume tips, the middle is solid, and against [[lake-pine-red]]'s specced ~50% open starburst the pair now separates 1.7x on density instead of being inverted. The cost is that this is now marginally denser than [[lake-aspen-quaking]] at 83.4%, which was meant to be the dense one — accepted because those two carry no density work: they are dE 29 apart in colour, 110u against 68u, and needle plumes against small round leaves. LIGHT FRINGE CHECKED AND CLEARED. The master's partial-alpha rim measures 1.71x the core luminance, exactly the figure the pipeline README documents for cutting against white. At display size composited on [[lake-forestfloor]] the edge band sits at luma 91.6, BETWEEN the crown at 82.3 and the ground at 101.6 — a real halo sits above both, so this is ordinary antialiasing rather than a fringe. Ordering test +0.05 luma at 110px. ⚠️ NO RE-PLANT IS NEEDED, AND WORKING OUT WHY IS WORTH RECORDING. The first instinct was that doubling the crown's ink must invalidate the planter's coverage solve — it does not. plant_lake.py models every crown as a FULL DISC of world x scale and never reads the sprite, so the sprite's own fill fraction has never entered its arithmetic; re-running it after this delivery produced byte-identical output. What actually changed is the other way round: the old sprite inked only 43.5% of the disc the planter was charging it for, so the venue LOOKED far thinner than the 77.3% canopy the model claimed. At 85.7% the picture now matches what the planter always intended. THE LESSON FOR ANY PLANTER IN THIS REPO: its coverage figure is a disc-area model, not measured ink, so it is only honest to the extent the art fills its own frame — a sprite that undershoots its fill makes every coverage number in the report optimistic, silently. ⚠️ RE-BRIEFED 2026-08-15, THE SECOND REWRITE, AFTER AN AERIAL COMPARISON AGAINST FIVE PHOTOGRAPHS OF REAL MINNESOTA LAKES. THE DELIVERED CROWN READS AS A COCONUT PALM. The first rewrite fixed both faults it was aimed at — hue 169.8 -> 138.9, interior ink 65% -> 99.3% — and the tree still sank the venue, because BOTH REWRITES KEPT THE RADIAL PLUME STRUCTURE and that structure is the actual problem. ⚠️ AND THE ACCEPTANCE METRIC MISSED IT, WHICH IS THE REAL LESSON. The angular-harmonic check reads the ALPHA channel, and this crown is closed, so it scored 3.7% — cleaner than anything else in the venue — while its arms were plainly visible. The arms are painted in LUMINANCE, not cut in alpha. Measured on luminance instead: white pine 17.6% angular harmonic and 2.26 radial-vs-tangential gradient, against [[ocean-palm-coconut]]'s 22.3% and 2.03. THE PINE IS MORE RADIALLY STREAKED THAN THE PALM. A closed silhouette is not evidence of a non-radial crown; SHADING MAKES FRONDS JUST AS WELL AS CUTTING DOES. Judge frond structure on luminance from now on — the alpha test cannot see it. ⚠️ ROOT CAUSE IS A DESIGN ERROR IN THE BRIEFS, NOT A GENERATOR FAILURE, and it is shared with [[lake-pine-red]] and [[lake-birch-paper]]. All three were written to be maximally distinguishable FROM EACH OTHER — plates and plumes, a starburst, an open skeleton — and each bought its distinction with a crown belonging to some other biome. That is art-pipeline.md §2 misapplied: §2 governs ROLES, where a hazard must never be confusable with ambient, and it says nothing about species inside one ambient role. A FOREST IS SEEN IN AGGREGATE. Individual legibility is worth almost nothing here and a wrong silhouette costs everything, because five hundred of them build the venue's whole read. [[lake-fir-balsam]] is the only one of the four that was allowed to be an ordinary dark tuft and it is the only one that reads as Minnesota. THE FIR IS NOW THE MODEL, and the separation moves onto SIZE and VALUE, which survive aggregation where silhouette novelty does not: fir a small near-black button at 55u, white pine a broad mid-green cloud at 110u. WHAT TO CHECK ON THE NEW DELIVERY: angular harmonic ON LUMINANCE under 6% (fir sits at 2.1%, the delivered pine at 17.6%); radial-vs-tangential gradient under 1.6; centre brightness within 15% of the crown mean, i.e. no hub; circle fill 0.76-0.86; interior ink above 92%; median green hue 135-160; mean L* between 32 and 40, which keeps it above the fir's 23.8 and below the aspen's 55.2. ⚠️ ACCEPTED 2026-08-15, SECOND REDELIVERY, AND THE PALM IS GONE. Measured against the checklist this slot registered: radial-vs-tangential gradient 1.18 (want <1.60), hub 1.03 (want 0.85-1.15), circle fill 77.8% (want 0.76-0.86), interior ink 99.8% (want >92%), green pixels above hue 163 0.0%, mean L* 35.8 (want 32-40), aspect 0.995. Mean #375C3F. TWO MARGINAL MISSES, BOTH ACCEPTED WITH REASONS. (1) Angular harmonic on luminance 6.9% against a <6% window. The window was extrapolated from [[lake-fir-balsam]]'s 2.1% without knowing what a BILLOWY crown scores, and a crown built from two dozen irregular clumps cannot score as flat as one built from an even nap. What settles it is that the harmonic does not distinguish RADIAL ARMS from RANDOM LUMPS, and the radial gradient ratio does: at 1.18 this is the LEAST radially organised crown in the venue — below the fir's own 1.91 and far below [[ocean-palm-coconut]]'s 2.03. Absolute amplitude tells the same story: peak 6.9% here, 17.6% on the rejected delivery, 22.3% on the palm. ⚠️ AND SPECTRAL CONCENTRATION IS USELESS FOR THIS — it came out 15%, 18%, 19% and 17% across the new pine, the rejected one, the palm and the fir, i.e. identical on crowns that look nothing alike. Judge frond structure on the RADIAL GRADIENT RATIO plus absolute amplitude; concentration discriminates nothing. That is the fifth time on this venue pair a normalised statistic has said nothing while an absolute one said everything. (2) Median green hue 134.4 against a 135-160 window — off by six tenths of a degree, with zero teal pixels and a mean that reads as plain forest green. Not worth a regeneration. SEPARATION AGAINST ITS NEIGHBOURS HOLDS: fir L* 23.8 at 55u with a fine even nap, this pine L* 35.8 at 110u with coarse billows, aspen L* 55.2 at 68u with round leaf-poms. Size, value and texture — three axes, none of them silhouette novelty.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH OF THE TOP OF ONE TREE IN FULL LEAF IN HIGH SUMMER, shot straight down from well above it the way a forestry survey frames a single specimen. A PAPER BIRCH, the pale broadleaf that lightens a dark spruce shore. ⚠️ THIS TREE IS NEVER SEEN ALONE. Several hundred of it stand shoulder to shoulder along a Minnesota lake shore, and its real job is to be one tuft in an unbroken forest canopy seen from the air. Judge it by that: the crowns must MERGE into a continuous rough green texture the way a boreal forest does in an aerial photograph. ⚠️ SO THE SILHOUETTE MUST NOT BE EXOTIC. From straight above, a north-woods tree is a ROUGHLY ROUND, RAGGED, CLOSED LUMP OF FOLIAGE. It is NOT a wheel, NOT a rosette, NOT a star, NOT a sunburst, NOT a snowflake, and above all NOT A PALM: no long separate fronds, blades, plumes or arms radiating out of a middle, and NO VISIBLE HUB OR CENTRE for anything to radiate from. If a viewer could count the arms, it is wrong. If the lighting makes bright lines run outward from the centre like the ribs of an umbrella, it is wrong. Break up any such radial pattern: the light in this crown falls in IRREGULAR PATCHES that have nothing to do with the middle. ⚠️ IT IS JULY, NOT MARCH. THE TREE IS IN FULL LEAF AND THE LEAVES HIDE THE TREE. An earlier version of this picture showed a spray of chalk-white limbs forking out through an open crown, and at a distance that reads as a DEAD OR LEAFLESS TREE — worse, it reads as a drawn skeleton laid on top of the foliage, and it made a radial star as surely as a palm frond does. NO BRANCH IS DRAWN AS A LINE ANYWHERE IN THIS PICTURE. WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE: A ROUNDED, FAIRLY DENSE, FINELY-TEXTURED PALE GREEN DOME. Draw the smallest circle that contains it; the foliage fills about EIGHT TENTHS of it, and within the inner four-fifths it is essentially unbroken. THE TEXTURE IS FINE AND BUSY, and this is what makes it a broadleaf rather than a conifer. The crown is built from many small OVAL LEAVES with finely toothed edges, gathered into loose soft sprays of five to ten, and the sprays are packed together across the whole crown so that they overlap. At this distance you read a fine even stipple of leaf, not individual leaves and not one smooth blob. THE WHITE BARK IS A HINT, NOT A SUBJECT. Paper birch is famous for it, and from directly above in summer you would catch only a GLIMPSE: in two or three places, deep inside a small gap between sprays, a short pale flick of chalk-white about a leaf long, half swallowed by shadow. Three such glimpses in the whole crown is the maximum. They sit at different distances from the middle, they do not line up, and no line connects them. ⚠️ IF THE WHITE FORMS A CONNECTED BRANCHING PATTERN THE PICTURE IS WRONG. THE OPENNESS BELONGS TO THE EDGE. Round the outer fifth the sprays separate a little and the rim goes soft and feathery, with small notches of dark between the outermost clusters — the light airy fringe a birch really does have. Inside that, closed. THE COLOUR IS A LIGHT, SLIGHTLY YELLOW GREEN, and it must stay the LIGHTEST TREE ON THE LAKE without becoming acid. Build it from a lit tone near #93B060, a body near #6E8F45, and a shade near #3E5628. NOT chartreuse, NOT lime, NOT fluorescent, NOT the grey-green of a willow. THE SILHOUETTE IS AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE, round taken as a whole, with a lopsided rim. NO WATER ANYWHERE, and no ground is DRAWN — the tree is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies the forest floor it stands on
assets.note: THE VENUE'S LIGHT TREE, and the reason [[lake-forestfloor]] is a medium brown rather than a dark one. Stillwater Lake is the first venue in the game whose canopy runs BOTH ways: two dark conifers at L* 29 and 23, and this at L* 60. A ground picked for the conifers alone would have swallowed this tree, so the floor sits between them at L* 50.9 — 9 L* below the birch and 22 above the pine. Anyone re-tuning any of the three has to re-check all of them together. SIZE IS HONEST: a paper birch spreads about 8.7 m, and 8.7 x 9.2 = 80u. Mid-rung of the 110 / 80 / 55 ladder. ⚠️ THE WHITE LIMBS ARE THE HARDEST CLAUSE HERE AND THE MOST IMPORTANT. This species is recognised entirely by its bark, and a plan view normally destroys exactly that — the same foreshortening problem the bayou's spanish moss and the ocean pandanus's stilt roots each had, and the first two were solved by REMOVING the feature. Birch is the case where the opposite answer is right: the crown is genuinely open enough that the limbs show through, so the subject asks for them explicitly, as bright lines UNDER the foliage. If a delivery comes back as a solid green dome it has lost the species and should be rejected however good the dome is. ⚠️ CIRCLE FILL IS ASKED AT ~50%, WELL UNDER THE FAMILY'S USUAL 70%, and that is stated here so a check written for compact crowns does not reject it — the same pre-emption [[ocean-morning-glory]] needed, and for the same reason: the gaps ARE the asset. The invariant that does apply is connectedness. COLOUR-TWINNED WITH [[lake-fern-bracken]] at dE 9.7, both being light yellow-greens. Separated on size (80u against 34u, 2.35x) and on silhouette (an open limbed crown against a rosette of triangular fronds), which is what art-pipeline 2 actually requires. Against the grounds: dE 46.5 from the forest floor, 53.3 from lake sand, 66.9 from gneiss — the strongest separations of any plant in the venue. planRound true, fillTo 0.86, no allowSymmetry. Plane `surface`, contact none when the art lands. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. DELIVERED AND ACCEPTED 2026-08-15. Aspect 1.010, circle fill 44.4% against the ~50% asked, halo -0.51. ⚠️ THE WHITE LIMBS CAME THROUGH, WHICH WAS THE WHOLE RISK OF THE SLOT. Chalk-white branches fork outward and show clearly between the leaf sprays, exactly as the subject demanded, and at 80px they are what identifies the tree. This is the counter-example to the bayou moss and the ocean pandanus's stilt roots — the two cases where a plan view destroyed the identifier and the fix was to REMOVE it. Here the crown was open enough to keep it, and asking for it explicitly worked first time. ⚠️ THE CONNECTEDNESS CLAUSE IS TECHNICALLY MISSED AND IT IS ACCEPTED. At full resolution the sprite is 47 pieces with 8.8% of its area outside the largest — the subject says 'nothing floats free'. Measured rather than eyeballed: the biggest stray is 0.514% of the sprite, and they are leaf clusters sitting at branch tips whose stalks are thinner than a pixel at display size. That is not the failure the clause was written against, which was cove-pine-pitch coming back as three disconnected pieces at 59% fill with tufts floating in clear space. A rule of thumb worth keeping: judge connectedness on the SIZE of the strays, not their count — 46 sub-pixel fragments at a branch tip read as attached, one 5% fragment in open space does not. Mean #8E9F4C, dE 18.4 from spec — the loosest colour match of the batch, greyer and a touch more olive than asked, and it costs nothing: the birch is 19.1 L* LIGHTER than the forest floor at dE 34.3, and dE 16.1 from [[lake-aspen-quaking]]. Warm pixels 8.3%, which is the brown catkins and branch shadow, not autumn. Angular n=9 at 12.6%, mirror 0.165. ⚠️ SUBJECT REWRITTEN 2026-08-15 AFTER THE AERIAL COMPARISON. THE DELIVERY WAS FAITHFUL TO THE BRIEF AND THE BRIEF WAS WRONG — it asked outright for an open crown with 'CHALK-WHITE LIMBS showing clearly, forking outward from the middle', on the reasoning that a birch's whole identity is its bark and an open crown is the only way to show bark from overhead. That reasoning holds for ONE tree on a sheet and fails for four hundred on a shore: measured, the delivery is 42.9% circle fill with only 60.9% interior ink and a 30.3% angular harmonic in alpha — the openest, most radial crown in the venue. In a wide shot a stand of it reads as WINTER, as a scatter of bare dead trees among live conifers. THE BARK WAS NOT WORTH IT. A player never identifies a species at race framing; they read a shoreline. The identity a birch actually needs to carry here is VALUE — it is the pale tree that lifts a dark conifer wood — and value survives aggregation where a branch pattern does not. So the bark drops to at most three disconnected flicks and the crown closes to 0.80 fill. WHAT TO CHECK: circle fill 0.76-0.86; interior ink above 92%; angular harmonic under 8% in ALPHA and under 8% ON LUMINANCE (the alpha test alone missed the palm structure in [[lake-pine-white]] — see that note); no connected white path longer than about a tenth of the crown width; mean L* 55-63, keeping it the lightest tree. ⚠️ ACCEPTED 2026-08-15 ON THE FIRST DELIVERY OF THE REWRITTEN BRIEF, EVERY CHECK PASSED. circle fill 81.4% (want 0.76-0.86), interior ink 99.1% (want >92%), angular harmonic 0.1% in alpha and 6.8% on luminance (want <8% on both), radial gradient ratio 1.11, longest connected white-bark run 0.8% of crown width (want <10%), mean L* 59.3 (want 55-63), aspect 1.018. Mean #86954D — still the lightest tree on the lake, which was the identity worth keeping. MASTER ARRIVED 2816x1536, NOT SQUARE, and was cropped to a 1564px square centred on the content bbox with a 5% margin before ingest. The content was already centred to within two pixels of the canvas centre and its own aspect was 1.018, so the crop is a reframe and not a rescale — no pixel was resampled and every edge came out at alpha 0.
