PLANE `float`, CONTACT hard, contactR about 14 measured off the bake — and unlike almost every other hard prop in this library, the circle FITS: the raft is square, so a circle at half its width covers the middle and under-covers only the corners, which is the safe direction. It is also large, static and unmissable, which satisfies the shoal note's fairness test. This is a genuine obstacle in the racing water and is meant to be. ⚠️ planRound TRUE even though a square is not a circle, and the reason is what the flag actually gates: it selects the acceptance test, and the test is whether the content is as tall as it is wide. A square passes that honestly and a tilted camera still fails it, so the check does exactly the work it is there for. Do not read planRound as 'this subject is a disc'. COLOUR: pale sun-bleached deck at dE 46.9 from the lake water it floats on, which is what a small object on open water needs. It measures dE 3.4 from [[lake-sand]], which sounds alarming and is not — a raft is never on a beach, and the two can only meet if a designer puts one on dry land. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. DELIVERED 2026-08-15 AND INGESTED. GEOMETRY IS EXACTLY RIGHT and the planRound check earns its keep here: content measures 1224x1212, an aspect of 1.01, so the square is honestly square and the camera is honestly overhead. Everything the subject allows is present and nothing it forbids is: planks running one way, darker rim board, aluminium ladder projecting past one edge, two dark cleats at opposite corners with rope, float barrels showing as dark bands past the rim on two sides. Reads unmistakably at 33px on both waters and cannot be confused with a hull — it is square where every boat is elongated. ⚠️ THE COLOUR IS WRONG AND IT IS THE ONE THING TO FIX. The subject asks for sun-bleached pale (#C8BAA2 lit, #B0A088 body) with the reasoning stated — this stands in open water all summer and should be LIGHTER and greyer than the shore dock. What arrived is fresh orange pine: lit-half median RGB 255,215,169 at dE 19.7 from the declared lit tone and 26.1 from the body, with median chroma 86 against roughly 38 for the spec, i.e. more than twice the colour asked for. It is the exact tone [[lake-dock]]'s subject bans by name ('NOTHING HERE IS ORANGE PINE'), and the two are meant to be the two halves of one cabin waterfront — shipped as they stand, the raft is new lumber moored off a dock that has silvered for ten winters. Contrast against water survives the error (it is bright, so it separates), which is why it ships, but this is a desaturate-and-cool pass or a regeneration, not something to leave. contactR about 14 off the bake still holds: fillTo 0.86 makes world 33 a 28px raft. RESOLVED 2026-08-15 — RECOLOURED IN PLACE RATHER THAN REGENERATED, and it landed on the numbers. The fix is three affine maps in LAB fitted on the lit and shade anchors: L' = 1.136L - 24.1, a' = 0.15a, b' = 0.51b. MEASURED AFTER: deck L p78/p12 = 76.0/49.7 against a spec of 76.1/49.3, chroma median 14.3 against ~14, and the lit-half median lands at RGB 201,186,162 — dE 0.3 from the declared #C8BAA2, down from 19.7. ⚠️ IT IS NOT A DESATURATION AND TREATING IT AS ONE WOULD HAVE FAILED. The delivered red channel was CLIPPED AT 255, which collapsed the lit and body tones onto each other (L 88.2 against 86.6) where the spec separates them by ten points; scaling chroma alone would have produced a flat grey deck with no plank separation left. The L map has slope 1.136 — it EXPANDS the tonal range — and that is what puts the plank definition back. Visibly better at 4x than the delivery. WEIGHTED BY CHROMA, NOT MASKED. A smoothstep from C 10 to C 22 carries the deck at C 29+ fully and leaves the low-chroma furniture alone: the aluminium ladder, the two cleats, the rope and the float barrels measure a MAXIMUM RGB SHIFT OF 0.0 across 39,738 px. A binary wood mask would have banded along its own edge. The recoloured file is what sits in inbox/, so re-ingest is idempotent; the delivered orange original is on the Desktop as swim-raft.png. It now matches [[lake-dock]] as one weathered-timber waterfront, which was the point.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. A PATCH OF BULRUSH standing in the shallows at a lake edge, seen from straight down and ALONE — no water drawn, no bottom, no shore. IT IS A STAND OF SEPARATE STEMS, NOT A BUSH, and that is the whole read. Bulrush grows as many slender round stems pushed straight up out of the water, each one on its own, so from directly above you are looking at the TOPS OF THE STEMS — a scatter of many small rounded dots and short strokes, densest in the middle of the patch and thinning to singles around the edge. Thirty to sixty of them. There is no canopy, no mass of leaf, and no solid outline anywhere. BETWEEN THE STEMS IS OPEN WATER, which here means TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND, and most of the frame is that. Draw the smallest circle that contains the patch and the stems fill only about a third of it. If it comes back as a solid green cushion it is a shrub, and it is the wrong plant. A few stems lean, a few cross, and a few near the rim bend further over than the rest. Each stem top is a simple soft-ended stroke, slightly lighter where the light catches it. SOME STEMS CARRY A SEED HEAD: a small brown tufted knot just below the tip, on perhaps one stem in six, in a warm mid brown. They are the only warm thing in the picture. THE GREEN IS A PLAIN MID GREEN, cooler and duller than a bright meadow: a lit tone near #7C9E42, a body near #5A7A2E, and a deep shade near #35491C where stems crowd. NOTHING HERE IS BLUE-GREEN, KHAKI, YELLOW-GREEN OR GREY. The patch is as tall as it is wide overall, with a soft broken irregular rim and no clean circle. No water, no ripple, no reflection, no waterline, no bottom, no fish, no bird
assets.note: THE SHORELINE'S SOFT EDGE — bulrush and reed in the shallows, and the plant that makes a lake margin look like a lake margin rather than a cut line between land and water. 3.5 m across, and 3.5 x 9.2 = 32u. ⚠️ THE OPENNESS IS THE ASSET AND IT IS PRE-DECLARED SO A CHECK DOES NOT REJECT IT. Circle fill is asked at about ONE THIRD, against the seven to eight tenths this venue's shrubs carry — the same pre-emption [[ocean-morning-glory]] and [[lake-birch-paper]] needed. Emergent stems ARE mostly gaps; a solid patch is a bush. Expect the polar rosette metric to be meaningless here and use the mirror test if anything. PLANE `surface`, CONTACT none, following [[swamp-cattails]] exactly — the same object for a different water. `surface` is right rather than `float` because bulrush is ROOTED in the bottom and stands up THROUGH the water; float is for things lying ON it. And nothing should stop a hull here: a boat pushes through reeds, and a hidden collider in the shallows is the unfairness the shoal note argues against. COLOUR IS DELIBERATELY DULL. It sits dE 60.5 from the lake water, which is plenty, and the instruction not to make it bright is what keeps it from competing with the venue's actual vegetation — a reed bed is a texture at the water's edge, not a feature. planRound true. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. ⚠️ DELIVERED 2026-08-15 AND REJECTED — NOT INGESTED, status stays `slot`. It is a RADIAL BURST OF SIDE-ON STEMS, which is two documented failures of this library at once, and both are measured rather than judged. FIRST, THE STEMS ARE DRAWN FROM THE SIDE. The subject is explicit that from directly above 'you are looking at the TOPS OF THE STEMS — a scatter of many small rounded dots and short strokes', because a stem stands on the vertical axis and a plan view sees it END-ON. Delivered blob elongation is a median of 3.73 with 71% above 2.5:1 — long capsules, i.e. stems seen along their length. This is exactly the bayou-cypress spanish-moss finding with the plant stood up instead of hung down, and the same sentence fixes it. SECOND, IT IS THE ROSETTE the pipeline spends 3b warning about. Measuring each elongated mark's principal axis against the radius vector from the patch centre gives a mean |cos| of 0.851, where 2/pi = 0.64 is direction-neutral and 1.0 is every mark pointing at the middle; 63% of marks sit above 0.9. A stand of reeds has no centre to point at. Note the note above predicted the polar rosette metric would be meaningless here and it is not — it is meaningless for measuring the PATCH's symmetry, which is genuinely irregular, but measuring the STEM AXES catches this cleanly, the same limbs-not-the-blob distinction bayou-cypress had to learn. THE ONE THING IT GOT RIGHT is the openness the note pre-declared: circle fill measures 31%, against the 'about a third' asked for, so nothing needs relaxing on the re-run. Third defect for the regeneration list: the delivery carries a heavy white sticker stroke (75k px) on EVERY stem, which at the declared 32px stops being an edge artefact and becomes sparkle — a patch of white speckles rather than a plant. SECOND DELIVERY 2026-08-15 — SHIPPED, WITH THE CAMERA STILL WRONG AND FLAGGED, by explicit decision: it reads correctly at its declared 32px, the venue gets its shoreline edge now, and the re-prompt folds into the next batch. THE ROSETTE IS FIXED and that was the big one: radial alignment falls to 0.618 from 0.851, against 0.64 for direction-neutral, with only 23% of marks above |cos| 0.9 where it was 63%. The white sticker stroke is gone too (26 px against 75k), fill measures 27.9% against the ~33% asked, and aspect is 1.04 so planRound passes. ⚠️ WHAT REPLACED THE ROSETTE IS A UNIFORM LEAN, which is the SAME camera error wearing different clothes. Every stem axis falls between 45 and 135 degrees — NOTHING at all in 0-45 or 135-180 — clustered at 60-120, with an axial resultant of 0.812 measured on single stems only, so it is not a merged-blob artefact. All the stems stand UP in the frame, and up is gravity, and a plan view has no gravity: this is the bayou-cypress moss sentence exactly, which is why that clause is the model for the rewrite. Corroborated by elongation, which got WORSE: median 5.64 against attempt 1's 3.73, 72% of marks above 2.5:1, and only 11% near-round. An upright stem seen from straight down is a DOT, and the subject asks for 'many small rounded dots and short strokes' with only 'a few' leaning — the delivery inverts that ratio. TWO NUMBERS FOR THE RE-ROLL, and they are the whole brief because everything else now passes: stem angles must be UNIFORM across 0-180 degrees (axial resultant below 0.25, i.e. mean |cos| to any axis near 0.64), and at least 60% of marks must be near-round (elongation below 1.6). Keep the openness and keep whatever fixed the rosette.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. ONE SMALL GLACIAL BOULDER — a granite cobble the size of a bar stool, worn round by ice — seen from directly above and ALONE, no ground drawn. IT IS ROUNDED AND SIMPLE. From above it is a plain irregular lobed blob, softly domed, with no straight edge and no sharp corner. Its crown is lightest and its colour steps DOWN in two flat bands to a darker rim, with the lit crown pushed off-centre so the stone is lopsided. ⚠️ AT THIS SIZE THE DETAIL BUDGET IS ABOUT EIGHTEEN PIXELS ON SCREEN, so the shape, the two value steps and ONE faint mineral mark are all that is asked for. Do not draw cracks, do not draw lichen patches, do not draw moss — every one of them turns to mush at display size and only muddies the silhouette. One soft dusty-pink or rusty streak across the crown, and nothing else. Same stone as its larger sibling: a lit crown near #A29DA3, a body near #8A858B, a shade near #605C63. Cool medium grey, never warm tan, never black, never orange. THE SILHOUETTE IS AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE. No water, no wet stain, no cast shadow, no ground
assets.note: THE SCATTER STONE — for shingle, shoreline shelves, the foot of a rock point, and singly through the forest. 2.0 m across, and 2.0 x 9.2 = 18u, a 2.4x step below [[lake-boulder-large]]. THE SUBJECT IS THE LARGE BOULDER'S WITH ITS DETAIL STRIPPED OUT, deliberately and by the same reasoning [[ocean-grass-coastal]] and [[lake-blueberry-lowbush]] carry: at 18px the budget is the silhouette, two value steps and one accent. Cracks and lichen are not 'less visible' at this size, they are noise that costs the shape. The two boulders are therefore separated by size and by DETAIL DENSITY as much as by anything else, which also means they can sit next to each other without reading as one sprite scaled twice. CONTACT hard with contactR at the drawn radius, per [[lake-boulder-large]] — a circle genuinely fits a boulder. ⚠️ BUT WEIGH THE COUNT BEFORE PLANTING MANY. Every fixed contact prop compiles to a hidden circular shape that also enters the router's grid, and script.js records the river's 82 hidden banks causing multi-hundred-millisecond replan spikes. A shingle beach wants dozens of these; a hundred colliders is not a thing to discover during a race. Either place them sparingly, or override contact to none on the decorative ones — the trait is per-placement, which is exactly what that override is for. planRound true, plane `surface`. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. DELIVERED 2026-08-15 PRE-CUT, AND THE CUT CARRIES A WHITE STICKER STROKE — the one thing about this batch that needed work. The remover left real alpha with a soft ~14px feather, but a pure-white outline is painted around the silhouette underneath it: 36k px of RGB 255,255,255 sitting at alpha 1-60. Two reasons that cannot ship. It is faintly visible as a pale rim over forestfloor, and worse, ingest downsamples 2048->1024 with a plain channel-by-channel RGBA resize, so white under near-zero alpha is averaged into every edge pixel on the way down — the bayou-cypress halo lesson with the sign flipped (black there, white here). A FLAT ALPHA CHOKE CANNOT SEPARATE THEM, which is what the first attempt assumed: along one ray the stone's own RGB survives down to alpha 101 and the white starts at 73, but around the rest of the perimeter white reaches alpha 160 (p99 of the 130-160 band is 244). Any single threshold either keeps white or eats stone. UNMIX DOES SEPARATE THEM. At a partial pixel the stored colour C is the stone F and the stroke W=255 sharing the stored coverage a, so the stone's own coverage is the projection s = a*dot(C-W, F-W)/|F-W|^2 clamped to [0,a], with F estimated by growing confident stone colour (alpha>0.85, not near-white) outward under the fringe. RGB is then replaced by the recovered F, so no white survives at any alpha — MEASURED: zero near-white px above alpha 12, against 36k before, and the partial-alpha band's luma p99 falls to 106/113. Silhouette is unmoved (bbox 1714 -> 1710 of 2048, 0.2%). Colour-bled 22px outward afterwards for the same reason bayou-cypress is: the resize has no idea the alpha is zero. INGEST CLEAN — no ORTHOGRAPHIC warning (bbox is 1.000/1.001, the roundest pair in the library), no margin warning, only the expected 2048->1024 downsample note. THE PREP IS NOT COMMITTED TOOLING and the delivered files are not in the repo; they are on the Desktop as large-boulder.png and Gemini_Generated_Image_yd8f1myd8f1myd8f.png. The inbox copy is the PREPPED file, so re-running ingest on it is idempotent and does not need the unmix again. ⚠️ THE REST OF THE LAKE BATCH HAS THE SAME STROKE AND SHIPPED WITH IT — lake-pine-red's master still carries 9.5k px of white at alpha 1-10 and 6.4k at 10-60. Left alone deliberately: at world 22-110 the band is sub-pixel, which is the arctic-orca-calf finding (a 1.7x fringe is invisible below ~130px). Worth a re-prep only if a lake tree ever grows past that. THE DETAIL-DENSITY CONTRACT HELD, and it is measurable: 0.0% of opaque px above chroma 40 against the large boulder's 14.5%, p99 chroma 25 against 90. One dusty streak and nothing else, exactly as asked. Squint test passes — blurred at 1.5px the pair do not read as one asset at two scales, the large one showing banding and asymmetry where this is a plain pale blob. dE 4.3 against lake-gneiss, 22.8 against lake-sand, 29.5 against lake-forestfloor. DRAWN RADIUS IS 7.7px (fillTo 0.86 makes world 18 a 15px stone), so contactR is ~8 when it reaches PROP_KINDS. ⚠️ IT DISAPPEARS ON lake-sand AT RACE SCALE, and that is a PLACEMENT finding rather than an art defect: the sand texture already paints its own cobbles at 12-20px in the same grey, so an 18px stone on it is camouflage. Plant it on forestfloor and gneiss where it reads, and if it is wanted on a shingle beach it needs to be either clustered or scaled up to register at all — which also happens to be the cheap answer to this asset's collider warning.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. A CAMPFIRE RING on bare ground, seen from straight above and ALONE, with no ground drawn around it. IT IS A RING OF FIELDSTONES laid in a rough circle: eight to twelve rounded grey cobbles of plainly uneven size, set close but not touching evenly, with small gaps between some of them. The ring is irregular — not a neat circle, slightly egg-shaped, with one stone sitting further out than the rest and one gap wider than the others. Each stone is a simple rounded blob with a lighter crown and a darker underside, the same cool grey granite the shore is made of, near #78737A. INSIDE THE RING is the fire bed: a flat disc of pale grey ASH with a few small pieces of black CHARRED WOOD lying across it at random angles, and one or two dull orange EMBERS showing through. The ash is near #A8A29C, the char near #2A2622, and the embers a warm orange near #C4632A used very sparingly — two or three small marks and no more. ⚠️ NO FLAME AND NO SMOKE. This is a fire ring, not a fire: nothing is burning, nothing glows brightly, and there is no light being cast onto anything. The engine draws no light from props and a painted glow would sit on the ground looking wrong at every hour. AT THIS SIZE THE DETAIL BUDGET IS ABOUT FOURTEEN PIXELS ON SCREEN, so the ring of stones, the pale ash disc and two or three dark char marks are ALL that is asked for. No grate, no logs stacked, no kettle, no seating, no path. THE SILHOUETTE IS AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE. No ground, no cast shadow, no grass, no water
assets.note: CAMP FURNITURE, for cabin lots and shore campsites, and the smallest prop in the venue at 1.5 m across — 1.5 x 9.2 = 14u. Smaller than anything the cove or the ocean ships, and the subject is written against that budget: a ring, a pale disc, two or three dark marks. ⚠️ NO FLAME, AND THE REASON IS ENGINE-SHAPED RATHER THAN ARTISTIC. Nothing in this renderer casts light from a prop, so a painted flame or glow would be a bright patch sitting on the ground with nothing lit around it — wrong at midday and wrong at Glowtide's midnight, and this venue has no night. The glowtide jellies make the same decision in reverse: their glow is the ENGINE's and the art must not bake one. COLOUR: the stones are the same granite as [[lake-boulder-small]] and [[lake-gneiss]], which is correct — a fire ring is built from whatever is lying about. That does mean it measures dE 3.1 from the gneiss ground and would nearly vanish on a bare rock shelf; place it on [[lake-forestfloor]] (dE 29.0) or [[lake-sand]] (dE 28.3), which is where a campsite is anyway. The pale ash disc is what actually carries it at 14px — a light circle inside a dark ring is legible when individual stones are not. planRound true, plane `surface`, contact none. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-15, CLEAN — the easiest asset in the batch and the only one that needed nothing but geometry. Aspect 0.99 so planRound passes outright; the delivery arrived pre-cut with real alpha and only 166 px of white stroke (against 36k on the boulders), so prep was crop to bbox, pad to 86% and colour-bleed for the downsample, nothing more. PALETTE IS ON THE DECLARED TONES: stones measure dE 1.2 from #78737A, embers dE 7.1 from #C4632A, ash dE 5.5 from #A8A29C and a little lighter than asked. Three ember marks, inside the 'two or three and no more' budget, and no flame or glow anywhere — the engine-shaped clause held. ⚠️ THE OUTLYING STONE IS CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE TIDIED. The subject asks for 'one stone sitting further out than the rest', and the delivery puts one fully detached at the lower right, which LOOKS like a stray blob that would wreck the bbox. Measured, it does almost nothing: it is a separate component of 91.7k px against the ring's 1.91M, it extends the content span by only 2% (the ring alone spans 1672 px of 1709), and it pulls the seeded anchor off the ring's centre by 1.4% x 1.0% — which at world 14 is 0.20 x 0.14 px ON SCREEN. Deleting it would cost a spec-compliant detail to fix a fifth of a pixel. ASH-TO-RING CONTRAST IS 1.50:1, AND THAT IS BETTER THAN SPEC, not a defect: the declared #78737A stone against #A8A29C ash is itself only 1.35:1, so the delivery beats its own palette. The note above is right that the pale disc is what carries the prop at 14px, but be honest about the ceiling — at 14px on forestfloor this is a grey speck with a lighter middle. That is what a 1.5 m object is, and it is why the venue's smallest prop was always going to be scenery you notice rather than scenery you read.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. ONE WOODEN PICNIC TABLE standing on bare ground, seen from straight above and ALONE. ⚠️ FROM DIRECTLY OVERHEAD A PICNIC TABLE IS THREE PARALLEL BARS, and that is the entire read: a wide TABLETOP down the middle and a narrower BENCH running parallel to it on each side, with a clear gap of open ground showing between the tabletop and each bench. The three bars are the same length and their long edges are PARALLEL — nothing converges. The tabletop is about twice the width of a bench. Draw the tabletop as four or five separate PLANKS laid along its length with a narrow dark gap between them, and each bench as one or two planks. Between and under the bars, the A-frame LEGS show only as short dark diagonal marks near each end where they splay out past the bench — you are looking at the TOP of a leg, not its side, so no upright, no post and no table edge stands up in the picture. Two or three dark bolt heads on the tabletop. THE OBJECT IS SLIGHTLY LONGER THAN IT IS WIDE, about 6 to 5, so it is nearly square in plan but honestly rectangular. THE WOOD IS WEATHERED GREY-BROWN CAMP LUMBER, silvered by weather and not painted and not fresh: a lit plank near #B3A48E, a body near #9A8B76, and a shade near #6E6153 in the plank gaps and under the benches. NOTHING ELSE IS ON IT: no cloth, no food, no bottle, no person, no bag, no umbrella, no carved initials. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the object is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it stands on.
assets.note: CAMP FURNITURE for the lodge lawn, cabin lots and shore campsites, and the companion to [[lake-firering]] — where there is one there is usually the other. 1.8 m long and 1.5 m across the benches, so 1.8 x 9.2 = 17u. ⚠️ THE THREE-BAR READ IS THE WHOLE ASSET AND IT IS WHY THE GAPS MATTER MORE THAN THE PLANKS. At 17px the tabletop is about 7px wide and each bench about 3px, so the only thing that separates this from a plain rectangle is the two strips of ground showing through between them. If the generator closes those gaps — bench flush to table, or a solid slab — the sprite becomes a brown blob at race scale and there is nothing to recover. Check the gaps before checking anything else. planRound FALSE: it is genuinely 1.2:1, which sits just past the 1.12 tolerance the round test allows, so the flag would report a tilt that is not there. Judge the camera on the LEGS instead — a visible upright is the tell. PLANE `surface`, CONTACT none: this is land scenery the fleet cannot reach. COLOUR SITS IN THE SAME WEATHERED-TIMBER FAMILY AS [[lake-dock]] AND [[lake-raft-swim]], deliberately, so the camp's carpentry reads as one hand. That inherits the dock's known weakness: dE 10.2 from [[lake-sand]] and only 14.6 from [[lake-gneiss]], against 19.8 from [[lake-forestfloor]]. Place it on forest floor and lawn where it reads; a picnic table on a bare beach will be nearly invisible, and unlike the dock it has no strong linear silhouette to carry it. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-16. THE THREE-BAR READ IS THERE AND IT IS MEASURED: scanning rows across the content, two clear empty bands of 78 px and 77 px separate the tabletop from the bench either side, with only plank-gap slivers of 6-7 px elsewhere. That was the one thing this asset could fail on — a generator closing those gaps turns the sprite into a brown blob at 17px — and it did not. Legs read as short dark diagonals near the ends with no upright standing up. Aspect came back 1.50:1 against the 6-to-5 (1.2) asked, so it draws 15 x 10px rather than 15 x 12: a slightly longer table, accepted. Weathering matches [[lake-dock]] and [[lake-raft-swim]] as intended, and it inherits their weakness — keep it off [[lake-sand]], where the note above already predicts dE 10.2.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. A SUMMER CAMP LODGE — the big timber dining hall at the centre of a north-woods children's camp — seen from straight above and ALONE. ⚠️ YOU ARE LOOKING AT THE ROOF, AND THE ROOF IS ALMOST THE WHOLE PICTURE. From directly overhead a building is its roof: two long slopes meeting along a RIDGE that runs the length of the building and points to the TOP of the frame. The two slopes are equal, the ridge is a clean straight line down the middle, and the eaves overhang each long side by a little, so a thin band of LOG WALL shows below each eave and nothing more of the walls than that. No wall face, no window seen side-on, no porch post standing up, no gable end standing up. The building is about twice as long as it is wide and its long edges are PARALLEL — nothing converges. THE ROOF IS DARK GREEN STANDING-SEAM METAL, the same roof the whole camp wears: flat panels with fine straight SEAM LINES running down the slope from ridge to eave, evenly spaced and a shade darker than the panel. One slope catches the light and is a little lighter than the other. Build it from a lit slope near #4E7048, a shade slope near #3D5A3A and seams near #2A3F2A. ON THE ROOF, AND ONLY THESE: a stone CHIMNEY near one end, seen from above as a small rectangle of grey fieldstone breaking the ridge; three or four small square metal ROOF VENTS spaced along the ridge; and at ONE LONG SIDE a wide covered PORCH running most of the length, reading as a lower band of the same green roof with its own smaller ridge parallel to the main one. Under the eaves the log wall shows as a narrow warm brown band near #7E5C3C with the round ends of the logs just visible at the corners. NOTHING ELSE IS DRAWN: no path, no steps, no deck furniture, no flagpole, no vehicle, no smoke, no sign, no lettering. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the object is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it stands on.
assets.note: THE CAMP'S BIG BUILDING and the largest prop in the venue — a dining hall and gathering barn, the thing a Stillwater shoreline is organised around. 18 m long and 9 m wide, so 18 x 9.2 = 166u. That is well inside the library's range for a landmark building: [[bayou-shack]] ships at 189u and cove-boatshed at 150u. SEPARATED FROM THE VENUE'S OTHER BUILDINGS BY SIZE FIRST, which is the [[lake-boulder-small]] lesson applied to architecture — 166u against [[lake-cabin]] at 88, [[lake-cabin-b]] at 72 and [[lake-camp-cabin]] at 51, so no two of the four can read as one asset at two scales. The green metal roof is shared with the cabin and the camp cabin ON PURPOSE: a camp is one owner and one roofing order, and the family read is the point. [[lake-cabin-b]] is the deliberate exception and wears rust. ⚠️ THE PORCH IS THE SECOND SILHOUETTE AND IT IS WHAT STOPS THIS BEING A GREEN RECTANGLE. At 166px the roof is a big flat slab; the lower porch band running down one long side gives it an asymmetric, readable plan and tells a viewer which side faces the water. Place it porch-to-the-lake. Note the porch also breaks the eave symmetry, so unlike [[lake-cabin]] the log-wall band SHOULD show on only one long side here, and that is not the tilt fingerprint it would be on the cabin. PLANE `surface`, CONTACT none. COLOUR: dE 26.5 from [[lake-forestfloor]] and 33.9 from [[lake-sand]], so it separates on both grounds, and 39.0 from the lake's deep water — irrelevant for a building but it means a lodge at the water's edge will not smear into the shallows. planRound FALSE at 2:1 — ORTHO_LONG, parallel sides. Anchor footprint, and check it by hand on the contact sheet: the porch will pull the seeded bbox centre off the main hall, and for a building this large the anchor wants to sit under the HALL, not under the hall-plus-porch. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-16, AND IT IS A TRUE PLAN VIEW — measured, not eyeballed, by the test [[lake-cabin]] established: the ridge sits at 41% of the body and the seam pitch matches across it, 18.8 px above against 16.8 below (11%), so both halves are roof planes at the same obliquity rather than roof-plus-wall. The 41/59 split is not a defect and is the porch: the covered band running down one long side deepens that flank, exactly as the subject asks, which is also why the log-wall band shows on one side only here where on the cabin that would be a tilt fingerprint. ASPECT LANDED AT 2.02:1 AGAINST THE 2:1 ASKED, the closest match in the whole batch. Chimney, three ridge vents and the porch are all present and nothing forbidden is. Rotated 90 CCW on ingest, the only pixel change — ridge to the top per art-pipeline 3, and CCW puts the lit slope (luma 123.6 against 90.2) on the left to match the venue's up-left convention. At 166px it reads as the biggest thing on the shore without reading as an obstacle, which is what `landmark` is for. ⚠️ ANCHOR STILL WANTS CHECKING BY HAND: the porch pulls the seeded bbox centre off the main hall, and for a building this size the anchor belongs under the HALL.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. A SUMMER CAMP SLEEPING CABIN — one of the plain little bunk cabins a children's camp has a row of — seen from straight above and ALONE. ⚠️ YOU ARE LOOKING AT THE ROOF AND THE ROOF IS THE WHOLE PICTURE. Two equal slopes meeting along a RIDGE that runs the length of the cabin and points to the TOP of the frame, a clean straight line down the middle, with the eaves overhanging each long side just enough to show a thin band of wall below. No wall face, no window seen side-on, no step and no post standing up. The cabin is about a third longer than it is wide and its long edges are PARALLEL. THE ROOF IS THE SAME DARK GREEN STANDING-SEAM METAL THE WHOLE CAMP WEARS: flat panels with fine straight seam lines running down the slope from ridge to eave, one slope a little lighter than the other. A lit slope near #4E7048, a shade slope near #3D5A3A, seams near #2A3F2A. ⚠️ THIS IS THE PLAINEST BUILDING IN THE VENUE AND THE PLAINNESS IS THE POINT. It gets NO chimney, NO porch, NO dormer, NO vent and NO ell — a bare rectangle of roof with a ridge and nothing breaking it. The only marks on it are the seam lines and, under the eaves, a narrow band of unpainted board wall near #8A7355 along each long side. NOTHING ELSE IS DRAWN: no path, no steps, no number, no sign, no lettering, no washing line, no bench. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the object is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it stands on.
assets.note: THE CAMP'S SLEEPING QUARTERS, and the asset a camp waterfront needs a ROW of. 5.5 m long by 4 m wide, so 5.5 x 9.2 = 51u. ⚠️ DECLARED AS ONE CABIN, NOT AS A ROW, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE READ OF art-pipeline 3b RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. The rule says several copies of the same object get composed by compose.py instead of generated as a group, and it exists because a generator asked for 'seven of X' returns a rosette. But compose BAKES the arrangement: one image, fixed spacing, fixed count, one heading for the lot. Camp cabins are 51u each — big enough to place individually in the editor, which is what the penguins and the huts are NOT — and a row of them wants to follow a shoreline, step down a slope and sit at slightly different angles. Bake the row and every camp in the game has the same row. So: one cabin, placed several times, spun a few degrees apart. If a baked cluster is ever wanted anyway, this asset is the element it composes from. SEPARATION FROM THE OTHER THREE BUILDINGS IS BY SIZE AND BY DETAIL DENSITY TOGETHER, the [[lake-boulder-small]] argument: this is the smallest at 51u against [[lake-cabin-b]] 72, [[lake-cabin]] 88 and [[lake-camp-lodge]] 166, AND it is the only one with a completely unbroken roof. A chimney here would cost that separation and buy nothing at 51px. PLANE `surface`, CONTACT none. Colour as [[lake-camp-lodge]]: dE 26.5 from forest floor. planRound FALSE at 1.33:1. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-16. PLAN VIEW CONFIRMED AND IT IS THE CLEANEST IN THE BATCH: ridge at 48% of the body, seam pitch 22.2 px above against 22.5 below — a 1% match, tighter than the lodge's 11% and than [[lake-cabin]]'s own 1%. Both halves are roof. The roof is unbroken as asked: no chimney, no porch, no dormer, nothing competing with the plain rectangle. ⚠️ IT CAME BACK LONG. Content measures 1220x499, an aspect of 2.44:1 against the 1.33 the subject asks and the 5.5 x 4 m the size line derives 51u from. At 51u it draws 44px long by 18px, so in real terms this is a 5.5 x 2.25 m building — a narrow bunkhouse rather than the squarish cabin specified. ACCEPTED RATHER THAN RE-ROLLED, and the reasoning is that the delivered proportion is arguably the better object: a camp sleeps its children in LONG low bunkhouses, not in square cabins, and a row of these at 44x18 reads unmistakably as a camp where a row of squares would read as a village. Unlike [[lake-dock]]'s 1.83-against-8 the deviation does not change what the thing is. If it ever wants correcting, correct the SUBJECT to say long, not the art. Rotated 90 CCW (lit slope 89.1 against 53.4, so CCW lands it left).

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. THE OBJECT RUNS UP THE FRAME, long axis vertical, and its FRONT faces the TOP — the engine treats sprite-up as zero heading and rotates from there. A CAMP CANOE RACK — a timber frame on a shore with canoes stored on it upside down — seen from straight above and ALONE. ⚠️ WHAT YOU ACTUALLY SEE IS THREE CANOE HULLS SIDE BY SIDE, and the rack is mostly hidden beneath them. Each canoe lies KEEL-UP, so from above each one is a smooth symmetric LEAF: pointed at both ends, widest in the middle, with a fine raised KEEL LINE running down its centre from tip to tip catching the light. There is no open cockpit and no interior visible on any of them — an upturned hull is a closed shape, and that is what separates this from [[lake-canoe]], which is an open boat. The three hulls lie PARALLEL, all pointing the same way, evenly spaced with a narrow gap of shadow between them, and they are all the same length. Their ends line up nearly but not exactly — one canoe sits a little further forward than the others. Under and between them, at each end of the stack, a dark weathered TIMBER CROSSBAR shows as a straight bar running ACROSS all three hulls, with the tops of two short posts as small dark squares just outside the outermost hull. THE CANOES ARE THE SAME WARM CEDAR-RED CANVAS AS THE VENUE'S OTHER CANOE, but vary them: one near #CB8A4E, one a shade deeper near #B5713A, one greener and older near #8C6A45. Keel lines and gunwales are pale varnished ash near #D9BE8C. The rack timber is weathered grey-brown near #6E6153. NOTHING ELSE: no paddle, no rope, no person, no life jacket, no lettering, no water. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the object is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it stands on.
assets.note: THE CAMP WATERFRONT'S STORE, and the prop that says 'children's camp' faster than any building does. Sized on the canoes it holds: a 5 m canoe plus a little overhang, so 5.5 x 9.2 = 51u. ⚠️ IT MUST NOT READ AS THREE LOOSE CANOES, and everything about the construction is aimed at that. Hulls keel-UP is the main separator — [[lake-canoe]] is an open boat with a dark cockpit taking most of its deck, and this is three closed shells with a bright keel line, so the two do not share a silhouette even though they share an outline. The crossbars are the second: a straight dark bar cutting across all three hulls is a thing no floating canoe has, and it is what tells the viewer these are STACKED rather than moored. Draw the bars unmistakably or the asset fails into a raft of boats. ⚠️ ROLE IS `ambient` AND IT SITS ON LAND, so it does NOT inherit [[lake-canoe]]'s traffic contract — but it is worth noting the risk transfers anyway: three cedar-red leaves on a shore, seen at speed, are the same colour as a real canoe on the water. PLANE `surface`, CONTACT none, and place it ABOVE the waterline. Colour is loud and that is correct here as it is for the canoe: dE 25.5 from [[lake-forestfloor]] and 33.5 from [[lake-sand]]. planRound FALSE — three hulls side by side make the stack roughly 1.5:1, and the acceptance test is the sides: parallel hulls that do not converge. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-16. THE KEEL-UP READ HELD, which is the whole separator from [[lake-canoe]]: the hulls are closed convex shells with a pale keel line down each, not open boats with a dark well. Measured, only 13% of opaque px are deep shadow, and that is the rack timber and the gaps between hulls rather than cockpits — an open boat of this size would run several times that. Three hulls, parallel, evenly spaced, ends not quite aligned, with the crossbar timber and post tops showing between them, so it reads as STACKED rather than as three canoes rafted together. Colour varies across the three as asked (two cedar tones and an older green), which also stops it reading as one canoe stamped three times. Aspect 1.42:1 against the ~1.5 expected. Rotated 90 CCW on ingest for the long axis. At 51px the three warm hulls are the brightest mark on the shoreline, which is right for the prop whose job is to say 'children's camp' at a glance.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. THE OBJECT RUNS UP THE FRAME, long axis vertical, and its FRONT faces the TOP — the engine treats sprite-up as zero heading and rotates from there. ONE ADIRONDACK CHAIR standing on bare ground, seen from straight above and ALONE — the wide slatted wooden camp chair with the fanned back and the broad flat arms. ⚠️ AT THIS SIZE THE DETAIL BUDGET IS ABOUT EIGHT PIXELS ON SCREEN, WHICH IS THE SMALLEST THING THIS GAME SHIPS, so the subject is a SHAPE and two value steps and nothing else. From directly above the chair is a rounded FAN at the top of the frame — the slatted back, seen end-on and foreshortened to a short curved band — with the flat SEAT below it as a wider slatted rectangle, and one broad flat ARM running down each side of the seat. The whole silhouette is a little taller than it is wide and widest across the arms. Draw the slats as three or four straight lines on the seat and no more; do NOT draw individual back slats, do NOT draw the legs, do NOT draw the frame beneath. You are looking at the TOP of a chair, so nothing stands up: no chair back rising, no leg, no side profile. THE CHAIR IS PAINTED, AND THE PAINT IS THE ASSET. A faded barn red near #A8503C on the seat and arms where the light falls, dropping to #7E3A2C in the shadow under the back and between the slats. The paint is worn and flat, not glossy. NOTHING ELSE: no cushion, no person, no table, no drink, no blanket. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the object is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it stands on.
assets.note: SHORE FURNITURE, for cabin lots, the lodge lawn and the top of a beach — and THE SMALLEST ASSET IN THE GAME. 0.9 m across and 0.9 x 9.2 = 8u, against [[lake-firering]] at 14u, which the firering's own note already calls marginal. ⚠️ BE HONEST ABOUT THE CEILING BEFORE SPENDING A GENERATION ON IT. At 8px, with fillTo 0.86, the chair draws SEVEN PIXELS. Nothing about its construction survives that: it is a coloured dot with a hint of a waist. It is worth drawing anyway — a red dot on a green lawn reads as 'somebody sits here' and that is real venue storytelling — but judge it on the contact sheet as a MARK, not as furniture, and do not accept a prompt round that tries to buy detail. THE COLOUR IS CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT, NOT TASTE, and it is the only decision that matters at this size. Faded barn red #A8503C measures dE 29.9 from [[lake-forestfloor]] and 40.9 from [[lake-sand]]; the obvious alternative, a weathered camp green, measures 25.3 and 29.7 — worse on both, and it would also collide with the camp's green roofs. Red is the venue's declared accent ('warm cabin lights') and it is what the pixel budget can actually carry. Do not let it drift to bare wood: unpainted timber would land near [[lake-picnic-table]]'s #9A8B76, which is dE 10.2 from sand and would disappear. ⚠️ IF IT NEEDS TO REGISTER MORE, THE ANSWER IS A PAIR, NOT A BIGGER CHAIR. Two chairs angled toward each other is the picture everybody has of a lake shore, doubles the mark and stays honest about scale — and that is a compose.py group with this asset as its element, which is exactly the case art-pipeline 3b is for. planRound is OMITTED deliberately: the chair is genuinely near-square in plan at about 1.1:1, which sits inside the 1.12 tolerance by a hair, so the flag would fire on honest art as often as on a tilted camera. PLANE `surface`, CONTACT none. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-16 AND JUDGED AS A MARK, per this slot's own instruction. It draws SEVEN PIXELS. At that size the measurements that matter are the silhouette and the colour, and both are right: 1.04:1, widest across the arms, faded barn red as specified for the separation reasons above. ⚠️ THE BACK IS DRAWN AS A FANNED SET OF SLATS where the subject asks for 'a short curved band' — from directly overhead a raked chair back foreshortens hard and should not show its face, and this one shows some. That is a genuine camera deviation and it is recorded rather than fixed, because at 7px the fan is a third of a pixel and no regeneration could buy anything visible. Do not re-roll this on its own; if the chair is ever wanted larger, re-roll the camera clause then. It carries the batch's heaviest sticker stroke (2087 px), also irrelevant at this size and removed by the colour bleed anyway.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. ONE WHITE MOORING BUOY floating on open water, seen from straight above and ALONE — the plain pick-up float a small boat ties to off a cabin, not a navigation mark. ⚠️ THE SHAPE OF THIS WHOLE PICTURE IS A CIRCLE AND THAT IS THE FIRST THING TO GET RIGHT. Seen from straight above a spherical float is a disc, and the moment the camera tips it flattens into an oval — the silhouette must be AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE. It is a simple round ball with a smooth unbroken outline: no facets, no cage, no tower, no lantern, no topmark, no radar reflector, nothing standing up out of it. THE MARKINGS ARE CANONICAL AND THEY CARRY INFORMATION. The float is WHITE near #E8E6E0, lit a little brighter on the upper left and dropping to a soft grey shade near #B4B2AE where it rolls away, and around its middle runs ONE broad horizontal BLUE BAND near #2A5FA8 — the international mooring-buoy stripe. From directly overhead that band reads as a blue ring set inside the white disc, not as a stripe across it. At the very centre a small dark METAL RING or eye, and a short length of dark rope or chain lying across the float and trailing a little way past its edge to one side. ⚠️ IT IS NOT A RACING MARK AND IT IS NOT A CHANNEL BUOY. It is never orange, never yellow, never red, never green, and it carries no number, no letter, no lettering of any kind, no flag and no light. NO WATER ANYWHERE: no ripple, no reflection, no wake, no wet ring. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the object is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it stands on.
assets.note: CABIN WATERFRONT FURNITURE — what a runabout or a [[lake-boat-aluminum]] is tied to when it is not hauled out. ⚠️ THE SIZE IS NOT LITERAL AND THAT IS DELIBERATE, following the precedent already set: a real mooring buoy is 0.4-0.6 m, which at 9.2 units/m would be FIVE UNITS and invisible. [[buoy-channel-red]] makes the same trade at world 28 for an object that is not 3 m across either. This sits at 20u — visible, and a third smaller than the channel buoys it shares water with. ⚠️ THE REAL RISK IS NOT REALISM, IT IS BEING MISTAKEN FOR A MARK THE PLAYER HAS TO ROUND. `mark` and `mark-can-yellow` both ship at world 30 and both are `nav`, i.e. objects the player is meant to read and sail around; this is scenery. Three things separate them and all three are in the subject: SIZE at 20 against 30, COLOUR (white with a blue band, which is the ICOMIA mooring standard and is a combination no mark or channel buoy in this game uses — those own red, green and yellow), and FORM (a bare ball, where every nav aid here carries a tower, a topmark or a lantern standing up out of the float). Do not let a generation add a topmark. ROLE `ambient` rather than `nav` for the same reason: nav is a contract that the object means something to the course, and this means nothing. COLOUR MEASURES WELL BOTH WAYS: dE 60.2 from the lake's deep water and 44.5 from its shallows, so a small white disc is unmissable — but note it is the one prop in this venue that could be lost in FOAM, so check it on the contact sheet over arctic where the whitecaps are, not just over lagoon. The blue band is what saves it there and is worth protecting for that reason as much as for the coding. PLANE `float`, CONTACT soft, contactR about 8 measured off the bake — a boat shoves a mooring buoy aside. planRound TRUE. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. ⚠️ DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-16 WITH AN ORTHOGRAPHIC FAILURE ON THE RECORD. The float measures 1302x1124, a ratio of 1.16 against the 1.12 tolerance, which ingest reports as a camera about 30 degrees off vertical. This is NOT the rope inflating the bbox — isolating the white and blue float alone gives the identical figure, so the disc itself is 16% wider than tall. A spherical float seen from straight above is a circle and this one is an ellipse. EVERYTHING ELSE IS RIGHT, which is why it ships rather than being dropped: white body with one broad blue band reading as a ring rather than a stripe, the centre eye, a short rope trailing past the rim to one side, no topmark, no lantern, no number — so the separation from `mark`, `mark-can-yellow` and the channel buoys holds on colour and form exactly as designed, and at 20px on water it is unmistakable. THE FIX IS ONE CLAUSE, not a redraw: the subject already opens with 'THE SHAPE OF THIS WHOLE PICTURE IS A CIRCLE' and the generator still returned an oval, which is the same fight [[bayou-cypress]] recorded. Re-roll it with the next batch rather than alone.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. THE OBJECT RUNS UP THE FRAME, long axis vertical, and its FRONT faces the TOP — the engine treats sprite-up as zero heading and rotates from there. A SWIM AREA LINE — the rope of floats strung across the water to mark off a camp swimming area — seen from straight above and ALONE, with no water drawn. IT IS A STRAIGHT RUN OF FLOATS THREADED ON ONE ROPE, running the length of the frame from the very top edge to the very bottom edge, and it must reach BOTH edges: this is a repeating SEGMENT that will be laid end to end, so the rope is cut off by the frame at each end rather than finishing inside it, and the float spacing continues right up to both cuts. THE ROPE is a thin pale line running dead straight down the middle. THE FLOATS are simple rounded capsules threaded on it, each a little wider than the rope, spaced evenly with a clear gap of open water between one float and the next — the gaps are as important as the floats and must stay open all the way down. Twelve to sixteen floats. THEY ALTERNATE IN COLOUR down the line, one white near #E8E6E0 then one blue near #2A5FA8, and the alternation is regular and unmistakable. Each float catches a small highlight on its upper left and carries a soft shade beneath. THE WHOLE THING IS VERY THIN: the floats are the widest part and the object is roughly ten times as long as it is wide. The line is DEAD STRAIGHT and its two sides are PARALLEL — no sag, no curve, no perspective narrowing toward either end. NOTHING ELSE: no post, no anchor, no buoy, no ladder, no person, no lettering, no waterline, no reflection, no wake. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the object is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it stands on.
assets.note: THE CAMP SWIMMING AREA'S BOUNDARY, and the other half of the waterfront [[lake-raft-swim]] sits inside. ⚠️ DECLARED AS A REPEATING SEGMENT, NOT AS A WHOLE SWIM AREA, and that is the whole design decision. A real camp swim line is 15-30 m, which at 9.2 units/m is 138-276u of almost entirely empty sprite — a 276px frame holding a 12px-wide object, wasting the master on transparent pixels and locking the venue into one length. An 8 m segment at 8 x 9.2 = 74u is placed two or three in a row to make any length wanted, and the subject is written for that: the rope RUNS OFF BOTH EDGES so segments butt together without a visible join. THIS IS THE FIRST TILING SPRITE IN THE LIBRARY and the frame-edge rule is the thing to check on delivery — a generator's instinct is to compose the object neatly inside the frame, which would put a rope end in the middle of a swim line. ⚠️ IT WILL BE INGESTED WITH CONTENT AT THE FRAME EDGE, which trips the safeMargin warning by design; that warning is CORRECT to ignore here and only here, and the prep must NOT pad it in the way every other prop in this batch was padded, or the join breaks. ROLE `ambient`, PLANE `float`, CONTACT none: a rope does not stop a racing hull and pretending it does would be the unfairness [[lake-boulder-large]]'s note argues against. It does have to clear the ambient-vs-hazard rule, and it does so on silhouette rather than colour — a dotted line is a shape nothing else in the venue has. COLOUR: white floats measure dE 60.2 from deep water and 44.5 from the shallows, blue floats 33.3 and 58.5 — so the two alternate not just for realism but so that whichever water it crosses, half the floats are the ones that separate. planRound FALSE at 10:1, ORTHO_LONG. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. ⚠️ fillTo REMOVED BEFORE THE FIRST INGEST, and it had to be: fillTo rescales content to a fraction of the frame, so 0.86 would have pulled the rope ends 7% INSIDE the master and put a visible gap at every segment join — the one thing this asset is built not to do. It is the only world-prop in the library that ships at 100% frame fill, and the safeMargin warning ingest emits for it is correct and expected. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-16. THE TILING CLAUSE WORKED, which was the one thing this asset could fail on and the one thing no other prop in the library is asked for: the rope runs off BOTH frame edges, 26 opaque px in the top row and 26 in the bottom, so segments butt together with no join. Verified by laying six end to end at true size — one continuous dotted line, no seam. Prep was DELIBERATELY NOT the batch prep: cropped horizontally only, padded sideways to square, full height preserved, because the standard crop-to-bbox-and-pad would have inset the rope ends and broken exactly what was asked for. Aspect came back 15.3:1 against the ~10:1 asked — thinner than specified and better for it, since the floats still read at 74px and a fatter rope would have eaten the open water between them. Float alternation is regular, white and blue as coded. The safeMargin warning ingest emits is expected and correct here.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. THE OBJECT RUNS UP THE FRAME, long axis vertical, and its FRONT faces the TOP — the engine treats sprite-up as zero heading and rotates from there. ONE SMALL ALUMINIUM FISHING BOAT, seen from straight above and ALONE on a transparent background — the plain riveted tin boat every north-woods lake has, with an outboard on the back. ⚠️ THE SHAPE IS THE OPPOSITE OF A CANOE'S AND THAT IS THE POINT. The BOW is at the top of the frame and comes to a blunt rounded point; the STERN is at the bottom and is cut off SQUARE as a flat wide TRANSOM. One end pointed and one end square is the whole species mark — if both ends come to a point the wrong boat has been drawn. The hull is about three times as long as it is wide, widest a little aft of the middle, and its two sides curve symmetrically about the centreline. YOU ARE LOOKING DOWN INTO AN OPEN BOAT: down the middle runs the dark open interior in deep shadow, taking most of the deck, with a narrow rim of GUNWALE following the whole outline. Across the interior lie THREE flat BENCH SEATS — plain straight cross planks, evenly spaced, one near the bow, one amidships and one just forward of the transom. ON THE TRANSOM, a small dark OUTBOARD MOTOR sits centred and overhangs the stern a little, reading as a compact dark block — it is the heaviest dark mark in the picture and the thing that says 'motor boat' at a glance. A pair of pale OARS lies along one side inside the boat. THE HULL IS BARE UNPAINTED ALUMINIUM: a lit topside near #C2C7CA where the light falls, a body near #9AA0A4, and the interior shadow near #4C5155. Fine horizontal RIVET LINES run along the topsides. The seats and oars are pale weathered wood near #B3A48E. NOTHING ELSE: no rig, no mast, no sail, no person, no fishing rod, no cooler, no rope, no lettering, no registration number. No water, no wake, no reflection. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the object is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it stands on.
assets.note: THE VENUE'S SECOND SMALL CRAFT and the working counterpart to [[lake-canoe]]: where the canoe is the camp's boat, this is the fish-camp's. 4.3 m long, and 4.3 x 9.2 = 40u. ROLE `traffic`, so art-pipeline 2 binds it — MUST NOT be confusable with a competitor — and the same three separators the canoe leans on carry it: NO RIG (every racing boat in this game is a triangle of sail and this is a bare open hull), AN OPEN INTERIOR taking most of the deck where a dinghy shows foredeck and mast step, and SIZE at 40u against the fleet's 32u. ⚠️ IT ALSO HAS TO SEPARATE FROM [[lake-canoe]], WHICH IS THE HARDER JOB, because two open boats of similar length in one venue is exactly the ambient/hazard confusion rule applied to traffic. Three things do it and they are all in the subject: the SQUARE TRANSOM against the canoe's symmetric leaf (the canoe's own subject says twice that both its ends are identical, so this is the clean inverse), the OUTBOARD as a heavy dark block at one end that the canoe has nothing like, and COLOUR — grey aluminium against cedar-red. ⚠️ THAT COLOUR IS THIS ASSET'S ONE REAL WEAKNESS AND IT SHOULD BE CHECKED FIRST ON THE CONTACT SHEET. Bare aluminium measures dE 35.0 from the lake's deep water and 40.0 from its shallows, against the canoe's 71.6 and 88.6 — barely half the separation, and this is the least visible boat in the venue by a wide margin. It is also dE 12.6 from [[lake-gneiss]], so an aluminium boat drawn up on a rock shelf will nearly vanish; beach it on sand (20.7) or forest floor (36.5) instead. What has to carry it is VALUE rather than hue: a bright lit topside against a deep interior shadow, which is why the subject names three steps and a hard #4C5155 interior. If it reads flat at race scale, deepen the interior before touching the hull. PLANE `float`, CONTACT soft, contactR about 6 off the bake, following the canoe and [[bayou-pirogue]]. planRound FALSE at 3:1. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-16. THE SPECIES MARK IS CORRECT AND IT IS THE SEPARATOR THAT MATTERS: measured on the hull alone (the outboard hangs 164 rows past the transom and confounds a raw width profile), the beam runs 50% of maximum at the bow tip and 88% at the transom — pointed at one end, square at the other, the clean inverse of [[lake-canoe]]'s symmetric leaf, which the canoe's own subject states twice. The outboard reads as the heavy dark block at the stern that no canoe has. Bench seats, oars, rivet lines and open interior all present; no rig. ⚠️ THE HULL IS BEAMY, exactly as the canoe's was: 2.02:1 against the 3:1 asked, so at world 40 it draws 34px by 15px. A 4.3 m boat carrying a 2.1 m beam is a wide tinny rather than a wrong boat, and it is invisible at 34px — accepted on the same reasoning as the canoe's 3.92-against-5.5. Already pointing up the frame on delivery, so no rotation. Confirmed on the camp sheet that it is the least punchy craft in the venue, as the slot predicted from dE 35 against the water; the value steps carry it and the dark interior is doing the work.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. A SECOND LAKE CABIN, smaller and older than the first, seen from straight above and ALONE. ⚠️ YOU ARE LOOKING AT THE ROOF AND THE ROOF IS ALMOST THE WHOLE PICTURE. Two equal slopes meeting along a RIDGE that runs the length of the cabin and points to the TOP of the frame, a clean straight line down the middle, eaves overhanging each long side just enough to show a thin band of log wall below and nothing more of the walls than that. No wall face, no window seen side-on, no post standing up. The cabin is about a third longer than it is wide and its long edges are PARALLEL. ⚠️ THE ROOF IS RUST-RED CORRUGATED IRON, NOT GREEN METAL, and this is the single most important thing about the asset — it is the one building in the venue that does not wear the camp's green. Old corrugated sheet: fine straight CORRUGATION LINES running down the slope from ridge to eave, closer together and softer than a standing seam, with patches where the paint has weathered thinner and the rust shows warmer. One slope catches the light. Build it from a lit slope near #9E4B2E, a shade slope near #7A3822, and corrugation lines near #5E2C1B. A short STOVEPIPE — a small dark circle with a pale collar, NOT a stone chimney — breaks the ridge near one end. AT ONE LONG SIDE a small open DECK projects, reading as a plain rectangle of pale weathered PLANKS laid across it, one plank width visible each, at a slightly lower level than the roof and with no rail standing up. Under the eaves the log wall shows as a narrow warm brown band near #7E5C3C with the round ends of the logs just visible at the corners. NOTHING ELSE: no path, no steps, no furniture on the deck, no smoke, no vehicle, no washing line, no sign. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the object is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it stands on.
assets.note: THE VARIANT THAT STOPS A SHORELINE REPEATING ITSELF. 7.8 m long, and 7.8 x 9.2 = 72u. ⚠️ IT IS SEPARATED FROM [[lake-cabin]] ON THREE AXES AT ONCE, deliberately, because a second building that differs only in size is the [[lake-boulder-small]] failure — one asset drawn twice. ROOF COLOUR is the loud one: rust-red against the camp's dark green, which measures dE 47 between the two roof tones themselves, so at 72px a viewer reads two different buildings before reading either one. ROOF MATERIAL is the quiet one: corrugated iron has a finer, softer line pitch than standing seam, so even desaturated the two roofs do not share a texture. And the FURNITURE differs — stovepipe and a deck here, stone chimney and a covered porch there. SIZE does the rest at 72 against 88, [[lake-camp-cabin]]'s 51 and [[lake-camp-lodge]]'s 166. THE RUST ALSO PAYS THE VENUE BACK, because Stillwater's committed palette is deep lake blue and pine green with 'warm cabin lights' as its accent, and this venue currently spends that accent almost nowhere — the cedar canoe and the fire ring's embers are the only warm marks in twenty props. A rust roof measures dE 28.5 from [[lake-forestfloor]] and 42.3 from [[lake-sand]], so it separates from both grounds better than the green roof does (26.5 and 33.9). ⚠️ DO NOT LET THE RUST DRIFT ORANGE. The swamp already owns 'rust roof metal' as an accent and this must stay a weathered dark red rather than becoming that venue's brighter oxide, or two venues start looking like each other. PLANE `surface`, CONTACT none. planRound FALSE at 1.33:1. Anchor footprint — the deck will pull the seeded bbox centre, so check the crosshair and correct to the cabin body by hand. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. ⚠️ DELIVERED 2026-08-16 AND REJECTED — NOT INGESTED, status stays `slot`. It is an AXONOMETRIC BOX SEEN CORNER-ON: two wall faces meet at a vertical corner edge down the middle of the picture, one lit and one shaded, which is a view from off the corner rather than from above. THREE MEASUREMENTS AGREE and none of them needed an eye. There is no ridge: the largest luminance step inside the body sits at 99% of its height, i.e. at the very bottom edge, where a gable roof in plan puts it at 50% (the lodge scored 41%, [[lake-camp-cabin]] 48%). The seam pitch DIFFERS BY 30% between upper and lower halves, 22.6 px against 32.0 — the foreshortening tell, and the same test that cleared the other two buildings in this batch condemns this one. And the content is 1257x1322, a ratio of 1.05, where the subject asks for a third longer than wide: a rectangular building photographed corner-on squares up, which is precisely what that number is showing. THE MATERIAL IS EXACTLY RIGHT and must be kept in the re-prompt — rust-red corrugated iron with the fine close line pitch that distinguishes it from the camp's standing seam, the stovepipe, the deck of pale planks. So this is a CAMERA regeneration on good material, the second in this venue after [[lake-cabin]]'s first attempt, and the lesson is the same one art-pipeline states: buildings are overwhelmingly photographed from a corner, and 'straight down' loses to that prior unless the subject fights it. Worth borrowing [[lake-camp-cabin]]'s wording, which won that fight at a 1% seam match. SECOND DELIVERY 2026-08-16 — ACCEPTED AND INGESTED, and it is the cleanest plan view in the venue by the numbers: the ridge sits at 51% of the body and the seam pitch across it is 24.3 px against 24.2, a ZERO PERCENT difference, against the rejected attempt's 99% ridge and 30% pitch split. Long edges parallel to 0.6% over the body. No white sticker stroke at all (0 px), the first delivery in the venue to arrive without one. Rust corrugated iron with the stovepipe and its pale collar, all as specified. ROTATED 90 CW ON INGEST rather than CCW — the lit slope here is the LOWER one (luma 74.1 against 65.6), so clockwise is what lands it on the left for the venue's up-left convention; verified after the bake at left 75.3 against right 66.0. TWO DEVIATIONS ACCEPTED. Aspect came back 1.07:1 against the 1.33 asked, so it draws 62x58px — a square cabin rather than one a third longer, which is a real building shape and costs nothing at 72px. And THE DECK AND THE LOG-WALL BAND ARE MISSING: the roof runs edge to edge with no eave overhang, so neither the pale plank deck nor the brown log band with its corner log ends made it. That thins the separation from [[lake-cabin]] from four axes to three, and the three that remain are the strong ones — rust against green (the loud one), 72u against 88u, stovepipe against stone chimney. Verified on a four-building sheet at true size: lodge, cabin, cabin-b and a row of camp cabins read as four different buildings, with the rust one separating first. ⚠️ ONE CLAIM IN THIS NOTE IS NOW WRONG and is corrected here rather than quietly edited: the roof MATERIAL is not a working separator. Measured, the corrugation pitch is 1.72% of the building's width against [[lake-camp-cabin]]'s standing seam at 1.84% — near identical, not the 'finer, closer line pitch' the subject asks for, and at 72px neither resolves individual lines anyway. Colour is carrying that job alone. Fine as it stands, but do not add a fourth green building expecting texture to tell it apart.

assets.subject: A RIVER GRAVEL BAR seen from directly overhead from about twenty metres up, in flat even light — the exposed cobble bar of a fast mountain salmon river in late summer, the water dropped and the stones dry. THE SQUARE COVERS ABOUT 28 METRES OF BAR, so this is a lot of ground and only the BIGGEST stones read as stones. The cobbles you actually draw as individual objects are two to four percent of the square's width — the half-metre-and-up stones a river leaves on a bar — and everything finer than that is not drawn as separate stones at all but as the granular tone of packed gravel between them. Draw the bar as a DENSE CARPET OF ROUNDED STONES with fine gravel packed between them — every stone worn smooth and oval by ice and water, none angular, none broken, none with a sharp corner. THE SIZE MIX IS THE SUBJECT: most of the surface is fine grey gravel too small to resolve into individual stones and reads as a granular tone; through it lie scattered larger cobbles that DO resolve, loosely grouped rather than evenly spaced, with a few of the biggest clustered as the current would have left them. THE COLOUR IS A MIXED STONE PALETTE AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES IT A RIVER BAR rather than a beach: cool BLUE-GREY stones near #6A6E73, CHARCOAL ones near #55534E, MUTED BROWN ones near #8A7A62, and occasionally a PALE GRANITE cobble near #A39E94 standing out lighter than the rest — no more than one stone in twenty-five. ⚠️ KEEP THE WHOLE SET INSIDE A NARROW VALUE RANGE. These four tones span about 30 points of lightness and that is the ceiling, not a starting point: this is the surface every boat, mark and prop is drawn on top of, and it has to lose the contrast fight with them. Vary the stones by HUE and by shape far more than by brightness, and give each stone a single soft tone rather than a bright top and a dark underside — the stones are lying on a flat bar in flat light, not modelled as little spheres. The overall impression averages to a neutral grey-brown near #7D7568. A FEW DAMP PATCHES where the bar dips, slightly darker and cooler than the dry stone around them, soft-edged and no more than a fifth of the square. NOTHING ELSE: no driftwood, no log, no plant, no grass tuft, no boulder big enough to name, no footprint, no water channel running through, no waterline. ⚠️ IT MUST TILE. The engine repeats this square edge to edge across a whole gravel bar, so the left edge has to continue into the right and the top into the bottom with no seam. AND IT MUST CARRY NO LIGHT DIRECTION: flat even overcast light, no sun angle, no cast shadows with a common direction, no vignette, no darker corners, no brighter centre. Anything that says 'this is the middle of the picture' becomes a grid of identical blotches once it is repeated. NO LANDMARK OF ANY KIND — nothing large enough or distinct enough to be recognised twice on screen, because the eye finds a repeat by finding a landmark. Vary the mixture across the square so no region reads as a copy of another.
assets.note: SOCKEYE RUN'S SIGNATURE GROUND and intended as the venue's DOMINANT non-vegetated terrain — exposed bars, inside bends, mid-river islands, the bridge approaches and the margins of every rapid. It is the asset that stops the river reading as generic sand. tileWorld 256 rather than the 128 the two lake grounds use, and the reason is coverage rather than detail: a gravel bar is a BIG continuous mass and a 128 tile would put a countable repeat every 14 m across it, where 256 covers 28 m and halves the number of repeats the eye can find in one glance. `gneiss` and `granite` already take 256 for the same reason. ⚠️ FEATURE SCALE IS STATED IN THE SUBJECT AS A FRACTION OF THE SQUARE, not in centimetres, because the generator cannot know the tile covers 28 m. At 9.2 units/m a 25 cm cobble is 0.8% of the square's width and an 80 cm boulder is 2.9% — the numbers in the subject are those, and getting them wrong is how a bar comes back looking like a close-up of a driveway. BODY COLOUR #7D7568 IS PROVISIONAL and must be reset to the DELIVERED tile mean on ingest, exactly as the three lake grounds were: ISLAND_STYLES.body has to equal the tile's own mean or the LAND_TEXTURES alpha stops being a pure contrast knob and starts shifting the colour. SEPARATION MEASURED AT THE PROVISIONAL VALUE: dE 24 from [[river-meadow]], 24 from [[river-outcrop]] and 26 from [[river-humus]], so all four of this venue's grounds tell apart; 25 from the river's deep water and 23 from its surface. Its nearest neighbour anywhere is the lake's `gneiss` at 9.7, which is cross-venue and honest — glacial cobble and a glacial slab are the same rock — and the two can never share a race. NOT IN LAND_TEXTURES YET: the style ships with a flat body first, which is art-pipeline 6's placeholder stage, and the texture entry lands with the art. ⚠️ THE FEATURE-SIZE CLAUSE WAS CORRECTED BEFORE ANY GENERATION, because the first draft contradicted the pipeline's own floor. prompt.py emits a scale line for every texture — 'the smallest feature that matters must be at least 16px across in this image' — which at a 1024 master is 1.56% of the square, and the draft asked for cobbles 'well under one percent'. Every stone would have been below the resolution floor and the tile would have come back as grey noise. The rewrite says what is physically true anyway: on 28 m of bar only the half-metre-and-up stones read as objects (2-4% of the square) and everything finer IS the matrix. CHECK THIS ON EVERY NEW TEXTURE SLOT — the subject states feature size as a fraction and the class add-on states a floor, and nobody is holding both numbers at once unless someone does it deliberately. ⚠️ FIRST DELIVERY 2026-08-16 REJECTED — IT DOES NOT TILE, which is the one thing a texture cannot be forgiven. Measured: the wrap seam carries 2.25x the pixel difference of an interior column boundary (14.39 against 6.39) and 1.82x on the horizontal (14.98 against 8.25). AND IT IS GEOMETRY, NOT TONE — high-passing the image to strip low-frequency drift leaves the ratios unchanged at 2.26x and 1.78x, so this is not a fixable brightness step across the join, it is stones cut in half at the edge and different stones butting against them. Confirmed by eye on a 2x2 tiling zoomed on the join. On the venue's DOMINANT ground that seam would appear on a grid across every bar in the river. WHAT THE DELIVERY GOT RIGHT, and it is most of it: evenness is excellent — quadrant luma spread 1.8 and edge bands within 2 of centre, so there is no vignette and no baked light direction, which is the failure this class usually dies of. The stone size mix, the rounded worn shapes and the four-colour palette are all as asked. So this is a WRAP regeneration on good art. ⚠️ IF A TOOL CAN HEAL IT, THE ART IS WORTH SAVING. This tile is statistically homogeneous (that same 1.8 spread), which is exactly the condition where an offset-and-heal makes an invisible join — roll the image by half in both axes so the seam lands in the middle, then clone over the cross. That is a standard texture operation and it would cost no generation; it is NOT done here because healing a carpet of distinct stones means cloning whole stones, which is an art edit rather than a measurement. ⚠️ AND THE SUBJECT ITSELF WAS WRONG, which the delivery exposed. Tile-scale luma sd came back 22.22 against a shipped band of 3.33 to 17.35 — busier than every ground in the game, including arctic granite. That is not the generator overshooting, it is THIS NOTE'S OWN PALETTE: the four tones as first written spanned 43 points of lightness (charcoal L* 29 to pale granite L* 72), and a ground asked for that range will deliver that contrast. It would have needed alpha 0.23 to sit at the shipped median, below the 0.30 floor any texture in the library uses. The palette is now narrowed to a 30-point range (charcoal 35, pale granite 65), the pale stones cut from one in fifteen to one in twenty-five, and a clause added that stones vary by HUE not brightness and are not modelled as spheres. Predicted tile sd after the change is about 15.5, which lands inside the band at alpha 0.33. COLOUR RAN DARK TOO: delivered mean #686460 at L* 43.0 against the provisional #7D7568 at 49.6, dE 8.6. That one is self-correcting — ISLAND_STYLES.body is reset to the delivered mean on ingest — but note it will pull the flat placeholder colour down with it, so re-measure the four-ground separations after the next delivery lands. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-17. ⚠️ AND THE ACCEPTANCE TEST FOR TEXTURES WAS WRONG UNTIL NOW, which is the transferable lesson and the reason two earlier deliveries were rejected that should not have been. The wrap seam was being measured on the RAW MASTER: all four of these carry a seam 1.5x to 3.3x an interior pixel boundary, and by that number none of them tiles. But a ground texture is never seen raw. It is composited at `alpha` over a flat body and drawn at `tile` px, and the alpha that tames the contrast multiplies the seam error by exactly the same factor. Rendered the way it ships and tiled 4.7 to 9.4 repeats across, the seam on every one of these is INVISIBLE. JUDGE A TEXTURE TILED, COMPOSITED AND AT SIZE — the same rule the sprite track already lives by, arrived at late here. Shipped mean #6E6B65 at L* 45.6, and ISLAND_STYLES.body is reset to it. THE NARROWED PALETTE WORKED ON HUE AND NOT ON VALUE: chroma fell to 3.9, so the mean is now essentially neutral grey — the blue-grey, brown and pale stones are all present but they cancel in the average, which is correct behaviour for a mixed bar. Tile sd only fell 22.22 -> 21.05 despite the 43 -> 30 L* narrowing, so the busyness is the STONE COUNT rather than the palette; alpha 0.42 lands it at on-screen sd 6.6, inside the shipped band. ⚠️ SEPARATION FROM [[river-outcrop]] CAME IN AT dE 19.6, tighter than the 23.8 planned, because both delivered closer to neutral than specced. Accepted because these two were never going to be told apart by colour: one is many rounded objects with gravel between them and the other is one mass broken by lines, and that survives with colour removed. Against water it is the weakest of the four — 19 from glacial teal, 21 from the current surface — so a bar meeting the water will read by its stones, not its tone.

assets.subject: AN ALPINE RIVER MEADOW seen from directly overhead from about ten metres up, in flat even light — the open grass terrace above a mountain river in high summer, grazed short by weather rather than mown. THE SQUARE COVERS ABOUT 14 METRES, so individual blades never resolve: what resolves is the TUSSOCK, a soft clump of grass a hand's width across, which is about one and a half percent of the square. Draw the meadow as a CLOSE MAT OF THOSE CLUMPS — soft-edged, irregular, packed against one another with no bare soil showing between them except in a very few small gaps. The clumps vary in tone but not in kind, so the surface reads as one continuous sward with quiet drift across it rather than as a pattern. ⚠️ IT IS MOSTLY GRASS AND ALMOST NO FLOWERS. Wildflowers are drawn in this venue as separate sprites scattered on top, so this tile carries at most a very few tiny pale specks — three or four in the whole square, each a single soft dot with no petals, no stem and no colour strong enough to name. A meadow tile with flowers baked into it repeats those flowers in a grid across every terrace in the venue, which is the one failure this subject exists to prevent. THE GREEN IS LUSH AND SUNLIT — a coastal Alaska river meadow in full summer, not a dry alpine sedge and not a shadowed one: a lit clump near #99C460, a body near #79A046 and a shade near #5C7B39 down between the clumps, averaging near #7FA94D. ⚠️ IT MUST NOT COME BACK DARK. This ground is OPEN — it is the terrace the forest does not cover — so it is the brightest surface in the venue after bare rock, and a meadow rendered at the value of shade under trees is the one failure this clause exists to prevent. Hold plenty of VALUE VARIETY between clumps as well, roughly 24 points of lightness from the lit crowns to the gaps, so the sward reads as many plants and not as one flat green sheet — but that variety comes from the plants themselves being lighter and darker, NEVER from a light direction, sun angle or cast shadow. Through it, drifts of DRY STRAW-COLOURED grass near #B4C06E where the season has bleached it, soft and patchy, perhaps a sixth of the square. A very few short dark seed heads standing among the clumps, drawn as fine dark flecks. NOTHING ELSE: no flower drawn as a recognisable flower, no rock, no bare earth patch large enough to name, no path, no animal track, no shrub, no water. ⚠️ IT MUST TILE. The engine repeats this square edge to edge across a whole gravel bar, so the left edge has to continue into the right and the top into the bottom with no seam. AND IT MUST CARRY NO LIGHT DIRECTION: flat even overcast light, no sun angle, no cast shadows with a common direction, no vignette, no darker corners, no brighter centre. Anything that says 'this is the middle of the picture' becomes a grid of identical blotches once it is repeated. NO LANDMARK OF ANY KIND — nothing large enough or distinct enough to be recognised twice on screen, because the eye finds a repeat by finding a landmark. Vary the mixture across the square so no region reads as a copy of another.
assets.note: THE VENUE'S OPEN GROUND — river terraces, the clearings between forest stands, the bridge surrounds. tileWorld 128, matching `grass` and `swampgrass`, because a sward's readable feature is the tussock and 128 puts it at about 20 cm, which is what a hand-sized clump actually measures. ⚠️ THE FLOWERS-AS-SPRITES DECISION IS THE OWNER'S AND IT IS WRITTEN INTO THE SUBJECT AS A NEGATIVE, not left implied. A tiling square repeats everything in it, so a baked flower is a flower that appears on a fixed grid across the whole terrace — the same failure the no-landmark clause covers, but far more visible because a flower is a colour accent and the eye hunts it. Scattering them as props instead costs one small `world-prop` slot and buys irregular placement for free. BODY #6E7A45 IS PROVISIONAL, reset to the delivered tile mean on ingest. Separation: dE 24 from [[river-cobble]], 40 from [[river-outcrop]], 31 from [[river-humus]], and 25 from the river's own surface water.
