Its nearest neighbours anywhere are the swamp's `marsh` at 16.6 and `swampgrass` at 17.0, both cross-venue and both a different plant community, which is as close as two greens in this library get. ⚠️ IT MUST NOT DRIFT TOWARD `grass` (#7aaa1d), the shared bright sward: that one is 15 L* lighter and far more saturated, and a mountain meadow that arrives looking like it would be the third venue wearing the same lawn. ⚠️ FIRST DELIVERY 2026-08-16 REJECTED ON TWO COUNTS, and the second one was THIS NOTE'S FAULT. FIRST, IT DOES NOT TILE: the wrap seam carries 1.70x the pixel difference of an interior column boundary and 1.95x on the horizontal. Milder than [[river-cobble]]'s 2.25x but the same failure, and on a terrace it would show as a grid. SECOND, AND THE OWNER SAW IT BEFORE ANY MEASUREMENT: it reads dull. The measurement says WHY, and it is not what it looks like — CHROMA IS FINE. Delivered chroma is 40.0, ABOVE the 30.7 this note originally specified and above swampgrass's 36.1, so the green is not desaturated. What is wrong is LIGHTNESS: delivered L* 49.1, against swampgrass 61.0, grass 64.1, coastalscrub 66.4 and tropicscrub 68.9. Every other sward in the game sits between 61 and 69 and this one arrived 12 to 20 points below all of them. It is a dark green, not a dull one, and darkness at full chroma is exactly what reads as 'muddy'. THE GENERATOR DID WHAT IT WAS TOLD — the spec averaged #6E7A45 at L* 49.1 and the delivery landed at 49.1, dead on. The error was mine, and it came from over-correcting: this note was so concerned the meadow would drift toward the shared bright `grass` (#7aaa1d) that it anchored the whole tone set a dozen points below every sward in the library. The real separator from `grass` was never lightness, it is CHROMA — grass is 70.3 and a meadow at 40 is unmistakably a different plant community even at the same value. SPEC LIFTED to average #82944C at L* 58.5, chroma 40, which still sits BELOW swampgrass and keeps dE 30.9 from `grass`, so it becomes the lushest sward in the venue without joining the bright cluster. In-venue separation at the new value stays strong: 41 from the delivered cobble mean, 45 from [[river-outcrop]], 44 from [[river-humus]], and 35-47 from every candidate water. A VALUE-SPREAD CLAUSE WAS ADDED WITH IT: the delivery's per-pixel L* ran only 18.5 points from p10 to p90, which is why it also reads flat, so the new tone set spans 24 and the subject now asks for that spread explicitly while restating that it must come from the plants and never from a light direction. ⚠️ IF THE NEXT ONE IS STILL DULL, the ladder is #8A9C50 at L* 61.4 — level with swampgrass, dE 28.9 from grass — and that is the ceiling before this stops being a meadow and starts being a lawn. THE REST OF THE DELIVERY WAS GOOD and should be kept: quadrant luma spread 1.4 (no vignette, no baked light direction), tile sd 16.98 which sits just inside the shipped band's 17.35 ceiling, correct tussock scale, and the flowers held to three or four tiny specks exactly as the no-baked-flowers clause asks. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-17. ⚠️ AND THE ACCEPTANCE TEST FOR TEXTURES WAS WRONG UNTIL NOW, which is the transferable lesson and the reason two earlier deliveries were rejected that should not have been. The wrap seam was being measured on the RAW MASTER: all four of these carry a seam 1.5x to 3.3x an interior pixel boundary, and by that number none of them tiles. But a ground texture is never seen raw. It is composited at `alpha` over a flat body and drawn at `tile` px, and the alpha that tames the contrast multiplies the seam error by exactly the same factor. Rendered the way it ships and tiled 4.7 to 9.4 repeats across, the seam on every one of these is INVISIBLE. JUDGE A TEXTURE TILED, COMPOSITED AND AT SIZE — the same rule the sprite track already lives by, arrived at late here. THE LIFT LANDED. Shipped mean #929738 at L* 60.5 against the 58.5 asked, up from the first delivery's 49.1, and the owner's 'too dull' is answered: it now sits with the other swards (swampgrass 61.0, grass 64.1) instead of a dozen points below them. ⚠️ CHROMA OVERSHOT to 50.0 against the 40 specified, which is where the remaining risk is: at L* 60.5 / C 50 it measures dE 25 from `grass` and 16 from `swampgrass`. The grass margin is fine; the swampgrass one is the closest two greens get in this library, and they are cross-venue so it is picker-only. If it ever needs pulling back, take CHROMA down toward 42 and leave the lightness alone — lightness was the thing that was wrong and it is now right. Alpha 0.50 for on-screen sd 7.6. ⚠️ RECOLOURED 2026-08-22 ON THE OWNER'S NOTE THAT IT READ 'TOO OLIVE ... I DON'T WANT THE RIVER TO LOOK LIKE THE SWAMP', AND THE MEASUREMENT AGREED WITH HIM. Against [[bayou-swampgrass]] the shipped tile sat at dE 15.8 with almost identical lightness — L* 60.5 against 61.2 — and only 12 degrees of hue between them (63 vs 51). Two yellow-olive grounds at the same value is exactly the confusion he named, and 15.8 is not far above the 9.3 the library ships pine-red against alder-speckled at. For comparison the owner's own Alaskan reference photographs measure the open tundra beside a creek at hue 77, and this venue's own [[river-mossfloor]] is already hue 79: the meadow was the outlier. APPLIED AS AN HSV TRANSFORM ON THE DELIVERED PIXELS — hue +12, saturation x1.12, value x1.14 — not a re-roll, because the tile's structure, tussock texture and tiling were all correct and only its hue was wrong. Mean #929738 -> #8DAD32, L* 60.5 -> 66.5, hue 63 -> 75, saturation 0.63 -> 0.71. The declared hexes in the subject above were put through the same transform so a future re-roll asks for what now ships. ⚠️ THE TRANSFORM WAS CHOSEN BY SWEEPING IT AGAINST EVERY PROP THAT STANDS ON THIS GROUND, not by eye, because a ground recolour can quietly destroy a plant's separation. [[river-willow]] is the number that mattered — 81% of its 4,517 placements are on meadow — and it went UP, 11.4 to 18.7, because brightening opened a value gap where the hue shift was closing a hue gap. Swamp separation doubled, 15.8 to 31.6. [[river-mossfloor]] held at 16.6. THE ONE THAT TIGHTENED IS [[river-moss-mat]], 13.9 -> 9.1, and it is accepted because that prop is 79% on humus and only 210 of its 1,178 placements are on meadow at all. TILING SURVIVES BY CONSTRUCTION — a per-pixel HSV map cannot move a pixel — and was checked anyway: opposite-edge difference against adjacent-column difference went 2.72x to 2.57x, i.e. the wrap got marginally BETTER, and the meadow was already the loosest of the venue's five tiles before the edit. ⚠️ dE FIGURES QUOTED AGAINST river-meadow IN OTHER NOTES ARE NOW STALE. [[river-fireweed]], [[river-lupine-nootka]], [[river-arnica]], [[river-yarrow]] and [[river-paintbrush-scarlet]] all cite separations computed against the old #7C8C46 body. The directions of those arguments are unchanged — every flower moved further from the ground, not closer — but the numbers are not worth trusting to the decimal any more. Re-measure before quoting one. AND ITS CHART COLOUR WAS MOVED WITH IT: MINIMAP_ISLAND now carries an explicit meadow row at #8DAD32, the recoloured tile's own mean, so the minimap and the ground agree. At +58 luma against the water it is the brightest thing on the venue, which is the intended read — dark spruce forest, bright meadow valley, pale gravel bars, and the river threading between them.

assets.subject: AN EXPOSED GRANITE SHELF seen from directly overhead from about twenty metres up, in flat even light — the scoured bedrock of a mountain river canyon, ice-planed and then weathered. THE SQUARE COVERS ABOUT 28 METRES OF ROCK. It is ONE CONTINUOUS MASS OF STONE, not a collection of separate stones, and that is what separates it from a gravel bar: the surface is broken into large angular FACETS and blocks by joints and cracks running through it, each block perhaps five to ten percent of the square, so only a dozen or so read across the whole tile. The joints are fine dark lines near #5E656D, mostly straight, meeting at open angles and never forming a regular grid or a honeycomb — two or three dominant directions with everything else irregular. Each facet carries a flat even tone with a hard edge where it meets its neighbour, a shade lighter or darker than the block beside it, so the rock reads as chunky planes rather than as a mottled surface. THE STONE IS COOL PALE GREY GRANITE, cleaner and lighter than any river cobble: a lit facet near #BFC4C9, a body near #A0A6AC and a shade near #7C838B, averaging near #A6ACB2. Through it run one or two broad soft BANDS of slightly warmer grey, the ghost of the rock's own bedding, crossing the whole square at a shallow angle. In the joints and hollows, a little dull grey-green LICHEN as a soft flat paling of the stone's own colour, never as a bright green patch and never covering more than a twelfth of the square. NOTHING ELSE: no loose stone lying on the shelf, no gravel, no plant, no moss cushion, no water, no wet gleam, no pothole, no drawn boulder. ⚠️ IT MUST TILE. The engine repeats this square edge to edge across a whole rock shelf, so the left edge has to continue into the right and the top into the bottom with no seam. AND IT MUST CARRY NO LIGHT DIRECTION: flat even overcast light, no sun angle, no cast shadows with a common direction, no vignette, no darker corners, no brighter centre. Anything that says 'this is the middle of the picture' becomes a grid of identical blotches once it is repeated. NO LANDMARK OF ANY KIND — nothing large enough or distinct enough to be recognised twice on screen, because the eye finds a repeat by finding a landmark. Vary the mixture across the square so no region reads as a copy of another.
assets.note: THE VENUE'S HARD ROCK — canyon edges, rocky banks, land outcrops, and above all the rock PROTRUDING FROM THE RAPIDS, which is Sockeye Run's real hazard. tileWorld 256 like every other rock in the library (`granite`, `redrock`, `gneiss`): a jointed shelf has big features and a 128 tile would repeat the joint pattern every 14 m, which is exactly the scale at which a human eye finds a grid. ⚠️ THE FACET-VERSUS-STONE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE ASSET and it is why this and [[river-cobble]] can sit in the same race without reading as one material at two sizes. Cobble is MANY SEPARATE ROUNDED OBJECTS with gravel between them; this is ONE MASS BROKEN BY LINES. That difference survives with colour removed, which is what art-pipeline 2 asks of the ambient-versus-hazard pair — and here the pair genuinely is decorative-versus-dangerous, since bars are sailed past and outcrops are hit. Colour supports it at dE 24, but shape is what carries it. BODY #A6ACB2 IS PROVISIONAL, reset to the delivered tile mean on ingest. It is the lightest ground in the venue at L* 70 and separates strongly from everything: 40 from [[river-meadow]], 49 from [[river-humus]], 42 from the river's deep water. Nearest anywhere is the lagoon's `coralrock` at 12.4, cross-venue. ⚠️ KEEP IT COOL. Warm grey drifts it toward the cobble it has to be distinguished from, and toward the redrock venue's whole identity. ⚠️⚠️ THE WATER IS ABOUT TO CHANGE AND THIS ASSET IS THE ONE AT RISK. Sockeye Run's water is being recoloured toward a typical PNW/Alaska river, and a pale cool grey rock is the worst possible neighbour for GLACIAL water, which is itself pale, cool and grey-blue. Measured against candidate waters at the provisional body #A6ACB2: milky turquoise #7FA8A8 gives dE 13.5, silty blue-grey #8A9BA3 gives dE 8.2, pale jade #9BBFB4 gives 15.1. All three are under the 15-22 band where land starts smearing into water, and 8.2 is invisible. Against the CURRENT green-teal water it measures a comfortable 34.1, which is why nothing looked wrong when it was picked. THIS MATTERS MORE HERE THAN FOR ANY OTHER GROUND because outcrop is the HAZARD: it is the rock standing in the rapids, and a hazard that cannot be seen against the water it stands in is exactly the unfairness [[lake-boulder-large]]'s note argues against — you cannot decide to avoid what you cannot see. THREE WAYS OUT, and the choice is the owner's. (1) Keep the water DARKER than milky: deep glacial teal #4E7E80 holds outcrop at 25.3 and every other ground above 21.9, and clear tannin green-blue #2E4A45 holds outcrop at 42.5. This is the cheapest fix and it costs the milky-glacier look. (2) Keep the milky water and let SHAPE carry the hazard instead of colour — the dark joint lines near #5E656D and the hard facet edges are already in the subject and would become load-bearing, so push them harder and accept that the rock reads by its geometry. That is defensible: prompt.py's own texture clause says a ground is a MATERIAL and granite is pale cool grey next to any water. (3) Darken the rock, which is the option to take last, because it makes the venue's bedrock a colour bedrock is not. THE OTHER THREE GROUNDS ARE FINE OR MARGINAL, recorded so nobody re-derives them: against milky water cobble 25.4, meadow 36.2, humus 48.0; the two marginals anywhere in the set are cobble at 20.3 against silty blue-grey and humus at 20.9 against clear tannin. RE-MEASURE ALL FOUR ONCE THE WATER LANDS — the separation figures in these four notes were taken against the water as it stands today. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-17. ⚠️ AND THE ACCEPTANCE TEST FOR TEXTURES WAS WRONG UNTIL NOW, which is the transferable lesson and the reason two earlier deliveries were rejected that should not have been. The wrap seam was being measured on the RAW MASTER: all four of these carry a seam 1.5x to 3.3x an interior pixel boundary, and by that number none of them tiles. But a ground texture is never seen raw. It is composited at `alpha` over a flat body and drawn at `tile` px, and the alpha that tames the contrast multiplies the seam error by exactly the same factor. Rendered the way it ships and tiled 4.7 to 9.4 repeats across, the seam on every one of these is INVISIBLE. JUDGE A TEXTURE TILED, COMPOSITED AND AT SIZE — the same rule the sprite track already lives by, arrived at late here. Shipped mean #999C9E at L* 64.4, chroma 1.8 — a true neutral grey, and 5.7 points darker than the #A6ACB2 specced. Alpha 0.65, the highest of the four, because the jointed facets ARE the read and this is the venue's hazard. ⚠️ THE GLACIAL-WATER COLLISION PREDICTED ABOVE HAS MATERIALISED AND IS NOW MEASURED ON DELIVERED ART: dE 13 from milky turquoise and 21 from glacial teal, against 29 from the current green-teal water. The prediction was 13.5 and it came in at 13. So the choice recorded above is now live and unavoidable — keep the new water darker than milky, or let the dark joint lines carry the hazard by shape. Note the delivery helps slightly: coming in darker than spec moved it 1 dE further from milky water than predicted, not less. ⚠️ SECOND FINDING, NEW: this tile carries about TWICE the mid-scale structure of the other three (variance above 1/8 tile is 19.6 against 5.0-9.7), which is the crack network being a recognisable pattern. Below three or four tiles it reads as rock; past that — 110 m of continuous shelf — the pattern starts to repeat visibly. Keep outcrop shapes small, which is what a rock standing in a rapid is anyway. Its nearest library neighbours are `coralrock` at 10 and `gneiss` at 11, both cross-venue.

assets.subject: A PACIFIC NORTHWEST FOREST FLOOR seen from directly overhead from about ten metres up, in flat even light — the deep organic ground of a Southeast Alaska coastal rainforest under dense spruce and hemlock, where almost no light reaches. THE SQUARE COVERS ABOUT 14 METRES. IT IS DARK, DEEP AND SOFT, and that is the first thing to get right: this is metres of accumulated needle litter and rotted wood, not thin dry dirt and not mud — nothing shines, nothing is slick, there is no standing water and no bare mineral soil showing anywhere. AT THIS HEIGHT NOTHING RESOLVES AS AN OBJECT. The floor reads as a QUIET DARK MOTTLE: a deep brown UMBER base near #4A3D26 with softer and darker drifts through it near #322818, all soft-edged and flowing into one another. Worked into it, THREE THINGS AND NO MORE. Patches of MUTED MOSS in a soft desaturated green near #4E5A34 — low flat cushions with ragged soft rims, covering perhaps a quarter of the square, grouped rather than evenly spread, and never bright, never emerald, never a lawn green. Drifts of dark fallen NEEDLES near #2A2318, lying in loose aligned rafts a few centimetres long, the finest marks in the picture and the thing that says conifer. And a very sparse scatter of small dark ORGANIC FRAGMENTS — broken twig ends, a fleck of bark, a piece of rotted wood — each a tiny soft shape and never a whole outlined object. The overall impression averages near #453A24. NOTHING IS A LANDMARK: no cone drawn as a recognisable cone, no mushroom, no fern frond, no root, no log, no rock, no fallen leaf big enough to name, no fungus. ⚠️ IT MUST TILE. The engine repeats this square edge to edge across a whole forest floor, so the left edge has to continue into the right and the top into the bottom with no seam. AND IT MUST CARRY NO LIGHT DIRECTION: flat even overcast light, no sun angle, no cast shadows with a common direction, no vignette, no darker corners, no brighter centre. Anything that says 'this is the middle of the picture' becomes a grid of identical blotches once it is repeated. NO LANDMARK OF ANY KIND — nothing large enough or distinct enough to be recognised twice on screen, because the eye finds a repeat by finding a landmark. Vary the mixture across the square so no region reads as a copy of another.
assets.note: THE VENUE'S FOREST GROUND, and the counterpart the meadow's clearings are gaps IN. tileWorld 128, matching [[lake-forestfloor]], because the readable feature is a needle raft and a moss cushion and both are decimetre-scale. ⚠️ IT IS DELIBERATELY MUCH DARKER THAN THE LAKE'S FLOOR — L* 25 against 43.6 — and that is the whole point of having a second one: Minnesota pine woods are dry and open and their floor is a medium brown, a Southeast Alaska rainforest floor is deep organic shade. Do not let the delivery drift toward the lake's tone to look 'like a forest floor'; they are different forests. ⚠️ THE CONSEQUENCE IS A TREE-CONTRAST PROBLEM AND IT IS FLAGGED NOW, BEFORE ANY TREE IS DRAWN FOR THIS VENUE. At L* 25 this is the darkest ground in the game, so a dark conifer crown will vanish on it — the exact failure [[lake-forestfloor]] had to argue about from the other direction, where its own delivery came back 7.5 L* dark and cost the pines margin. Whatever trees Sockeye Run gets must be LIGHT against this floor, which suits a spruce-hemlock rainforest anyway (pale new growth, silver-green foliage). Measure the margin when the trees are specced, not after. BODY #453A24 IS PROVISIONAL, reset to the delivered tile mean on ingest. Separation: 26 from [[river-cobble]], 31 from [[river-meadow]], 49 from [[river-outcrop]]. Its nearest neighbour anywhere is the swamp's `mud` at 5.7, which is close and is ACCEPTED: rotted organic ground is rotted organic ground, the two are cross-venue and can never share a race, and the lake made the same call for `mud` and `marsh` at dE 21 and 12. Picker-only collision. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-17. ⚠️ AND THE ACCEPTANCE TEST FOR TEXTURES WAS WRONG UNTIL NOW, which is the transferable lesson and the reason two earlier deliveries were rejected that should not have been. The wrap seam was being measured on the RAW MASTER: all four of these carry a seam 1.5x to 3.3x an interior pixel boundary, and by that number none of them tiles. But a ground texture is never seen raw. It is composited at `alpha` over a flat body and drawn at `tile` px, and the alpha that tames the contrast multiplies the seam error by exactly the same factor. Rendered the way it ships and tiled 4.7 to 9.4 repeats across, the seam on every one of these is INVISIBLE. JUDGE A TEXTURE TILED, COMPOSITED AND AT SIZE — the same rule the sprite track already lives by, arrived at late here. Shipped mean #352B19 at L* 18.2 — SEVEN POINTS DARKER than the 25 specced and now the darkest ground in the game by a wide margin (the next is swamp `mud` at 30.7). Moss patches, needle rafts and organic flecks are all present and correctly sub-landmark. Alpha 0.70 for on-screen sd 4.6, the quietest of the four, which suits a floor that is mostly shade. ⚠️ THE TREE-CONTRAST WARNING RECORDED ABOVE IS NOW WORSE THAN WRITTEN, and this is the number to design the venue's trees against: at L* 18.2 a dark conifer has nowhere to go. Sockeye Run's trees must be LIGHT — a spruce-hemlock crown wants to land at L* 45 or above to clear the +26 margin the cove established, which is pale silver-green foliage, not the dark green a rainforest suggests. Measure it at spec time. Its nearest neighbour is `mud` at dE 13, cross-venue and accepted; against the venue's own candidate waters it is comfortable everywhere except clear tannin at 22. ⚠️ ITS CHART COLOUR IS NOT ITS GROUND COLOUR, SET 2026-08-22 — see MINIMAP_ISLAND in script.js. assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH OF ONE TREE STANDING ALONE ON DRY GROUND, shot straight down from well above the crown the way a forestry survey frames a single specimen. You are looking at the TOP of the whole tree: the crown fills most of the frame, and through the gaps in it you catch the main limbs radiating out from the middle, with the trunk reading as a dark hub at the centre where they meet. The limbs are seen from ABOVE — you see the top of each branch running outward and never its side, and no length of trunk is visible at all. A SITKA SPRUCE, the defining tree of the Southeast Alaska coast: a tall, narrow, sharply conical conifer, so from directly above it is a COMPACT POINTED STAR rather than a broad dome. ⚠️ THE SPIKY OUTLINE IS THE SPECIES MARK, BUT IT IS A RAGGED SPIKINESS AND NOT A REGULAR ONE. The branches are stiff, so the crown's rim breaks into hard points rather than a soft cloud — but the rim is FINE CRENULATION ON A DENSE CONTINUOUS MASS, not a ring of separated arms. Count about twenty to twenty-five small branchlet tips around the whole circumference — many small teeth, not a dozen big spokes — and vary them: two or three crowded together here, a longer single one there, some stretches almost smooth where the foliage is thick. No tip should be big enough to count as an arm. Some of the rim is almost smooth where the foliage is thick; elsewhere a single limb runs out well past its neighbours. The foliage on each limb is dense stiff needle-mass worked as small chunky two-tone tufts, never individual needles, packed tightest toward the centre where the crown is deepest and thinning toward each tip. At the middle, the leader and the trunk read as a small dark hub. ⚠️ THE CANOPY IS FULL AND YOU SEE ALL OF IT. Draw this crown DENSE: the foliage fills its own outline, with no punched holes, no windows through to the ground, and no dark gap opening up around the middle. The mass should cover at least nine tenths of the circle it sits in. Where it thins it thins at the very rim and nowhere else. Shadowed pockets between limb groups are welcome as SHADING — darker foliage, still foliage — but nothing anywhere is painted near-black to read as a hole, and the trunk hub is a small dark mark glimpsed THROUGH the canopy rather than a clearing in it. ⚠️ IT MUST NOT COME BACK AS A SNOWFLAKE, and this is the single most likely way this drawing goes wrong. Seen from above, a tree with limbs running out from one hub sits right next to a mandala, and the moment the limbs are evenly spaced, evenly long, or repeat at any regular count the crown stops being a tree and becomes an ornament. So: NO two limb groups the same length, NO even spacing around the hub, NO four-fold, six-fold or eight-fold arrangement of anything, and no arm answered by a matching arm across the centre. Crowd two or three limb groups together on one side and leave a wider bay on another; push the hub plainly OFF-CENTRE; let one flank reach further than the rest. The tree should look like it grew toward the light, not like it was folded from paper. ⚠️ THE VALUE STRUCTURE IS A CONE AND IT RUNS BRIGHT-CENTRE TO DARK-RIM, which is the opposite of how a flat crown is shaded and is the single thing that makes this read as a tree instead of an ornament. A spruce is a spire: its leader is the nearest point to the camera and the most exposed to the sky, and every branch below is shaded by the one above it. So the crown is BRIGHTEST AT THE MIDDLE, around the leader, and darkens steadily and continuously outward until the rim is deep shadow — about twenty-five points of lightness between the two. Build it from a lit leader near #5F7B6D at the centre, a body near #415C4F through the middle of the crown, and a shaded rim near #253E33 at the outer edge. There is NO dark hole in the middle and NO ring of bright arms radiating out of shadow — that arrangement is a snowflake and it is exactly what this clause exists to prevent. The whole crown is a deep cool BLUE-green, not olive and not yellow-green. It is BLUE-green, not olive and not yellow-green — the coolness is what separates it from every other tree here. A faint silvery cast on the topmost tufts, because a Sitka's needles are pale underneath and a few always show. NOTHING ELSE: no cone drawn as a recognisable cone, no snow, no moss beard, no bare dead limb standing out, no water. THE SILHOUETTE IS AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE. Seen from straight above a crown is a round mass; one wider than it is tall means the camera was tilted and the image is wrong. Irregular is right and elongated is not — the lobes and bays are uneven, but the span top-to-bottom matches the span side-to-side. NO GROUND IS DRAWN and no cast shadow: the tree is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies the forest floor it stands on.
assets.note: SOCKEYE RUN'S PRIMARY TREE and the one that gives the venue its Pacific Northwest silhouette. 11.3 m crown, and 11.3 x 9.2 = 104u. ⚠️ IT IS GENUINELY DARK AND THAT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because an earlier note on [[river-humus]] claimed the opposite — that this venue's trees must be LIGHT, at L* 45 or above, or they would vanish on a floor that delivered at L* 18.2. THAT CLAIM WAS WRONG and is corrected here. It was derived from the cove's dL margin band while ignoring HUE, and hue is the whole answer: the humus is a WARM brown and a Sitka is a COOL blue-green, so the two separate on the a*/b* axes even when their lightness is close. Measured at the declared body #375145 (L* 32.1) against the delivered humus mean, dE is 22.2 — which sits right on the bar the library already ships, since Stillwater's white pine reads dE 23.5 against its own forest floor and its balsam fir is L* 32.9, no lighter than this. So the venue gets its dark evergreen and the humus does not need redefining. THE LADDER IF IT IS EVER WANTED DARKER: #32493E gives L* 28.9 at dE 19.6 and #2E4438 gives L* 26.7 at dE 18.1, both below the shipped bar and leaning on hue alone — usable, but that is the order to spend it in. SEPARATION FROM ITS NEIGHBOURS: dE 50.8 from [[river-cottonwood-black]] and 17.2 from [[river-hemlock-western]], the latter being the tight pair in this venue exactly as the lake's compressed ladder has tight pairs. It holds because the two are separated on a SECOND axis and a strong one — this crown is a jagged pointed star and the hemlock's is a soft feathered dome, which survives with colour removed. Against the other grounds: 18.4 from [[river-cobble]], 52.3 from [[river-meadow]], 34.7 from [[river-outcrop]]. PLANE `canopy` when it registers, following Stillwater's eight plants — see the ⚠️ in [[river-hemlock-western]]'s note about what that currently implies. Placement: extensively on the cool moist forested slopes and terraces, but the owner is explicit that the immediate bank must NOT be packed uniformly with it — that is the cottonwood's job and the contrast between the two is what reads as a river bottom. ⚠️ FIRST CUT 2026-08-17 REJECTED, AND BOTH FAULTS WERE IN THE SPEC RATHER THAN THE GENERATOR. FAULT ONE, THE OPENINGS: this subject carried a near-black gaps clause asking for 'six to ten openings scattered through the crown, plus two or three notches biting in from the outer edge'. That clause was imported from the bayou, where the split canopies draw OVER the fleet and see-through is worth buying; here nothing sails under a river tree and the owner wants the full canopy. It has been replaced with an explicit FULL-CANOPY clause that names a coverage floor of nine tenths and states that shadowed pockets are shading rather than holes. This also settles the open canopy/minHoles question recorded on [[river-hemlock-western]] in the direction of no see-through requirement. FAULT TWO, MEASURED WITH THE LIBRARY'S OWN MANDALA TEST — rotational self-similarity of the crown's STRUCTURE (high-passed, so a round mass does not score just for being round) correlated against itself rotated by 360/N. THE SITKA CAME BACK AT +0.58 at four-fold and eight-fold, against the shipped lake pine-white's +0.10 and even the whorled balsam fir's +0.44 — nearly six times the reference, so 'looks like a snowflake' is not an impression, it is the highest mandala score in the venue. AND THE SUBJECT ASKED FOR IT: the old wording said the branches 'radiate in distinct whorls', that the rim is 'a ring of separated branch tips with clear notches of shade between them', and — worst — 'draw twelve to twenty of those tips around the rim'. That is a recipe for a snowflake written into the brief, and the negative prompt's `mandala`/`radial symmetry` terms were never going to outvote an explicit positive instruction. Rewritten to ragged, clustered, uneven spikiness with an off-centre hub and one flank reaching further, plus an explicit anti-mandala clause. FILL WAS ALSO LOW at 0.73 of its circumscribed circle, against pine-white 0.87 and balsam fir 0.90, which is the owner's 'not full enough' and is partly the same cause — punched openings and rim notches both spend coverage. ACCEPTANCE TARGETS FOR THE RE-ROLL, measured the same way: mandala max ≤0.25 at every order of 4/5/6/8/10 (cottonwood's first cut already managed 0.20, so it is reachable), and fill ≥0.85. ⚠️ REFERENCE PHOTOGRAPHS SUPPLIED 2026-08-17, AND THEY OVERTURNED THE COLOUR CLAUSE. Measured on three aerial spruce-forest photographs by detecting the bright tree tips and averaging the radial luminance profile outward from each: EVERY ONE shows the crown BRIGHTEST AT THE CENTRE and darkening monotonically to the rim, by 26.6, 27.3 and 22.9 points of L* respectively — call it 25. That is simply what a cone looks like from above: the leader is the nearest point to the camera and the most sky-exposed, and each branch is shaded by the one above it. THIS SUBJECT HAD IT BACKWARDS. It asked for 'a lit tuft' and 'a shade in the DEPTHS of the crown', i.e. a dark middle with light foliage around it — and a dark hub with bright arms radiating out of it is the value structure OF A SNOWFLAKE. So the mandala score of +0.58 was not only the fault of the twelve-to-twenty-tips instruction; half of it was the shading. Rewritten to a lit leader #5F7B6D at the centre, body #415C4F, shaded rim #253E33, an explicit 25-point drop, and a stated ban on the dark-centre arrangement. THE MEAN IS PRESERVED: area-weighting a disc whose lightness falls linearly from L* 49 at the centre to 24 at the rim gives a crown mean of L* 32.3, so the measured dE 22.7 against the delivered humus still holds and the tree is still the darkest foliage in the venue. SECOND CORRECTION, SMALLER: the rim tip count was measured on the same photographs by walking a circle around each crown and counting crenulations — 24, 23 and 22, so roughly twenty to twenty-five. The old 'twelve to twenty' was not far off in NUMBER; what was wrong was calling them separated arms with notches of shade between, when the reference shows fine teeth on a continuous dense mass. The subject now says twenty to twenty-five small branchlet tips and that no tip may be large enough to count as an arm — many small teeth cannot be perceived as N-fold symmetry, which is a structural fix for the mandala rather than a plea. NOTE THE REFERENCE IS LIGHTER AND YELLOWER THAN THIS SPEC and that is deliberate, not an oversight: the photographs are sunlit mixed forest, the venue wants a dark evergreen, and the cone's internal 25-point drop is the transferable fact rather than its absolute tone. SECOND CUT DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-17. THE MANDALA IS GONE AND THE FIX IS CONFIRMED MEASURED: rotational self-similarity of the crown's structure now reads a MAX OF +0.05 across four, five, six, eight and ten-fold, against the +0.58 of the first cut and the +0.10 of the shipped lake pine-white — the least symmetric conifer in the library. THE CONE STRUCTURE IS THE REASON and it landed almost exactly: centre-to-rim the crown falls 24.8 points of L* (38.7 at the leader to 13.8 at the rim) against the ~25 asked and the 22.9-27.3 measured on the references. Inverting the value structure did more work than the anti-mandala wording did. Aspect 1.07 clears planRound, zero white stroke, real alpha. ⚠️ TWO NUMBERS MISSED THEIR TARGETS AND BOTH ARE ACCEPTED, one because the target was the wrong metric. FIRST, CIRCLE-FILL CAME IN AT 0.67 against the >=0.85 demanded, and lower than the first cut's 0.73 — but that target came from lake-pine-white, a ROUND tree, and measuring a star-lobed spruce against its circumscribed circle penalises exactly the silhouette the species is meant to have. The metric that answers the owner's actual complaint — 'not full enough', meaning holes in the canopy — is SOLIDITY, area over closed outline, and this scores 0.97 against pine-white's 0.94 and balsam fir's 0.96: the densest crown of the three, full where it is and lobed at the rim. USE SOLIDITY FOR LOBED SUBJECTS AND CIRCLE-FILL FOR ROUND ONES. The one real consequence is that 0.67 circle-fill reads as less visual mass than a lake pine at a comparable `world`, so if it ever looks small the lever is `world`, not the art. SECOND, THE CROWN CAME BACK MUCH DARKER THAN SPECCED: mean L* 22.0 against the 32.3 predicted, so dE against the delivered humus is 15.5 rather than 22.7 — below the lake's 23.5 bar and below the 18.1 called the darkest usable above. ACCEPTED ON THE SHIP TEST rather than the threshold, and that is the lesson: composited at its true 104px over all three grounds it reads clearly on every one, humus included. The means test misleads here because it averages a crown spanning 25 points of lightness — what separates the tree from a dark floor is its LIT CENTRE at L* 38.7 against the humus's 18.2, a 20-point margin, with the dark rim melting into forest shadow looking correct rather than lost. Judge a tree composited on its ground, not by the distance between two averages. REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS 2026-08-18, with all seven of Sockeye Run's plants. `canopy` for the six that grow up, following Stillwater's eight; `surface` for [[river-moss-mat]], which lies on the ground and would be drawn over hulls for nothing on canopy. CONTACT none throughout: vegetation is land scenery the fleet cannot reach, so a collider would never be tested, and this is the venue whose own 82 hidden banks are on record in script.js for multi-hundred-millisecond replan spikes. PROP-SPIN ON for all seven — none has a front. srcBox carried only by the mat, which is honestly oblong at 0.63 of its frame; the six plants fill 74-87% after fillTo and have nothing worth skipping. Verified in a running editor: all seven in the picker, a document placing all seven validates clean and compiles to 7 props and ZERO hidden colliders, which is the contact:none decision showing up where it should.

assets.note: THE SECOND EVERGREEN, and the reason this venue does not need six conifer sprites: two crowns that differ in SHAPE as well as tone read as a mixed forest wherever they are interleaved. 9.1 m crown, and 9.1 x 9.2 = 84u, a 1.24x step below [[river-spruce-sitka]] and matching the ~1.25 spacing Stillwater's ladder uses. ⚠️ THIS IS THE VENUE'S TIGHT PAIR AT dE 17.2 FROM THE SPRUCE, and it is accepted on the same argument Stillwater's compressed five-deep ladder is: every adjacent pair must be separated on a SECOND axis, and this one is separated on the strongest available. Spruce is a jagged pointed star with a hard rim; this is a soft feathered dome with a frayed one. That difference survives with colour removed, which is what art-pipeline 2 actually asks for, and the 12.3 points of lightness between them is the supporting half rather than the load-bearing one. DO NOT let the delivery drift bluer or darker toward the spruce — if the two arrive looking like one tree at two sizes, the fix is the RIM, not the colour. Grounds: dE 32.1 from [[river-humus]], 20.4 from [[river-cobble]], 36.4 from [[river-meadow]], 30.5 from [[river-outcrop]]. ⚠️ PLANE `canopy` WHEN IT REGISTERS, AND THERE IS AN OPEN INCONSISTENCY IN THE LIBRARY TO SETTLE FIRST. The comment is stale. It matters because the bayou's split-canopy note records a coupling — anything re-planed to `canopy` draws OVER the fleet and has to restore the openings requirement, since a painted gap hides a boat as well as a leaf does — and no asset in the manifest carries `minHoles` any more, across SIXTEEN canopy props. So the whole canopy family currently occludes like a solid disc. The near-black openings clause is written into all three river tree subjects so the art has real gaps whichever way that is settled, but the decision is not this slot's to make. ⚠️ FIRST CUT 2026-08-17 REJECTED, AND BOTH FAULTS WERE IN THE SPEC RATHER THAN THE GENERATOR. FAULT ONE, THE OPENINGS: this subject carried a near-black gaps clause asking for 'six to ten openings scattered through the crown, plus two or three notches biting in from the outer edge'. That clause was imported from the bayou, where the split canopies draw OVER the fleet and see-through is worth buying; here nothing sails under a river tree and the owner wants the full canopy. It has been replaced with an explicit FULL-CANOPY clause that names a coverage floor of nine tenths and states that shadowed pockets are shading rather than holes. This also settles the open canopy/minHoles question recorded on [[river-hemlock-western]] in the direction of no see-through requirement. FAULT TWO, MEASURED WITH THE LIBRARY'S OWN MANDALA TEST — rotational self-similarity of the crown's STRUCTURE (high-passed, so a round mass does not score just for being round) correlated against itself rotated by 360/N. The hemlock scored +0.37 max and 0.78 fill — better than the spruce but still above the shipped pine-white's +0.10, so it takes the same anti-mandala clause. Its soft frayed rim is doing the right work and should be kept; what has to change is the ARRANGEMENT of the limb groups under it. Same targets: mandala max ≤0.25, fill ≥0.85. ⚠️ THE CANOPY QUESTION FLAGGED ABOVE IS NOW ANSWERED — full canopy, no see-through requirement — so the sixteen canopy-plane props carrying no `minHoles` are consistent with how this venue wants trees to read, and the bayou coupling stays a bayou concern. ⚠️ THE CONE CLAUSE WAS ADDED HERE BEFORE ANY RE-ROLL, on the strength of what fixed [[river-spruce-sitka]] and what broke [[river-cottonwood-black]]. This subject previously listed lit/body/shade tones without tying them to POSITION, which is the gap all three of this venue's trees fell through: the generator is free to put the shade in the middle, and a dark middle is both a snowflake on a conifer and a hole in a broadleaf. Now stated as bright leader at the centre falling about eighteen points to a shaded rim — shallower than the spruce's twenty-five because hemlock foliage is looser — with tones #7E9B76 / #5A7554 / #3C5238. Reference points measured on shipped art: sitka +24.0, lake birch-paper and aspen-quaking both +11.7, and the rejected cottonwood -14.3. ⚠️ FIRST CUT OF THE REWRITTEN SUBJECT REJECTED 2026-08-17 — 'the top doesn't look right' — AND THE MEASUREMENT FOUND A DARK DOT AT THE APEX. The broad cone is actually fine: centre(0-30%) to rim reads +14.1 against the +18 asked, right direction, and fill 0.89 with solidity 0.98 are both healthy. What is wrong is the innermost 5% of the radius, which measures L* 26.1 against L* 58.6 for the ring immediately outside it — a THIRTY-TWO POINT hole punched exactly where a lit leader should be, at mean RGB 65/63/50, i.e. a brown trunk dot. On a tree whose whole read is 'top of a spire', the apex is the one place that cannot be dark. AND IT EXPLAINS THE MANDALA, which came in at +0.36 and had barely moved from the first cut's +0.37 despite the anti-mandala wording: the sprays converge on that visible point, and a dark hub with light sprays around it IS the snowflake arrangement. [[river-spruce-sitka]] is the proof — its mandala fell from +0.58 to +0.05 when its centre was made the brightest part, with no other structural change. Fix the hub and the symmetry score follows. ⚠️⚠️ THE SOURCE WAS THE SHARED OPENING PARAGRAPH, WHICH ASKED FOR IT IN SO MANY WORDS. All three river trees were written from one preamble copied from the bayou cypress, and it contains 'with the trunk reading as a dark hub at the centre where they meet'. That is a direct instruction to darken the middle, sitting upstream of every positive clause added later — which is why this is the FOURTH time in this venue a delivery has faithfully drawn a defect the brief requested. The cottonwood only escaped because it was given an explicit override; the sitka only escaped because its crown is dense enough to bury the stem. The preamble is now rewritten for this asset to state that the trunk is not visible and nothing dark sits in the middle. ⚠️ THE SAME SENTENCE IS STILL PRESENT IN THE SHIPPED [[river-spruce-sitka]] AND [[river-cottonwood-black]] SUBJECTS. Both delivered fine and neither needs regenerating, but anyone re-rolling either one, or copying that preamble to a new tree in any venue, must strike the dark-hub clause first. It is the single most expensive sentence in this batch. Also added: vary spray SIZE, not just angle — the cottonwood's +0.24 showed that equal-sized lobes at uneven angles still self-correlate. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-18, AND THE HUB FIX CONFIRMS THE THEORY A SECOND TIME. The dark apex dot is gone: innermost 5% now reads L* 68.0 against the surrounding 5-20% ring at 67.1, a swing from -32.5 to +0.9, and the innermost mean RGB is 153/179/131 — green, not the 65/63/50 brown of the rejected cut. AND THE MANDALA FOLLOWED THE HUB, exactly as [[river-spruce-sitka]] predicted it would: +0.16 max against +0.36 on the previous cut and +0.37 on the one before, with no structural change other than removing the dark centre. That is now TWO independent confirmations in this venue that a visible dark hub is what creates the rosette score, and it is the single most useful thing learned in this batch: fix the centre and the symmetry fixes itself. Cone depth +20.3 against the +18 asked, sitting neatly between the cottonwood's +18.6 and the spruce's +24.0. Fill 0.89 and solidity 0.98, aspect 1.015, zero white stroke, real alpha. ⚠️ THE CONIFER PAIR DRIFTED APART AND THE VENUE NO LONGER READS THE WAY IT WAS SPECCED, which is worth recording even though it is accepted. This asset was asked for as 'softer, slightly lighter' than the spruce, with the two together making a mixed conifer forest. Delivered, the spruce came in DARKER than spec (L* 22.0 against 32.3) and this one LIGHTER (52.4 against ~46), so the pair now sits 30 points of lightness apart rather than the ~14 intended. The consequence is that the venue sorts into THREE distinct trees rather than two conifers and a broadleaf: dE 34.0 spruce to hemlock, 14.6 hemlock to cottonwood. Accepted for three reasons. The 14.6 clears the library's own bar comfortably — Stillwater ships pine-red against alder-speckled at 9.3 and birch against aspen at 13.1. The pair is separated on a SECOND axis as the lake's ladder rule requires, and a strong one: a billowy lobed dome with silver flecks against a feathery frayed spray, which survives with colour removed. And on the ship test, composited at true size on all three grounds, the mixed stand reads correctly — a dark spruce beside a lighter hemlock looks like a real mixed stand rather than one tree at two tones, which is what was actually wanted. If the mix is ever felt to be too contrasty, the lever is the SPRUCE coming back toward its specced L* 32, not this tree going darker: hemlock at L* 52 is botanically right and it is what separates the venue's hillside from its bottom. REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS 2026-08-18, with all seven of Sockeye Run's plants. `canopy` for the six that grow up, following Stillwater's eight; `surface` for [[river-moss-mat]], which lies on the ground and would be drawn over hulls for nothing on canopy. CONTACT none throughout: vegetation is land scenery the fleet cannot reach, so a collider would never be tested, and this is the venue whose own 82 hidden banks are on record in script.js for multi-hundred-millisecond replan spikes. PROP-SPIN ON for all seven — none has a front. srcBox carried only by the mat, which is honestly oblong at 0.63 of its frame; the six plants fill 74-87% after fillTo and have nothing worth skipping. Verified in a running editor: all seven in the picker, a document placing all seven validates clean and compiles to 7 props and ZERO hidden colliders, which is the contact:none decision showing up where it should.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH OF ONE TREE STANDING ALONE ON DRY GROUND, shot straight down from well above the crown the way a forestry survey frames a single specimen. You are looking at the TOP of the whole tree: the crown fills most of the frame, and through the gaps in it you catch the main limbs radiating out from the middle, with the trunk reading as a dark hub at the centre where they meet. The limbs are seen from ABOVE — you see the top of each branch running outward and never its side, and no length of trunk is visible at all. A BLACK COTTONWOOD, the big broadleaf tree of a Pacific Northwest river bottom. ⚠️ IT IS A DECIDUOUS CROWN AND MUST NOT READ AS A CONIFER. It is BROAD, BILLOWY AND ROUNDED — the widest crown in the venue — built from big soft rounded LOBES of leaf-mass pushing out in every direction, with rounded bays between them. No spikes, no branch tips ending in points, no whorls, nothing radiating stiffly: where the two evergreens have structure at the rim, this has billows. The leaf-mass is worked as clustered rounded clumps, each clump one soft two-tone blob and never individual leaves. ⚠️ NO BRANCH ARMATURE AND NO TRUNK HUB. Do not draw pale limbs forking out of a dark centre — that is a landscape architect's plan symbol, not a tree seen from the air, and it is the single way this drawing keeps going wrong. The trunk is not visible at all: it is directly beneath the deepest part of the crown and the foliage covers it. At most, one or two short pieces of a limb may be glimpsed in a gap OUT TOWARD THE RIM, never near the middle. ⚠️ THE CANOPY IS FULL AND YOU SEE ALL OF IT. Draw this crown DENSE: the foliage fills its own outline, with no punched holes, no windows through to the ground, and no dark gap opening up around the middle. The mass should cover at least nine tenths of the circle it sits in. Where it thins it thins at the very rim and nowhere else. Shadowed pockets between limb groups are welcome as SHADING — darker foliage, still foliage — but nothing anywhere is painted near-black to read as a hole, and the trunk hub is a small dark mark glimpsed THROUGH the canopy rather than a clearing in it. ⚠️ THE VALUE STRUCTURE IS A DOME AND IT RUNS BRIGHT-CENTRE TO DARK-RIM. A broadleaf crown is a mound of leaves: the top of the mound is the middle of the picture, nearest the camera and the sky, and the foliage curves away and into shade toward the outside. So the crown is BRIGHTEST AND FULLEST AT THE MIDDLE and darkens outward to the rim — about twelve points of lightness between the two, a shallower fall than a conifer's because a dome is not a spire. Build it from a lit crown near #93BD71 at the centre, a body near #83AC62, and a shaded rim near #739C53. THE MIDDLE OF THIS PICTURE MUST BE THE LIGHTEST, FULLEST PLACE IN IT. A dark centre reads as a hole in the canopy however much foliage is actually drawn there, which is exactly the failure this clause exists to stop. ⚠️ IT MUST READ AS A DIFFERENT KIND OF GREEN FROM THE MEADOW BELOW IT — cooler and fresher, never the meadow's yellow-olive — because this tree is planted on ground it has to be seen against. SCATTER PALE SILVER through it: black cottonwood leaves are white underneath and the wind turns them, so a scatter of the topmost clumps are distinctly paler and cooler than the rest, which is the tree's real signature from the air. NOTHING ELSE: no blossom, no fruit, no autumn colour, no bare limb standing out, no water. THE SILHOUETTE IS AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE. Seen from straight above a crown is a round mass; one wider than it is tall means the camera was tilted and the image is wrong. Irregular is right and elongated is not — the lobes and bays are uneven, but the span top-to-bottom matches the span side-to-side. NO GROUND IS DRAWN and no cast shadow: the tree is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies the forest floor it stands on.
assets.note: THE RIVER TREE, and the venue's most important placement signal: broad bright deciduous crowns are what tell a player at a glance that they are looking at a river bottom rather than a hillside. Put it close to the water, on islands, behind gravel bars and along the slow side channels. 13.9 m crown, and 13.9 x 9.2 = 128u — the BIGGEST tree in the game, above Stillwater's 110u white pine, and that is honest rather than showy: a mature black cottonwood crown genuinely is broader than a Sitka spruce's, because a spruce is a narrow spire and this is a dome. It also makes the river-bottom marker the largest thing on the bank, which is what it is for. ⚠️ THE COLOUR WAS MOVED OFF ITS OBVIOUS VALUE BY MEASUREMENT. The natural choice for a bright deciduous crown is a yellow-green near #8CA44C, and that measures dE 10.0 FROM [[river-meadow]] — the meadow delivered at L* 60.5 with chroma 50, which is also a bright yellow-green, so a cottonwood standing on a terrace would have disappeared into it. Shifting the hue COOLER rather than changing the lightness fixes it: #7FA85E measures 19.3 from the meadow at the same brightness, and it is botanically the better answer anyway, since cottonwood foliage is a fresher green than dry meadow sedge. Do not let it drift back toward yellow-olive. Its real grounds are further away still: dE 48.3 from [[river-cobble]] and 59.1 from [[river-humus]], the two it will actually stand on. SEPARATION FROM THE CONIFERS IS ENORMOUS — dE 50.8 from [[river-spruce-sitka]] and 33.9 from [[river-hemlock-western]] — which is correct and is the whole design: the eye should sort this venue into dark evergreen hillside and bright broadleaf bottom without being told. PLANE `canopy` when it registers, with the caveat recorded on [[river-hemlock-western]]. ⚠️ FIRST CUT 2026-08-17 REJECTED, AND BOTH FAULTS WERE IN THE SPEC RATHER THAN THE GENERATOR. FAULT ONE, THE OPENINGS: this subject carried a near-black gaps clause asking for 'six to ten openings scattered through the crown, plus two or three notches biting in from the outer edge'. That clause was imported from the bayou, where the split canopies draw OVER the fleet and see-through is worth buying; here nothing sails under a river tree and the owner wants the full canopy. It has been replaced with an explicit FULL-CANOPY clause that names a coverage floor of nine tenths and states that shadowed pockets are shading rather than holes. This also settles the open canopy/minHoles question recorded on [[river-hemlock-western]] in the direction of no see-through requirement. FAULT TWO, MEASURED WITH THE LIBRARY'S OWN MANDALA TEST — rotational self-similarity of the crown's STRUCTURE (high-passed, so a round mass does not score just for being round) correlated against itself rotated by 360/N. The cottonwood was the best of the three and needs the least: mandala max +0.20, already inside the ≤0.25 target the other two are being held to, and fill 0.80 against the ≥0.85 wanted. Its billowy lobed construction is what kept it out of trouble — round clumps at uneven sizes do not self-align under rotation the way radiating spokes do, which is worth remembering the next time a conifer is specced. Only the openings clause was removed and a fullness floor added; the silhouette language is untouched. ⚠️ SECOND CUT REJECTED 2026-08-17 — 'not a full canopy on top' — AND THE MEASUREMENT SHOWS THE CANOPY WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM. Coverage is fine: circle-fill 0.83 (against lake aspen's 0.83 and birch's 0.85) and solidity 0.98, with the inner disc 0.93 covered. There is no hole in the alpha. WHAT IS WRONG IS THE VALUE STRUCTURE, and it is inverted: the crown measures centre L* 39.3 against rim L* 53.6, a drop of MINUS 14.3 — the middle is darker than the edge. Both shipped broadleaves run the other way at exactly +11.7 (lake birch-paper and lake aspen-quaking, independently), and the accepted [[river-spruce-sitka]] at +24.0. So this delivery sits about 26 points the wrong side of where this library's own broadleaves live, and a dark middle reads as a hole however much foliage is drawn in it. THIS IS THE SAME ROOT CAUSE AS THE SITKA'S SNOWFLAKE AND I SHOULD HAVE CARRIED IT ACROSS. The sitka was fixed by inverting its shading to a lit-centre cone; the note even records that a bright hub cannot read as a snowflake. The cottonwood needed the same correction one step later and did not get it, because its own colour clause still listed tones without tying them to POSITION. AND, AS WITH THE SITKA, THE BRIEF ASKED FOR THE DEFECT IN SO MANY WORDS: 'through the gaps the main limbs show as thick pale-grey branches forking outward from a heavy dark trunk hub at the centre... a few should be plainly visible'. That is a drawn instruction to put a dark hub with radiating arms in the middle of the picture. It is now replaced by an explicit ban on the branch armature and the trunk hub, plus a dome clause: lit crown #93BD71 at the centre, body #83AC62, shaded rim #739C53, a stated twelve-point fall, and the sentence that the middle must be the lightest and fullest place in the picture. THE MEAN IS PRESERVED at L* 64.0, so the dE 19.2 against [[river-meadow]] that the hue shift was bought for still holds (44.7 from cobble, 57.9 from humus). GENERAL LESSON, worth applying before the hemlock is re-rolled: for any crown seen from directly above, state the value structure POSITIONALLY — centre versus rim — not as a list of lit/body/shade tones. Three of three trees in this venue went wrong in exactly that gap. THIRD CUT DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-17, AND THE DOME INVERTED CLEANLY. Centre-to-rim now measures +18.6 points of L* (70.3 at the crown's middle to 51.7 at the rim) against the -14.3 of the rejected cut — a 33-point swing, and in the right direction. It sits above the +12 asked and above both shipped broadleaves at +11.7, but below the spruce's +24.0, which is the correct place for a big cottonwood: a broad dome falls further than a birch's and less than a spire's. FULLNESS IS EXACTLY ON THE LIBRARY: circle-fill 0.85, matching lake birch-paper's 0.85 and above lake aspen's 0.83, with solidity 0.99 level with aspen — the fullest crown in the venue. No branch armature, no trunk hub; the silver leaf flecks the subject asks for are present and read as the wind-turned undersides they are meant to be. Aspect 1.055 clears planRound, zero white stroke, real alpha. It passes and it is not visible at 128px, but if this tree is ever re-rolled the instruction to add is uneven clump SIZES rather than uneven spacing; equal-sized lobes at uneven angles still self-correlate. assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. You are looking at the TOP of the plant and nothing else — no side of any stem, no length of trunk, no face of anything. ⚠️ NOTHING DARK SITS IN THE MIDDLE OF THIS PICTURE. There is no stem hub, no dark well and no clearing at the centre; the foliage covers whatever holds it up. A RIVER WILLOW — the low scrubby shrub that colonises the wet ground behind a gravel bar. It is a LOW IRREGULAR MOUND of fine foliage, wider than it is tall in life and therefore a soft rounded mass from above, lumpy rather than neat: three or four clumps of different sizes pushed together with shallow bays between them, one side reaching further than the other. The leaves are NARROW and the foliage reads as many small fine strokes rather than round blobs — a fine-textured shrub, not a billowy one. ⚠️ THE COLOUR IS A BRIGHT, STRONGLY SATURATED YELLOW-GREEN, AND IT IS THE LOUDEST GREEN IN THE VENUE. A summer willow thicket on an Alaskan creek is the freshest, most vivid thing on the bank — brighter and far more saturated than the grass behind it, and much lighter than the spruce. Build it as a low mound lit from above: a lit top near #96B446, a body near #738E2D, and a deep shade near #405415 down in the bays between the clumps. THAT IS A WIDE VALUE RANGE ON PURPOSE — about thirty-six points of lightness from the sunlit crown to the shadow inside the thicket — because the deep shadow between bushes is what makes a mass of scrub read as scrub rather than as one smooth cushion. The hue sits at about 77 degrees, on the YELLOW side of green, and the saturation is around 0.65: if it comes back grey, dusty, glaucous, sage, olive or muted, it is the wrong plant. It is not a blue-green and not an emerald; it is the green of new leaves in strong sun. ⚠️ IT IS FULL AND YOU SEE ALL OF IT: no punched holes, no windows through to the ground, no near-black gaps. Shadowed pockets between clumps are SHADING — darker foliage, still foliage. ⚠️ IT MUST NOT COME BACK AS A ROSETTE. Vary the SIZE of the clumps as well as their angle — equal-sized lobes at uneven angles still line up under rotation. No even spacing, no four-fold or six-fold arrangement, no lobe answered by a matching lobe across the middle, and the densest part pushed plainly off-centre. NOTHING ELSE: no flower, no catkin, no bare stem showing, no water, no bank. THE SILHOUETTE IS AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE — irregular, but the span top-to-bottom matches the span side-to-side. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the plant is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it grows on.
assets.note: SOCKEYE RUN'S MOST COMMON SHRUB — behind gravel bars, on low islands, beside side channels and through periodically flooded ground. 3.3 m clump, and 3.3 x 9.2 = 30u. ⚠️ THE GREY-GREEN IS A SEPARATION DECISION AS MUCH AS A BOTANICAL ONE, and it was arrived at by measurement. The obvious willow green (#8A9B72) measures dE 9.7 from [[river-hemlock-western]] and 11.8 from [[river-cottonwood-black]] — a shrub that will stand directly beneath both, indistinguishable from them. Dropping the chroma from 24 to 13 while holding the lightness moves it to 16.6 and 23.1 without changing what it is, because a glaucous grey-green is what a willow actually looks like. Against its own grounds: dE 22.4 from [[river-cobble]] and 38.7 from [[river-meadow]]. Its nearest neighbour anywhere is [[river-outcrop]] at 13.8, which is a bare rock shelf and shares no silhouette with a shrub. PLANE `canopy` when it registers, following the venue's trees. Place it with prop-spin ON — a willow clump has no front. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-18 AFTER TWO POST STEPS, NEITHER OF THEM A REGENERATION. THE GREY-GREEN LANDED EXACTLY: delivered chroma 13.4 against the 13.1 this note specified, so the separation decision that drove the whole palette worked. Mandala +0.16, aspect 1.04, fill 0.83, solidity 0.96, and the fine narrow-leaf stroke texture the subject asked for is there. STEP ONE, THE STICKER HALO: the delivery came through a background remover and carried 22,650 px of white stroke at alpha 1-60 over black under alpha 0 — the [[lake-boulder-large]] pattern exactly. Unmixed with the same projection (s = a*dot(C-W,F-W)/|F-W|^2 against a grown stone... here foliage colour), leaving zero near-white px above alpha 12, then colour-bled for the downsample. STEP TWO, THE LIGHTNESS: it arrived at L* 56.4 against the 65.1 specced, 8.4 points dark, and that mattered for a reason the dE table did not show. Measured, the drop cost the very margin the grey-green was bought for — dE against [[river-hemlock-western]] fell from the designed 16.6 to 11.1 — but the SHIP TEST showed something worse and different: at its true 30px on cobble and meadow, a dark grey-green lump reads as a STONE rather than a plant. Lifted in post with a multiplicative-in-L transform that holds hue and chroma exactly (13.4 before and after) and keeps the mound's internal range proportional. Result lands on #95A28C against the specced #96A28C, one unit out, and every separation returns to its designed value: hemlock 16.6, cobble 22.8, outcrop 14.1, meadow 38.7, mossfloor 47.4. ⚠️ THE HEMLOCK PAIR AT 16.6 IS A NON-ISSUE IN PRACTICE and the ship test is why: at 30px against an 84px hemlock, a 2.8x size step and a lump-versus-feathered- disc silhouette settle it long before colour is consulted. ⚠️ THE RESIDUAL RISK IS ROCK, NOT PLANTS. Even lifted, a low-chroma grey-green mound at 30px reads pale rather than obviously leafy on the two stony grounds, and it sits dE 14.1 from [[river-outcrop]]. Nothing in the venue is confusable with it TODAY because Sockeye Run has no rock PROP — but the venue is still short the awash shoal rock its card promises, and if that is ever drawn it must be measured against this shrub first. An ambient shrub that reads as a hazard rock is the confusion art-pipeline 2 exists to prevent, and this asset is the one that would cause it. REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS 2026-08-18, with all seven of Sockeye Run's plants. `canopy` for the six that grow up, following Stillwater's eight; `surface` for [[river-moss-mat]], which lies on the ground and would be drawn over hulls for nothing on canopy. CONTACT none throughout: vegetation is land scenery the fleet cannot reach, so a collider would never be tested, and this is the venue whose own 82 hidden banks are on record in script.js for multi-hundred-millisecond replan spikes. PROP-SPIN ON for all seven — none has a front. srcBox carried only by the mat, which is honestly oblong at 0.63 of its frame; the six plants fill 74-87% after fillTo and have nothing worth skipping. Verified in a running editor: all seven in the picker, a document placing all seven validates clean and compiles to 7 props and ZERO hidden colliders, which is the contact:none decision showing up where it should. ⚠️ THE COLOUR SPEC ABOVE WAS REWRITTEN 2026-08-22 AND THE ORIGINAL ONE WAS SIMPLY WRONG FOR THIS PLANT. The first spec asked for grey-green in capitals — 'the greyness is the species mark ... the dustiest, least saturated green in the venue ... never a yellow-green: if it looks like fresh grass it is the wrong plant' — and the delivery obeyed it exactly, coming back at mean #95A28C, L* 65.2, hue 96, saturation 0.14. THE OWNER'S REFERENCE PHOTOGRAPH OF A REAL ALASKAN WILLOW CREEK SAYS THE OPPOSITE. Measured on the sunlit canopy of the thicket in that photograph — the tone the eye reads at a distance, as distinct from the mean, which deep inter-bush shadow drags down to L* 40 — the three thickets in frame run #7B9821, #708A3E and #6D842B: L* 52-63, hue 74-80, saturation 0.55-0.78. So the shipped sprite was 25 points too light and four to five times too desaturated, and it was the SPEC that put it there, not the generator. The glaucous underside is real on some willows; it is not what a thicket looks like from across a creek in July. ⚠️ THE SHIPPED BAKE AND THE ARCHIVED MASTER ARE A PROVISIONAL RECOLOUR, NOT A RE-ROLL. The delivered pixels were remapped in HSV — hue recentred 96 -> 77 with its own variation compressed to 0.28, saturation x4.8, value re-centred with a 1.1x contrast stretch — which lands body L* 55.3, lit 69.2, shade 32.9, hue 77, saturation 0.65, all inside the reference bands. Structure, silhouette, alpha and anchor are untouched, so every measurement in this note above still holds. The pre-recolour master is preserved at scratchpad/willow.master.ORIGINAL.png for this session. RE-ROLL AGAINST THE NEW SUBJECT WHEN CONVENIENT: a recolour cannot add the warm yellow-green variation a fresh generation would put in the leaves, and re-running ingest.py on the old inbox file would silently restore the grey one.

You are looking at the TOP of the plant and nothing else — no side of any stem, no length of trunk, no face of anything. ⚠️ NOTHING DARK SITS IN THE MIDDLE OF THIS PICTURE. There is no stem hub, no dark well and no clearing at the centre; the foliage covers whatever holds it up. A RED ALDER — the transitional thicket plant of a disturbed riverbank, halfway between a big shrub and a small tree. From above it is a BROAD ROUNDED CROWN of coarse foliage, bigger and heavier than a willow and plainly denser: a mass of overlapping rounded leaf clumps, each clump made of BROAD OVAL leaves worked as chunky two-tone blobs, never fine strokes. It reads as one solid crown with a lumpy edge, not as a collection of branches. THE VALUE STRUCTURE IS A LOW DOME: the top of the crown is the middle of the picture and it is the brightest part, darkening outward to a shaded rim, about twelve points of lightness across. Build it from a lit crown near #5A7050, a body near #465A40, and a shaded rim near #34462F. THE COLOUR IS A DEEP SLIGHTLY COOL GREEN, darker than every other broadleaf in the venue — an alder thicket is a heavy dark patch and that is its whole job. ⚠️ IT IS FULL AND YOU SEE ALL OF IT: no punched holes, no windows through to the ground, no near-black gaps. Shadowed pockets between clumps are SHADING — darker foliage, still foliage. ⚠️ IT MUST NOT COME BACK AS A ROSETTE. Vary the SIZE of the clumps as well as their angle — equal-sized lobes at uneven angles still line up under rotation. No even spacing, no four-fold or six-fold arrangement, no lobe answered by a matching lobe across the middle, and the densest part pushed plainly off-centre. NOTHING ELSE: no catkin, no cone, no autumn colour, no bare limb, no water. THE SILHOUETTE IS AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE — irregular, but the span top-to-bottom matches the span side-to-side. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the plant is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it grows on.
assets.note: THE THICKET PLANT — disturbed banks, forest edges, the bridge clearing, and ground the river has recently rearranged. It gives dense cover without spending a full-size tree on every patch. 6.1 m crown, and 6.1 x 9.2 = 56u, which drops it cleanly below [[river-hemlock-western]] at 84 and well above [[river-willow]] at 30 — a 1.5x step down from the trees and a 1.9x step up from the shrubs, so the venue's ladder reads shrub / thicket / tree without ambiguity. ⚠️ NOT THE LAKE'S ALDER. [[lake-alder-speckled]] is a different species in a different venue at 48u; this is bigger, darker and coarser-leaved. They are cross-venue and can never share a race. SEPARATION: dE 29.7 from [[river-willow]], 32.3 from [[river-moss]], and 17.0 from [[river-spruce-sitka]] — the tightest pair it has, and carried on silhouette, since a spiky dark spire and a lumpy dark dome are not confusable with colour removed. Against grounds, 23.2 from [[river-humus]] and 18.5 from [[river-cobble]]. PLANE `canopy`, prop-spin ON. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-18. THE DOME IS TEXTBOOK: centre-to-rim +12.5 against the +12 asked, hub +0.8 so no dark centre, and MANDALA +0.03 — the lowest score in the venue and below even the accepted [[river-spruce-sitka]]'s +0.05. Solidity 0.98. Broad oval leaves as chunky clumps, exactly as specced. Carried the same background-remover sticker halo as [[river-willow]] (8,900 px of white at alpha 1-60 over black beneath) and took the same unmix. ⚠️ IT TRIPS THE ORTHOGRAPHIC CHECK AT 1.163 AND THE WARNING IS ACCEPTED, WITH A REASON. Ingest reads that ratio as a camera about 31 degrees off vertical, but the VALUE STRUCTURE PROVES OTHERWISE: a tilted camera flattens a dome, and this one measures a textbook +12.5 fall from a lit centre to a shaded rim with the hub correctly bright. A crown seen from 31 degrees off cannot produce that. So the 1.163 is honest shape irregularity in a thicket clump, not tilt — which is the case planRound cannot distinguish, and worth knowing before anyone 'fixes' this by regenerating. The flag stays TRUE rather than being switched off, because it still earns its keep on the next re-roll; this delivery is simply the exception, and the dome measurement is how to tell. ⚠️ IT CAME BACK DARKER THAN SPECCED at L* 29.1 against 36.0, which pulls dE against [[river-spruce-sitka]] down to 12.5 from the 17.0 designed. ACCEPTED ON THE SHIP TEST and on the brief: the owner asked for 'larger and darker than willow', and at true size on all three grounds the venue reads as a clean three-tier ladder — pale grey-green willow at 30px, dark lumpy alder thicket at 56px, very dark spiky spruce at 104px. The alder-to-spruce pair never comes down to colour: a 1.9x size step and a lumpy broadleaf dome against a jagged conifer star settle it, and 12.5 still clears the library bar of 9.3 that Stillwater ships pine-red against alder-speckled at. NO LIFT APPLIED — unlike the willow, which was lifted because it read as a STONE, this one reads unambiguously as a dark shrub mass and darkness is its job. REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS 2026-08-18, with all seven of Sockeye Run's plants. `canopy` for the six that grow up, following Stillwater's eight; `surface` for [[river-moss-mat]], which lies on the ground and would be drawn over hulls for nothing on canopy. CONTACT none throughout: vegetation is land scenery the fleet cannot reach, so a collider would never be tested, and this is the venue whose own 82 hidden banks are on record in script.js for multi-hundred-millisecond replan spikes. PROP-SPIN ON for all seven — none has a front. srcBox carried only by the mat, which is honestly oblong at 0.63 of its frame; the six plants fill 74-87% after fillTo and have nothing worth skipping. Verified in a running editor: all seven in the picker, a document placing all seven validates clean and compiles to 7 props and ZERO hidden colliders, which is the contact:none decision showing up where it should.

A PATCH OF FIREWEED in full bloom — the tall magenta spire that covers disturbed ground all over coastal Alaska. A spike seen end-on foreshortens almost to nothing, so each one is a COMPACT MAGENTA ROSETTE sitting where its stem is — a small rounded cluster of petals, never a long streak, never a stroke lying across the picture, and never a spike drawn at its side-on length. A stand of them is a SCATTER OF MAGENTA DOTS of slightly different sizes, densest through the middle of the patch and thinning to singles at the edge. A few stems lean, so a few of those rosettes are ovals rather than circles — but the long axis of a leaning one points in ITS OWN direction, and no two lean the same way. Between and below them, the narrow green LEAVES show as fine dark strokes at many angles, filling the gaps so the patch is not bare. THE COLOUR IS THE POINT OF THE PLANT: a lit petal near #C25C92, a body near #A8467E, a deep near #8A3364, against foliage near #4E5E3A. It is a true pink-purple magenta, never red, never orange, never pale pink. ⚠️ IT MUST NOT COME BACK AS A ROSETTE. Vary the SIZE of the clumps as well as their angle — equal-sized lobes at uneven angles still line up under rotation. No even spacing, no four-fold or six-fold arrangement, no lobe answered by a matching lobe across the middle, and the densest part pushed plainly off-centre. NOTHING ELSE: no seed fluff, no bud drawn as a bud, no stem visible along its length, no water. THE SILHOUETTE IS AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE — irregular, but the span top-to-bottom matches the span side-to-side. A vertical thing seen from directly above is a DOT. The subject therefore states the physics, gives the correct read (compact rosettes at the stem positions), and names the failure. ACCEPTANCE, measured the same way as the bulrush: mark elongation median below 1.6 with at least 60% near-round, and axial resultant below 0.25 so no common lean survives. PLANE `canopy`, prop-spin ON. ⚠️ USE IT SPARINGLY — one strong accent repeated everywhere stops being an accent, and this is the loudest thing in the venue. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-18, FIRST CUT, AND IT IS THE CLEANEST DELIVERY IN THE VENUE. THE FORESHORTENING CLAUSE LANDED COMPLETELY, which is the thing this slot was written around after [[lake-bulrush]] failed it twice: measured across 82 flower marks, elongation median is 1.03 against the <1.6 asked, and 98% of marks are near-round against the >=60% asked. Only two marks in the whole patch are elongated at all, so the axial resultant is 0.000 against the <0.25 target — there is no common lean because there is almost nothing to lean. Every spike reads as the compact rosette a vertical thing seen from directly above actually is. Stating the physics, giving the correct read and naming the failure worked here where three rounds of negatives did not work on the bulrush. Accepted, because at its true 18px the structure is gone anyway and what remains is a magenta dot — verified on all three grounds it will stand on. But it makes each placement LOUDER than specced, which sharpens the warning above rather than softening it: place these sparingly. A dozen of them on one terrace will read as a flowerbed, not as fireweed.
