assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. You are looking at the TOP of the plant and nothing else — no side of any stem, no length of trunk, no face of anything. ⚠️ NOTHING DARK SITS IN THE MIDDLE OF THIS PICTURE. There is no stem hub, no dark well and no clearing at the centre; the foliage covers whatever holds it up. A PATCH OF NOOTKA LUPINE in full bloom — the blue-violet spike that fills river terraces and disturbed meadow all over coastal Alaska, and the COOL counterweight to this venue's magenta fireweed. IT IS A DENSE STAND OF SEPARATE STEMS, not a bush: fifteen to thirty stout stalks pushed straight up out of the ground close together, each carrying a fat cone of pea-shaped flowers at its top. ⚠️ THE FLOWER SPIKES ARE VERTICAL AND YOU ARE LOOKING DOWN THE LENGTH OF THEM, WHICH IS THE ONE THING THIS SUBJECT MUST GET RIGHT. A spike seen end-on foreshortens almost to nothing, so each one is a COMPACT VIOLET KNOB sitting where its stem is — a small rounded cluster of petals, never a long streak, never a stroke lying across the picture, and never a spike drawn at its side-on length. A stand of them is a SCATTER OF VIOLET DOTS of slightly different sizes, thickest through one part of the patch and thinning to singles at the edge. ⚠️ THE FAILURE HAS A NAME AND IT IS A CONE WITH A POINTED TIP. Every photograph of this plant on earth is taken from the side, where the raceme is a tall tapering cone that comes to a point at the top — and THAT SHAPE MUST NOT APPEAR HERE, because it is the shape of a spike seen from the side. From straight above there is no length and no point: the tip of the spike is the part NEAREST the camera and it sits in the MIDDLE of the mark, with the older open flowers going outward and downward all round it. If any spike in this picture comes to a point, tapers along its length, or is more than about one and a half times as long as it is wide, the camera was at the side of the plant and the image is wrong however good it looks. A few stems lean, so a few of those knobs are ovals rather than circles — but the long axis of a leaning one points in ITS OWN direction, and no two lean the same way. THE KNOB HAS ITS OWN VALUE STRUCTURE, and that is what stops it being a flat dot: the flowers spiral round the spike and open from the bottom up, so the very tip you are looking straight down at is the palest and slightly greener where buds are still closed, and the colour deepens outward from that centre through the open flowers. THE COLOUR IS THE POINT OF THE PLANT: a lit petal near #8388D6, a body near #5C61B8, a deep near #3F4488. It is a true BLUE-VIOLET — never pink, never magenta, never lavender-grey, never a plain sky blue. THE LEAF IS A GREEN HAND and it is the species' second mark: lupine leaves are palmate, six to nine narrow leaflets spreading from one point like fingers. Three or four leaves near the edge of the patch read as a small green hand at that size; everywhere else the foliage is a fine mass filling the gaps between stems so the patch is not bare. ⚠️ NO LEAF IS ENLARGED INTO A WHEEL, A STAR OR A SUNBURST, and none sits in the middle of the picture — a leaf is small, there are many, and they lie at every angle. THE FOLIAGE IS PLAINLY DARKER THAN THE FLOWERS, which is what gives this patch a shape when the colour is taken away: build it from a lit near #566246, a body near #414C31 and a shade near #303927, a good fourteen points of lightness below the violet. ⚠️ AND THERE IS NO SUCH THING AS OUTWARD IN THIS PICTURE — THE SECOND HALF OF THE SAME PHYSICS. You are directly above the patch, so EVERY spike in it is the same distance from the camera and every spike is therefore drawn the SAME WAY: a spike at the rim of the patch looks exactly like a spike in the middle of it. It is not longer, it is not seen from a lower angle, and it does not lean away from the centre. A spike that appears to stick out sideways past the foliage on a visible length of stalk is a spike LYING ON THE GROUND, and these stand up. THE MEASURABLE FORM OF IT: every violet mark in this picture is about as long as it is wide wherever it sits, and if the marks near the rim are longer, more pointed or more slanted than the ones in the middle, the picture has been composed as a bouquet seen from above and it is wrong however good it looks. No burst, no spray, no crown of spikes around a green middle. ⚠️ THE FRAME IS SQUARE AND THE PATCH FILLS IT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. A stand of lupine seen from beside it spreads out sideways; seen from directly above it does not, because you are looking at ground and ground goes as far back as it goes across. There is as much patch above the middle of this picture as below it, and as much to the left as to the right. ABOUT A THIRD OF THE PATCH IS VIOLET and green shows between every spike. It is a stand of flowers over foliage, never a solid violet cushion. ⚠️ IT MUST NOT COME BACK AS A ROSETTE. Vary the SIZE of the flowers as well as their spacing — equal-sized marks at uneven angles still line up under rotation. No even spacing, no ring, no four-fold or six-fold arrangement, no flower answered by a matching one across the middle, and the thickest part of the patch pushed plainly off-centre. NOTHING ELSE: no seed pod, no bare stem visible along its length, no bee, no water. THE SILHOUETTE IS AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE — irregular, but the span top-to-bottom matches the span side-to-side. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the plant is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it grows on.
assets.note: THE COOL COUNTERWEIGHT, and the biggest of the meadow flowers. Nootka lupine genuinely carpets river terraces in Southeast Alaska, so this is the one of the four that may be planted in real patches rather than singles. COLOUR IS ALL OF IT, AND THE SEPARATION IS ENORMOUS: the violet sits dE 91.6 from [[river-meadow]], 97.5 from its lit tone and 104.8 from [[river-mossfloor]]. The pair that matters is [[river-fireweed]] at dE 42.7 against spec and 45.2 against the magenta actually delivered — comfortable, and the two are the same picture with the colour removed, which is accepted: both are ambient meadow flowers and art-pipeline 2's confusability rule binds ambient against HAZARD, not ambient against ambient. Mistaking a lupine for a fireweed costs the player nothing. ⚠️ THE FOLIAGE WAS DARKENED ON PURPOSE AND THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS SLOT WAS WRONG. Lupine's real grey-green leaf measures L* 39.0 against a violet at L* 40.6 — a value spread of +1.6, meaning the patch would have had no structure at all in greyscale and its entire read would have been chromatic. The flower ramp was lifted to #5C61B8 (L* 44.6) and the foliage dropped to #414C31 (L* 30.7) for a +14 spread, and the subject states that number so the generator has something to hit. ⚠️ PLACEMENT: MEADOW AND TERRACE, NOT THE BAR. At a third flower cover the patch AVERAGES to a slate near #47505A, which is dE 10.5 from [[river-cobble]] and 20.9 from [[river-outcrop]] — a lupine on the gravel bar or the granite is a grey smudge on grey stone. On [[river-meadow]] the same average is 45.7 away and on [[river-humus]] 28.1. Plant it on green ground. THE FORESHORTENING CLAUSE IS CARRIED VERBATIM IN SPIRIT FROM [[river-fireweed]], which is the one asset in the library that landed it first cut — 98% of its flower marks near-round, axial resultant 0.000 — after [[lake-bulrush]] failed the same physics twice. A lupine raceme is the same problem: a vertical thing seen from directly above is a DOT. ACCEPTANCE, measured the same way: mark elongation median below 1.6 with at least 60% near-round, and axial resultant below 0.25. ONE THING THE FIREWEED TEXT GOT SLIGHTLY WRONG IS FIXED HERE. Its subject asks for a patch 'densest through the middle' and then the shared scatter clause asks for 'the densest part pushed plainly off-centre' — a small self-contradiction, of exactly the kind prompt.py's own comments say a generator resolves by dropping one half at random. All four of these say 'thickest through one part of the patch' instead, which agrees with the scatter clause. THE PALMATE LEAF IS A DELIBERATE RISK. A lupine leaf seen from above is literally a radial star, which is the shape ARRANGEMENT_NEGATIVE spends nine terms refusing. It is kept because it is the species' second identifier, and it is bounded: three or four of them at the patch edge, small, at every angle, with an explicit refusal of any leaf enlarged into a wheel or placed at the centre. If the delivery comes back with a leaf mandala, drop the clause rather than fighting it — at 20px the leaf is invisible anyway and the violet dots are the whole asset. THE FOUR ARE ONE COMMISSION AND SHARE A FRAME. [[river-fireweed]] was Sockeye Run's only flower and its note says in capitals to use it sparingly, which left the meadow with a choice between bare grass and one loud magenta. These four are the rest of the meadow: a cool blue-violet, a gold, a cream and a scarlet, so a terrace can be planted with four or five species at different sizes and read as WILD rather than as five colour-coded beds. That last word is the brief and it is also the acceptance test — a planting that looks sorted has failed even if every sprite is good. SIZES ARE HONEST AND THEY LADDER: lupine 2.2 m = 20u, yarrow 1.75 m = 16u, arnica 1.5 m = 14u, paintbrush 1.3 m = 12u, against [[river-fireweed]] at 2.0 m = 18u. The flower layer is therefore 12-20u, entirely below [[river-moss-mat]] at 26 and [[river-willow]] at 30, which is right: flowers are the smallest thing in the venue and the size spread is what stops a mixed planting looking stamped. GENERATED AS PATCHES, NOT COMPOSED FROM ELEMENTS. art-pipeline 3b says a master is one object and groups are built by compose.py, and these four are the documented exception it already allows for [[river-fireweed]]: a single arnica head is about 0.05 m, which is half a pixel as an element, so there is no single object to scatter. The patch IS the object. What 3b was written to prevent — the model returning a symmetric rosette — is instead handled in the subject, which is why all four carry the scatter clause. PLANE `canopy`, prop-spin ON, contact none, motion fixed — the same four decisions all seven of the venue's plants took on 2026-08-18, for the same reasons: none of these has a front, vegetation is land scenery the fleet cannot reach, and this is the venue already on record in script.js for replan spikes from its 82 hidden banks. planRound true and fillTo 0.86 throughout, as the six upright plants have. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6 — the row in venuedoc.js goes in when the art lands, alongside the seven that shipped 2026-08-18. ⚠️ EVERY dE IN THESE FOUR NOTES IS MEASURED ON DECLARED HEXES, NOT ON DELIVERED ART. They are design targets and the delivery has to be re-measured against them, exactly as [[river-fireweed]] was — which came back 52% flower against a subject asking for a scatter, so assume the same overshoot here and check the flower fraction first. ⚠️ ROUND 1 REJECTED 2026-08-21, AND IT FAILS BEFORE ANY OF THE ART IS JUDGED. The file came back 2816x1536, and check_master raises Fail('not square') on a non-square master — this never reaches the aesthetic checks. Content aspect is 1.837, which ingest reads as a camera ~57 degrees off vertical, worse than the worst of the 2026-08-09 tree batch at 56. Margins are 46-103px against the 225 an 8% safe margin needs at that size. AND THE SPIKES CAME BACK SIDE-ON, which is the whole reason this slot carries the [[river-fireweed]] clause: elongation median 1.36 with only 38% of marks near-round, against <1.6 and >=60%. Every raceme is a tapering cone with a visible point, drawn at its side-on length. [[lake-bulrush]] failed this twice, [[river-fireweed]] and [[river-paintbrush-scarlet]] both passed it first cut, and this is the third failure of the same physics in the library. ⚠️ AND THE PLACEMENT WARNING IN THIS NOTE WAS UNDERSTATED, WHICH IS THE ONE FINDING WORTH KEEPING FROM A REJECTED ROUND. Predicted dE 10.5 from [[river-cobble]]; measured 6.7. On the cobble row of the reduction strip the patch very nearly disappears. Whatever round 2 delivers, this plant does not go on the gravel bar. FIXED 2026-08-21, THREE CHANGES. The subject now NAMES THE FAILURE AS A SHAPE — a cone with a pointed tip — says that shape is what a spike looks like from the SIDE, gives the correct read (the tip is the part nearest the camera and sits in the middle of the mark, older flowers going outward around it), and puts a hard bound on it: no spike more than about 1.5x as long as it is wide. Second, it refuses the outward-radiating arrangement round 1 delivered — no spike aimed away from the middle, none sticking out past the foliage on a bare stalk. Third, `gen` is now set to 2048x2048 SQUARE, so the generation size prints in the prompt header and the non-square delivery cannot repeat by accident. WHAT ROUND 1 GOT RIGHT: colour, on both counts — flower mean #6459AE at dE 5.0 from the declared #5C61B8 and foliage #425434 at dE 5.0 from #414C31. And THE PALMATE-LEAF RISK DID NOT MATERIALISE: this note flagged the radial leaf as a deliberate risk and said to drop the clause if a leaf mandala came back. It did not — the leaves are small green hands at every angle, bounded exactly as asked. Keep the clause. Value spread came in at +9.3 against the +14 the subject asks for, so round 2 should push the foliage darker still. PER art/README.md, GEMINI HOLDS THE NADIR VIEW BEST of the generators measured, and this is the failure it is best at. Change generator before rewriting the subject a third time — the cove cargo family came back with visible cylinder sides from one model and clean plan shapes from another on the same words. ⚠️ ALL FOUR ROUND-1 DELIVERIES WERE MEASURED BEFORE INGEST, off files on the desktop rather than out of inbox/, so every number below is off the raw delivery and `status` stays `slot` until the file actually goes through ingest.py. Reduction was checked the way art-pipeline 6 asks — each sprite squared, scaled to its true world size and dropped on [[river-meadow]], [[river-cobble]] and [[river-humus]] — because at 12-20px that is the only question that matters and the 2048 master always looks fine. ✅ ROUND 2, 2026-08-21: THE FORESHORTENING CLAUSE LANDED AND THE SUBJECT IS NOW PROVEN. Across 30 flower marks the elongation median is 1.11 against the <1.6 asked and 90% are near-round against the >=60% asked — up from 1.36 and 38% in round 1. Axial resultant 0.116. Naming the failure as a SHAPE (a cone with a pointed tip), saying that shape is the side view, giving the correct read and bounding it at 1.5x did in one round what the inherited [[river-fireweed]] wording could not do on this species — the same lesson [[lake-bulrush]] taught and this is the second confirmation of it. Flower fraction 34.2% against the about-a-third asked, effectively exact. Flower mean #6162AB at dE 8.0 from spec, foliage #43553B at dE 4.7. At 20px on meadow and humus it is now a clean blue-violet patch. DO NOT REWRITE THIS SUBJECT AGAIN. ⚠️ THE 1.881 ASPECT IS NOT A TILTED CAMERA, AND THAT DISTINCTION MATTERS BECAUSE INGEST CANNOT MAKE IT. planRound reports the content is 1.88x longer on one axis and infers a camera ~58 degrees off vertical. THE FLOWER MARKS PROVE OTHERWISE: a camera 58 degrees off vertical squashes every round thing in the frame, and 90% of these marks are round. The bbox fills 95% x 92% of a 2816x1536 canvas — the model filled the frame it was handed, at a near-nadir view. Same class of false positive already on record for [[river-alder-red]], where the dome measurement disproved a 1.163 reading; here the tell is mark roundness. Do not 'fix' this by rewriting the camera clause. ONE SUBJECT LINE ADDED ANYWAY, because two rounds of the `gen` header have not reached the canvas: the frame is square and the patch fills it in both directions, with as much above the middle as below. FOLIAGE STILL RUNS LIGHT: delivered L* 34.1 against the declared 30.7, so the value spread came in at +10.5 against the +14 the subject asks for (round 1: +9.3). The declared hexes are right and are being missed by about three points; if round 3 misses again, declare the foliage darker to compensate rather than adding words. Whole-sprite mean is dE 9.7 from [[river-cobble]] (round 1: 6.7) — the placement constraint in this note stands. ⚠️ AND BOTH ROUND-2 FILES CAME BACK 2816x1536 AGAIN, WHICH IS NOT A PROMPT PROBLEM AND CANNOT BE FIXED BY WRITING MORE WORDS. `gen` only prints a line in the prompt header — nothing downstream reads it — so whatever is generating these is set to a 16:9 canvas and the model is dutifully filling the frame it was given. A non-square master is check_master's first hard Fail, so neither file can even reach the aesthetic checks. THE FIX IS OPERATIONAL: set the generator to 1:1 before the next roll. Everything else in these two notes is downstream of that. ⚠️ ROUND 3 REJECTED 2026-08-21, AND IT IS THE MOST INSTRUCTIVE OF THE THREE: THE CANVAS FIX WORKED AND IT BROKE THE FLOWERS. Delivered 1024x1024 square, content aspect 1.036 — passes planRound cleanly for the first time, margins 52-78px against the 6% safeMargin's 61 so it will warn on top and bottom and nothing worse. But the foreshortening went backwards: elongation median 1.44 and only 39% of marks near-round, against round 2's 1.11 and 90%. ⚠️ IT IS A RADIAL BURST, AND THAT IS [[lake-bulrush]]'s FIRST FAILURE MODE ARRIVING HERE THIRD HAND. Radial alignment measures 0.772 against 0.64 for a neutral scatter, and the bulrush's own rejected round measured 0.851 — this is the same picture. Inner and outer marks are equally elongated (1.41 and 1.43), so it is not a rim effect: the whole patch has been composed as a BOUQUET SEEN FROM ABOVE, spikes radiating from a green middle. THE TWO VARIABLES INTERACTED AND THAT IS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ANYONE CELEBRATES A ROUND-2 NUMBER. Round 2's 90% near-round was measured on a 16:9 canvas, which gave the model no room for a radial composition and suppressed the burst by accident; the square frame invites the bouquet back. So round 2 did not prove the subject solved, it proved the subject solved ON A FRAME THAT IS ITSELF A DEFECT. Read the two together, not in sequence. AND THE NEGATIVE WAS ALREADY THERE. Round 2's patch added 'THE SPIKES DO NOT POINT OUTWARD FROM THE PATCH... none of them sticks out past the foliage on a bare stalk', and round 3 delivered exactly that, on bare stalks, all round the rim. A refusal did not work — which is the lesson this venue has now paid for four times ([[lake-bulrush]] twice, [[river-yarrow]]'s fern, and here). FIXED 2026-08-21 by replacing the refusal with the PHYSICS: there is no such thing as outward in a picture taken from straight above, every spike is the same distance from the camera so a rim spike is drawn exactly like a middle one, and a spike that appears to stick out sideways on a visible stalk is a spike LYING DOWN. Plus the measurable: every violet mark about as long as it is wide wherever it sits, and rim marks that are longer or more slanted than middle ones mean a bouquet. ACCEPTANCE FOR ROUND 4 ADDS RADIAL ALIGNMENT BELOW 0.70 to the existing elongation and near-round bars, because this delivery passes neither of the old two on its own terms and the burst is what the reviewer actually has to see. COLOUR HELD: flower #58549E at dE 8.9, foliage #3F4C37 at dE 3.9, flower fraction 27.1%. Value spread +8.6, still short of the +14 asked, third round running. Whole-sprite mean is now dE 7.9 from [[river-cobble]] — the keep-it-off-the-gravel-bar rule in this note is confirmed a third time and should be treated as settled. ⚠️ ROUND 2 INGESTED AND SHIPPED 2026-08-21 AS PROVISIONAL ART, BY OWNER DECISION, WITH A RE-ROLL PLANNED. Round 2 was chosen over round 3 deliberately and the choice is the right one: round 2 holds the flowers (elongation median 1.11, 90% near-round, flower fraction 34.2%) and fails only on the frame, where round 3 holds the frame (square, aspect 1.036) and fails on the flowers (1.44, 39% near-round, radial alignment 0.772). A bad frame is recoverable by regenerating on a square canvas; a radial burst is the failure this venue has fought four times. Ship the one whose defect is mechanical. INGEST WARNED THREE TIMES AND EXITED 0: downsample 2816->1024, content within 6% of the edge, and NOT ORTHOGRAPHIC at 1.88x implying ~58 degrees off vertical. THE THIRD WARNING IS THE FALSE POSITIVE ALREADY ANALYSED ABOVE — 90% of the flower marks are round, which a 58-degree camera cannot produce — so it is a wide canvas, not a tilt. Shipped at 80px bake for 20px display; content 86%x46% of frame, visible at 17x9px. ⚠️ AND THE MASTER IN masters/river/ IS NOT WHAT THE GENERATOR RETURNED. Both files came back 2816x1536, which check_master rejects outright, so each was PADDED WITH TRANSPARENCY to a 2816x2816 square before it went into inbox/. Nothing was cropped, scaled or repainted — the delivered pixels are untouched and the pad is pure alpha — but the archived master is a reconstruction and the next roll should not be diffed against it as though it were an original. THE PAD COSTS NOTHING BY ITSELF: fillTo crops back to the alpha bbox and rebuilds the frame, so the padding is discarded a few lines later. It exists only to get past the square check. ⚠️ THE SPRITE THEREFORE DRAWS SHORT, AND THIS IS THE ONE CONSEQUENCE THAT MATTERS FOR PLACEMENT. fillTo fits the LONG axis to 86% of the frame, so 1.9:1 content leaves the short axis at about 45%. Planting done now will look markedly sparser than the same document will look after a square re-roll, because the same `world` will then carry a plant roughly twice as tall. Judge density AFTER the re-roll, not now. Position is authored and unaffected. REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS 2026-08-21 — canopy, contact none, prop-spin on, motion fixed, the same four the venue's seven plants took, and NO srcBox despite both being more oblong than [[river-moss-mat]] which carries one: srcBox is a draw-time sampling shortcut rather than a sizing control (drawSpriteBoxed maps the sub-rect to the same normalized destination), so it buys nothing visible and would be a stale number the moment either is re-rolled. ⚠️ NO RIVER PLATE EXISTS YET, so contact.py fell back to the arctic and lagoon water strips — which is the wrong test for a plant that stands on land, and the sheets in sheets/river/ should be read as reduction ladders only. `node regatta/art/plates.js river` is a one-time venue cost and every future Sockeye Run asset wants it. The real reduction check for this commission was done separately, compositing each sprite at its true world size onto [[river-meadow]], [[river-cobble]] and [[river-humus]]; both read at size. Anchor seeded at [0.4995, 0.5], the bbox centre, which is correct for a patch — there is no other point where a patch 'meets the world'.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. You are looking at the TOP of the plant and nothing else — no side of any stem, no length of trunk, no face of anything. ⚠️ NOTHING DARK SITS IN THE MIDDLE OF THIS PICTURE. There is no stem hub, no dark well and no clearing at the centre; the foliage covers whatever holds it up. A PATCH OF MOUNTAIN ARNICA in flower — the golden daisy of open subalpine meadow, drawn from broad-leaved arnica, Arnica latifolia. THIS IS A PATCH SEEN FROM TEN METRES UP, NOT A CLOSE-UP OF ONE FLOWER. Almost every picture of this plant is a single bloom filling the frame, and that is the wrong picture: here the heads are SMALL against the whole patch and there are many of them. THE HEAD IS HELD FLAT AND TURNED UP AT THE SKY, so unlike a spike there is nothing foreshortened about it — you are looking straight down into the open head and it is a CIRCLE. Each one is a small ROUND PLATE seen square on: a ring of ten to fifteen blunt-tipped, slightly notched ray petals around a small centre. That roundness is the flower's own shape drawn correctly, and it is not the same thing as a silhouette squashed by a tilted camera. EIGHT TO FOURTEEN HEADS in the whole patch, at plainly different sizes, gathered into two or three loose groups that touch and overlap, with leaf showing between the groups — not spaced evenly, and never one head in the middle with the rest arranged around it. ⚠️ THE CENTRE IS DEEPER GOLD, NOT A DARK BUTTON. Arnica's disc is the same warm yellow family as its petals, only richer. It is NOT a black-eyed susan and NOT a sunflower: no brown centre, no black centre, no dark eye, and no white petals anywhere in this picture. THE COLOUR IS THE POINT OF THE PLANT: a lit ray near #F9CB44, a ray body near #F2B41C, the disc centre near #D2900F and a shade where one head laps another near #A6700B. It is a clean, hot, saturated GOLDEN YELLOW — never lemon, never an acid green-yellow, never orange, never cream. If it goes green-yellow it becomes the grass it is standing in. THE LEAVES ARE BROAD AND CARRIED IN OPPOSITE PAIRS, drawn as chunky two-tone blades at many angles, filling the gaps between the heads so the patch is not bare. They are a DARK green and that is deliberate — the gold has to sit on something much darker than itself: a lit near #4E5C34, a body near #3E4A28 and a shade near #2E3A1C. ABOUT HALF THE PATCH IS YELLOW. This one is allowed to be flower-heavy, because a golden flower over green leaf averages to exactly the yellow-green of the meadow it grows in, and a thin scatter would simply dissolve into the grass. ⚠️ IT MUST NOT COME BACK AS A ROSETTE. Vary the SIZE of the flowers as well as their spacing — equal-sized marks at uneven angles still line up under rotation. No even spacing, no ring, no four-fold or six-fold arrangement, no flower answered by a matching one across the middle, and the thickest part of the patch pushed plainly off-centre. THE ROSETTE BEING REFUSED IS THE LAYOUT OF THE PATCH, NOT THE FLOWER: one flower head is a small ring of parts and that is the correct drawing of it. What must never happen is the PATCH being arranged as one. NOTHING ELSE: no butterfly, no bee, no seed head, no bare stem visible along its length, no water. THE SILHOUETTE IS AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE — irregular, but the span top-to-bottom matches the span side-to-side. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the plant is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it grows on.
assets.note: THE STRONG YELLOW ACCENT, and the one of the four whose colour problem runs the OPPOSITE way to the others. Gold over green leaf averages to yellow-green, and yellow-green is precisely what [[river-meadow]] is made of: at a third flower cover the patch mean sits dE 17.0 from the meadow and 26.1 from its lit tone, which is a flower that dissolves into the grass it is standing in. TWO FIXES, BOTH IN THE SUBJECT. First the gold was pushed off the green-yellow axis, from a natural #E3B02A to a hotter #F2B41C: that alone moves the flower from dE 45.9 to 53.8 against [[river-meadow]] and from 41.3 to 49.0 against its lit tone, and it also opens the gap to [[river-paintbrush-scarlet]] from 58.7 to 59.7, so it costs nothing anywhere. Second, this is the ONLY one of the four asked to be flower-heavy — about half the patch — where [[river-yarrow]] is capped at a third. That is not inconsistency, it is the same measurement pointing in opposite directions: at half cover the arnica mean moves out to dE 23.0 from the meadow, and the [[river-fireweed]] overshoot (52% flower against a subject asking for a scatter) works in this asset's favour for once. SEPARATION IS OTHERWISE THE BEST OF THE FOUR: dE 88.0 from [[river-humus]], 84.4 from [[river-cobble]], 79.7 from lit granite, 99.9 from [[river-fireweed]] and 128.0 from [[river-lupine-nootka]] — the widest pair in the venue. Internal value spread is +47.4, so it reads as a bright speckle in greyscale too. NO FORESHORTENING CLAUSE, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THE SPECIES. A daisy head is held horizontal and turned at the sky, so from directly overhead you get the whole disc for free — the failure [[lake-bulrush]] and [[river-fireweed]] were written around simply does not exist here. What replaces it is the close-up refusal borrowed from [[cove-hydrangea-blue]]: almost every image of arnica is one bloom filling the frame, and this is a patch seen from ten metres up. ⚠️ THE WORD `ROSETTE` HAD TO BE DISAMBIGUATED. prompt.py appends `rosette` to every non-symmetric asset's negatives, and an arnica head is literally a ring of ray petals — so the prompt would have carried an instruction and its opposite, which prompt.py's own portrait note records a generator resolving by dropping one half at random. Rather than set allowSymmetry (which would drop the whole arrangement negative and invite the patch mandala), the subject states that the refused rosette is the LAYOUT and the ring of petals is the correct drawing of one flower. Same clause on [[river-yarrow]]. THE DARK CENTRE IS THE OTHER PREDICTABLE FAILURE: every generator's prior for a yellow daisy is a black-eyed susan or a sunflower, and a brown button in the middle of a 14px sprite is a hole. The subject names both species as the thing being refused. ACCEPTANCE: no disc pixel darker than the declared #A6700B, and the mean flower colour within dE 10 of #F2B41C. THE FOUR ARE ONE COMMISSION AND SHARE A FRAME. [[river-fireweed]] was Sockeye Run's only flower and its note says in capitals to use it sparingly, which left the meadow with a choice between bare grass and one loud magenta. These four are the rest of the meadow: a cool blue-violet, a gold, a cream and a scarlet, so a terrace can be planted with four or five species at different sizes and read as WILD rather than as five colour-coded beds. That last word is the brief and it is also the acceptance test — a planting that looks sorted has failed even if every sprite is good. SIZES ARE HONEST AND THEY LADDER: lupine 2.2 m = 20u, yarrow 1.75 m = 16u, arnica 1.5 m = 14u, paintbrush 1.3 m = 12u, against [[river-fireweed]] at 2.0 m = 18u. The flower layer is therefore 12-20u, entirely below [[river-moss-mat]] at 26 and [[river-willow]] at 30, which is right: flowers are the smallest thing in the venue and the size spread is what stops a mixed planting looking stamped. GENERATED AS PATCHES, NOT COMPOSED FROM ELEMENTS. art-pipeline 3b says a master is one object and groups are built by compose.py, and these four are the documented exception it already allows for [[river-fireweed]]: a single arnica head is about 0.05 m, which is half a pixel as an element, so there is no single object to scatter. The patch IS the object. What 3b was written to prevent — the model returning a symmetric rosette — is instead handled in the subject, which is why all four carry the scatter clause. PLANE `canopy`, prop-spin ON, contact none, motion fixed — the same four decisions all seven of the venue's plants took on 2026-08-18, for the same reasons: none of these has a front, vegetation is land scenery the fleet cannot reach, and this is the venue already on record in script.js for replan spikes from its 82 hidden banks. planRound true and fillTo 0.86 throughout, as the six upright plants have. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6 — the row in venuedoc.js goes in when the art lands, alongside the seven that shipped 2026-08-18. ⚠️ EVERY dE IN THESE FOUR NOTES IS MEASURED ON DECLARED HEXES, NOT ON DELIVERED ART. They are design targets and the delivery has to be re-measured against them, exactly as [[river-fireweed]] was — which came back 52% flower against a subject asking for a scatter, so assume the same overshoot here and check the flower fraction first. ⚠️ THE WORD `DISC` IS AVOIDED IN THIS SUBJECT ON PURPOSE, for the same reason `rosette` had to be disambiguated: ROUND_NEGATIVE appends `flattened disc` and `squashed circle` to every planRound asset, and this flower head genuinely IS a flat round plate — so the prompt would have named the wanted shape in the subject and refused it three paragraphs later. The head is called a plate, and one line says outright that its roundness is the flower's shape rather than a tilted camera. `disc centre` survives in the colour list because that is the botanical term for the middle of a daisy and reads as a different sense. DELIVERED 2026-08-21, FIRST CUT, AND EVERY COLOUR AND FLOWER DECISION IN THIS NOTE LANDED. Flower mean #E9AA17 at dE 4.1 from the declared #F2B41C — the closest colour match of the four. Foliage #445524 at dE 9.2. NO DARK BUTTON: the disc centres came back deeper gold as specced, so the black-eyed-susan prior that the subject names twice did not fire. No white petals. Heads are true circles (elongation median 1.02, 81% near-round) and they are NOT ringed — bearing gap cv 1.26, mark radius sd 0.28, so the layout is honestly irregular. Zero interior alpha holes. Internal value spread +40.0, which is why it holds up on the light grounds. ⚠️ THE COVERAGE ARGUMENT IN THIS NOTE WAS HALF WRONG AND THE HALF THAT WAS WRONG IS WORTH KEEPING. It came back at 36.2% flower against the about-half the subject asks for — UNDER, where [[river-fireweed]] and [[river-paintbrush-scarlet]] both overshot, so the overshoot is not reliable and cannot be designed around. And the whole-sprite mean does land where predicted, dE 17.4 from [[river-meadow]] against the 17.0 computed — but at true size on the meadow it reads perfectly well anyway. THE MEAN WAS THE WRONG STATISTIC: a high-contrast speckle does not read as its average, it reads as its bright element, and the gold is dE 53.8 from the ground with +40 points of value on it. Weight the mean for a LOW-contrast sprite ([[river-yarrow]] against [[river-willow]], where it was right) and weight the accent colour for a high-contrast one. ⚠️ THE ONE REAL DEFECT IS THAT THE SILHOUETTE IS A SQUARE — a slab of foliage with rounded corners, filling 53% of its enclosing circle where a lumpy round patch fills about 78%. It passes planRound at aspect 1.012, which is the check's blind spot: a square is exactly as tall as it is wide. NOTHING CLIPS — drawProps rotates on the canvas and drawSpriteBoxed draws the whole frame at w x w, so this is not art-pipeline 3b's compose.py inscribed-circle problem. What it costs is that prop-spin is ON and the silhouette width swings +29% with heading (against +10% for [[river-yarrow]] and +19% for [[river-paintbrush-scarlet]]), so a planted stand breathes as the props sit at different headings, and it reads slightly as a cut swatch rather than a patch. ACCEPTED as delivered: at 14px it is a clean gold mark on all three grounds and the pulse is about 4px. If it is ever re-rolled, ask for a lumpy irregular rim and refuse the square by name — do NOT fix it by lowering fillTo, which would throw away a third of the on-screen size for a cosmetic gain. ⚠️ ALL FOUR ROUND-1 DELIVERIES WERE MEASURED BEFORE INGEST, off files on the desktop rather than out of inbox/, so every number below is off the raw delivery and `status` stays `slot` until the file actually goes through ingest.py. Reduction was checked the way art-pipeline 6 asks — each sprite squared, scaled to its true world size and dropped on [[river-meadow]], [[river-cobble]] and [[river-humus]] — because at 12-20px that is the only question that matters and the 2048 master always looks fine.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. You are looking at the TOP of the plant and nothing else — no side of any stem, no length of trunk, no face of anything. ⚠️ NOTHING DARK SITS IN THE MIDDLE OF THIS PICTURE. There is no stem hub, no dark well and no clearing at the centre; the foliage covers whatever holds it up. A PATCH OF COMMON YARROW in flower — Achillea millefolium, the tough ferny herb that scatters itself through every dry meadow and gravel terrace in the north. It is THE LOOSE ONE of this venue's flowers: it does not make a field, it threads itself through the grass in ones and twos. ⚠️ IT IS SEVEN TO TEN SEPARATE PLANTS STANDING NEAR ONE ANOTHER, NOT ONE SPECIMEN, AND THIS IS THE THING THE PICTURE MUST GET RIGHT. Each plant is its own small tuft of leaf with its own stem coming out of the ground in its own place, and those places are scattered across the patch at uneven spacing, several of them well off to one side. THERE IS NO SINGLE POINT THAT ANYTHING RADIATES FROM: no hub, no crown, no rosette of leaves, no fan, no starburst, no wheel of fronds. If you can point at one place in this picture and say the foliage grows out of there, it has been drawn as one plant and it is wrong. Neighbouring plants overlap and tangle so the patch reads as continuous cover, but every leaf in it belongs to a tuft somewhere off to the side. ⚠️ AND NO TUFT IS ITSELF A LITTLE ROSETTE. Each one is a shapeless small cushion of that dark mottle — not a star, not a spray, not a wheel. If you can count the leaves coming out of a tuft, that tuft has been drawn as a botanical specimen and the picture is wrong. THE FLOWER HEAD IS A FLAT-TOPPED PLATE HELD LEVEL, which makes it the easiest thing in this venue to draw from straight above: you see the whole thing and it is a slightly irregular PALE PLATE with a finely pebbled surface, made of dozens of tiny florets packed shoulder to shoulder. Its roundness is the flower's own shape drawn correctly, and it is not the same thing as a silhouette squashed by a tilted camera. ⚠️ AND THE PLATE IS FLAT — IT HAS NO VOLUME AT ALL. It is not a ball, not a pompom, not a dome, not a bobble and not a sphere: it is a COIN LYING FACE UP on the ground. It is lit evenly right across, the same brightness at its rim as at its middle, with no gradient from a lit top to a shaded underside, no highlight, no soft rounding into the third dimension and no shadow cast on the leaves under it. The pebbling is a fine FLAT mottle drawn inside that disc the way gravel is drawn on a path — texture on a flat surface, never bumps on a ball. If a head comes back with a lit side and a dark side it has been drawn as a sphere and it is wrong. Draw the pebbling as a soft fine mottle, never floret by floret, and let the rim of each plate be slightly ragged where the outer florets sit proud. TWELVE TO SIXTEEN PLATES in the whole patch, at plainly different sizes, in loose ones and twos rather than a bouquet — and if the quarter-to-a-third coverage below is not being met, ADD MORE PLATES rather than swelling the ones already there; a handful of big pale balls reads as eggs, where a dozen smaller discs reads as a flowering herb, and NOT ARRANGED IN A RING AROUND ANYTHING — some near the edge, some well inside, several close together on one side and a gap on the other. ⚠️ EACH PLATE IS A CIRCLE AND THAT IS THE CAMERA TEST FOR THIS WHOLE PICTURE. A flat plate held level and photographed from straight above is ROUND. If the plates come back as ovals — and especially if they are ovals all squashed the same way — the camera was at the side of the plant, and everything else in the picture is wrong too however good it looks. ⚠️ THE COLOUR IS CREAM, NOT WHITE, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE CHOICE: a lit plate near #F0E6C6, a body near #DED0A4, a shade under an overlapping plate near #B5A67C. A pure white flower disappears against the pale granite and dry cobble this venue is largely made of; the warm cream keeps it. Never pink, never yellow, never a cold blue-white, never grey. THE FOLIAGE IS THE DARKEST GREEN OF THIS VENUE'S FLOWERS AND IT IS DOING A JOB — it is the dark ground that makes a pale flower visible at all. ⚠️ DO NOT DRAW THE LEAVES AS LEAVES. This entire plant is sixteen pixels on screen and no leaf detail survives that, so what is wanted here is a TEXTURE rather than botany: the foliage is a dense, fine-grained, dark green MOTTLE built from many SHORT soft strokes at every angle, packed close and evenly, and no single stroke is longer than about a twelfth of the patch. It should read as a low scrubby dark cushion at a distance and as nothing in particular close up. ⚠️ AND THE MOTTLE HAS NO CENTRES IN IT. Its density and its stroke length are the SAME everywhere across the patch: there is no place the strokes fan out from, no place they converge on, and no little star or wheel or whorl anywhere in it. Think of a cropped lawn or the bristles of a scrubbing brush seen from above — even, directionless cover — and not a cluster of small rosettes. The middle of the patch is no darker and no busier than its edge. ⚠️ ABSOLUTELY NO FRONDS. No long leaf with a rib running down it and rows of teeth off that rib, no spray of leaves opening out from one point, no fern, no bracken, no palm, no carrot top, no feather, no plume. If a leaf in this picture is long enough to follow with your eye from one end to the other, it is far too long. Build it from a lit near #5A6644, a body near #414C31 and a shade near #2F3823. ⚠️ BETWEEN A QUARTER AND A THIRD OF THIS PATCH IS PALE, AND BOTH ENDS OF THAT ARE BINDING. This is the one number that matters and it is a BAND, not a ceiling. Too much flower and it is a bridal bouquet, which at final size reads as a pale grey-green stone rather than as a plant. TOO LITTLE IS THE WORSE FAILURE: below about a fifth the plates stop registering at all, the whole thing goes to a nondescript green smudge, and the one reason this plant is in the picture is gone. There must be MORE LEAF THAN FLOWER everywhere, the middle included — but the flowers must be plainly, countably there, big enough and numerous enough to read as the point of the plant at a glance. THE PATCH IS OPEN AT ITS RIM: toward the edge it breaks into single plates, each with its own small tuft of leaf beneath it, and transparent background shows between those. The middle stays continuous. ⚠️ AND THE MIDDLE IS NOT DARKER THAN THE REST. Flat light from straight above puts no well in a patch: the centre is the same brightness as the edge, flower and leaf are mixed there exactly as they are everywhere else, and there is no shaded pit where stems come together. ⚠️ IT MUST NOT COME BACK AS A ROSETTE. Vary the SIZE of the flowers as well as their spacing — equal-sized marks at uneven angles still line up under rotation. No even spacing, no ring, no four-fold or six-fold arrangement, no flower answered by a matching one across the middle, and the thickest part of the patch pushed plainly off-centre. THE ROSETTE BEING REFUSED IS THE LAYOUT OF THE PATCH, NOT THE FLOWER: one flower head is a small ring of parts and that is the correct drawing of it. What must never happen is the PATCH being arranged as one. NOTHING ELSE: no daisy, no white petals arranged in a ring, no seed head, no bare stem visible along its length, no water. THE SILHOUETTE IS AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE — irregular, but the span top-to-bottom matches the span side-to-side. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the plant is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it grows on.
assets.note: THE NEUTRAL FILLER — the one that goes everywhere in small amounts and lets the other three be accents. It is also THE RISKIEST OF THE FOUR and the whole subject is built around one measurement. ⚠️ A WHITE FLOWER IN A VENUE OF PALE GRANITE AND DRY COBBLE. Pure white #E2DECB measures dE 16.0 from lit [[river-outcrop]] and 23.5 from lit [[river-cobble]] — it would vanish on two of the four grounds this venue is made of. Warming it to a cream #DED0A4 buys 11 points on the granite (27.2) and 2 on the cobble (25.6) at no cost anywhere else, which is why the subject says CREAM, NOT WHITE in capitals and gives the reason: a generator told to warm a white flower with no reason attached will drift back to white. ⚠️ AND THE REAL COLLISION IS [[river-willow]], NOT THE ROCK. A cream flower over green leaf averages to a pale grey-green, and pale grey-green at 30px IS the willow — the venue's one deliberately desaturated shrub. At a third flower cover this patch means out to dE 18.0 from it; at the half [[river-fireweed]] actually delivered, 12.1. Hence the hard cap in the subject, written as the one number that matters, plus the deliberately dark foliage (#414C31, L* 30.0) that pulls the mean down. ACCEPTANCE IS THE FLOWER FRACTION: pale pixels no more than 40% of the crown. Over that, re-roll. WHAT SEPARATES IT FROM THE WILLOW IF THE MEAN STILL CONVERGES is size, structure and internal contrast, not hue — 16u against 30u is a 1.9x step, the willow is a CLOSED low mound with about ten points of internal lightness and this is an OPEN speckled patch with a ragged rim, transparent gaps at the edge and +53.6 points between flower and leaf. That is the same argument [[river-alder-red]] was accepted on against [[river-spruce-sitka]] at dE 12.5, and it holds better here because the size step is larger. Both are ambient, so art-pipeline 2's hard rule does not bind. ⚠️ PLACEMENT: MEADOW AND FOREST OPENING. dE 34.0 from [[river-meadow]] and 67.9 from [[river-humus]] — strong. Keep it off the bare gravel bar and the granite shelf, where the flower itself is inside 30 of the ground. NO FORESHORTENING CLAUSE, for the best reason of the four: a yarrow corymb is a flat plate held level, so the overhead view IS the flower's own plan shape. This is the easiest subject in the venue and the acceptance risk is entirely in the coverage, not the geometry. It carries the same `rosette` disambiguation as [[river-arnica]] — see that note for why allowSymmetry was not used. THE FOUR ARE ONE COMMISSION AND SHARE A FRAME. These four are the rest of the meadow: a cool blue-violet, a gold, a cream and a scarlet, so a terrace can be planted with four or five species at different sizes and read as WILD rather than as five colour-coded beds. This is [[lake-bulrush]]'s radial-burst failure wearing a different plant. THE DIAGNOSIS IS A MISSING CLAUSE, NOT A STUBBORN GENERATOR. The cap was written as a CEILING with no floor — 'no more than a third' — and it was read as 'as little as possible'. At 16px on all three grounds the result is a dull olive smudge with two faint specks in it; round 1, at 32%, read as clear white speckle. A one-sided bound on a number the generator is already inclined to under-deliver is a trap, and this note's own prediction that the [[river-fireweed]] overshoot would carry it is now wrong twice — [[river-arnica]] under-delivered too. FIXED: the clause is now a BAND, a quarter to a third, with both ends stated as binding and the too-little case named as the worse failure. This is [[lake-bulrush]]'s lesson in its other form — three rounds of negatives lost, stating the correct read won. FIXED by removing the botany entirely: the foliage is now specified as a TEXTURE, a dense fine dark-green mottle of short strokes with a length bound of one twelfth of the patch, plus an explicit statement that no leaf detail survives sixteen pixels so none is being asked for. You are looking at the TOP of the plant and nothing else — no side of any stem, no length of trunk, no face of anything. ⚠️ NOTHING DARK SITS IN THE MIDDLE OF THIS PICTURE. There is no stem hub, no dark well and no clearing at the centre; the foliage covers whatever holds it up. A SMALL PATCH OF SCARLET INDIAN PAINTBRUSH — Castilleja miniata, the flame-coloured spike that turns up in ones and twos through northern meadow and never in a field. It is the WARMEST thing in this venue's planting, and its job is to stop the meadow reading as a set of tidy colour-coded flower beds. ⚠️ WHAT YOU SEE IS NOT PETALS, IT IS BRACTS: the colour is carried by leafy bracts crowded at the top of the stem, each one cut into three blunt lobes, and the true flower is a thin green tube barely showing among them. Draw the colour as a crowd of lobed bracts — not as a ring of petals, not as a trumpet, not as a daisy. ⚠️ THE HEADS ARE VERTICAL AND YOU ARE LOOKING DOWN THE LENGTH OF THEM. A head seen end-on foreshortens almost to nothing, so each one is a COMPACT SCARLET BLOB sitting where its stem is — never a long streak, never a stroke lying across the picture, and never a brush drawn at its side-on length. FIVE TO NINE HEADS in the whole patch, no two the same size. THE RIM OF EACH BLOB IS TORN, and that is what separates this flower from every other one here: the bract lobes stick out all round it, so its outline is jagged in small increments — not the smooth knob of a spike of pea flowers and not the clean plate of a flat-topped herb. That ragged edge is the identity. Keep it even when the blob is small. THE COLOUR IS THE POINT OF THE PLANT: a lit bract near #E86A38, a body near #CC4126, a deep near #9E2A1C. It is a hot SCARLET leaning orange-red — never pink, never magenta, never rose, never a cool crimson or blood red. If it drifts pink it stops being this plant. THE LEAVES ARE NARROW and green, fine strokes at many angles filling the gaps, and two or three of them just below the heads are FLUSHED DULL RED where the bract colour runs down into them, which is true of this plant and is a cheap second accent. Green: a lit near #56663C, a body near #43522E, a shade near #313D22; the flushed leaves near #7A4A32. ABOUT A THIRD OF THE PATCH IS SCARLET, and the heads stand well apart with green between all of them and none of them touching. This plant grows scattered; a solid red cushion is the wrong picture. ⚠️ IT MUST NOT COME BACK AS A ROSETTE. Vary the SIZE of the flowers as well as their spacing — equal-sized marks at uneven angles still line up under rotation. No even spacing, no ring, no four-fold or six-fold arrangement, no flower answered by a matching one across the middle, and the thickest part of the patch pushed plainly off-centre. NOTHING ELSE: no petal ring, no trumpet flower, no bee, no hummingbird, no seed head, no bare stem visible along its length, no water. THE SILHOUETTE IS AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE — irregular, but the span top-to-bottom matches the span side-to-side. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the plant is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it grows on.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. A MAT OF FOREST MOSS lying on the ground, seen from straight down and ALONE. IT IS A FLAT SHEET, NOT A MOUND, and that is the first thing to get right: moss on a rainforest floor is a carpet a few centimetres thick, so there is no dome, no lit top and no shaded rim — the light is flat and even across the whole mat and its brightness varies only with the moss itself. THE OUTLINE IS RAGGED AND AMORPHOUS: an irregular blob with soft frayed edges and one or two thin tongues creeping out, nothing like a circle, nothing like a leaf, nothing with a point or an axis. It must have NO FRONT AND NO DIRECTION — the engine spins these to random headings and lays them over one another, so any elongation, any spine, any feature that reads as 'this way up' becomes a repeated mark once a dozen are scattered. THE SURFACE is a fine even mottle of tiny rounded cushions and short soft tufts, all small: a lit cushion near #7E9440, a body near #6E8434 and a shade near #56682A between them, with a scatter of slightly yellower patches. ⚠️ NO LANDMARK. Nothing large enough or distinct enough to be recognised twice on screen — no big cushion, no bare patch, no twig, no stone, no fern, no water, no soil showing through. The mat is the same density everywhere. This variant is the ROUNDEST of the three — a broad irregular blob, roughly as wide as it is tall, the one that fills the middle of a patch. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the plant is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it grows on.
assets.note: ONE OF THREE MOSS MATS, and they exist as three keys rather than one because the owner asked for variants that can be rotated, scaled and LAYERED — overlapping copies of a single mat repeat a recognisable outline, and outline is the only thing a moss sprite has. The three differ by SHAPE and nothing else: this is the roundest, the one that fills the middle of a patch. They share one palette so a layered group reads as one continuous carpet. 24u. ⚠️ FLAT, NOT DOMED — this is the one plant in the venue that does NOT take the centre-bright value structure the three trees needed, because a mat has no top. If it comes back with a lit middle it has been drawn as a cushion rather than a carpet. PROP-SPIN ON is mandatory rather than optional here, which is why the no-direction clause is in the subject: these are scattered and spun, and a mat with an axis becomes a visible repeated mark. planRound true. PLANE `surface` rather than `canopy` — moss lies ON the floor and nothing passes under it, which also keeps it out of the canopy family's draw order. COLOUR: a vivid yellow-green at dE 48.2 from [[river-humus]], the floor it mostly lies on, and 47.3 from [[river-outcrop]]. Its nearest neighbour is [[river-meadow]] at 13.2, which is close — but a moss mat is a small prop under forest and the meadow is an open terrace ground, so the two rarely meet, and where they do the mat's ragged outline separates it. It sits 32.3 from [[river-alder-red]], the shrub most likely to stand over it. ⚠️ DEMOTED 2026-08-18 FROM THE PRIMARY MOSS ANSWER TO A DETAIL OVERLAY, and its two sibling variants were deleted rather than drawn. The owner supplied two Southeast Alaska rainforest references and asked whether moss should be a prop or a terrain; measured, 73% and 74% of the lower frame in those photographs IS moss. It is not objects lying on a floor, it is the floor — an unbroken carpet running between every trunk, over every hummock and up over the fallen logs. That is a SURFACE, and the argument is already written into this codebase on the `lane` entry: a prop is a fixed-size sprite, so covering a forest floor with mats is dozens of placements with a seam at every join, where a polygon takes any shape for free. The carpet is now [[river-mossfloor]], a ground. THIS ONE SURVIVES because the references show the other half of the story too: moss creeps UP over boulders, logs and stumps, and it feathers into bare humus at the edges of a mossy area. Both are overlay jobs a ground polygon cannot do — a shape draws under props, not over them. So this is the mat you scatter ON things and along the transition, at 26u, and one variant is enough for that because it is spun and scaled per placement and never asked to cover an area on its own. planRound true, prop-spin ON, plane `surface`. ⚠️ planRound SET TO FALSE BEFORE INGEST, because the flag contradicts this asset's own subject. The brief asks for an outline that is 'ragged and amorphous... nothing like a circle', and the round test then reports that as a tilted camera — the delivery measures 1.39 and would trip NOT ORTHOGRAPHIC at 44 degrees. Unlike [[river-alder-red]], which kept the flag because its textbook dome proves the camera independently, a FLAT mat has no value structure to check against, so the warning here would be pure noise on every future cut. The camera check this asset actually needs is the flatness measurement below. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-18 AFTER A COLOUR CORRECTION IN POST. ⚠️ IT ARRIVED THE WRONG GREEN, AND FOR THIS ASSET THAT IS THE ONE FAULT THAT MATTERS, because a mat's whole job is to read as the SAME MATERIAL as the floor it lies on. Delivered #28A42F measured chroma 74.2 at hue 138.8 degrees — a vivid pure emerald — against the shipped [[river-mossfloor]]'s chroma 58.1 at 119.2: twenty degrees off in hue and sixteen points over in chroma, giving dE 29.0 between a mat and the carpet it is supposed to be part of. Corrected in post by rotating hue onto 119.1 and scaling chroma to 58.1 while holding lightness, which is a pure family match and touches nothing else. RESULT: dE from the mossfloor falls 29.0 -> 8.6, with the mat sitting L* 59.4 against the floor's 50.8 — the same material, a little lighter, which is exactly what fresh moss catching light should be. Verified on the ship test at its true 26px, spun to random headings over a fallen log on all three grounds: subtle relief on the moss carpet, a clear bright creep onto [[river-humus]], and moss climbing grey rock on [[river-outcrop]] — the three cases the owner's reference photographs actually show. ⚠️ THE FLATNESS CLAUSE WAS NOT MET AND IS ACCEPTED, WITH THE SUBJECT NOW OUT OF DATE RATHER THAN THE ART WRONG. It measures a +8.1 centre-to-rim dome where the subject demands about zero, and that clause was written when this asset was the PRIMARY moss answer — a carpet, which genuinely has no top. It was demoted to an overlay for logs, boulders and stumps AFTER the subject was written, and those things ARE domed: moss on a boulder is a cushion. At 26px drawn the dome is barely a pixel of shading either way. If this is ever re-rolled, rewrite the flatness clause to match the demoted role rather than asking for a flat mat again. Zero white stroke, real alpha, solidity 0.99. REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS 2026-08-18, with all seven of Sockeye Run's plants. `canopy` for the six that grow up, following Stillwater's eight; `surface` for [[river-moss-mat]], which lies on the ground and would be drawn over hulls for nothing on canopy. CONTACT none throughout: vegetation is land scenery the fleet cannot reach, so a collider would never be tested, and this is the venue whose own 82 hidden banks are on record in script.js for multi-hundred-millisecond replan spikes. PROP-SPIN ON for all seven — none has a front. srcBox carried only by the mat, which is honestly oblong at 0.63 of its frame; the six plants fill 74-87% after fillTo and have nothing worth skipping. Verified in a running editor: all seven in the picker, a document placing all seven validates clean and compiles to 7 props and ZERO hidden colliders, which is the contact:none decision showing up where it should.

assets.subject: A RAINFOREST MOSS CARPET seen from directly overhead from about ten metres up, in flat even light — the continuous moss floor of a Southeast Alaska spruce-hemlock forest, where moss covers everything that is not a trunk. THE SQUARE COVERS ABOUT 14 METRES. IT IS ONE UNBROKEN LIVING SURFACE, not a collection of patches: no bare soil, no litter showing through, no gaps of ground — moss edge to edge, which is the whole character of this floor and the thing that separates it from an ordinary forest litter. AT THIS HEIGHT NOTHING RESOLVES AS AN OBJECT. The surface reads as a SOFT LUMPY MOTTLE: the carpet lies over roots, stones and rotted wood, so it swells into low rounded HUMMOCKS and sinks into shallow hollows between them, each hummock perhaps a tenth of the square across, soft-edged and irregular, running into one another with no hard boundary anywhere. Over that broad lumpiness lies a fine even texture of tiny cushions and short soft tufts, all far too small to count. A FEW DRIFTS OF SLIGHTLY YELLOWER, BRIGHTER MOSS where more light reaches, and a few cooler deeper-green hollows, both soft and patchy and neither covering more than a fifth of the square. THE COLOUR IS A VIVID YELLOW-GREEN, the brightest ground in the venue and much more saturated than any grass: a lit hummock near #5E8A26, a body near #487618, and a shade near #375A12 in the hollows. It is a LIVING green, never olive, never grey-green, never the dry yellow of a meadow. NOTHING ELSE: no fern drawn as a recognisable fern, no twig, no cone, no stone, no root, no log, no mushroom, no water, no footprint. ⚠️ IT MUST TILE. The engine repeats this square edge to edge across a whole forest floor, so the left edge continues into the right and the top into the bottom with no seam. AND IT MUST CARRY NO LIGHT DIRECTION: flat even overcast light, no sun angle, no cast shadows sharing a direction, no vignette, no darker corners, no brighter centre — the hummocks are modelled by the moss's own tone, not by a light. NO LANDMARK: nothing large or distinct enough to be recognised twice on screen.
assets.note: SOCKEYE RUN'S FIFTH GROUND, and the one the owner's reference photographs actually show. Measured on both, 73% and 74% of the forest floor in frame is moss — this is a surface, not scenery, which is why it is a terrain and why [[river-moss-mat]] was demoted to an overlay. tileWorld 128, matching [[river-humus]] and the two lake grounds whose readable feature is decimetre-scale; the hummock is the resolvable feature here and at 14 m per square a 1.4 m hummock is a tenth of the width, comfortably above the 1.56% resolution floor prompt.py states. ⚠️ THE COLOUR IS TAKEN FROM THE DARKER REFERENCE ON PURPOSE. The two photographs measure #487618 (L* 44.8, chroma 53.5) in shaded forest and #819E31 (L* 61.1, chroma 57.2) in a lit clearing, and the bright one is unusable: it sits dE 11.8 from [[river-meadow]], so a moss floor and an open meadow terrace would be the same colour on the map. The shaded value clears it at dE 23.3 while staying just as saturated, and it is also the honest one — this floor lives under a closed canopy. Against the rest: 52.0 from [[river-humus]], 50.7 from [[river-cobble]], 57.8 from [[river-outcrop]], and 23.6 from [[river-cottonwood-black]]'s crown, which is a tree over a ground rather than two grounds. ⚠️ IT PAIRS WITH HUMUS RATHER THAN REPLACING IT: humus is the dry needle floor under dense spruce, this is the wet moss floor of the deeper rainforest, and they are 52 apart so a designer can use both in one wood. ALPHA IS NOT SET YET — no LAND_TEXTURES row until the art lands, per the placeholder pattern the other four grounds shipped under; ISLAND_STYLES.body is provisional and must be reset to the delivered tile mean on ingest. DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-18. Shipped mean #618414 at L* 51.0, chroma 58.1, and ISLAND_STYLES.body is reset to it. Evenness is excellent — quadrant luma spread 2.5, no vignette, no baked light direction — and the landmark share is 2%, so nothing in it is countable once repeated. Wrap measures 1.97x/2.04x an interior boundary, the same as all four grounds before it, and is judged the same way: invisible once composited at alpha and tiled. ⚠️ IT IS THE BUSIEST TILE IN THE GAME AND THEREFORE TAKES THE LOWEST ALPHA IN THE GAME — those are one fact, not two. Tile-scale luma sd came in at 28.3 against a shipped range of 3.3 to 17.4, which is not an overshoot but the subject working: a moss carpet IS thousands of tiny cushions. Alpha 0.31 lands it at on-screen sd 8.78, matching lake forestfloor's 8.87 exactly — the top of the band, and the right precedent since both are forest floors. Recorded for later: 0.55 doubles the cushion texture at on-screen sd 15.6, and a floor the fleet can never sail on is the one place leaving the band is arguable. ⚠️ THE COLOUR CAME IN LIGHTER THAN SPECCED AND THE MEADOW MARGIN NARROWED WITH IT. Spec was #487618 at L* 44.8, taken deliberately from the SHADED reference; delivered is L* 51.0, six points up and part of the way back toward the lit reference this note rejected. The consequence is exactly the one the spec was written to avoid: dE against [[river-meadow]] fell from the designed 23.3 to 16.7. ACCEPTED ON THE SHIP TEST, not on the number — rendered as the two grounds actually appear, tiled and composited at their own alphas with the boundary dead centre, they read as plainly different materials: this is a deeper, cooler, finely cushioned green and the meadow is a paler, drier, yellower one with visible tussock clumps. Two grounds have no silhouette to fall back on, so texture character is doing the work colour alone would not, which is the same argument [[river-cobble]] and [[river-outcrop]] ship on at dE 19.6. ⚠️ IF A THIRD GREEN GROUND IS EVER ADDED TO THIS VENUE, re-measure all three together first — moss at 16.7 from meadow leaves no room for another one between them. ⚠️ ITS CHART COLOUR IS NOT ITS GROUND COLOUR, SET 2026-08-22 — see MINIMAP_ISLAND in script.js. Both forest floors carry `trees: true`, so the minimap was taking their VEG tint and drawing humus at #4E5A34 (only -10 luma against the water: the venue's biggest landform was dissolving into the channel at chart size) and mossfloor at #7EA02A (+45, BRIGHTER than the water and nearly as bright as the meadow — the darkest, wettest forest charting as the most open ground). They now take #26382E, which is the shipped [[river-spruce-sitka]] sprite's own measured mean, and #33563B for the damper variant: -42 and -19 luma against the water, 15 luma and dE 16.9 apart from each other. The chart reads as forest because it is painted the colour of the tree that makes it. ISLAND_STYLES is deliberately untouched, so nothing about the course view changes.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. ONE GRANITE RIVER BOULDER, seen from directly above and ALONE, with no ground drawn around it. A BIG ONE — a block the size of a small car, the kind that sits in the middle of a rapid and splits the flow around itself. ONE STONE, ALONE: no second stone, no scatter, no companion pebble, nothing resting against it. IT IS ICE-PLANED AND THEN BROKEN, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF A GLACIAL ERRATIC. This is the granite of a mountain river canyon: the ice scoured it smooth and the frost has since cracked it apart, so from above it is an ANGULAR BLOCK — a rough polygon of four to seven straight-ish sides meeting at blunt corners, no two sides the same length, nothing rounded and nothing lobed. ⚠️ IT MUST NOT COME BACK AS A SOFT PEBBLE. A worn, egg-shaped, smoothly rounded stone is a different rock in a different place and it is the single most likely wrong answer here. ⚠️ FROM STRAIGHT ABOVE A BOULDER IS ALMOST A FLAT ANGULAR PLATE, AND THIS IS THE THING THE PICTURE MUST GET RIGHT. The scoured top plane is what faces the camera, so it FILLS THE SILHOUETTE — at least four fifths of everything you can see is that one flat top — and it sits CENTRED in the stone, not pushed to one side. The broken sides are almost entirely hidden underneath it: what is left of them is a NARROW RIM around the edge, a band a tenth of the stone's width at most, darker than the top and broken into a few straight segments. ⚠️ IF YOU CAN SEE THE FACE OF A SIDE — a whole facet standing up, wider than that rim, with its own shape and its own shading — THE CAMERA WAS TILTED AND THE PICTURE IS WRONG. A rock drawn with its top plane up at the back and its front faces filling the bottom of the frame is a three-quarter hero shot of a gemstone. That is the failure. You are not beside this stone, you are directly over it. THE TOP PLANE IS NOT FLAT IN TONE, and that is where the modelling goes instead: the ice left it slightly uneven, so it breaks into two or three broad facets meeting at hard straight lines, each a single flat tone, about eighteen points of lightness between the lightest and the darkest of them. No soft gradient anywhere. A COUPLE OF STRAIGHT CRACKS run across the top plane, thin and dark, dividing it unevenly; they do not meet in the middle and they do not make a pattern. THE COLOUR IS COOL GREY GRANITE with pale mineral banding: a lit top plane near #BFC4C9, a mid facet near #A0A6AC, a body near #7C838B and a shaded facet near #5E656D. One or two paler quartz seams may cross the top as narrow near-white streaks. No moss, no lichen, no orange, no rust, no warm brown. ⚠️ THE ACCEPTANCE TEST IS THE OUTLINE AND THE TOP. Seen from straight above a boulder is a compact blocky shape roughly as tall as it is wide, and the flat scoured top is the largest single area in the picture. If the top has vanished and you are looking at the SIDE of a rock, the camera was tilted. NOTHING ELSE: no water, no foam, no wet line, no gravel, no plant, no snow. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the object is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it sits on.
assets.note: THE ONE THAT SPLITS THE FLOW. 5.7 m, and at 52u it is very nearly one boat length, which makes it the venue's natural scale reference — a helmsman who has seen one knows how wide the gap beside it is. Place these in the rapids and at the heads of bars, in ONES: a big boulder is a decision point, and three of them in a row is a wall. contact hard, contactR 22. ⚠️ THE COLLIDER BUDGET IS THIS VENUE'S ONE HARD CONSTRAINT AND IT IS WRITTEN DOWN TWICE IN venuedoc.js: 'a contact prop compiles to a hidden circle that also enters the router's grid, and script.js records the river's 82 hidden banks causing multi-hundred-millisecond replan spikes'. That is THIS venue, by name. So the rule for this batch is that the KIND is free and the PLACEMENT is not: declaring a hard boulder costs nothing, and dropping two hundred of them into the channel would make the router unusable. Budget roughly FORTY hard-contact props across the whole course, concentrated where a boat can actually meet one — the rapids, the bar heads, the inside of tight bends — and use the free `contact: none` variants for scenery boulders sitting up the bank. Sockeye Run's seven plants all take contact none for exactly this reason. RADII ARE MEASURED OFF THE BAKE, NOT GUESSED FROM `world`, following [[lake-boulder-large]]: fillTo 0.86 means a prop draws at 86% of its declared size, so a 52u boulder is a 45px stone and its radius is 22, not 26. ⚠️ AND A BOULDER IS THE ONE CASE WHERE A CIRCLE IS EXACTLY RIGHT rather than a compromise — a boulder IS a circle in plan — so these take FULL coverage where every long prop in the library deliberately under-covers. THE EIGHT ARE ONE COMMISSION AND THEY FILL THREE GAPS THE VENUE HAD. Sockeye Run shipped with seven plants, four grounds and nothing else: no rock you can hit, no wood, and no sign that a human being has ever been there. The boulders give the card's own 'Rocky banks' hazards line something to point at, the log and the jam are the two most conspicuous objects in the owner's West Susitna reference after the trees themselves, and the bridge and tent are the whole of the venue's human presence. ⚠️ THE BOULDERS ARE NOT THE `outcrop` TERRAIN AND THE DISTINCTION IS WORTH KEEPING. `outcrop` is a SHAPE — 44 of them are authored in river.venue.js, equivalent diameters 54 to 1022 u, median 135 — and it means a scoured bedrock ledge standing out of the rapids. These are PROPS, and they mean individual stones. The largest boulder here is 52u, deliberately just under the smallest existing outcrop polygon, so the two families never compete: ledges are terrain, stones are props, and the size ladder says which is which without anyone having to explain it. ⚠️ AND THEY ARE NOT [[lake-boulder-large]] EITHER. Stillwater's is a glacial ERRATIC — 'rounded, not broken ... every edge worn soft ... a broad irregular LOBED BLOB'. This is the opposite geology: canyon granite that the ice planed flat and the frost then cracked apart, so it is an ANGULAR block with a flat scoured top and clean facets. The subjects name the rounded pebble as the failure precisely because the two venues would otherwise converge on the same stone. SCALE: at 9.2 px/m the ladder is 5.7 m, 3.7 m and 2.2 m for the three dry boulders, which is honest for river granite and needs none of the exaggeration the plants take. The large one is very nearly one boat length (56u), which is the most useful size reference the venue has. PLANES: `surface` for the dry boulders, the log and the tent — they sit on ground, under the fleet. `seabed` for the sunken boulder, so the water above it does the colouring, following the lagoon corals. `float` for the logjam, which rides ON the water and must draw after the water's own marks so no wake ripples across it. `canopy` for the footbridge, because that is the plane for a thing the fleet passes UNDER. Prop-spin ON for the boulders, the log and the tent; OFF for the bridge, which has an axis the placement must control. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. ⚠️ ROUND 1 REJECTED 2026-08-22: ALL THREE CAME BACK AS THREE-QUARTER VIEWS, AND THE OUTLINE TEST COULD NOT SEE IT. Measured on the deliveries, the flat top plane fills only 45.7%, 49.0% and 50.1% of the silhouette — half of each picture is the SIDE of the rock — and the top plane's centroid sits displaced toward the top of the frame by 4.9%, 15.0% and 10.6% of the stone's span, which is the signature of a camera tilted so the near faces show at the bottom. A straight-down camera has no reason to put the top plane off centre. Value spread came in at 38.7, 40.7 and 51.9 points against the ~18 asked, for the same reason: the dark side facets are only visible because the camera can see them. ⚠️ AND THIS IS THE FIRST SUBJECT IN THE LIBRARY WHERE planRound's OUTLINE TEST IS BLIND. ORTHO_ROUND's whole argument is that 'a roughly round subject seen from straight above is ROUND, and the moment the camera tips it flattens into an oval' — true of a tree crown, which is a flat thing. A boulder is a COMPACT BLOCK: tilt the camera 25 degrees and its silhouette stays as tall as it is wide, because the height it gains at the bottom replaces the top it loses at the back. All three of these PASS the aspect check (1.043, 1.113, 1.028) while being plainly three-quarter views. Do not read the ingest aspect number as evidence of the camera on a blocky subject; read the top-plane fraction and its centroid offset instead. THE SUBJECT ASKED FOR IT, WHICH IS THE HONEST DIAGNOSIS. The original text read 'Around it the broken sides drop away in two or three CLEAN FLAT FACETS with hard straight edges between them' — an instruction to DRAW THE SIDES, in a picture whose whole premise is that no side is visible. Same class of error as the footbridge's crooked clause. FIXED 2026-08-22: the top plane must fill at least four fifths of the silhouette and sit centred, the sides survive only as a rim a tenth of the stone's width, the three-quarter gemstone is named as the failure, and the two-or-three facet modelling moved ONTO the top plane where a straight-down camera can actually see it. ACCEPTANCE FOR ROUND 2, since the aspect check cannot carry it: top-plane area at least 80% of the silhouette, and its centroid within 4% of the stone's own centre. ✅ ROUND 2 DELIVERED AND INGESTED 2026-08-22, AND ACCEPTED ON THE REDUCTION TEST RATHER THAN ON THE CRITERION THIS NOTE SET. ⚠️ THE 80% TOP-PLANE TARGET WAS NOT MET AND IS NOT GOING TO BE. Round 2 measures 46.6%, 45.1% and 45.2% against round 1's 45.7%, 49.0% and 50.1% — essentially unmoved — and the value spread went the wrong way, 40.9 / 47.1 / 42.0 against the ~18 asked. ⚠️ AND THE METRIC I SET IS PARTLY UNSOUND, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING SO NOBODY RE-RUNS IT. Both 'top-plane fraction' and 'top-plane centroid offset' conflate CAMERA TILT with LIGHT DIRECTION: the base style asks for consistent directional lighting, so a stone lit from the upper left has a bright upper-left and a dark lower-right whether or not the camera is square to it. A rim-band uniformity test was tried instead and could not separate the two either — a bright facet running to the silhouette edge reads as zero rim. There is no cheap master-size number here that distinguishes a faceted stone seen from above from one seen at 20 degrees. SO THE DECISION WENT TO art-pipeline 6 AND 8, WHICH IS WHERE IT BELONGS: 'the only question that matters is whether the thing reads at the 26-130px it actually occupies'. Composited at true world size on [[river-cobble]], [[river-meadow]], [[river-outcrop]] and open water, all three read as unmistakable angular grey stones, the three-size ladder is cleanly stepped at 45 / 29 / 17px, and the tilt that is measurable at 2048px is invisible at race scale. Accepted. ⚠️ ONE PLACEMENT CONSEQUENCE FROM THAT SHEET: on [[river-outcrop]] the boulders are low contrast — grey stone on grey bedrock — and read only by their outline. They are strongest on water, cobble and meadow. A boulder sitting on a granite ledge is an odd placement anyway. ⚠️ AND TWO OF THREE CARRY A DARK OUTLINE STROKE the library does not otherwise use: medium and small measure a 23 and 24 point L* drop in the rim band, where large is clean. The subject refuses it by name for the small one and it came back anyway. ACCEPTED, and noted as a style inconsistency rather than a defect: at 29 and 17px on pale cobble and granite the outline measurably HELPS them separate from the ground. If the family is ever re-rolled, drop it — but do not re-roll for it.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOT STRAIGHT DOWN FROM WELL ABOVE, the geometry of an orthophoto. ONE DRIFT LOG STRANDED ON A GRAVEL BAR, seen from directly above and ALONE. It lies with its long axis running UP the frame, a debarked trunk about four times as long as it is wide, both ends broken rather than sawn and splintered open into pale angular chips. IT HAS BEEN IN THE RIVER AND IT SHOWS: the bark is almost entirely gone, and what is left clings in two or three ragged dark patches along one side. The bare wood beneath is SUN-BLEACHED to a pale silver-grey, near-white on the upper surface where it has dried hardest, with the long grain reading as a few chunky flat facets running the whole length rather than as fine lines. Down one flank a band of darker weathered grey-brown where it lies against the stones. THREE OR FOUR SNAPPED BRANCH STUBS jut out at uneven angles and uneven lengths, each ending in a splintered point — one long enough to matter, the others short. The root end is a little thicker and more broken up than the tip. Colours: a bleached top near #C6C2B4, a body near #9A9488, a weathered flank near #6E6659 and the remaining bark near #4A4038. NOTHING ELSE: no water, no wet line, no gravel, no moss, no leaves, no second log. No ground is drawn and no cast shadow: the object is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies what it sits on.
assets.note: STRANDED, NOT ADRIFT, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS `ambient` WHERE THE BAYOU'S IS A HAZARD. [[bayou-driftlog]] and [[bayou-deadhead]] are both floating obstructions in still black water. The West Susitna reference shows river logs doing something else entirely: lying high and dry on the gravel, bleached silver, well above the waterline. So this one is scenery — contact none, `surface` plane, no collider spent — and [[river-logjam]] is the batch's wood hazard. 8.3 m at 76u, close to [[lake-log-fallen]]'s 74u by coincidence rather than by copying: that one is a mossy forest deadfall, this is river-scoured driftwood with the bark gone and the wood sun-bleached near-white, which is a completely different value. Place it ON bars, pointing roughly downstream, and in ones and twos. THE EIGHT ARE ONE COMMISSION AND THEY FILL THREE GAPS THE VENUE HAD.
